Gradually replaced {{m|en|fowl}} as the most common term starting in the 14th century.

Pokorny suggests this root might be somehow related to {{m|ine-pro|*bū-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*bew-||to blow; swell}}, which could account for the alternation between "pig" and "big".

tiger.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:tygre|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|tygre}}, in part from {{inh|en|ang|tigras}} (pl.), in part from {{der|en|xno|tigre}}, both from {{der|en|la|tigris}}, from {{der|en|grc|τίγρις}}, from {{der|en|ira|-}} (compare {{cog|ae|𐬙𐬌𐬔𐬭𐬌|t=arrow}}, {{m|ae|𐬙𐬌𐬖𐬭𐬀|t=pointed}}). Ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)teyg-|t=to pierce, prick, be sharp}}. Compare English {{m|en|stick}}.

Likely a distant cognate with {{m|en|kaak}}. Perhaps related to {{m|en|cookie}}, {{m|en|kuchen}}, and {{m|en|quiche}}. {{doublet|en|coca|pos1=pastry}}.

chicken.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:chiken|id=bird|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|chiken}} (also as {{m|enm|chike}} > {{cog|en|chick}}), from {{inh|en|ang|ċicen}}, {{m|ang|ċycen||chicken}}, of uncertain origin. Possibly from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kiukīn||chicken}}, or alternatively from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kukkīn}}, equivalent to {{af|en|cock|-en|id2=diminutive noun}}.

Sense of "soft drink" most likely an {{ellipsis|en|fizzy juice|nocap=1}}, another similarly common term in Scotland.

milk.raw: {{ety|en|id=a white liquid|tree=1|:inh|enm:mylk}} From {{inh|en|enm|mylk}}, {{m|enm|milk}}, from {{inh|en|ang|meolc}}, {{m|ang|meoluc||milk}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*meluk||milk}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*meluks||milk}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂melǵ-||milk, to milk}}.

Theorized to have come to Iranian languages from {{cog|sa|व्रीहि}}.

must.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*med-}}{{etymid|en|hasto}} From {{inh|en|enm|moste}} {{gloss|"must", literally, "had to", the past tense of {{der|en|enm|moten|t=to have to|id=to have to}}}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mōste||had to}}, 1st & 3rd person singular past tense of {{m|ang|mōtan||to be allowed, be able to, have the opportunity to, be compelled to, must, may}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*mōtaną}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|moest||had to}}, {{cog|de|musste||had to}}, {{cog|sv|måste||must, have to, be obliged to}}. More at ''[[mote#Etymology_2|mote]]''.

should.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|scholde}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sċolde||}}, first and third person preterite form of {{m|ang|sċulan||should,” “have to,” “to owe}}, the ancestor of {{cog|en|shall}}. {{surf|en|shall|-ed}}. Cognate with {{cog|de|sollen|sollte}}, {{cog|got|𐍃𐌺𐌿𐌻𐌰𐌽|𐍃𐌺𐌿𐌻𐌳𐌰}}, {{cog|sv|skulle}}. Related to {{cog|enm|shild}} and {{m|enm|shildy}}.

OK.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂el- (other)||*h₃reǵ-}} Origin {{unk|en|title=disputed}}. Wikipedia lists {{w|List of proposed etymologies of OK|many possible etymologies}}, of which the most widely accepted is that it is an abbreviation of {{m|en|oll korrect|oll/orl korrect}}, a comical spelling of {{m|en|all correct}}, which first appeared in print in ''The Boston Morning Post'' on March 23, 1839, as part of a fad for similar fanciful abbreviations in the United States during the late 1830s. The expression became popular through its use in the presidential campaign of Martin Van Buren in 1840,

hi.raw: [[American English]]. First recorded reference is to speech of a Kansas Indian (1862); originally to attract attention, probably a variant of {{inh|en|enm|hey}}, {{m|enm|hy}} ([[circa]] 1475). Also an exclamation to call attention. See {{m|en|hey}}.{{rfref|en}}

good.raw: {{etymon|en|id=positive|:inh|enm:good<ety:inh<ang:gōd<id:good>>>|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰedʰ-}} {{inh+|en|enm|good}}, from {{inh|en|ang|gōd}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*gōd}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*gōdaz|t=good}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰedʰ-|t=to unite, be associated, suit, fit}}.

bad.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰedʰ-|id1=bend|*bʰeydʰ-}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:badde|tree=+}} From {{inh|en|enm|bad}}, {{m|enm|badde|t=wicked, evil, depraved}}, of {{unk|en|title=uncertain}} origin. Perhaps a shortening of {{der|en|ang|bæddel||hermaphrodite}} (for loss of ''-el'' compare {{m+|enm|muche}} from {{m+|ang|myċel}}, and {{m+|enm|wenche}} from {{m+|ang|wenċel}}), or at least related to it and/or to {{m|ang|bædan|bǣ̆dan|t=to defile}}, compare {{cog|goh|pad||hermaphrodite}}.

age.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:age|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂ey-|id=life}} From {{inh|en|enm|age}}, {{der|en|fro|eage|aage, eage, edage}}, from an assumed {{der|en|la-vul|*aetāticum}}, derived from {{der|en|la|aetas|aetātem}}, itself derived from {{m|la|aevum||lifetime}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂eyu-||vital force}}. Compare {{cog|fr|âge}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|ieldu}}.

sit.raw: {{etymon|en|id=to sit|:inh|enm:sitten<id:to sit>|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*sed-}} From {{inh|en|enm|sitten}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sittan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sittjan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*sitjaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sed-||sit}}.

stand.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*steh₂-}} {{etymon|en|id=to position|:inh|enm:stonden|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|stonden}}, {{m|enm|standen|pos=verb}} and {{m|enm|stand}}, {{m|enm|stond|pos=noun, from the verb}}, from {{inh|en|ang|standan||to stand, occupy a place}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*standan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*standaną||to stand}}, from Pre-Germanic {{m|ine-pro|*sth₂-n-t-´}}, an innovative extended ''n''-infixed form of {{der|en|ine-pro|*steh₂-}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|staund|t=to stand}}, {{cog|yol|sthoan}}, {{m|yol|sthoane}}, {{m|yol|sthone}}, {{m|yol|stoane|t=to stand}}, {

let.raw: {{der+|en|enm|leten}}, {{m|enm|læten}}, from {{der|en|ang|lǣtan||to allow, let go, bequeath, leave, rent}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*lātan}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*lētaną||to leave behind, allow}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*leh₁d-||to be tired, leave}}.

hurry.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|horien||to rush, impel}}, probably a variation of {{m|enm|hurren||to vibrate rapidly, buzz}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hurzaną||to rush}} (compare {{cog|gmh|hurren||to hasten}}, {{cog|no|hurre||to whirl around}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱers-||to run}} (compare {{cog|la|currō||to run}}, {{cog|xto|kursär}}/{{cog|txb|kwarsär||league; course}}). Related to {{m|en|hurr}}, {{m|en|horse}}, {{m|en|rush}}.

wrong.raw: {{ety|en|tree=1|:inh|enm:wrong}} From {{inh|en|enm|wrong}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wrang|id=wrong|t=wrong, twisted, uneven}}, from {{der|en|non|rangr}}, {{m|non|vrangr|t=crooked, wrong}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*wrangaz|t=crooked, twisted, turned awry}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*werḱ-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*wrengʰ-|t=to twist, weave, tie together}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*wer-|t=to turn, bend}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|wrang|t=wrong}}, {{cog|da|vrang|t=wrong, crooked}}, {{cog|sv|vrång|t=perverse, distorted}}, {{cog|is|rangur|t=wrong}}, {{cog|nn|rang|t=wrong}}, {{cog|nl|wrang|t=bitter, sour}} and the first element

welcome.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:welcome|tree=+}} From {{inh|en|enm|welcome}}, {{m|enm|wolcume}}, {{m|enm|wulcume}}, {{m|enm|wilcume}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wilcuma}} {{gloss|“a wished-for guest”; compare also {{m|ang|wilcume||welcome!|pos=interjection}}}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*willjakwemō}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wiljakwemô|t=a wished-for arrival or guest}}, possibly from {{m|gem-pro|*wiljakwemaną|t=to be welcome}}, equivalent to {{com|en|will|t1=desire|come|t2=comer, arrival}}. The component ''wil-'' was replaced by ''wel-'' when the sense “guest” of the second component was no longer understood, likely un

next.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|nexte}}, {{m|enm|nexste}}, {{m|enm|nixte}}, from {{inh|en|ang|nīehsta}}, {{m|ang|nīehste}}, etc., inflected forms of {{m|ang|nīehst|t=nearest, next}}, superlative form of {{m|ang|nēah||nigh}} (the comparative would become {{m|en|near}}), corresponding to {{inh|en|gem-pro|*nēhwist|t=nearest, closest}}; equivalent to {{suffix|en|nigh|est|nocat=1}}.

middle.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:myddel|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|myddel}}, {{m|enm|middel}}, from {{inh|en|ang|middel||middle, centre, waist}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*midlą}}, {{m|gem-pro|*midilą}}, {{m|gem-pro|*medalą||middle}}, a diminutive of {{der|en|gem-pro|*midjō||middle, midst}} (compare {{m|gem-pro|*midjaz||mid, middle|pos=adjective}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*médʰyos||between, in the middle, middle}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|stq|Middel||middle}}, {{cog|fy|mul||middle}}, {{cog|nl|middel||means; medicine, cure}}, {{cog|de|mittel||middle|pos=adjective}}, {{m|de|Mittel||means; medicamen

down.raw: {{etymon|en|id=direction|:inh|enm:doun<id:direction>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|doun}}, {{m|enm|doune||down}}, from {{inh|en|ang|dūne||down}}, [[w:Apheresis (linguistics)|aphetic]] form of {{m|ang|adūne||down, downward}}, from earlier {{m|ang|ofdūne|t=down|lit=off the hill}}, from {{m|ang|of||of, off of}} + {{m|ang|dūn||hill, mount, dune, down}}. More at Etymology 2 below. For the development from directional phrases to prepositions, compare {{ncog|ofs|dene|t=down|pos=adverb|lit=(to the) floor}}, {{ncog|gml|dāle|t=down, downwards|lit=(in/to the) dale/valley}}, whence {{ncog|nds-de|dal||down}}.

out.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:oute|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|out}}, {{m|enm|oute}}, from a combination of {{inh|en|ang|ūt||out|pos=preposition & adverb}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*ūt}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*ūt||out}}; and {{inh|en|ang|ūte||outside; without|pos=adverb}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*ūtai||out; outside}}; both from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*úd||upwards, away}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|oot|t=out}}, {{cog|yol|out}}, {{m|yol|outh}}, {{m|yol|udh}}, {{m|yol|ut}}, {{m|yol|uth|t=out}}, {{cog|frr|üt}}, {{m|frr|ütj|t=out}}, {{cog|stq|uut|t=out of}}, {{cog|fy|út|t=out}}, {{cog|cim|aus}}, {{m|c

Cognate with {{cog|de|entgegen|t=contrary to}}, {{cog|frr|ijen|t=against}}, {{cog|da|igen||again}}, {{cog|sv|igen||again}}, and {{cog|nb|igjen||again}}{{,}} and {{cog|is|í gegnum|t=through}}. {{surf|en|on-|gain|t2=against}}.

cogs: to come to pass, fare, go forth
ago.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:agon|tree=1}} From {{der|en|enm|ago}}, {{m|enm|agon|t=passed}}, [[Appendix:Glossary#past participle|past participle]] of {{m|enm|agon|t=to depart, escape, pass}}, from {{der|en|ang|āgān|t=to go away, pass away, go forth, come to pass}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*uz-|t=out}}, {{m|gem-pro|*gāną|t=to go}}, equivalent to {{pre|en|a|gone}}, and {{surf|en|a-|go|nocap=1}}. Cognate with {{cog|de|ergehen|t=to come to pass, fare, go forth}}. Compare also {{cog|osx|āgangan|t=to go or pass by}}, {{cog|got|𐌿𐍃𐌲𐌰𐌲𐌲𐌰𐌽|t=to go forth}}.

dear.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|dere}}, from {{inh|en|ang|dēore}}, {{m|ang|dīere}}, {{m|ang|dīore}}, {{m|ang|dȳre|t=of great value or excellence, expensive, beloved}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*diurī}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*diurijaz|t=dear, precious; expensive}}, probably from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*dʰegʷʰ-|t=to burn; hot, warm}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|yol|dear|t=dear}}, {{cog|stq|djuur|t=precious, dear, costly, expensive}}, {{cog|gsw|tüür|t=expensive}}, {{cog|nl|dier}}, {{m|nl|duur|t=expensive}}, {{cog|de|teuer|t=expensive}}, {{cog|wym|taojer}}, {{m|wym|tojer|t=dear}}, {{cog|vls|diere|t=expensive}

candle.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:candle|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|candle}}, from {{inh|en|ang|candel|t=candle}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|candēla|t=candle}}, from {{der|en|la|candeō|t=be white, bright, shining|pos=verb}}; see {{m|en|candid}}. {{doublet|en|candela|chandelle}}.

cream.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:creme}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰrey-}} From {{inh|en|enm|[[creime]], [[creme]]}}, from {{der|en|fro|[[creme]], [[cresme]]}}, blend of {{der|en|la-lat|chrisma||ointment}} (from {{der|en|grc|χρῖσμα||unguent}}), and {{der|en|la-lat|crāmum||cream}}, from {{der|en|cel-gau|*crama}} (compare {{cog|cy|cramen||scab, skin}}, {{cog|br|crammen}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)krama-}} (compare {{cog|mga|screm||surface, skin}}, {{cog|nl|schram||abrasion}}, {{cog|lt|kramas||scurf}}). {{doublet|en|crema|crème}}.

into.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|in-to}}, from {{inh|en|ang|intō}}, equivalent to {{compound|en|in|to}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|intae}}.

soon.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|sone}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sōna|t=immediately, at once}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sān(ō)}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*sēna}}, {{m|gem-pro|*sēnô|t=immediately, soon, then}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*sa|pos=demonstrative pronoun}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*só|pos=demonstrative pronoun}}.

as.raw: {{etymon|en|id=also|:inh|enm:as<id:also>|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂el-|id=all}}{{word|en|ine|swé}} From {{inh|en|enm|as|as, als(a), alswa}}, from {{inh|en|ang|eallswā||just so; as}}, thus representing a reduced form of {{dbt|en|also|notext=1}}. Compare {{cog|nds-de|a(l)s}}, {{cog|de|als}}, {{cog|nl|als}}.

around.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|arounde|around, arounde}}, from {{m|enm|a-}} (from {{inh|en|ang|a-||on, at}}) + {{inh|en|enm|round||circle, round}} borrowed from French, equivalent to {{prefix|en|a|round|id1=on}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|aroond}}, {{m|sco|aroon||around}}. Displaced earlier {{cog|enm|umbe}}, {{m|enm|embe||around}} (from {{cog|ang|ymbe||around}}).

off.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:of|tree=+}} From {{inh|en|enm|of}}, from {{inh|en|ang|of}}, {{m|ang|af}}, {{m|ang|æf|t=from, off, away}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*ab}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*ab|t=from}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*h₂epo|t=from, off, back}}. {{doublet|en|of}}.

Cognate with {{cog|osx|uppan|t=upon}}, {{cog|goh|ūfan}}, {{m|goh|ūffan|t=upon}}, {{cog|is|upp}} {{m|is|á}}, {{m|is|upp á||up on, upon}}, {{cog|sv|uppå||up on, upon}} (thence {{cog|sv|på}}), {{cog|da|på||up on, upon}}, {{cog|no|på||up on, upon}}.

shall.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|schal}} (infinitive {{m|enm|schulen}}), from {{inh|en|ang|sċeal}} (infinitive {{m|ang|sċulan||should, must}}), from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*skulan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*skal}} (infinitive {{m|gem-pro|*skulaną}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*skel-||to owe, be under obligation}}.

said.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|seide|pos=preterite}} and {{m|enm|seid}}, {{m|enm|iseid|pos=past participle}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sǣde}}, {{m|ang|sæġde|pos=preterite}} and {{m|ang|ġesæġd|pos=past participle}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|say|ed}}.

going.raw: Verb form from {{inh|en|enm|goinge}}, {{m|enm|goynge}}, {{m|enm|gayng}}, variants of {{m|enm|gonde}}, {{m|enm|goonde}}, {{m|enm|gaand}}, from {{inh|en|ang|gānde}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*gēndz}}, present participle of {{der|en|gem-pro|*gēną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*gāną|t=to go}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|go|ing}}. does.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|dos}}, variant of {{m|enm|doth}}, {{m|enm|doþ}}, equivalent to {{af|en|do|-s}}. For the shortened vowel compare {{m|en|says}}.

done.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:don|tree=+}} From {{inh|en|enm|don}}, {{m|enm|idon}}, {{m|enm|ydon}}, {{m|enm|ȝedon}}, {{m|enm|gedon}}, from {{inh|en|ang|dōn}}, {{m|ang|ġedōn}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*dān}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*dēnaz}} (past participle of {{m|gem-pro|*dōną|t=to do}}). Equivalent to {{suffix|en|do|en<id:past participle><pos:past participle ending>}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|dune}}, {{m|sco|deen}}, {{m|sco|dene}}, {{m|sco|dane|t=done}}, {{cog|stq|däin|t=done}}, {{cog|fy|dien|t=done}}, {{cog|nl|gedaan|t=done}}, {{cog|nds-de|daan|t=done}}, {{cog|de|getan|t=done}}. More at {{m|en|do}}.

could.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵneh₃-}} From {{inh|en|enm|coude}}, {{m|enm|couthe}}, {{m|enm|cuthe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cūþe}}, past indicative and past subjunctive form of {{m|ang|cunnan||to be able}} (compare related {{m|ang|cūþ}}, whence English {{m|en|couth}}). Cognate with {{cog|de|konnte}}, {{cog|sv|kunde}}.

would.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|ang:wolde|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|ang|wolde}}, past tense of {{m|ang|willan}}, predecessor of {{m|en|will}}.

what.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:what|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*kʷ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|what}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hwæt||what}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hwat}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hwat||what}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*kʷód||what}}, neuter form of {{m|ine-pro|*kʷós||who}}.

where.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:wher|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*kʷ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|wher}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hwǣr|t=where|lit=at what place}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hwār}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hwar||where}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kʷ-|pos=interrogative pronoun}}.

act.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:acte|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eǵ-|id=drive}} From {{inh|en|enm|acte}}, from {{der|en|fro|acte}}, from {{der|en|la|ācta||register of events}}, plural of {{m|la|āctum||decree, law}}, from {{m|la|ago|agere|to do, to act}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂éǵeti}}. Compare {{cog|de|Akte||file}}. Partially displaced {{m|en|deed}}, from {{noncog|ang|dǣd||act, deed}}.

video.raw: {{etymon|en|id=motion picture|:bor|la:videō<id:see>|:influence|audio|tree=1}} From the root ''vide'' of {{bor|en|la|videō||to see}} + ''-o'', formed in analogy to {{m|en|audio}}.

chain: personal, official, or moral duty; official position; function; ceremony, ''esp.'' last rites
office.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃ep-}} From {{inh|en|enm|office}}, from {{der|en|fro|office}}, from {{der|en|la|officium||[[personal]], [[official]], or [[moral]] [[duty]]; [[official]] [[position]]; [[function]]; [[ceremony]], ''[[especially|esp.]]'' [[last rites]]}}, contracted from {{m|la|opificium||[[construction]]: the [[act]] of [[building]] or the [[thing]] [[built]]}},<ref>''Oxford English Dictionary''. "office, ''n.''" Oxford University Press (Oxford), 2004.</ref> from {{m|la|opifex||[[doer]] of [[work]], [[craftsman]]}} + {{m|la|-ium||[[-y]]|pos=forming actions}},<ref>''Oxford English Dictionary

safe.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*solh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|sauf}}, {{m|enm|safe}}, {{m|enm|saf}}, {{m|enm|saaf}}, from {{der|en|fro|sauf}}, {{m|fro|saulf}}, {{m|fro|salf||safe}}, from {{der|en|la|salvus||whole, safe}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*salawos}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*solh₂-|gloss=whole, every}}. Displaced {{cog|ang|sicor||secure, sure}}.

part.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*perh₃-}} {{ety|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:part|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|part}}, from {{inh|en|ang|part||part}} and {{der|en|fro|part||part}}; both from {{der|en|la|partem}}, accusative of {{m|la|pars||piece, portion, share, side, party, faction, role, character, lot, fate, task, lesson, part, member}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*par-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*per-||to sell, exchange}}. Akin to {{cog|la|portiō||a portion, part}}, {{m|la|parō|parāre|to make ready, prepare}}. {{displaced|enm|del}}, {{m|enm|dele||part}} (from {{noncog|ang|dǣl||part, distribution}} > Modern English {{m|en|deal||por

movie.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*m(y)ewh₁-}} From {{m|en|moving picture|moving (picture)}} {{suffix|en||ie}}. Attested since at least 1912 (if not 1908),<ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary}}</ref> originally in American English.

science.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:science<id:knowledge>|id=collective discipline}} From {{inh|en|enm|science}}, {{m|enm|scyence}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|science}}, {{m|fro|escience}}, from {{der|en|la|scientia||[[knowledge]]}}, from {{m|la|sciēns}}, the [[Appendix:Glossary#present participle|present participle]] stem of {{m|la|scire||to [[know]]}}.

circle.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:circle<ety:bor<fro:cercle>>|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)ker- (turn)}} From {{inh|en|enm|circle}}, {{m|enm|cercle}}, from {{der|en|fro|cercle}} and {{der|en|la|circulus}}, diminutive of {{der|en|la|circus|t=circle, circus}}, from {{der|en|grc|κίρκος|t=circle, ring}}, related to {{cog|ang|hring|t=ring}}. Compare also {{cog|ang|ċircul|t=circle, zodiac}}, which came from the same Latin source. {{surf|en|la:circus|alt1=circ(us)|-ule|alt2=-(u)le}}.

cogs: early apparatus converting sound into electrical signals
telephone.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|fr:téléphone<id:telephone>|id=device}} The {{lg|noun}} is derived from {{affix|en|tele-|pos1={{lg|prefix}} meaning ‘from a distance’|-phone|pos2={{lg|suffix}} denoting a device which makes a sound}}, modelled after {{cog|de|Telephon|t=early apparatus converting sound into electrical signals}} {{qualifier|dated}} (now {{cog|de|Telefon}}).<ref name="OED">{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=2015603579|date=September 2025|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=n}}</ref> The word was first used to refer to the modern device in 1876 by the Scottish-born Canadian-American engineer {{w|Alexander Graham Bell}}

minute.raw: {{etymon|en|id=time|:inh|enm:mynute}} From {{inh|en|enm|mynute}}, {{m|enm|minute}}, {{m|enm|mynet}}, from {{der|en|fro|minute}}, from {{der|en|la-med|minūta|t=60th of an hour; note}}. {{doublet|en|menu|menudo}}.

handbag.raw: From {{af|en|hand|bag}}. The music genre is named from women dancing around a pile of their handbags in nightclubs. The verb is a reference to {{w|Margaret Thatcher}}'s handbag.<ref>{{cite-book|editor=David Levi-Faur|title=The Oxford Handbook of Governance|year=2012|publisher=OUP Oxford|page=316|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=11qVVxK2y24C&lpg=PA316&dq=%22handbagging%20thatcher&hl=es&pg=PA316#v=onepage&q&f=false|isbn=978-0-19-162842-9|passage=Governance appeared to give way to hierarchical and even impositional Government, hence the invention of the new verb “to handbag” (coined beca

snowball.raw: From {{der|en|enm|snoweball}}, {{m|enm|snoweballe}}, {{m|enm|snaweballe}}, {{m|enm|snayballe}}, equivalent to {{compound|en|snow|ball}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|snawbaw}}, {{cog|de|Schneeball}}, {{cog|lb|Schnéiball}}, {{cog|nl|sneeuwbal}}, {{cog|af|sneeubal}}, {{cog|li|snieëbal}}, {{cog|fy|sniebal}}, {{cog|stq|Sneebaal}}, {{m|stq|Sneebal}}, {{cog|sv|snöboll}}, {{cog|ovd|sniųoboll}}, {{cog|da|snebold}}, {{cog|nb|snøball}}, {{cog|nn|snøball}} and {{cog|is|snjóbolti}}.

sunshine.raw: In the {{w|Coverdale Bible}} in 1535, in ''Genesis and Exodus'' about 1250 as {{inh|en|enm|sunnesine}};<ref>''Chambers Dictionary of Etymology'', Robert K. Barnhart (ed.), Chambers, 1988</ref> synchronically {{com|en|sun|shine}}. Compare isolated {{cog|ang|sunsċīn|t=mirror}}.

yesterday.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:yesterday}} From {{inh|en|enm|yesterday}}, {{m|enm|yisterday}}, {{m|enm|ȝesterdai}}, {{m|enm|ȝisterdai}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ġiestrandæġ}}, {{m|ang|ġister dæġ}}, {{m|ang|ġestor dæġ}}, {{m|ang|ġeostran dæġ|t=yesterday}}, {{surf|+pre|en|yester|day|nocap=1}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|yisterday}}, {{m|sco|yesterday|t=yesterday}}, {{cog|stq|jässendeeg}}, {{m|stq|järsendeges|t=yesterday|pos=adverb}}, {{cog|fy|justerdei|t=yesterday}}, {{cog|nl|gisterdag|t=yesterday}}, dialectal {{cog|de|gestertag|t=yesterday}}, {{cog|sv|gårdag|t=yesterday}}, {{cog|got|𐌲𐌹𐍃𐍄𐍂𐌰𐌳𐌰𐌲𐌹𐍃|t=tomorrow|pos=adve

holiday.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:halyday|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|halyday}}, {{m|enm|holyday}}, {{m|enm|halidei}}, {{m|enm|haliȝdei}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hāliġdæġ|t=holy day, Sabbath}}, equivalent to {{com|en|holy|day}}. Compare {{cog|fy|hjeldei|t=holiday}}, {{cog|da|helligdag|t=holiday}}, {{cog|no|helligdag|t=holiday}}, {{cog|sv|helgdag|t=holiday, feast}}.

away.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|enm:awey}} From {{inh|en|enm|away}}, {{m|enm|awey}}, {{m|enm|awei}}, {{m|enm|oway}}, {{m|enm|o wey}}, {{m|enm|on way}}, from {{inh|en|ang|āweġ}}, {{m|ang|onweġ||away}}, originally {{m|ang|on weġ||on one's way; onward; on}}, equivalent to {{prefix|en|a|t1=on|way}}.

something.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|somþyng}}, {{m|enm|some-thing}}, {{m|enm|som thing}}, {{m|enm|sum thinge}}, {{m|enm|sum þinge}}, from {{der|en|ang|sum}} {{m|ang|þing|lit=some thing}}, equivalent to {{compound|en|some|thing}}. Compare {{cog|ang|āwiht|t=something|lit=some thing, any thing}}, {{cog|sv|någonting|t=something|lit=some thing, any thing}}.

care.raw: {{etymon|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:care|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|care}}, from {{inh|en|ang|caru}}, {{m|ang|ċearu|t=care, concern, anxiety, sorrow, grief, trouble}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*karu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*karō|t=care, sorrow, cry}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ǵeh₂r-|t=shout, call}}. Cognate with {{cog|osx|cara}}, {{m|osx|kara|t=concern, action}}, {{cog|gmh|kar|t=sorrow, lamentation}}, {{cog|is|kör|t=sickbed}}, {{cog|got|𐌺𐌰𐍂𐌰|t=concern, care}}. Related also to {{cog|nl|karig|t=scanty}}, {{cog|de|karg|t=sparse, meagre, barren}}, {{cog|la|garriō}}, {{cog|grc|γῆρυς}}. See also {{l|en|chary}}

use.raw: {{etymon|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:use<ety:bor<fro:us>>|tree=1}} {{inh+|en|enm|use}}, from {{der|en|fro|us}}, from {{der|en|la|ūsus|t=use, custom, skill, habit}}, from past participle stem of {{m|la|ūtor|t=use}}. Displaced native {{cog|enm|note|t=use}} (see [[note#Etymology_2|note]]) from {{cog|ang|notu}}; {{cog|enm|nutte|t=use}} from {{cog|ang|nytt}}; as well as {{cog|ang|fricu}} and {{cog|ang|sidu}}.

hope.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:hopen|id=verb|tree=0}} From {{inh|en|enm|hopen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hopian||hope}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hopōn}}; further etymology unclear. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|stq|-}}, {{cog|fy|hoopje|t=to hope}}, {{cog|cim|hòffan|t=to hope}}, {{cog|nl|hopen|t=to hope}}, {{cog|de|-}}, {{cog|lb|hoffen|t=to hope}}, {{cog|wym|höfnan|t=hope}}, {{cog|yi|האָפֿן|t=to hope}}, {{cog|da|håbe|t=to hope}}, {{cog|nb|håpe|t=to hope}}, {{cog|nn|håpa}}, {{m|nn|håpe|t=to hope}}, {{cog|sv|hoppas|t=to hope}}. {{col-bottom}}

wonderful.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|wonderful}}, {{m|enm|wondirful}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wundorful|t=wonderful}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wundrafull}}, equivalent to {{af|en|wonder|-ful|pos=adjective}}. Cognate {{cog|nl|wondervol|t=wonderful}}, {{cog|de|wundervoll|t=wonderful}}. Compare {{cog|ang|wuldorful|t=glorious}}.

beautiful.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:bewteful<ety:af<beaute><-ful>>|:afeq|beauty|-ful<id:adjective>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|bewteful}}, {{m|enm|beautefull||attractive to the eye, beautiful}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|beauty|ful|pos=adjective}}. In this sense, largely displaced {{noncog|ang|fæġer}} (whence {{m|en|fair}}).

tidy.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|tidy}}, {{m|enm|tydy}}, {{m|enm|tidi||timely, seasonal, opportune}}, from {{suf|en|tide|t1=time|-y|id2=adjectival}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|tiedig|t=timely, early}}, {{cog|nl|tijdig|t=timely}}, {{cog|nds-de|tiedig|t=timely}}, {{cog|de|zeitig|t=seasonal, timely}}, {{cog|da|tidig|t=timely}}, {{cog|sv|tidig|t=timely}}.

usually.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|usualli}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|usual|ly<id:adverbial>}}. Broadly displaced native {{ncog|ang|ġewunelīċe}} (from which {{ncog|en|wontly}}).

repeat.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*peth₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|repeten}}, from {{der|en|fro|repeter}}, from {{der|en|la|repetō}}, from the prefix {{m|la|re-||again}} + {{m|la|petō|t=to attack, beseech}}.

remember.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)mer-|id=remember}} From {{inh|en|enm|remembren}}, from {{der|en|fro|remembrer||to remember}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|rememorari||to remember again}}, from {{m|la|re-}} + {{m|la|memor||mindful}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)mer-||to think about, be mindful, remember|id=remember}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|mimorian}}, {{m|ang|mymerian||to remember, commemorate}}, {{cog|ang|māmorian||to deliberate, plan out, design}}. More at {{l|en|mimmer}} and {{l|en|mammer}}. Compare also dialectical {{noncog|en|umbethink}}.

worker.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:worchere<alt:werkere, worchere>|tree=+}} {{inh+|en|enm|worchere}}, {{m|enm|werkere}}, equivalent to {{af|en|work|-er|id2=agent noun}}. Displaced the older term {{m|en|wright}}, from {{cog|ang|wyrhta}}.

chain: a steward, bailliff, collector of taxes
a farmer, a lessee, husbandman, bailliff
one to whom land is rented, a collector of taxes, deputy
farmer.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|fermour|t=a steward, bailliff, collector of taxes}}, from {{der|en|fro|fermier|t=a farmer, a lessee, husbandman, bailliff}}, from {{der|en|la-med|firmarius|t=one to whom land is rented, a collector of taxes, deputy}}, from {{m|la|firma}}; equivalent to {{af|en|farm|-er|id2=agent noun}}. Compare {{inh|en|ang|feormere|t=a purveyor of a guild, a supplier of food, a grocer, farmer}}. More at {{l|en|farm}}.

farm.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*perkʷ-}} {{inh+|en|enm|ferme}}, {{m|enm|farme|t=rent, revenue, produce, factor, stewardship, meal, feast}}, influenced by {{der|en|xno|ferme|t=rent, lease, farm}}, from {{der|en|la-med|ferma}}, {{m|la|firma}}.

piano.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*pleh₂-}} {{etymon|en|id=musical instrument|:clipping|pianoforte|tree=1}} {{clipping|en|pianoforte}}, from {{bor|en|it|pianoforte}}, from {{m|it|piano||soft}} + {{m|it|forte||strong}}. So named because it could produce a wide range of varied volumes note-by-note, in contrast to older keyboard instruments, notably the [[harpsichord]]. {{doublet|en|llano|plain|plane|plan}}.

cook.raw: {{etymon|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:cook|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|cook}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cōc|t=a cook}}, from {{der|en|la|cocus}}, ultimately from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*pekʷ-|t=to cook, become ripe}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|cim|khoch|t=cook}}, {{cog|nl|kok|t=cook}}, {{cog|de|Koch|t=cook}}, {{cog|lb|Kach|t=cook}}, {{cog|da|kok|t=cook}}, {{cog|is|kokkur|t=cook}}, {{cog|nb,nn|kokk|t=cook}}, {{cog|sv|kock|t=cook}}. Also compare {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kokōn|t=to cook}} (whence {{cog|frr|kööge}}, {{m|frr|kööki|t=to cook, boil}}, {{cog|fy|koaitsje|t=to cook}}, {{cog|cim|khochan}}, {{m|cim|khòchan|

lucky.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|lukky}}, equivalent to {{af|en|luck|-y|id2=adjectival}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|lucky|t=lucky}}, {{cog|fy|lokkich|t=lucky, fortunate}}, {{cog|nl|gelukkig|t=lucky, fortunate, happy}}. Compare also {{cog|da|lykkelig|t=happy}}, {{cog|sv|lycklig|t=happy, lucky}}, {{cog|de|glücklich|t=happy}}, {{cog|stq|glukkelk|t=happy}}.

dirty.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|dirti}}, alteration of earlier {{m|enm|dritti}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|dirt|y<id:adjectival>}}. Cognate with {{cog|gml|drēterich|t=dirty}}. See also {{m|en|drite}}.

thirsty.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|thirsty}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þurstiġ}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*þurstug}}. Equivalent to {{af|en|thirst|-y|id2=adjectival}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|dorstig}}, {{cog|de|durstig}}.

station.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*steh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|stacioun}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|estation}}, from {{der|en|la|statiōnem}}, accusative of {{m|la|statiō||standing, post, job, position}}, whence also Italian {{m|it|stazione}}. {{doublet|en|stagione}}. Cognate with {{cog|grc|ἵστημι}}, {{m|grc|στάσις}}, {{cog|ang|standan}} (whence {{cog|en|stand}}).

question.raw: {{wikidata lexeme|L784}} From {{inh|en|enm|questioun}}, from {{der|en|xno|questiun}}, from {{der|en|fro|question}}, from {{der|en|la|quaestiōnem}}, accusative of {{m|la|quaestiō||a seeking, investigation, inquiry, question}}, from {{m|la|quaerere||to seek, ask, inquire}},<ref name="Cent1911">{{R:Century}}</ref> of uncertain origin, but possibly from {{der|en|itc-pro|*kʷaizeō}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kʷeh₂-||to acquire}}. {{doublet|en|quest}}.

ill.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|ille||evil; wicked}}, from {{der|en|non|íllr|pos=adj}}, {{m|non|ílla|pos=adv}}, {{m|non|ílt|pos=n}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*ilhilaz}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₁elḱ-}} (whence {{cog|la|ulcus||sore}}, {{cog|grc|ἕλκος||wound, ulcer}}, {{cog|sa|अर्शस्|tr=árśas||hemorrhoids}}).<ref>Michiel de Vaan, ''Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the Other Italic Languages'', s.v. "ulcus" (Leiden: Brill, 2008), 637.</ref> {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|-}} and {{cog|yol|ill}}, {{cog|da|ilde|t=bad}}, {{cog|fo|-}}, {{cog|is|illur|t=bad, ill, wicked}}, {{cog|nb|-}}, {{cog|nn|ille|t=b

quick.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷeyh₃-}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:quyk|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|quik}}, {{m|enm|quic||living, alive, active}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cwic||alive}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kwiku||alive, lively quick}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kwikwaz||alive, lively, quick}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*gʷih₃wós||alive}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*gʷeyh₃-||to live}}, {{m|ine-pro|*gʷeyh₃w-|t=to live}}. For semantic development, compare {{m|en|lively}}.

easy.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(H)yeh₁-}} From {{der|en|enm|esy}}, {{m|enm|eesy}}, partly from {{der|en|enm|ese||ease}} + {{m|enm|-y}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|ease|y}}, and partly from {{der|en|xno|eisé}} from {{der|en|fro|aisié||eased, at ease, at leisure}}, past participle of {{m|fro|aisier||to put at ease}}, from {{m|fro|aise||empty space, elbow room, opportunity}}, of uncertain origin. See {{l|en|ease}}. Merged with {{der|en|enm|ethe}}, {{m|enm|eathe||easy}}, from {{der|en|ang|īeþe}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*auþuz}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂éwtus}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂ew-||to enjoy, consume}}

loud.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱlew-}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:loud|tree=+|id=adjective}} From {{inh|en|enm|loud}}, from {{der|en|ang|hlūd||loud, noisy, sounding, sonorous}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*hlūd}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*hlūdaz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*hlūþaz||heard}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱlewtos||heard, famous}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱlew-||to hear}}. More at [[listen]].

lovely.raw: {{etymid|en|adjective}} From {{inh|en|enm|lovely|id=adjectival}}, {{m|enm|luvelich}}, {{m|enm|lufli}}, from {{inh|en|ang|luflīċ}}, {{m|ang|luflīc|t=amiable, loving, lovable}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|love|ly|id2=adjectival}}.

thirty.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|thirty}}, metathetic alternant of {{m|enm|thritty}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þrītiġ}}, {{m|ang|þrittiġ||thirty}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*þrīz tigiwiz||thirty|lit=three tens}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|three|-ty|id2=multiple}}.<ref name="MW">{{R:Merriam Webster Online}}</ref><ref name="Dictcom">{{R:Dictionary.com}}</ref> Cognate with {{cog|sco|therty}}, {{m|sco|tretty||thirty}}, {{cog|fy|tritich||thirty}}, {{cog|nl|dertig||thirty}}, {{cog|de|dreißig||thirty}}.

fifty.raw: {{PIE word|en|pénkʷe}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:fifty|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|fifty}}, from {{inh|en|ang|fīftiġ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*fimf tigiwiz||five tens}}. {{surf|en|five|-ty<id:multiple>}}.

sixty.raw: {{inh+|en|enm|sixty}}, {{m|enm|sexty}}, {{inh|en|ang|sixtiġ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*sehs tigiwiz|t=sixty}}, equivalent to {{af|en|six|-ty<id:multiple>}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|sexty}}, {{m|sco|saxty|t=sixty}}, {{cog|stq|säkstich|t=sixty}}, {{cog|fy|sechstich|t=sixty}}, {{cog|nl|zestig|t=sixty}}, {{cog|nds-de|sesstig|t=sixty}}, {{cog|de|sechzig|t=sixty}}, {{cog|sv|sextio|t=sixty}}, {{cog|no|seksti|t=sixty}}, {{cog|is|sextíu|t=sixty}}. Compare also {{cog|sa|षष्टि}}.

seventy.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|seventy}}, {{m|enm|sevynty}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hundseofontiġ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*sebuntēhundą|t=seventy}}, equivalent to {{af|en|seven|-ty<id:multiple>}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|seiventy|t=seventy}}, {{cog|stq|soogentich|t=seventy}}, {{cog|fy|santich|t=seventy}}, {{cog|nl|zeventig|t=seventy}}, {{cog|nds-de|söventig|t=seventy}}, {{cog|de|siebzig|t=seventy}}, {{cog|sv|sjuttio|t=seventy}}, {{cog|no|sytti|t=seventy}}, {{cog|is|sjötíu|t=seventy}}.

eighty.raw: {{inh+|en|enm|eightety}}, {{m|enm|eiȝti}}, {{m|enm|eiȝtety}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hundeahtatiġ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*ahtōutēhundą|t=eighty}}, equivalent to {{af|en|eight|-ty<id:multiple>}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|hechty}}, {{m|sco|auchty|t=eighty}}, {{cog|stq|tachentich|t=eighty}}, {{cog|fy|tachtich|t=eighty}}, {{cog|nl|tachtig|t=eighty}}, {{cog|nds|tachentig|t=eighty}}, {{cog|de|achtzig|t=eighty}}, {{cog|sv|åttio|t=eighty}}, {{cog|no|åtti|t=eighty}}, {{cog|is|áttatíu|t=eighty}}.

ninety.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|nynty}}, {{m|enm|nynety}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hundniġontiġ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*newuntēhundą|t=ninety}}, equivalent to {{af|en|nine|-ty<id:multiple>}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|nynty}}, {{m|sco|nynety|t=ninety}}, {{cog|stq|njuugentich|t=ninety}}, {{cog|fy|njoggentich|t=ninety}}, {{cog|nl|negentig|t=ninety}}, {{cog|nds-de|negentig|t=ninety}}, {{cog|de|neunzig|t=ninety}}, {{cog|sv|nittio|t=ninety}}, {{cog|nb|nitti|t=ninety}}, {{cog|nn|nitti|t=ninety}}, {{cog|is|níutíu|t=ninety}}.

cogs: to green; thrive; take hold; flourish
grow.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰreh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|growen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|grōwan|t=to grow, increase, flourish, germinate}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*grōan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*grōaną|t=to grow, grow green}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰreh₁-|t=to grow, become green}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|nl|groeien|t=to grow}}, {{cog|nds-de|grojen|t=to green; thrive; take hold; flourish}}, {{cog|da,nb,nn,sv|gro|t=to grow}}, {{cog|fo|grógva|t=to grow}}, {{cog|is|gróa|t=to grow}}; also {{cog|la|grāmen|t=grass, turf; herb, plant}}, {{m|la|herba|t=grass, herbage; weeds; plant}}, {{cog|uk|гря́ний

between.raw: {{PIE word|en|dwóh₁}} From {{inh|en|enm|betwene}}, from {{inh|en|ang|betwēonum|t=between, among|lit=by the two, near both|pos=dative plural}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*bi-|t=be-}} + {{m|gem-pro|*twīhnaz|t=two each}}, corresponding to {{prefix|en|be|twain}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|between|t=between}}, {{cog|sco|atween|t=between}}, {{cog|got|𐍄𐍅𐌴𐌹𐌷𐌽𐌰𐌹|t=two each}}, {{cog|ang|betweoh|t=between}}, {{cog|ang|twinn|t=double, twofold}}. More at {{l|en|betwixt}}, {{l|en|twin}}.

only.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|oonly}}, {{m|enm|only}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ānlīċ}}, {{m|ang|ǣnlīċ|t=only; singular; solitary}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*ainalīkaz}}. Cognate with obsolete {{cog|nl|eenlijk}}, {{cog|de|ähnlich|t=similar}}, {{cog|non|álíkr}}, {{cog|sv|enlig||unified}}. {{surf|+suf|en|one|ly|alt1=on(e)|id2=adjectival}}. * Regarding the different phonological development of ''only'' and ''one'', see the note in {{m|en|one}}.

road.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:rode<id:ride>}} From {{inh|en|enm|rode|id=ride}}, {{m|enm|rade|id=ride|t=ride, journey}}, from {{inh|en|ang|rād||riding, hostile incursion}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*raidu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*raidō||a ride}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*reydʰ-||to ride}}. {{doublet|en|raid}}, acquired from {{cog|sco|-}}. Cognates include West Frisian {{m|fy|reed}} (paved trail/road, driveway).

true.raw: {{ety|en|id=factual|:inh|enm:trewe|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|trewe}}, {{m|enm|true}}, from {{inh|en|ang|trēowe}}, {{m|ang|trīewe|t=faithful, true}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*triwwiz|t=faithful, true}}, from pre-Germanic *''drewh₂yos'', from {{der|en|ine-pro|*drew-|*drewh₂-|t=firm, hard, true}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|stq|trjou|t=honest}}, {{cog|gsw|trüüw|t=loyal}}, {{cog|nl|trouw|t=loyal, true}}, {{cog|de|treu|t=loyal, true}}, {{cog|lb|trei|t=loyal}}, {{cog|da|tryg|t=safe, secure}}, {{cog|fo,is|tryggur|t=faithful, loyal; safe}}, {{cog|nb,nn,sv|trygg|t=safe, secure}}, {{cog|got|𐍄𐍂𐌹

then.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|[[then]]([[thenne|ne]])}}, {{m|enm|[[than]]([[thanne|ne]])}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þonne}}, {{m|ang|þanne}}, {{m|ang|þænne||then, at that time}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*þan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*þan||at that (time), then}}, from earlier {{m|gem-pro||*þam}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*tóm}}, accusative masculine of {{m|ine-pro|*só||demonstrative pronoun, that}}.

bright.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:bright|tree=1|id=luminous}} The {{glossary|adjective}} is from {{inh|en|enm|bright}}, from {{inh|en|ang|berht}}, {{m|ang|beorht}}, {{m|ang|bryht}}, {{m|ang|byrht}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*berht}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*berhtaz|t=bright}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰerHǵ-|t=to gleam, shine, whiten}}.

chain: high, tall, lofty, high-class, exalted, sublime, illustrious, important, proud, haughty, deep, right
cogs: stick with thick end, pounder, pestle
high.raw: {{etymon|en|id=tall|:inh|enm:heigh|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*kewk-}} From {{inh|en|enm|high}}, {{m|enm|heigh}}, {{m|enm|heih}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hēah|t=high, tall, lofty, high-class, exalted, sublime, illustrious, important, proud, haughty, deep, right}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hauh|t=high}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hauhaz|t=high}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kewk-|t=to bend; crooked}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|heich|t=high}}, {{cog|yol|heegh}}, {{m|yol|heigh}}, {{m|yol|heighe}}, {{m|yol|hia}}, {{m|yol|hie|t=high}}, {{cog|frr|hoog}}, {{m|frr|huuch|t=high}}, {{cog|stq|hooch}}, {{m

chain: to make a laborious journey, travel
to trouble, suffer, be worn out
cogs: to go [a long distance], to travel
travel.raw: {{PIE word|en|tréyes}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*peh₂ǵ-}} {{rfc|en|Middle Scots comes after Middle English.}} From {{inh|en|enm|travelen|t=to make a laborious journey, travel}} from {{der|en|gmw-msc|travailen|t=to toil, work, travel}}, alteration of {{cog|enm|travaillen|t=to toil, work}}, from {{der|en|fro|travailler|t=to trouble, suffer, be worn out}}. See the {{glossary|doublet}}s {{doublet|en|travail|travois|notext=1}}.

cross.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:cross|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|cross}}, {{m|enm|cros}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cros|t=rood, cross}}, from {{der|en|non|kross}}, from {{der|en|sga|cros}}, from {{der|en|la|crux}} ({{m|la|crucī}}). In this sense displaced native {{cog|enm|rode}}, from {{cog|ang|rōd|t=cross}}; see {{m+|en|rood}}. {{dbt|en|crouch|t1=cross|crux}}. Compare {{cog|cy|croes}}, {{cog|ga|crois}}.

pass.raw: {{etymon|en|id=verb|:inh|enm:passen|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|passen}}, from {{der|en|fro|passer||to step, walk, pass}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*passo|*passāre|t=step, walk, pass}}, derived from {{der|en|la|passus||a step}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*pattus|*pat-s-tus}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*peth₂-||to spread, stretch out}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|fæþm||armful, fathom}}. More at {{l|en|fathom}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|genġan}}.

chain: sound, safe, whole, uninjured, healthy, prosperous
cogs: strong, mighty, powerful, active, severe, violent
sound.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|sound}}, {{m|enm|sund}}, {{m|enm|isund}}, {{m|enm|ȝesund}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sund|t=sound, safe, whole, uninjured, healthy, prosperous}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sund}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*sundaz|t=healthy}}, merged with synonymous {{inh|en|ang|ġesund}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*gasund}}.

goose.raw: {{PIE word|en|ǵʰh₂éns}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:gos|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|goos}}, {{m|enm|gos}}, from {{inh|en|ang|gōs}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*gans}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*gans}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*ǵʰh₂éns}}.

men.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|men}}, from {{inh|en|ang|menn|t=people}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*manniz}}, nominative plural of {{der|en|gem-pro|*mann-|t=person}}. Cognate with {{cog|de|Männer||men}}, {{cog|da|mænd||men}}, {{cog|sv|män||men}}. More at {{l|en|man}}.

women.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|wimmen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wīfmenn||women}}, from {{m|ang|wīf||female}} + {{m|ang|menn||men, persons, human beings}}, equivalent to {{compound|en|wife|men|nocat=1}}. Spelling (with ''o'') influenced by the singular; see {{m|en|woman}} for more.

chain: anything with an arched cover, a covered carriage or boat, a vaulted chamber, a vault
camera.raw: {{ety|en|:lbor|la:camera}} {{lbor|en|la|camera|t=chamber or bedchamber}}, from {{der|en|grc|καμάρα|t=anything with an arched cover, a covered carriage or boat, a vaulted chamber, a vault}}, of {{der|en|ira-old|-}} origin, from {{der|en|ira-pro|*kamarā-|t=something curved}}, from {{m|ira-pro|*kamárati}}, from {{der|en|iir-pro|*kmárati}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kh₂em-||to bend, curve}}. {{dbt|en|chamber}}.

move.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:moven<ety:bor<fro-nor:movoir<alt:mover>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|moven}}, {{m|enm|moeven}}, {{m|enm|meven}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro-nor|mover}}, {{m|fro|moveir}} and {{der|en|fro|mouver}}, {{m|fro|moveir|t=to move}} (compare modern French {{m|fr|mouvoir}} from Old French {{m|fro|movoir}}), from {{der|en|la|moveō|movēre|t=move; change, exchange, go in or out, quit}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*m(y)ewh₁-|t=to move, drive}}. Cognate with {{cog|lt|mauti|t=to push on, rush}}, {{cog|sa|मीवति|tr=mī́vati|t=pushes, presses, moves}}, {{cog|dum|mouwe|t=sleeve}}. Largely displaced

bookmark.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|*boke-merk}}, {{m|enm|*boke-merke}} (attested only in the bare form {{m|enm|merk|t=bookmark}}), equivalent to {{com|en|book|mark}}. Cognate with {{cog|da|bogmærke|t=bookmark}}, {{cog|sv|bokmärke|t=bookmark}}, {{cog|no|bokmerke|t=bookmark}}, {{cog|is|bókamerki|t=bookmark}}. Eclipsed non-native {{ncog|ang|æstel|t=bookmark}}, from {{ncog|sga|astal}}, from {{ncog|la|hastula|t=little spear, splint}}.

washroom.raw: From {{compound|en|wash|room}} in reference to its [[sink]]s, but generally used euphemistically outside of Canada and the United States.

raindrop.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|rein-drope}}, {{m|enm|reyn-drope}}, {{m|enm|reyn drope}}, from {{inh|en|ang|reġndropa}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*regnadrupô}}. Equivalent to {{compound|en|rain|drop}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Riendruppe}}, {{cog|fy|reindrip}}, {{cog|nl|regendroppel}}, {{m|nl|regendruppel}}, {{cog|nds-de|Regendrüpp}}, {{cog|de|Regentropfen}}, {{cog|sv|regndroppe}}, {{cog|is|regndropi}}.

earth.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:erthe<id:earth>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|erthe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|eorþe}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*erþu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*erþō||dirt, ground, earth}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*h₁er-|*h₁érteh₂|earth|id=earth}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|erd}}, {{m|sco|yerd}}, {{m|sco|yird}}, {{m|sco|yirth|t=earth, loam, mould, soil; ground}}, {{cog|yol|eard}}, {{m|yol|eart}}, {{m|yol|eord}}, {{m|yol|eorth}}, {{m|yol|erth|t=earth}}, {{cog|frr|eerd}}, {{m|frr|eerde}}, {{m|frr|iarde}}, {{m|frr|Iart}}, {{m|frr|iir}}, {{m|frr|jard}}, {{m|frr|örd}}, {{m|frr|Öört|t=earth; w

key.raw: {{etymon|en|id=open|:inh|enm:keye<id:open>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|keye}}, {{m|enm|kaye}}, {{m|enm|keiȝe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cǣġ||key, solution, experiment}} (whence also {{cog|sco|key}} and {{m|sco|kay||key}}), from [[w:Anglo-Frisian languages|Anglo-Frisian]] {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kaiju}}, of uncertain origin.<ref>{{cite-web |titleurl=https://en.oxforddictionaries.com/definition/key |title=Archived copy |accessdate=19 March 2018 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190525150410/https://en.oxforddictionaries.com/definition/key |archivedate=25 May 2019 }}</ref> The only sure cognates are {

blackberry.raw: {{etymon|en|id=black fruit|:inh|enm:blakberie<id:blackberry>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|blakberie}}, {{m|enm|blakeberie|t=[[brambleberry]]}}, from {{inh|en|ang|blacu berġe}}, {{m|ang|blæcberġe}} (attested in plural {{m|ang|blaca berġan}}), equivalent to {{compound|en|black|berry}}.

peanut.raw: From {{compound|en|pea|nut}}, perhaps a [[folk etymology]] of {{m|en|pinda}}, {{m|en|pinder}} ''(still found in Southern US dialects)''.

coconut.raw: From {{com|en|coco|nut}}. In reference to assimilated Hispanic or black people, derived from the fruit's exotic origins. The slur originates from the idea that one is "brown on the outside, white on the inside". In reference to Polynesians, from the ubiquity of coconut palms in the area.

dumpling.raw: A folk word, {{etydate|c|1600s|nocap=1}}, apparently from a [[Norfolk]] ([[w:East Anglian English|East Anglian]]) dialect, of uncertain origin:

dragonfly.raw: {{ety|en|:af|dragon<id:mythical creature>|fly<id:insect>|tree=1}} From {{af|en|dragon|fly}}. Compare the {{glossary|piecewise doublet}} {{piecewise doublet|en|drakefly<t:mayfly>|notext=1}}.

polar bear.raw: Coined by {{w|Thomas Pennant}} in '' A Synopsis of Quadrupeds'' (1771).

paint.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:peynten<ety:der<fro:peintier>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|peynten}}, from {{der|en|fro|peintier}}, {{m|fro|paincter}}, itself from {{m|fro|paint}}, the past participle of {{m|fro|paindre}}, from {{der|en|la|pingō||to paint}} (perfect passive participle {{m|la|pictus}}). Displaced native {{ncog|ang|tēafor|t=paint}}, {{m|ang|*tīefran|t=to paint}}; and {{ncog|ang|mētan|t=to paint}} and {{m|ang|mǣlan|t=to paint, mark with colour}}.

drawing.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|drauinge}}, {{m|enm|drawinge}}, alteration of earlier {{m|enm|drawende}}, {{m|enm|drawand}}, from {{inh|en|ang|dragende}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*dragandz|t=drawing}}, present participle of {{der|en|gem-pro|*draganą|t=to draw; pull}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|draw|ing}}.

chain: to climb, go up by clinging
climb.raw: {{etymon|en|id=slope|:inh|enm:clymben<id:climb>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|climben}}, {{m|enm|clymben}}, from {{inh|en|ang|climban||to climb}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*klimban}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*klimbaną|t=to climb, go up by clinging}}, believed to be a nasalised variant of {{der|en|gem-pro|*klibaną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*klibāną||to stick, cleave}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gley-||to stick}}. Cognate with {{cog|fy|klimme||to climb}}, {{cog|nl|klimmen||to climb}}, {{cog|de|klimmen||to climb}}, {{cog|non|klembra||to squeeze}}, {{cog|is|klifra||to climb}}. Related to {{l|en|clamber}}. See also {{l|

chain: to keep, guard, look after, watch
keep.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|kepen|t=to keep, guard, look after, watch}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cēpan|t=to seize, hold, observe}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kōpijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kōpijaną|t=to look, heed, watch, observe}} (compare {{cog|fy|kypje|t=to look}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ǵab-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*ǵāb-|t=to look after}} (compare {{cog|lt|žẽbti|t=to eat reluctantly}}, {{cog|ru|забо́та|t=care, worry}}).

salt.raw: {{ety|en|id=substance|:inh|enm:salt|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|salt}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sealt}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*salt}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*saltą}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*sḗh₂l|t=salt}}. {{doublet|en|sal|salary|salsa}}, all ultimately from {{cog|la|sāl|t=salt}}, which it superseded as the general term for "salt".

tasty.raw: From {{suffix|en|taste|-y|id2=adjectival}}. The Philippine sense is due to a {{glossary|genericized trademark}} from Taystee Bread Company, a [[defunct]] [[American]] company.

cogs: large, wide, roomy, spacious, capacious, capable, apt
heavy.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id=seize}} From {{inh|en|enm|hevy}}, {{m|enm|heviȝ}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hefiġ}}, {{m|ang|hefeġ}}, {{m|ang|hæfiġ|t=heavy; important, grave, severe, serious; oppressive, grievous; slow, dull}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*habīg|t=heavy, hefty, weighty}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*habīgaz|t=heavy, hefty, weighty}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id=seize|t=to take, grasp, hold}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|heave|-y}}. Related to {{m|en|have}}.

clear.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:cler|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|clere}}, from {{der|en|xno|cler}}, from {{der|en|fro|cler}} (Modern {{cog|fr|clair}}), from {{der|en|la|clarus}}. Displaced native [[Middle English]] {{m|enm|schir||clear, pure}} (from [[Old English]] {{m|ang|scīr||clear, bright}}), [[Middle English]] {{m|enm|skere||clear, sheer}} (from [[Old English]] {{m|ang|scǣre}} and Old Norse {{m|non|skær|skǣr|sheer, clear, pure}}), [[Middle English]] {{m|enm|smolt||clear (of mind), serene}} (from [[Old English]] {{m|ang|smolt||peaceful, serene}}). Cognate with {{cog|da,de,nb,nn,sv|klar}}, {{cog|nl|klaar}

forget.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰed-}} From {{inh|en|enm|forgeten}}, {{m|enm|forgiten}}, {{m|enm|foryeten}}, {{m|enm|forȝiten}}, from {{inh|en|ang|forġietan||to forget}} [influenced by Old Norse {{m|non|geta}} ("to get, to guess")], from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*fragetan||to give up, forget}}. Equivalent to {{af|en|for-|get}}.

dark.raw: {{ety|en|id=adjective|:inh|enm:derk}} From {{inh|en|enm|derk}}, from {{inh|en|ang|deorc}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*derk|t=dark}}, of uncertain origin, but possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰerg-|t=dim, dull}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰer-|t=dull, dirty}}.

enjoy.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|enjoyen}}, from {{der|en|fro|enjoier}}, {{m|fro|anjoier}}, {{m|fro|enjoer||to give joy, receive with joy, rejoice}}, equivalent to {{prefix|en|en|joy}}.

chopstick.raw: Apparently a compound of {{m|en|chop}} + {{m|en|stick}}, but the sense of the first element is not clear. The term was earliest applied to fishing tackle (from 1615), later being transferred to the dining utensil (attested since 1637) driven by their visual resemblance.

lamp.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:laumpe|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|laumpe}}, {{m|enm|lampe}}, from {{der|en|fro|lampe||lamp, light}}, from {{der|en|la|lampas||torch, lamp, light}}, from {{der|en|grc|λαμπάς||torch, lamp, beacon, light, meteor}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*leh₂p-||to shine}}. Cognate with {{cog|lt|lópė||light}}, {{cog|cy|llachar||bright}}. Displaced native {{cog|ang|lēohtfæt|lit=light-vat}}.

knife.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|knyf}}, {{m|enm|knif}}, from late {{inh|en|ang|cnīf}}, from {{der|en|non|knífr}} or {{der|en|gmw-pro|*knīb}},<ref>{{R:enm:Gersum|knyf|n.|10182|cat=BB2a}}</ref> from {{der|en|gem-pro|*knībaz}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*knīpaną|t=to pinch}}, {{der|en|ine-pro|*gneybʰ-}} (compare {{cog|lt|gnýbti}}, {{m|lt|žnýbti|t=to pinch}}, {{m|lt|gnaibis||pinching}}). Displaced native {{ncog|enm|sax|t=knife}}, from {{ncog|ang|seax}}; and {{ncog|enm|coutel}}, {{m|enm|qwetyll|t=knife}} from {{ncog|fro|coutel}}.

beef.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:bef}} From {{inh|en|enm|bef|beef, bef, beof}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|beof}}, {{der|en|fro|buef}}, {{m|fro|boef||ox}} (modern {{m+|fr|bœuf}}); from {{der|en|la|bōs|bovem|ox}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*gʷōs}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʷṓws}}. {{doublet|en|cow}}.

pork.raw: {{etymon|en|id=pig|:inh|enm:pork|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|pork}}, {{m|enm|porc}}, via {{der|en|xno|-}}, from {{der|en|fro|porc||swine, hog, pig; pork}}, from {{der|en|la|porcus||domestic hog, pig}}.

mango.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|id=Mangifera|pt:manga<id:mango>|tree=+}} {{bor+|en|pt|manga}}, from {{der|en|ml|മാങ്ങ}} / {{der|en|ta|மாங்காய்}}, possibly via {{der|en|ms|mangga}}, ultimately from {{der|en|dra-sou-pro|*mām|*mām-kāy|t=unripe mango}}, a compound of {{m|dra-sou-pro|*mām|t=mango tree}} + {{m|dra-pro|*kāy|t=unripe fruit}}.<ref>{{R:dra:DL|pages=526, 530}}</ref> First used for the fruit as early as the 1580s and the tree by the 1670s.<ref name="OnlineED">{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary|entry=mango}}</ref><ref name="OxfordED">{{R:OED Online|entry=mango|pos=''n.''{{sup|1}}|noformat=1|id=113430|date=J

kangaroo.raw: {{ety|en|:bor|kky:gangurru}} {{bor+|en|kky|gangurru||eastern grey kangaroo}}. Despite a popular misconception, the Guugu Yimidhirr term does not mean "I don't know".

deer.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|der}}, {{m|enm|deer|t=animal, deer}}, from {{inh|en|ang|dēor||animal}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*deuʀ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*deuzą}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*dʰewsóm|t=living thing}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*dʰéws|t=breath}}<!--please verify-->, full-grade derivative of {{m|ine-pro|*dʰwes-}}.

goat.raw: [[File:Goat 01.jpg|thumb|Domestic goat ({{taxfmt|Capra hircus|species}})]] [[File:PikiWiki Israel 38769 Male Ibex.jpg|thumb|[[Nubian ibex]] ({{taxlink|Capra nubiana|species}})]]

The verb is from the noun.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=v|id=4578744069}}</ref>

wood.raw: {{etymid|en|substance}} {{ety|en|id=material|:inh|enm:wode|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|wode}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wudu}}, {{m|ang|widu||wood, forest, grove; tree; timber}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*widu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*widuz||wood}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₁weydʰh₁-||to separate}}. The spelling developed as it did in {{m|en|wool}}.

city.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:cite|tree=1}} {{inh+|en|enm|cite}}, {{der+|en|fro|citet|cite|nocap=1}}, {{der+|en|la-lat|civitas|cīvitātem|city|nocap=1}}, in {{der|en|la-cla|-}} "citizenry", derived from {{m|la|cīvis|t=fellow-citizen}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱey-|t=lie down; settle}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|hīwan|g=p|t=members of one's household, servants}}. See {{m|en|hewe}}. {{doublet|en|civitas}}. Mostly displaced native {{ncog|ang|burg}}, whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|borough}}.

present.raw: {{wp}} {{ety|en|id=now|:inh|enm:present<ety:bor<fro:present>>}} From {{inh|en|enm|present}}, from {{der|en|fro|present}}, from {{der|en|la|praesens|praesent-, praesens}}, present participle of {{m|la|praesum|praeesse|to be present}}, from {{der|en|la|prae-||pre-}} + {{m|la|sum|esse|to be}}. {{displaced|ang|andweard||present, current}}.

cogs: to move quickly to and fro
flag.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|flag}}, {{m|enm|flagge||flag}}, further etymology {{unc|en|nocap=1}}. Perhaps from or related to early {{der|en|enm|flage}} {{gloss|name for a baby's garment}} and {{der|en|ang|flagg}}, {{m|ang|flacg||[[cataplasm]], [[poultice]], [[plaster]]}}. Or, perhaps ultimately {{onomatopoeic|en|title=imitative}}, or otherwise drawn from {{der|en|gem-pro|*flaką|t=something flat}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*pleh₂-||flat, broad, plain}}, referring to the shape.<ref name = harper>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary|flag}}</ref>

blackboard.raw: From {{compound|en|black|board}}, because such surfaces were once typically made of black [[slate]].

computer.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*pewH-}} {{etymon|en|id=device|:af|compute<id:calculate>|-er<id:agent noun>|text=+}} {{doublet|en|cantore|counter|kontor}}. The sense referring to people first appears c. 1613 in the works of the poet {{w|Richard Brathwait}}. The sense referring to a machine first appears c. 1897 in the magazine ''{{w|Engineering (magazine)|Engineering}}''.

Largely displaced native {{noncog|en|still}} in the sense of "with little or no sound".

cogs: tight, strict, powerful, intense, mighty, strong
strong.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:strong}} From {{inh|en|enm|strong,strang}}, from {{inh|en|ang|strang||strong}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*strang|t=severe, strict, rigorous, strong}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*strangaz||tight, strict, straight, strong}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*strengʰ-||taut, stiff, tight}}.

fridge.raw: The {{glossary|noun}} is a {{clipping|en|refrigerator|nocap=1}}, perhaps influenced by the {{w|Frigidaire}} brand of refrigerators, or {{m|en|frigerator|t=(''dated'') refrigerator}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=74639|date=March 2019|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=n}}</ref> The spelling is likely influenced by analogy with ''[[bridge]]'', ''[[ridge]]'', etc.<ref>https://www.merriam-webster.com/video/why-is-d-in-fridge-but-not-refrigerator</ref> The {{glossary|verb}} is derived from the noun.

kitchen.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*pekʷ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|kichene}}, {{m|enm|kichen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cyċen}}, {{m|ang|cyċene}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kukinā}}, a borrowing from {{der|en|la-lat|cocīna}}, from earlier {{m|la|coquīna|t=kitchen; cuisine}}, from {{m|la|coquō||to cook}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*pekʷ-||to cook, become ripe}}.

Cognate also with {{cog|frr|forck|t=fork}}, {{cog|nl|vork|t=fork}}, {{cog|da|fork|t=fork}}, {{cog|de|
