spoon.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|spoon}}, {{m|enm|spoune}}, {{m|enm|spone}}, {{m|enm|spon|t=spoon, chip of wood}}, from {{inh|en|ang|spōn|t=sliver, chip of wood, shaving}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*spānu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*spēnuz|t=chip, flake, shaving}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)peH-|t=chip, shaving, log, length of wood}}.

doctor.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:doctour|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*deḱ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|doctor}}, {{m|enm|doctour||an expert, authority on a subject}}, from {{der|en|xno|doctour}}, from {{der|en|la|doctor||teacher}}, from {{m|la|doceō||to teach}}. Displaced native {{cog|enm|lerare||doctor, teacher}} (from {{cog|enm|leren||to teach, instruct}} from {{cog|ang|læran|lǣran, lēran|to teach, instruct, guide}}, compare {{cog|ang|lārēow||teacher, master}}). Displaced {{cog|ang|lǣċe||doctor, physician}}.

driver.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:drivere<ety:af<driven><-ere<id:agent suffix>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|drivere}}, {{m|enm|dryvere}}, {{m|enm|dryvare}}, equivalent to {{af|en|drive|-er|id2=agent noun}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Drieuwer|t=driver}}, {{cog|nl|drijver|t=driver}}, {{cog|nds-de|Driever|t=driver}}, {{cog|de|Treiber|t=driver}}, {{cog|sv|drivare|t=driver}}.

nurse.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)neh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|norice}}, from {{der|en|fro|norrice}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|nūtrīcia}}, noun based on {{der|en|la|nūtrīcius||that which nourishes}}, from {{m|la|nūtrīx||wet nurse}}, from {{m|la|nūtriō||to suckle}}.

chain: fence, hedge; enclosure, pen; court, yard; garden; house
cogs: enclosed uncultivated patch of land; farm
line of traps with small trees between them felled as a fence
garden.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰerdʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|garden}}, {{m|enm|gardeyn}}, {{m|enm|gardin}}, {{m|enm|gardyn}}, {{m|enm|gardyne}}, {{m|enm|gardyng}}, {{m|enm|garthen}}, {{m|enm|garthyn}}, from {{der|en|xno|gardin}}, from {{der|en|frk|*gardō|*gardin-}}, oblique stem of {{m|frk|*gardō|t=enclosure, yard}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*gardô|t=fence, hedge; enclosure, pen; court, yard; garden; house}} (whence also inherited {{cog|en|yard}}), from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*gʰórdʰos|t=fence, hedge}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*gʰerdʰ-|t=to enclose; belt, fence}}. {{doublet|en|jardin}} and of {{doublet|en|garth|notext=1}}.

library.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*lewbʰ- (cut off)}} From {{inh|en|enm|librarie}}, from {{der|en|xno|librarie}}, from {{der|en|fro|librairie}}, from {{der|en|la|librarium||bookcase, chest for books}}, from {{m|la|librarius||concerning books}}, from {{m|la|liber||the inner bark of trees; paper, parchment, book}}, probably derived from a {{der|en|ine-pro|-}} base {{m|ine-pro|*lewbʰ-|*leub(ʰ)-|to strip, to peel}}. Displaced native {{ncog|enm|bochous|bochous, bokhus|lit=book house}}, from {{ncog|ang|bōchūs}} (compare {{m|en|bookhouse}}).

breakfast.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|brekefast}}, {{m|enm|brekefaste}}, equivalent to {{compound|en|break|fast}} {{gloss|''literally'', "to end the nightly fast"}}, likely a variant of {{inh|en|ang|fæstenbryċe}}, {{gloss|''literally'', "fast-breach"}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|breekvasten|t=breakfast}}.

dinner.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁yaǵ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|dyner}}, from {{der|en|fro|disner||lunch”, but originally “breakfast}}, (modern {{cog|fr|dîner}}), from {{der|en|la-vul|*disiūnō|*disiūnō, *disiūnāre}} from {{der|en|la|dis-}} + {{m|la|iēiūnō||to break the fast}}.

lunch.raw: Recorded since 1580 in the sense “piece, hunk”. The word {{m|en|luncheon}} with the same meaning is presumably an extension on the pattern of {{m|en|puncheon|t=cask}} and {{m|en|truncheon|t=cudgel}}. But earliest found forms of {{m|en||luncheon}} include {{m|en|lunshin}} and {{m|en|lunching}}, which are equivalent to {{af|en||alt1=lunch|-ing}}, with the suffix {{m|en|-ing}} possibly later modified to imitate a French origin.

weather.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂weh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|weder}}, {{m|enm|wedir}}, from {{inh|en|ang|weder}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wedr}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wedrą}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*wedʰrom}} (={{m|ine-pro|*we-dʰrom}}), from {{m|ine-pro|*h₂weh₁-||to blow}}.

carrot.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:karette|tree=1}} {{inh+|en|enm|karette}} and {{bor|en|frm|carotte}}, both from {{der|en|la|carōta}}, from {{der|en|grc|καρωτόν}}. {{doublet|en|carotte}} and related to {{m|en|caraway}}. Displaced native {{ncog|enm|more}}, from {{ncog|ang|more}}, {{m|ang|moru|t=edible root, parsnip, carrot}}, related to {{ncog|de|Möhre|t=carrot}}. * Noun sense of "motivational tool" refers to {{m|en|carrot and stick}}. * Verb sense in felt manufacture refers to the orange colour of drying furs.

cow.raw: {{PIE word|en|gʷṓws|nobox=1}} [[Image:Koe in weiland bij Gorssel.JPG|thumb|{{lang|en|A '''cow''' eats [[grass]].}}]]

cogs: aiding, assisting; defending; ally, helper; hireling
horse.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:hors<id:horse>|id=Equus ferus|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|hors}}, {{m|enm|horse}}, {{m|enm|ors}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hors|t=horse}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hross|*hors, *hross}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hrussą|t=horse}}, most likely from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*ḱr̥sós|t=vehicle}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱers-|t=to run}}. {{doublet|en|car|carrus}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|horse|t=horse}}, {{cog|fy|hoars|t=horse}}, {{cog|cim|ross|t=horse}}, {{cog|nl|hors}}, {{m|nl|ros|t=horse}}, {{cog|de|Ross}}, {{m|de|Roß|t=horse}}, {{cog|da,nn|hors|t=horse, mare}}, {{cog|fo|hors}},

sheep.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:schep|tree=1}} {{inh+|en|enm|schep}}, {{m|enm|schepe}}, from {{inh|en|ang-ang|sċēp}} (West Saxon {{m|ang|sċēap}}), from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*skāp}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*skēpą}}, of unknown origin.

tomato.raw: Variant of earlier {{m|en|tomate}}, from {{bor|en|es|tomate}}, from {{der|en|nci|tomatl}}, from {{der|en|azc-nah-pro|*toma-|*toma-tl}}. Compare {{m|es|tomatillo}}.

coat.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:cote<id:coat>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|cote}}, {{m|enm|coate}}, {{m|enm|cotte}}, from {{der|en|fro|cote}}, {{m|fro|cotte||outer garment with sleeves}}, from {{der|en|la|cotta||undercoat, tunic}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*kuttô}}, {{m|gem-pro|*kuttǭ||cowl, woolen cloth, coat}}, of unclear origin; possibly eventually from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gew-|*gew-t-|t=to curve, curl}}. {{dbt|en|cot<t:covering><id:cover>|cot<q:dialectal><t:matted lock of wool><id:cover>}}.

cheap.raw: As a noun, from {{inh|en|enm|chep}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cēap|t=trade, market, value}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kaup}}. As a verb, from {{inh|en|enm|chepen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ċēapian|t=to buy, bargain, trade}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kaupōn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kaupōną}}, a verbal derivative of {{m|gem-pro|*kaupô|t=trader}}, from {{der|en|la|caupō}}.

expensive.raw: From {{bor|en|la|*expēnsīvus}}, from {{m|la|expendō||to weigh out (money), to pay out}} (whence {{cog|en|expend}}).<ref>{{R:OED Online|id=5682531809}}</ref> {{surf|en|expense|-ive}}. In the sense of "high-priced" has largely displaced {{m|en|dear}}.

glove.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|glove}}, {{m|enm|glofe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|glōf}}, {{m|ang|*glōfe}}, {{m|ang|*glōfa}}, {{gloss|"glove"; weak forms attested only in plural form {{m|ang|glōfan||gloves}}}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*galōfô||glove}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*ga-||collective and associative prefix}} + {{der|en|gem-pro|*lōfô||flat of the hand, palm}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*lāp-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*lēp-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*lep-||flat}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|gluve}}, {{m|sco|gluive||glove}}, {{cog|is|glófi||glove}}. Related to {{cog|enm|lofe}}, {{m|enm|lufe||palm of the hand}}. More at {{m|en|loof}}.

cogs: pilgrim's purse suspended from the neck
scarf.raw: Probably from {{der|en|fro-nor|escarpe}} (compare {{cog|fro|escharpe||pilgrim's purse suspended from the neck}}, which see). The verb is derived from the noun. {{dbt|en|scrip}}.

umbrella.raw: {{bor+|en|it|ombrella|t=parasol, sunshade}}, from {{der|en|LL.|umbrella}} (influenced by {{m|la|umbra||shadow, shade}}), from {{der|en|la|umbella}}, from {{af|la|umbra|-lus|alt2=-la|pos2=diminutive suffix|nocat=1}}.

please.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|plesen}}, {{m|enm|plaisen}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|plaise}}, conjugated form of {{m|fro|plaisir}} or {{m|fro|plaire}}, from {{der|en|la|placeō|t=to please, to seem good}},<ref name="dictionary">{{R:Dictionary.com}}</ref> from the {{der|en|ine-pro|*pleHk-|t=pleasingness, permission}}. In this sense, displaced native {{ncog|ang|līcian}}, whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|like}}.

cogs: clod, lump; frozen ground; mud fever, scratches
great.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰer-|id=rub}} {{etymon|en|id=grand|:inh|enm:grete}} From {{inh|en|enm|greet}}, {{m|enm|grete|t=great, large}}, from {{inh|en|ang|grēat|t=big, massive; tall; thick; coarse}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*graut}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*grautaz|t=coarse, crude; big, large}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰrewd-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*gʰer-|t=to rub; to stroke; to grind; to remove|id=rub}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|graat}}, {{m|sco|great}}, {{m|sco|greet|t=great}}, {{cog|yol|graat|t=great}}, {{cog|frr|grat}}, {{m|frr|groot}}, {{m|frr|grot}}, {{m|frr|grut}}, {{m|frr|gråt}}, {{m|fr

chain: money, a place for coining money, coin, mint
money.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:moneye|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*men- (think)}} From {{inh|en|enm|moneye}}, {{m|enm|moneie}}, {{m|enm|money}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|muneie||money}}, from {{der|en|la|monēta||money, a place for coining money, coin, mint}}, from the name of the temple of Juno Moneta in Rome, where a mint was.

busy.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|bisy}}, {{m|enm|busie}}, from {{inh|en|ang|bisiġ|t=busy, occupied, diligent}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*bisīg|t=diligent; zealous; busy}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|biesich|t=active, diligent, hard-working, industrious}}, {{cog|nl|bezig|t=busy}}, {{cog|nds|besig|t=busy}}. The spelling with ⟨u⟩ represents the pronunciation of the West Midland and Southern dialects while the Modern English pronunciation with {{IPAchar|/ɪ/}} is from the dialects of the East Midlands.<ref>Upward, Christopher & George Davidson. 2011. [https://books.google.com/books?id=fNfebt79zdwC&pg=PT85 ''The History

late.raw: From {{der|en|enm|late}}, {{m|enm|lat}}, from {{der|en|ang|læt||slow; slack, lax, negligent; late}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*lat}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*lataz||slow, lazy}}. {{surf|+deverbal|en|let}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|yol|laate||late}}, {{cog|frr|leed}}, {{m|frr|leet}}, {{m|frr|lääs||late}}, {{cog|stq|leet||late}}, {{cog|nl|-}}, {{cog|nds-de|laat||late, tardy}}, {{cog|de|lass||lazy, sluggish}}, {{cog|da|lad||languid, lazy, indolent}}, {{cog|fo|-}}, {{cog|is|latur||lazy}}, {{cog|nb|-}}, {{cog|nn|-}} and {{cog|sv|lat||lazy}}, {{cog|got|𐌻𐌰𐍄𐍃||lazy, slothful}}. {{col-bottom}}

free.raw: {{etymon|en|id=adjective|:inh|enm:fre|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|fre}}, from {{inh|en|ang|frēo}}, {{m|ang|frēoh}}, {{m|ang|frī}}, {{m|ang|friġ}}, {{m|ang|frīoh|t=free}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*frī}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*frijaz|t=beloved, not in bondage}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*priHós|t=pleased, loved}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*preyH-|t=to please; to love}}. Related to {{m|en|friend}}. {{box-top|cognates, etc}} Germanic cognates include {{cog|sco|fre|t=free}}, {{cog|frr|frai}}, {{m|frr|frei}}, {{m|frr|fri}}, {{m|frr|Frii|t=free}}, {{cog|stq|fräi|t=free}}, {{cog|fy|frij|t=free}}, {{cog|nl|vrij|t=f

cute.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eḱ-}} [[Appendix:Glossary#aphetic|Aphetic]] form of {{m|en|acute}}, originally meaning “keenly perceptive or discerning, shrewd” (1731). Meaning transferred to “pretty, fetching” by US students (slang) {{circa2|1834|short=yes}}. Meaning drifted further to describe the pleasing attraction to features usually possessed by the young.

China.raw: {{etymon|en|id=country|:bor|pt:China<id:country>|tree=1}} {{wp}} {{commonscat}} [[File:Flag of the People's Republic of China.svg|thumb|240px|Flag of the People's Republic of '''China''']]

actor.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:actour|:afeq|act|-or<id:agent noun>|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eǵ-|id=drive}} {{inh+|en|enm|actour}}, from {{der|en|xno|actor}}, {{der|en|frm|actor}}, and their source, {{der|en|la|āctor||doer}}, from {{m|la|agō||to do}}. Equivalent to {{suffix|en|act|or}}. Cognate with {{cog|grc|ἄκτωρ||leader}}, from {{m|grc|ἄγω||lead, carry, convey, bring}}.

actress.raw: From {{suf|en|actor|ess<id:female>}}.<ref>{{R:Dictionary.com}}</ref><ref>{{R:Merriam-Webster Online}}</ref><ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary}}</ref> Probably formed independently of {{cog|frm|actrice}}.<ref>{{R:OED2|id=00002230}}</ref>

active.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:actyf|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eǵ-|id=drive}} From {{inh|en|enm|actyf}}, from {{der|en|fro|actif}}, from {{der|en|la|activus|alt=āctīv(us)}}, from {{m|la|ago|agere|t=to do, to act}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂éǵeti}}. {{surf|+suf|en|act|ive}}.

action.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:accioun|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eǵ-|id=drive}} From {{inh|en|enm|accioun}}, {{m|enm|accion}}, from {{der|en|fro|aucion}}, {{m|fro|acciun}}, from {{der|en|la|āctiō|alt=āctiō(n)||act of doing or making}}, from {{m|la|āctus|āct(us)}} + action suffix {{m|la|-iō|-iō(n)}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|agō|agere|do, act}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂éǵeti}}. See also {{m|en|act}}, {{m|en|active}}. {{surf|+suf|en|act|ion}}.

visitor.raw: Partly from {{inh|en|enm|visiter}}, {{m|enm|visitere}}, equivalent to {{af|en|visit|-er|id2=agent noun|nocat=1}}; and partly from {{inh|en|enm|visitour}}, from {{der|en|xno|visitour}}, from {{der|en|fro|visetëor}}. {{surf|en|visit|-or<id:agent noun>}}.

fact.raw: {{etymon|en|id=deed|:inh|enm:fact<ety:bor<la:factum<id:participle>>>|tree=1}} {{inh+|en|enm|fact}}, from {{der|en|la|factum||an act, deed, feat, etc.}}; also [[Medieval Latin]] for “state, condition, circumstance”; neuter of {{m|la|factus||done or made}}, [[perfect passive participle]] of {{m|la|faciō||do, make}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-||to put, place, set}}. Old/Middle French later evolved it into [[faict]] and [[fait]]. <!-- Century 1911: The English words derived from "facere" are many.-->{{doublet|en|feat}}.

difficult.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|difficult}} (ca. 1400), a {{back-form|en||nocap=1}} from {{m|enm|difficulte}} (whence modern {{m|en|difficulty}}), from {{uder|en|fro|difficulté}}, from {{uder|en|la|difficultas}}, from {{m|la|difficul}}, older form of {{m|la|difficilis||hard to do, difficult}}, from {{m|la|dis-}} + {{m|la|facilis||easy}}; see [[difficile]]. Replaced native {{cog|enm|earveþ||difficult, hard}}, from {{cog|ang|earfoþe||difficult, laborious, full of hardship}}, cognate to {{cog|de|Arbeit||work}}.

special.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:especial}} From {{inh|en|enm|*special}}, {{m|enm|especial}}, {{m|enm|especiall}}, from {{der|en|fro|especial}} (whence also {{cog|fr|spécial}}), from {{der|en|la|speciālis}} (from {{m|la|speciēs}}). In this sense displaced native {{ncog|ang|synderlīċ}}. {{doublet|en|especial}}.

cogs: a press, crowd, anything that presses or confines
press.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id=beat}} From {{der|en|enm|presse||throng, crowd, clothespress}}, partially from {{der|en|ang|press||clothespress}} (from {{der|en|la-med|pressa}}) and from {{der|en|fro|presse|}} (Modern {{cog|fr|presse}}) from {{der|en|fro|presser||to press}}, from {{der|en|la|presso|pressāre}}, from {{m|la|pressus}}, past participle of {{m|la|premo|premere|to press}}.Largely displaced native {{cog|enm|thring||press, crowd, throng}} (from {{cog|ang|þring||a press, crowd, anything that presses or confines}}). see {{cog|en|thring}}

sign.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*sek-}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|id=follow}} From {{inh|en|enm|signe}}, {{m|enm|sygne}}, {{m|enm|syng}}, {{m|enm|seine}}, {{m|enm|sine}}, {{m|enm|syne}}, from {{inh|en|ang|seġn|t=sign; mark; token}} and {{der|en|fro|signe}}, {{m|fro|seing||sign; mark; signature}}; both from {{der|en|la|signum|t=a mark; sign; token}}; root uncertain. {{doublet|en|signum|signal}}. Partially displaced native {{m|en|token}}.

serve.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ser-|id=guard}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:serven|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|serven}}, from {{der|en|fro|servir}}, from {{der|en|la|serviō||be a slave; serve}}, from {{der|en|la|servus||slave; servant}}, which perhaps derives from {{der|en|ett|-}} (compare {{cog|ett|-}} proper names {{m|ett|𐌔𐌄𐌓𐌅𐌉}}, {{m|ett|𐌔𐌄𐌓𐌅𐌄}}), or from [[:W:Proto-Indo-European|Proto-Indo-European]] {{m|ine-pro|*ser-||watch over, protect}}.<ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary}}</ref>

save.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*solh₂-}} {{etymon|en|id=to keep safe|:inh|enm:saven<id:to keep safe>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|saven}}, {{m|enm|sauven}}, a borrowing from {{der|en|fro|sauver}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|salvo|salvāre|t=to save}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|nerian}}.

partner.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|partener}}, {{m|enm|partiner}}, alteration (due to {{cog|enm|part}}) of {{cog|enm|parcener}}, from {{der|en|fro|parçonier}}, {{m|fro|parçonneour|t=joint heir}} from {{m|fro|parçon|t=partition}}, from {{der|en|la|partītiōnem}}, singular accusative of {{m|la|partītiō|t=portion}}. The word may also represent {{cog|fro|part tenour|t=part holder}}. Compare also {{noncog|enm|partifere|t=partner}}, {{m|enm|partifelewe|t=partner}}. {{doublet|en|parcener}}.

apartment.raw: From {{bor|en|fr|appartement}}, from {{der|en|it|appartamento}}, from {{der|en|es|apartamiento|t=separation, seclusion}}, equivalent to {{af|en|apart|-ment}}. See {{m|en|apart}} and {{m|en|-ment}}.

mobile.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*m(y)ewh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|-}}, from {{der|en|fro|-}}, from {{der|en|la|mōbilis|t=easy to be moved, moveable}}, from {{m|la|moveō|t=move}}. The video-gaming sense was coined by {{w|Richard Bartle}} to describe [[NPC]]s or creatures capable of moving "under their own power" in the 1978 video game ''{{w|MUD1|Multi-User Dungeon}}''. Bartle retracted an earlier claim of his that it was from the {{w|kinetic sculpture}} sense of ''mobile'' (for the "[[unpredictable]] but [[limited]]" motion of the hanging [[ornament]]s).

country.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:contre<ref:{{R:Etymonline|pos=n}}<<name::0>>>|tree=1|text=++}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|kintra}}. Unrelated to {{m|en|county}}. Displaced native {{m+|en|land}} in some of its senses.

hotel.raw: {{ety|en|:bor|fr:hôtel|tree=1}} {{bor+|en|fr|hôtel}}, from {{der|en|frm|hostel}}, from {{der|en|fro|ostel}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|hospitālis||hospice, shelter, guesthouse}}, from {{der|en|la|hospitālis||hospitable}}. {{doublet|en|hostel|hospital}}.

chain: stranger, guest, host, someone with whom one has reciprocal duties of hospitality
guest.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|gest}}, from {{der|en|non|gestr}}, which replaced or was merged with {{cog|ang|ġiest}}, both from {{der|en|gem-pro|*gastiz}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰóstis||stranger, guest, host, someone with whom one has reciprocal duties of hospitality}}. {{doublet|en|host}}, from Latin.

centre.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|center}}, {{m|enm|centre}}, from {{der|en|frm|centre}}, from {{der|en|la|centrum}}, from {{der|en|grc|κέντρον|}}, from {{m|grc|κεντεῖν||to prick, goad}}. {{doublet|en|centrum}}.

closet.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|closet}}, from {{der|en|fro|closet}}, from {{suffix|fro|clos|t1=[[private]] [[space]]|-et|pos2={{lg|diminutive}} suffix|nocat=1}}, from {{der|en|la|clausum}}. Equivalent to {{suffix|en|close|et}}, but generally applied in French solely to small open-air enclosures.<ref>''Oxford English Dictionary''. "closet, ''n.''"</ref> {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)kleh₂w-}}

volleyball.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷelH-|id=throw}} {{ety|en|:af|volley|ball<id:Q18545>|tree=1}} From {{af|en|volley|ball<id:Q18545>}}. In 1895, in Holyoke, Massachusetts, William G. Morgan created a new game called Mintonette, a name derived from the game of badminton. After an observer, Alfred Halstead, noticed the volleying nature of the game at its first exhibition match in 1896, played at the International YMCA Training School (now called Springfield College), the game quickly became known as volleyball (it was originally spelled as two words: "volley ball") {{rfv-etym|en}}

sunlight.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|sonnelight}}, {{m|enm|sunneliht}}, from {{inh|en|ang|[[sunnan]] [[lēoht]]|t=sunlight}},<ref>''Chambers Dictionary of Etymology'', Robert K. Barnhart (ed.), Chambers, 1988</ref> equivalent to {{af|en|sun|light}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|zonlicht|t=sunlight}}, {{cog|nds-de|Sünnenlücht|t=sunlight}}, {{cog|de|Sonnenlicht|t=sunlight}}.

waterfall.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|waterfal}}, {{m|enm|waterfalle}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wæterġefeall||waterfall}}, equivalent to {{compound|en|water|fall}}. Cognate with {{cog|fy|wetterfal||waterfall}}, {{cog|nl|waterval||waterfall}}, {{cog|de|Wasserfall||waterfall}}, {{cog|sv|vattenfall||waterfall}}.

sometimes.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|sumtymes}}, {{m|enm|somtymes}}, {{m|enm|som tymes}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|sometime|-s|pos2=adverbial suffix|id2=adverbial}}. Compare {{noncog|fy|somstiden|t=sometimes}}, {{noncog|nl|somtijds}}, {{m|nl|somwijlen|t=sometimes}}.

always.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:alweyes|:afeq|alway|-s<id:adverbial>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|alweyes}}, {{m|enm|alwayes}}, {{m|enm|alweys}}, a variant of {{der|en|enm|alwey}}, {{m|enm|alway|t=always}}, from {{der|en|ang|ealneġ}}, {{m|ang|ealne weġ|t=always, perpetually|lit=all the way, all the while, continuously}}, from {{m|ang|ealne}} + {{m|ang|weġ|pos=accusative case}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|alway|s|id2=adverbial}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|always|t=always}}, {{cog|nds|allerwegens|t=very often|lit=all ways'}}. More at {{l|en|all}}, {{l|en|way}}.

someone.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|sum on}}, {{m|enm|sum one}}, {{m|enm|sum oon}}, equivalent to {{compound|en|some|one}}.

nobody.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|nobody}}, {{m|enm|no-body}}, {{m|enm|no body}}. {{surf|en|no|t1=none, not any|pos1=adjective|body|t2=one, person, individual}}.

anything.raw: {{etymon|en|id=any thing|:inh|enm:anything<id:any thing><ety:inh<ang:aniþing<ety:af<ǣniġ><þing>>>>|:afeq|any|thing|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|anything}}, {{m|enm|enything}}, {{m|enm|onything}}, from Late {{inh|en|ang|aniþing}}, from earlier {{m|ang|ǣniġ þing|lit=any thing}}, equivalent to {{af|en|any|thing}}.

nothing.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:nothyng}} From {{inh|en|enm|nothyng}}, {{m|enm|noon thing}}, {{m|enm|non thing}}, {{m|enm|na þing}}, {{m|enm|nan thing}}, {{m|enm|nan þing}}, from {{inh|en|ang|nāþing}}, {{m|ang|nān þing|t=nothing|lit=not any thing}}, equivalent to {{compound|en|no|thing}}. careless.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:careles<ety:inh<ang:carlēas>>|:afeq|care<id:noun>|-less|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|careles}}, from {{inh|en|ang|carlēas|t=careless, reckless, void of care, free from care, free}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|care|less}}. Cognate with {{cog|is|kærulaus|t=careless, negligent}}.

wonder.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*wenh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|wonder}}, {{m|enm|wunder}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wundor||wonder, miracle, marvel}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wundr}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wundrą}}.

beauty.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:beaute|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|bewty}}, {{m|enm|bewte}}, {{m|enm|beaute}}, {{m|enm|bealte}}, from {{der|en|xno|-}} and {{der|en|fro|beauté}} (early Old French spelling {{m|fro|biauté}}), from {{der|en|la-vul|*bellitātem|t=beauty}}, from {{der|en|la|bellus|t=beautiful, fair}}; see {{m|en|beau}}. In this sense, mostly displaced native {{m+|ang|fæġernes}}, whence [[Modern English]] {{m|en|fairness}}.

famous.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|famous}}, from {{der|en|xno|famous}}, from {{der|en|la|fāmōsus}}, equivalent to {{af|en|fame|-ous}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|hlīsful}}.

danger.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*demh₂-}} From {{der|en|enm|daunger||power, dominion, peril}}, from {{der|en|xno|-}} {{m|fro|dangier}}, from {{der|en|fro|dangier}}, alteration of {{cog|fro|dongier}} (due to association with {{cog|la|damnum||damage}}) from {{der|en|la-vul|*dominiārium||authority, power}} from {{der|en|la|dominus||lord, master}}.<ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref> Displaced native {{noncog|ang|frēcennes}}.

usual.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|usual}}, from {{der|en|fro|usuel}}, from {{der|en|la|ūsuālis|t=for use, fit for use, also of common use, customary, common, ordinary, usual}}, from {{m|la|ūsus|t=use, habit, custom}}, from the past participle stem of {{m|la|utor|ūtī|t=to use}}, possibly ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₃eyt-||to take along, fetch}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|ġewunelīċ}}.

review.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*weyd-}} From {{inh|en|enm|revewe}}, {{m|enm|reveue}}, from {{der|en|fro|reveue|reveüe}}, {{m|fro|revue}} (Modern French: {{m|fr|revue}}), feminine form of {{m|fro|reveu|reveü}}, past participle of {{m|fro|reveoir}} (French: {{m|fr|revoir}}), from {{der|en|la|revideō}}, from {{m|la|re-}} +{{m|la|videō||see, observe}} (English: {{m|en|video}}). Compare {{m|en|beturn}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|eftċierran|lit=again-turn}}.

cover.raw: {{etymon|en|id=place upon|:inh|enm:coveren<id:place upon>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|coveren}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|covrir|covrir, cueuvrir}} (modern {{cog|fr|couvrir}}), from {{der|en|la-lat|coperire}}, from {{der|en|la|cooperiō|t=to cover completely}}, from {{m|la|co-|pos=intensive prefix}} + {{m|la|operiō|t=to close, cover}}. Displaced native {{cog|enm|thecchen}} and {{m|enm|bithecchen|bethecchen|t=to cover}} (from {{cog|ang|þeccan}}, {{m|ang|beþeccan|t=to cover}}), {{cog|enm|helen|helen, (over)helen, (for)helen|t=to cover, conceal}} (from {{cog|ang|helan|t=to conceal, cover, hide}})

singer.raw: {{inh+|en|enm|syngere}}, {{m|enm|syngere}}, {{m|enm|singere}}, equivalent to {{affix|en|sing|-er|id2=agent noun}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|singar}}, {{cog|stq|Sjunger}}, {{cog|fy|sjonger}}, {{cog|nds-de|Singer}}. Compare also {{cog|ang|sangere}}, {{cog|nl|zanger}}, {{cog|nds-de|Sänger}}, {{cog|de|Sänger|t=singer}}, {{cog|da|sanger}}, {{cog|sv|sångare}}, {{cog|is|söngvari}}.

writer.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:writere|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|writer}}, {{m|enm|writere}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wrītere|t=draughtsman; painter; writer; scribe; copyist}} and {{m|ang|ġewritere|t=writer; composer}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|write|-er|id2=agent noun}}. Cognate with {{cog|is|ritari|t=clerk, secretary}}, {{cog|fo|ritari|t=clerk, secretary}}.

player.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:pleyere|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|pleyere}}, {{m|enm|pleyer}}, from {{inh|en|ang|pleġere|t=player, athlete, wrestler}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*plegārī}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|play|er|id2=agent noun}}.

reader.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|reder}}, {{m|enm|redar}}, {{m|enm|redere}}, {{m|enm|redare}}, from {{inh|en|ang|rēdere}}, {{m|ang|rǣdere|t=a reader; scholar; diviner}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*rādāri}}, equivalent to {{af|en|read|-er|id2=agent noun}}. slowly.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|slowly}}, {{m|enm|slowli}}, {{m|enm|slouli}}, {{m|enm|slowliche}}, from {{inh|en|ang|slāwlīċe|t=slowly; sluggishly}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|slow|-ly|id2=adverbial}}. Compare {{cog|non|slæliga}}, {{m|non|sljóliga}}.

real.raw: {{etymon|en|id=actual|:inh|enm:real|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|real}}, from {{der|en|fro|reel}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|reālis||actual}}, from {{der|en|la|rēs||matter, thing}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*reh₁ís||wealth, goods}}. {{doublet|en|realis}}. In modern times, likely strengthened by or conflated with the use of the prefix ''re-'', analyzable as {{m|en|re-}} + {{m|en|-al}}.

fourth.raw: {{inh+|en|enm|fourthe}}, an alteration (due to {{m|enm|four}}) of {{m|enm|ferthe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|fēorþa}}, {{m|ang|fēowerþa}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*feurþō}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*fedurþô}}, equivalent to {{af|en|four|-th|pos2=ordinal suffix|id2=ordinal}}.

fifth.raw: {{PIE word|en|pénkʷe}} From {{inh|en|enm|fifthe}}, {{m|enm|fifte}}, {{m|enm|fift}}, from {{inh|en|ang|fīfta||fifth}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*fimftô||fifth}} or {{m|gem-pro|*femftô}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|five|-th|id2=ordinal|pos2=ordinal suffix}}. The ''-n-'', lost in northern Proto-West Germanic, was later reinserted by analogy with {{m|en|seven}}, equivalent to {{af|en|seven|-th|id2=ordinal}}.

Ultimately from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*tehundô}}. Equivalent to {{af|en|ten|pos1=numeral|-th|id2=ordinal|pos2=suffix forming ordinals}}.

twelfth.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|twelfthe}}, {{m|enm|twelfte}}, from {{inh|en|ang|twelfta|t=twelfth}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*twaliftô|t=twelfth}}, equivalent to {{af|en|twelve|-th|id2=ordinal|pos2=ordinal suffix}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|twalt|t=twelfth}}, {{cog|stq|tweelfte|t=twelfth}}, {{cog|fy|tolfde|t=twelfth}}, {{cog|nl|twaalfde|t=twelfth}}, {{cog|nds-de|twalfde}}, {{m|nds-de|twalvde|t=twelfth}}, {{cog|de|zwölfte|t=twelfth}}, {{cog|da|tolvte|t=twelfth}}, {{cog|sv|tolfte|t=twelfth}}, {{cog|is|tólfta|t=twelfth}}.

twentieth.raw: From earlier {{m|en|twenteth}}, {{m|en|twentith}}, from {{inh|en|enm|twentithe}}, {{m|enm|twentiþe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|twēntigoþa}}. Equivalent to {{af|en|twenty|-eth}}.

building.raw: [[File:Fotothek df roe-neg 0006285 033 Blick auf die Wohnbauten Straße der III. Weltfes.jpg|thumb|white '''buildings''' in Leipzig]] From {{inh|en|enm|bildynge}}, {{m|enm|byldynge}}, equivalent to {{af|en|build|-ing|id2=gerund noun}}. Compare also related {{cog|enm|bold|t=edifice, castle, mansion}}, from {{cog|ang|bold|t=building, dwelling, house}}.

build.raw: {{etymon|en|id=form with materials|:inh|enm:bilden<id:build>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|bilden}}, {{m|enm|buylden}}, {{m|enm|bylden}}, from {{inh|en|ang|byldan}} and {{m|ang|bytlan}}, {{m|ang|bytlian|t=to build}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*buþlijan|t=to build}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*buþlą}}, {{m|gem-pro|*bōþlą|t=house, dwelling, farm}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*bʰuH-||to become, grow, thrive, be, live, dwell}}. Related to {{cog|ang|botl||building, house}}. More at {{l|en|bottle#Etymology_2|bottle}}. {{false cognate|de|bilden}}.

twin.raw: {{PIE word|en|dwóh₁}} From {{inh|en|enm|twinne}}, {{m|enm|twynne}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ġetwin}}, {{m|ang|ġetwinn||twin, multiple|pos=noun}} and {{m|ang|twinn||twin, two-fold, double, two by two|pos=adjective}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*twinaz|t=double/two each, twin}}, {{inh|en|gem-pro|*twinjaz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*twīhnaz||two each}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dwino-||twin}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*dwóh₁||two}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|twyn||twin}}, {{cog|nl|tweeling||twin}}, {{cog|de|Zwilling||twin}}, {{cog|da,nb,nn,sv|tvilling||twin}}, {{cog|fo|tvinnur||a double set}}, {{cog|is|tvenna||duo, pair}}, {{cog|lt

twice.raw: From earlier {{m|en|twise}}, from {{inh|en|enm|twies}}, {{m|enm|twiȝes}}, from {{inh|en|ang|twīġes||twice}}, from {{m|ang|twīwa}}, {{m|ang|twīġa}} {{gloss|"twice"; whence Middle English {{m|enm|twie||twice}}}} + {{m|ang|-es|pos=adverbial genitive ending}}. Similarly constructed to the prefixes {{dbt|notext=1|nocat=1|en|bis-|dis-}}, borrowed from {{cog|ine}} cognates.

once.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|ones|}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ānes}}, a remodelling (after {{m|ang|ān|t=one}}) of {{m|ang|ǣnes}}, itself an extension of {{m|enm|ǣne|t=once}} with the genitive suffix {{m|ang|-es}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|one|-s}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|enst}}, {{m|stq|insen|t=once}}, {{cog|fy|iens|t=once}}, {{cog|nl|eens|t=once}}, {{cog|nds-de|eens}}, {{m|nds-de|ins|t=once}}, {{cog|de|einst|t=once}}. More at {{l|en|one}} (including regarding the development of the pronunciation) and [[-s#Etymology_3|-s]].

More at {{l|en|food}}, {{l|en|fodder}}.

February.raw: [[File:Abel Grimmer The Month of February.jpg|thumb|A 17th-century depiction of February in [[the Netherlands]]]] {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:Februarie<ety:der<la:Februārius>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|Februarie}}, {{m|enm|februari}}, {{m|enm|februare}}, from {{der|en|la|Februārius||the [[month]] of the [[Februa]]}}, from {{m|la|Februa||the [[purging|Purging]]s, the [[purification|Purification]]s}}, a Roman holiday two days after its [[ides]] (i.e., Feb. 15), + {{m|la|-arius||[[-ary]]: ''[[form]]ing [[adjective]]s''}}. {{m|la|Februa}} from {{m|la|februum||[[purging]]}}, from an earlier {{der|en|sbv}

March.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:March|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|March}}, {{m|enm|Marche}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|marche}}, from {{der|en|fro|marz}}, from {{der|en|la|mensis Mārtius|gloss=the Martian month}}, from earlier {{m|la|Mavors}}.

chain: the month of the goddess Venus
April.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:Aprill|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|apprile}}, {{m|en|Aprill}}, re-Latinised from {{cog|enm|aueril}}, from {{der|en|fro|avrill}}, from {{der|en|la|Aprīlis||the month of the goddess [[Venus]]}}, perhaps based on {{der|en|ett|𐌀𐌐𐌓𐌖}}, from {{der|en|grc|Ἀφροδίτη||Venus}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|ēastermōnaþ|t=April|lit=Easter month}}, see {{m|en|Eastermonth}}.

May.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:May<ety:bor<fro:mai<ety:der<la:Maius<id:May>>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|May}}, {{m|enm|Mai}}, from {{der|en|fro|mai}}, from {{der|en|la|Maius||Maia's month}}, from {{m|la|Maia}}, a Roman earth goddess.

July.raw: {{etymon|en|id=month|:inh|enm:Julie<ety:bor<xno:julie<ety:from<fro:jule<ety:inh<la:iūlius>>>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|Julie,julius,julye}}, from {{der|en|xno|julie}}, from {{der|en|fro|jule}}, {{m|fro|juil}}, from {{der|en|la|iūlius}} ({{w|Julius Caesar|Gaius Julius Caesar}}'s month), perhaps a contraction of ''*Iovilios'', "descended from [[Jove]]".

August.raw: {{ety|en|id=month|:der|enm:August<ety:der<ang:Augustus>>|tree=1}} Early {{der|en|enm|August|August(us)}}, re-Latinized from {{der|en|ang|Agustus}}, from {{cog|la-lat|Agustus}}, from {{der|en|la|augustus||month of August}}, from the agnomen {{m|la|Augustus||venerable}} of {{w|Augustus|Gaius Julius Caesar Augustus}}, possibly from either Old Latin {{m|itc-ola|*augos|t=increase}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*augos}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|-}} base {{m|ine-pro|*h₂ewg-||to increase}}; or {{cog|la|avis||bird}}, referring to divination by observing bird flights, singing, feeding or entrails + {{m|la|garri

November.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:Novembre<ety:bor<fro:novembre>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|Novembre}}, from {{der|en|fro|novembre}}, from {{der|en|la|November||ninth month}}, from Latin {{m|la|novem}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₁néwn̥||nine}}; + {{der|en|la|-ber}}, from {{m|la|-bris}}, an adjectival suffix. November was the ninth month in the Roman calendar.

myself.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|myself}}, {{m|enm|meself}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mē}} {{m|ang|selfum}} and similar phrases, equivalent to {{af|en|me|self}}, later partly reinterpreted as {{af|en|my|self}} / {{affix|en|-self}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|mysel}}, {{m|sco|mysell|t=myself}}, {{noncog|fy|mysels|t=myself}}, {{noncog|nl|mijzelf|t=myself}}, {{noncog|de|mich selbst}}, {{m|de|mir selbst|t=myself}}, {{noncog|nb|meg selv|t=myself}}.

across.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:acros|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|acros}}, from early {{inh|en|enm|a-croiz}}, {{m|enm|a-creoyz}}, from {{der|en|xno|an||in, on}} + {{m|fro|croiz||in the form of a cross}}. More at {{m|en|cross}}. {{surf|+pre|en|a|cross}}.

chain: to burn, smoke, smoulder; tar, pitch
smell.raw: {{etymon|en|id=sense|:inh|enm:smellen<id:sense>|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)meld-}} From {{inh|en|enm|smellen}}, {{m|enm|smillen}}, {{m|enm|smyllen}}, {{m|enm|smullen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*smyllan}}, {{m|ang|*smiellan|t=to smell, emit fumes}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*smallijan|t=to glow, burn, smoulder}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*smel-|t=to burn, smoke, smoulder; tar, pitch}}. The noun is from {{inh|en|enm|smel}}, {{m|enm|smil}}, {{m|enm|smul||smell, odour}}. Related to {{cog|stq|smeele|t=to smoulder}}, {{cog|dum|smolen|smōlen|to burn, smoulder}} (whence {{cog|nl|smeulen||to smoulder}}), {{cog

taste.raw:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*teh₂g-|id=touch}} The verb is from {{inh|en|enm|tasten}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|taster||to taste, touch or hit}}, from [[unattested]] {{der|en|la-vul|*tastāre||to touch or feel}}, from {{m|la-vul||*taxitāre}}, an [[w:Innovation (linguistics)|innovated]] {{lg|iterative}} form of {{der|en|la-cla|taxo|taxāre|to touch sharply}}, from {{m|la|tango|tangere|to touch, to grasp}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*teh₂g-|id=touch}}, which is assumed to have had the same meaning as {{m|la||tangere}}.
The noun came from the verb, and the two [[conflate]]d after English lost i

cogs: to pay tribute, make an offer
sell.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*selh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|sellen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sellan||give; give up for money}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*salljan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*saljaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*selh₁-}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|sell|t=to sell}}, {{cog|da|sælge|t=to sell}}, {{cog|nb|selge|t=to sell}}, {{cog|nn|selja}}, {{m|nn|selje|t=to sell}}, {{cog|sv|sälja|t=to sell}}, {{cog|fo,is|selja||t=to sell}}, {{cog|got|𐍃𐌰𐌻𐌾𐌰𐌽|t=to pay tribute, make an offer}}. {{col-bottom}}

sale.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*selh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|sale}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sala||act of selling, sale}}, from {{der|en|non|sala||sale}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*salō||delivery}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*selh₁-||to grab}}.

life.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*leyp-}} {{dercat|en|gmw-pro|inh=1}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:lyf|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|lyf}}, from {{inh|en|ang|līf}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*līb}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*lībą|t=life, body}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*lībaną|t=to remain, stay, be left}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*leyp-|t=to stick, glue}}.

chain: birth, origin, natural constitution or quality
nature.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:nature|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵenh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|nature}}, {{m|enm|natur}}, from {{der|en|fro|nature}}, from {{der|en|la|nātūra||birth, origin, natural constitution or quality}}, future participle from perfect passive participle {{m|la|natus|(g)natus|born}}, from [[deponent]] verb {{m|la|nasci|(g)nasci|to be born, originate}} + future participle suffix {{m|en|-urus}}.

mice.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|mys}}, {{m|enm|mice}}, {{m|enm|muis}}, {{m|enm|mise}}, {{m|enm|mis}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mȳs|t=mice}}, from an [[umlaut]]ed form of {{inh|en|gem-pro|*mūsiz|t=mice}}, nominative and vocative plural of {{der|en|gem-pro|*mūs|t=mouse}}. Compare {{cog|sco|mice}}, {{m|sco|mise}}, {{m|sco|myse}}, {{m|sco|myce|t=mice}}, {{cog|fy|mûzen|t=mice}}, {{cog|nl|muizen|t=mice}}, {{cog|de|Mäuse|t=mice}}, {{cog|sv|möss|t=mice}}, {{cog|fo|mýs|t=mice}}, {{cog|is|mýs|t=mice}}. More at {{l|en|mouse}}.

perfect.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|perfit}}, from {{der|en|fro|parfit}} (modern: {{m|fr|parfait}}), from {{der|en|la|perfectus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|[[perficio|perficere]]||to finish}}, from {{m|la|per-||through, thorough}} + {{m|la|[[facio|facere]]||to do, to make}}. The spelling was modified in the 15th century to conform to its Latin etymon. {{doublet|en|parfait|perfecto|perfectus}}.

center.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:center<ety:bor<frm:centre<ety:der<la:centrum>>>>|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱent-}} From {{inh|en|enm|center}}, {{m|enm|centre}}, from {{der|en|frm|centre}}, from {{der|en|la|centrum}}, from {{der|en|grc|κέντρον|}}, from {{m|grc|κεντεῖν||to prick, goad}}. {{doublet|en|centrum}}. * {{sense|group theory}} In the notation ''Z''(''G''), the letter ''Z'' derives from the {{semantic loan|en|de|Zentrum||center|notext=1}}.

circus.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)ker- (turn)}} From {{inh|en|enm|circus}}, {{m|enm|circo}}, from {{der|en|la|circus|t=ring, circle}}, from {{der|en|grc|κρίκος}}, {{m|grc|κίρκος|t=ring}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)ker-|t=to bend, turn}}.<ref>[http://books.google.ca/books?id=cm-VwKgY8jcC&lpg=PA358&ots=eROURhD0f9&dq=sker%20indo%20european%20bend&hl=en&pg=PA358#v=onepage&q=sker%20indo%20european%20bend&f=false A grammar of modern Indo-European, p. 398, 3rd paragraph]</ref><ref>[http://books.google.ca/books?id=4IHbQgz1nZYC&lpg=PA78&ots=1OVtwSboYY&dq=sker-2%20Indo-European%20roots&hl=en&pg=PA78#v=onepage&q&f=f

restroom.raw: From {{com|en|rest|room}}, from an earlier sense of {{m|en|break room|"breakroom"}}.

sunset.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|son-sett}}, {{m|enm|Sonne set}}, equivalent to {{af|en|sun|set}}. In Gower's ''Confessio Amantis'', before 1393.<ref>''Chambers Dictionary of Etymology'', Robert K. Barnhart (ed.), Chambers, 1988</ref>

sunrise.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|sonne-rys}}, {{m|enm|sunne ryse}}, equivalent to {{af|en|sun|rise}}. Compare {{noncog|enm|son risyng}}, {{m|enm|sunne rijsyng}}, {{m|enm|sonne-rysing|t=sunrise|lit=sun rising}}.

mooncake.raw: {{multiple images |direction = vertical |image1 = Moon Cakes.jpg |caption1 = A tray of mooncakes. |image2 = Mooncakes.jpg |caption2 = A mooncake [[slice#Verb|sliced]] [[open#Adjective|open]] to [[reveal#Verb|reveal]] its [[lotus seed]] [[paste#Noun|paste]] [[filling#Noun|filling]]. }}

seaside.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|see-syde}}, {{m|enm|sey-syde}}, {{m|enm|see syde}}, {{m|enm|se side}}, equivalent to {{compound|en|sea|side}}. Compare ''[[waterside]]''.

spaceship.raw: * {{compound|en|space|ship}} * {{sense|programming operator}} From its resemblance to the shape of a [[flying saucer]].

tablecloth.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|tabyllcloth}}, {{m|enm|table cloth}}, {{m|enm|tabylle clothe}}, a partial translation of earlier {{der|en|enm|bord cloth}}, {{m|enm|bordcloth|t=tablecloth}}, from {{der|en|ang|bordclāþ}}, equivalent to {{compound|en|table|cloth}}.

password.raw: From {{af|en|pass|word}}. The sentry-passing sense predates the cryptographic sense and was its inspiration.

grapefruit.raw: {{ety|en|:af|grape<id:wine-berry>|fruit|:from|greatfruit}} Widely assumed to be a marketing term from {{compound|en|grape|fruit}}, an allusion to the supposed grapelike clusters of fruit on the tree,{{ref|{{cite-book|title=Appendix to the Journals of the Senate and Assembly of the twenty-first Session of the Legislature of the State of California|volume=V|chapter=Report of the Secretary–the pomelo|location=Sacramento|year=1895|page=65|pageurl=https://books.google.de/books?id=7SNIAQAAMAAJ&pg=RA1-PA65&hl=it&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwjW_YqHiMrgAhUmMuwKHcCPClIQ6AEIKTAA#v=onepage&f=false|passage=The pomelo i

firefly.raw: {{com|en|fire|fly|type=endo}}, because the insects glow; whence also {{m|en|lightning bug}}. Compare {{m|en|glow fly}}, {{m|en|glowworm}}, {{m|en|lampfly}}, and {{m|en|lanternfly}}.

grasshopper.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|grashoppere}}, alteration of earlier {{m|enm|grashoppe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|græshoppa||grasshopper}}. Equivalent to {{af|en|grass|hopper}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Gäärshupper}}, {{cog|nl|grashupper}}, {{m|nl|grashipper}}, {{cog|nds-de|Grashüpper}}, {{m|nds-de|Gresshüpper}}, {{cog|de|Grashüpfer}}, {{cog|da|græshoppe}}, {{cog|sv|gräshoppa}}, {{cog|no|gresshoppe}}.

earthworm.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|erthe-worm}}, {{m|enm|erþe-worm}}, {{m|enm|erþe worm}} (also as {{m|enm|worm of þe erthe}}, {{m|enm|worm of þe erþe}}), equivalent to {{af|en|earth|worm}}. Compare {{cog|stq|Äidwurm|t=earthworm}}, {{cog|fy|ierdwjirm|t=earthworm}}, {{cog|nl|aardworm|t=earthworm}}, less common {{cog|de|Erdwurm|t=earthworm}}.

housewife.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|houswyf}}, {{m|enm|housewif}}, {{m|enm|huswijf}}, equivalent to {{af|en|house|wife}}; a {{doublet|en|nocap=1}} of {{m|en|hussy}}, which it was long distinguished from and displaced due to gradual negative connotation (see [https://www.etymonline.com/word/housewife ''Online Etymology Dictionary'' entry]). Cognate with {{cog|fy|húswiif}}, {{cog|nl|huiswijf}}, {{cog|nds-de|Huuswief}}, {{cog|de|Hausweib}}.

neighbour.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰuH-}} From {{inh|en|enm|neighebour}}, {{m|enm|neighbour}}, {{m|enm|neyghebour}}, from {{inh|en|ang|nēahġebūr|t=neighbour}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*nāhwagabūrō}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*nēhwagabūrô|t=neighbour|lit=near-dweller}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*nēhwaz|t=close, near}} + {{m|gem-pro|*gabūrô|t=dweller}}. Equivalent to {{com|en|nigh|t1=near|bower|t2=farmer|id2=farmer|nocat=1}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|nebour}}, {{m|sco|neebour}}, {{m|sco|neibour|t=neighbour}}, {{cog|yol|nipore}}, {{m|yol|nypore|t=neighbour}}, {{cog|frr|Naiber}}, {{m|frr|naibüür}}, {{m|frr|nä

painter.raw: [[Image:Milan-Kecic.jpg|thumb|A painter at work]] {{ety|en|id=one who paints|:inh|enm:peyntour|:afeq|paint|-er<id:agent suffix>}} {{inh+|en|enm|peyntour}}, from {{der|en|fro|peintor}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|paint|-er|id2=agent noun}}.

gardener.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|gardener}}, either calqued or loaned from {{der|en|xno|-}} and {{der|en|fro-nor|gardinier}}.

baker.raw: {{inh+|en|enm|bakere}}, from {{inh|en|ang|bæcere||baker}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*bakārijaz||baker}}, equivalent to {{affix|en|bake|-er|id2=agent noun}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|bakker||baker}}, {{cog|de|Bäcker||baker}}, {{cog|nb|baker||baker}}, {{cog|sv|bagare||baker}}, {{cog|is|bakari||baker}}.

bake.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:baken<id:verb>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|baken}}, from {{inh|en|ang|bacan||to bake}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*bakan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*bakaną||to bake}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰeh₃g-||to roast, bake}}.

bakery.raw: From {{af|en|bake|-ery<t:place of>}}. Replaced earlier {{m|en|bakehouse}}. Originally "place for making bread"; as "shop where baked goods are sold", it was believed by British travelers by 1832 to be an [[American]]-invented term.<ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary}}</ref>

waiter.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*weǵ-}} From late 14th century {{der|en|enm|waiter}}, {{m|enm|wayter|t=attendant, watchman}}. {{surf|en|wait|-er}}. Sense of "servant who waits at tables" is from late 15th century, originally in reference to household servants; in reference to inns, eating houses, etc., it is attested from 1660s. Feminine form {{m|en|waitress}} first recorded 1834.<ref>http://dictionary.reference.com/browse/waiter?s=t</ref>

swimmer.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|swimmere}}, equivalent to {{af|en|swim|-er|id2=agent noun}}. The dumplings are so called because they are often served in stew.

runner.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|rennere}}, {{m|enm|rynner}}, {{m|enm|urnare}}, equivalent to {{affix|en|run|-er|id2=agent noun}}. Cognate with {{cog|non|rennari|t=runner; messenger}}. Displaced earlier {{cog|enm|runel|t=runner}}, from {{cog|ang|rynel}} (“runner”; also “messenger, courier”).

chain: that which is on the outside
strange.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:straunge|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|straunge}}, {{m|enm|strange}}, {{m|enm|stronge}}, from {{der|en|fro|estrange}}, from {{der|en|la|extrāneus|t=that which is on the outside}}. {{doublet|en|extraneous|estrange}}. Cognate with {{cog|fr|étrange||strange, foreign}} and {{cog|es|extraño||strange, foreign}}. Largely displaced native {{m|en|fremd}}, {{m|en|selcouth}}, and {{m|en|uncouth}}, from {{ncog|ang|fremede}}, {{m|ang|seldcūþ}}, and {{m|ang|uncūþ}}.

foggy.raw: From {{suf|en|fog|y|id2=adjectival}}, originally in the sense "covered with tall grass; marshy; thick".<ref>{{R:MWO}}</ref> It is not clear whether {{m|en|fog||mist}} is a back-formation from {{m|en|foggy||covered with tall, obscuring grass}}<ref name="DC">{{R:Dictionary.com|fog}}</ref> or has a separate Germanic origin,<ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref> and hence whether {{m|en|foggy||covered with tall grass}} and {{m|en|foggy||obscured by mist}} represent one word or two. See {{m|en|fog}} ("mist"; "tall grass") for more.

cogs: spray, any light thing tossed by the wind, snowdrift
fog.raw: Origin {{unc|en|nocap=1}}; but probably of {{der|en|gmq}} origin. Probably either a back-formation from {{m|en|foggy||covered with tall grass; thick, marshy}}, from the earlier-attested {{m|en|fog||tall grass}} (see below),<ref>{{R:Dictionary.com|fog}}</ref><ref name="Etymonline">{{R:Etymonline}}</ref> or from or related to {{bor|en|da|fog|t=spray, shower, drift, storm}},<ref name="Etymonline"/> related to {{cog|is|fok|t=spray, any light thing tossed by the wind, snowdrift}}, {{cog|is|fjúka|t=to blow, drive}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*feukaną|t=to whisk, blow}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*pug-|t=bil

stormy.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|stormy}}, {{m|enm|stormi}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*stormiġ|t=stormy}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|storm|y|id2=adjectival}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|stormig||stormy}}, {{cog|de|stürmisch||stormy}}, {{cog|sv|stormig||stormy}}.

chain: disturbed state of the atmosphere; heavy precipitation; battle, conflict; attack
tempest, storm; attack; storm of arrows; disquiet, disturbance, tumult, uproar; onrush, rush
storm.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)twerH-}} From {{inh|en|enm|storm|t=disturbed state of the atmosphere; heavy precipitation; battle, conflict; attack}}{{nb...|starme, steorm, storem, storme, stourme, strom|otherforms=1}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|pos=n|id=MED43115}}</ref> from {{der|en|ang|storm|t=tempest, storm; attack; storm of arrows; disquiet, disturbance, tumult, uproar; onrush, rush}}{{nb...|steorm, (Northern England) stearm|otherforms=1}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sturm|t=storm}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*sturmaz|t=storm}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)twerH-|t=to agitate, stir up; to propel; to urge on}}.<ref

sandy.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|sandi}}, {{m|enm|sondy}}, {{m|enm|sandiȝ}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sandiġ|t=sandy}}, equivalent to {{af|en|sand|-y}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|zandig|t=sandy}}, {{cog|de|sandig|t=sandy}}, {{cog|sv|sandig|t=sandy}}.

grassy.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|grasy}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*græsiġ}}, {{m|ang|*gærsiġ}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*grasagrōnī}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*grasagrōniz}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|grass|-y|id2=adjectival}}. Compare {{cog|stq|gäärsich|t=grassy}}, {{cog|nl|grazig|t=grassy}}, {{cog|de|grasig|t=grassy}}, {{cog|is|grösugur|t=grassy}}.

wooden.raw: {{PIE word|en|dwóh₁}} From {{suffix|en|wood|-en|id2=made of}}. Dates from 1530s, gradually replaced {{m|en|treen||made from a tree}}, from {{noncog|enm|treen}}, from {{noncog|ang|triewen}}.

golden.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:golden|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|golden}}, a restored form (due to the noun {{m|en|gold}}) of earlier {{der|en|enm|gulden}}, {{m|enm|gylden}}, {{m|enm|gilden}} {{gloss|"golden"; > {{cog|en|gilden}}}}, from {{der|en|ang|gylden||golden}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*gulþīn}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*gulþīnaz||golden, made of gold}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|gold|en|id2=made of}}.

broken.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|broken}}, from {{inh|en|ang|brocen}}, {{m|ang|ġebrocen}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*brukanaz}}, past participle of {{der|en|gem-pro|*brekaną|t=to break}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|gebroken|t=broken}}, {{cog|nds-de|broken|t=broken}}, {{cog|de|gebrochen|t=broken}}. Morphologically {{suffix|en|broke|n<id:past participle>}}.

chain: deep, profound; awful, mysterious; heinous; serious, solemn, earnest; extreme, great
