forest.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*perkʷ-}} {{inh+|en|enm|forest}}, from {{der|en|fro|forest}}, from {{der|en|la-eme|forestis}}. The Latin could be:

mountain.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*men-|id=stand out}} From {{inh|en|enm|mountayne}}, {{m|enm|mountain}}, {{m|enm|montaigne}}, from {{der|en|xno|montaigne|muntaine}}, {{m|fro|montaigne|muntaigne}}, from {{der|en|la-eme|montānia}}, a collective based on {{der|en|la|mōns|montem|t=mountain}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*monti}} (compare {{cog|cy|mynydd||mountain}}, {{cog|sq|mat||bank, shore}}, {{cog|ae|𐬨𐬀𐬙𐬌|t=promontory}}), from {{m|ine-pro|*men-||to project, stick out}}. Displaced native {{ncog|en|barrow}} (from {{ncog|ang|beorg}}) and {{m|en|down}} (from {{ncog|ang|dūn}}), and partially displaced non-native {{cog|a

river.raw: {{ety|en|id=stream|:inh|enm:ryver|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|ryver}}, from {{der|en|xno|riviere|rivere}}, from {{der|en|la-eme|rīpāria|t=littoral, riverbank}}, from {{der|en|la|rīpārius|t=of a riverbank}}, from {{der|en|la|rīpa|t=river bank}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₁reyp-|t=to scratch, tear, cut}}. Unrelated to {{cog|la|rīvus||stream}} (whence {{m|en|rival}}, {{m|en|derive}}). {{doublet|en|riviera|rivière}}. Largely displaced native {{ncog|en|ea}}.

exercise.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:exercise<ety:bor<fro:exercise<ety:der<la:exercitium>>>>|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂erk-}} From {{inh|en|enm|exercise}}, from {{der|en|fro|exercise}}, from {{der|en|la|exercitium}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|plega||an exercise}} whence [[Modern English]] {{l|en|play}}.

island.raw: {{word|en|ine|h₂ékʷeh₂}} {{etymon|en|iland|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*lendʰ-|id=land}} From earlier {{m|en|iland}}, from {{inh|en|enm|iland}}, {{m|enm|yland}}, {{m|enm|ylond}}, from {{inh|en|ang|īeġland}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*auwjuland}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*awjōlandą}} (from {{der|en|gem-pro|*awjō|t=island, waterland, meadow}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂ekʷeh₂}}) + {{m|gem-pro|*landą|t=land}}, equivalent to {{af|en|ey|id1=island|land}}.

snowman.raw: * {{af|en|snow|-man}}. * {{sense|score of eight; card ranked eight}} A typical snowman, built from two balls of snow, resembles a figure eight.

December.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:December<ety:bor<fro:decembre>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|December}}, {{m|enm|Decembre}}, from {{der|en|fro|decembre}}, from {{der|en|la|december|t=tenth month}}, from {{der|en|la|decem|t=ten}}; + {{der|en|la|-ber}}, from {{m|la|-bris}}, an adjectival suffix; December was the tenth month in the Roman calendar.

January.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:Januarie<ety:from<Janevere<ety:bor<xno:genever<ety:der<la:Iānuārius>>>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|Januarie}}, {{m|enm|januari}}, re-latinised forms of {{cog|enm|Janevere}}, {{m|enm|Ieneuer}}, from {{der|en|xno|genever}}, from {{der|en|la|Iānuārius||(month) of Janus}}, a compound of {{com|la|Iānus|-ārius||pos1="[[Janus]]"|pos2=adjectival suffix|nocat=1}}, with the first element perhaps from the [[Proto-Indo-European]] root {{m|ine-pro|*yeh₂-||to go}}. {{doublet|en|Gennaro}}.

June.raw: {{etymon|en|id=month|:inh|enm:June<id:month><ety:from<Juyn<ety:bor<fro:juin>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|June}}, {{m|enm|june}}, re-Latinised variants of earlier {{der|en|enm|Juyn}}, {{m|enm|juyng}}, from {{der|en|fro|juing}}, {{m|fro|juin}}, from {{der|en|la|iūnius}}, the month of the goddess {{m|la|Iuno||Juno}}, perhaps from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂yéwHō}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂óyu||vital force, youthful vigor}}.

October.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:<ety:bor<fro:octobre>>}} From {{inh|en|enm|-}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|octobre}}, from {{der|en|la|Octōber||eighth month}}, from {{der|en|la|octō||eight}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*oḱtṓw||twice four}}; + {{der|en|la|-ber}}, from {{m|la|-bris}}, an adjectival suffix; October was the eighth month in the Roman calendar.

September.raw: {{PIE word|en|septḿ̥}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:-<ety:inh<ang:-<ety:der<fro:septembre<ety:inh<la:September>>>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|-}}, from late {{der|en|ang|-}}, from {{der|en|fro|septembre}}, {{der|en|la|September||seventh month}}, from {{m|la|septem||seven}}, which see; September was the seventh month in the Roman calendar.

first.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*preh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|first}}, {{m|enm|furst}}, {{m|enm|ferst}}, {{m|enm|fyrst}}, from {{inh|en|ang|fyrest}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*furist}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*furistaz|t=first, foremost}}, superlative of {{der|en|gem-pro|*furai}}, {{m|gem-pro|*furi|t=before}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*preh₂-|t=before}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*per-|t=before; first}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|fore|est|nocat=1}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|first|t=first}}, {{cog|nl|voorste|t=foremost, first}}, {{m|nl|vorst|t=prince}}, {{cog|de|Fürst|t=chief, prince|lit=first (born)}}, {{cog|

second.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|id=follow}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:secunde<id:in array>|id=order|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|secunde}}, {{m|enm|second}}, {{m|enm|secound}}, {{m|enm|secund}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|second}}, {{m|fro|seond}}, from {{der|en|la|secundus||following, next in order}}, from root of {{m|la|sequor||to follow}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-||to follow}}. {{doublet|en|secund|secundo}}. Displaced native {{m|en|twoth}} and partially displaced native {{m|en|other}} (from {{noncog|ang|ōþer|t=other; next; second}}).

third.raw: {{PIE word|en|tréyes}} From {{inh|en|enm|thirde}}, {{m|enm|thridde}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þridda}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*þridjô}}, from Pre-Germanic {{m|ine-pro||*tretyós}}, a remodeling of {{inh|en|ine-pro|*tr̥tyós}}.

cogs: feeble, poor; indisposed; short; lame; good, pretty, snug
clean.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:clene|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|clene}}, from {{inh|en|ang|clāne}}, {{m|ang|clǣne|t=clean; pure; clear}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*klainī|t=dainty, fine, small; clean}}, perhaps from {{der|en|ine-pro|*glēy-|t=gleaming}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gel-|t=to gleam}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|gsw|chlei}}, {{m|gsw|chli}}, {{m|gsw|chlii}}, {{m|gsw|chly}}, {{m|gsw|klei|t=small}}, {{cog|bar|gloa}}, {{m|bar|kla}}, {{m|bar|klaa}}, {{m|bar|kloa}}, {{m|bar|kloan|t=small; young; insignificant}}, {{cog|gmw-cfr,nds|kleen|t=small}}, {{cog|cim|khlòan}}, {{m|cim|khlumma|t=small}},

nice.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*skey-}} From {{inh|en|enm|nyce}}, {{m|enm|nice}}, {{m|enm|nys}}, from {{der|en|fro|nice}}, {{m|fro|niche}}, {{m|fro|nisce||simple, foolish, ignorant}}, from {{der|en|la|nescius||ignorant, not knowing}}; compare {{m|la|nesciō||to know not, be ignorant of}}, from {{m|la|ne||not}} + {{m|la|sciō||to know}}.

chain: to call; shout; refer to as; name
call.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:callen|tree=+}} From {{inh|en|enm|callen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ċeallian|t=to call, shout}} and {{der|en|non|kalla|t=to call; shout; refer to as; name}}; both from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kalzōną|t=to call, shout}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*golH-so-|t=voice, cry}}, from {{m|ine-pro||*gel(H)-|to vocalize, call, shout}}.

cogs: a turn; bend; wind; back-flip; u-turn
chore.raw: From earlier {{m|en|char}}, from {{inh|en|enm|charr}}, {{m|enm|charre}}, {{m|enm|cherre||odd job, turn, occasion, business}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ċerr}}, {{m|ang|ċierr||a turn}}, from {{m|ang|ċierran||to turn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*karzijaną||to turn}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*gers-||to bend, turn}}.

when.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*kʷ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|when|when(ne)}}, {{m|enm|whan|whan(ne)}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hwonne}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hwannē}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hwan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hwan||at what time, when}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kʷís|pos=interrogative base}}.

cogs: because, since, on that account, therefore, then
why.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*kʷ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|why}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hwȳ|t=why}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hwī|t=by what, how}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kʷey}}, instrumental case of {{m|ine-pro|*kʷís|t=who}}, {{m|ine-pro|*kʷid|t=what}}.

which.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*kʷ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|which}}, {{m|enm|hwic}}, {{m|enm|wilche}}, {{m|enm|hwilch}}, {{m|enm|whilk}}, {{m|enm|hwilc}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hwelċ||which}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hwilīkaz||what kind|lit=like what}}, derived from {{m|gem-pro|*hwaz}}. <!--{{surf|+com|en|who|like|nocat=1}}.-->

whose.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*kʷ-}} From {{inherited|en|enm|whos}}, from {{inherited|en|ang|hwæs}}, from {{inherited|en|gem-pro|*hwes}}, genitive case of {{m|gem-pro|*hwaz|gloss=who}} {{m|gem-pro|*hwat|gloss=what}}.

advice.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:avys|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*weyd-}} From {{inh|en|enm|avys}}, from {{der|en|fro|avis}}, rebracketed from the phrase {{m|fro||ce m'est a vis|t=I think”, “it seems to me|lit=it is to my view}}, where {{m|fro|vis}} is from {{der|en|la|vīsus#Noun||vision, sight}}. The unhistoric -d- was introduced during the 15th century due to influence from [[advise]] and [[ad-]], see [[advance]]. {{doublet|en|aviso}}. See {{m|en|vision}}, and compare {{m|en|avise}}, {{m|en|advise}}.

dictate.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*deyḱ-}} {{ety|en|:bor|la:dictātum|id=an order, a command|tree=1}} {{etydate|1581}}; {{bor+|en|la|dictātum|t=a thing said, something dictated|nocap=1}}, [[substantivize]]d from the {{glossary|nominative}} {{glossary|neuter}} {{glossary|singular}} of {{m|la|dictātus}}, the {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|dictō||pronounce or declare repeatedly; dictate}}, {{glossary|frequentative}} of {{m|la|dīcō||say, speak}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=6675761461}}</ref><ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary|pos=n}}</ref> {{doublet|en|diktat}}.

predict.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*deyḱ-}} Early 17th century, from {{bor|en|la|praedicō||to mention beforehand}} (perfect passive participle {{m|la|praedictus}}), from {{m|la|prae-||before}} + {{m|la|dīcō||to say}}. Equivalent to Germanic {{m|en|forespeak}}, {{m|en|foretell}}, and {{m|en|foresay}}.

chain: to carry back, return, remit, refer
report.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*per- (fare)}} From {{inh|en|enm|reporten}}, from {{der|en|xno|reporter}}, from {{der|en|la|reporto|reportāre|to carry back, return, remit, refer}}, from {{af|la|re-|porto<alt:portāre>|nocat=1}}.

information.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:enformacioun|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|enformacioun}}, {{m|enm|informacioun}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|informacioun}}, {{m|en|enformation}}, {{der|en|fro|information}}, from {{der|en|la|īnfōrmātiō||formation, conception; education}}, from the participle stem of {{m|la|īnformāre||to inform}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|inform|ation}}.

cogs: to perform, execute, carry out, accomplish
perform.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|parformen}}, {{m|enm|performen||to perform}}, from {{der|en|xno|performer}}, {{m|fro|parfourmer}}, alteration of {{der|en|fro|parfornir}}, {{m|fro|parfurnir||to complete, accomplish, perform}}, from {{m|fro|par-}} + {{m|fro|fornir}}, {{m|fro|furnir||to accomplish, furnish}}, from {{der|en|frk|*frummjan||to accomplish, furnish}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*frumjaną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*framjaną||to further, promote}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*promo-||in front, forth}}, {{m|ine-pro|*per-||forward, out}}. Cognate with {{cog|goh|frummen||to do, execute, accomplish, provide}}, {{cog|osx|frum

respect.raw: {{ety|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:respect<ety:bor<fro:respect<ety:inh<la:respectus>>>>|tree=1}} {{ety|en|id=verb|:denominal|respect<id:noun>}} From {{inh|en|enm|respect}}, from {{der|en|fro|respect}}, also {{m|fro|respit||respect, regard, consideration}}, from {{der|en|la|respectus||a looking at, regard, respect}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|respiciō||look at, look back upon, respect}}, from {{m|la|re-||back}} + {{m|la|speciō||to see}}, equivalent to {{confix|en|re|spect}}. {{doublet|en|respite}}.

expect.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} From {{bor|en|la|expectāre}}, infinitive form of {{m|la|exspectō||look out for, await, expect}}, from {{m|la|ex||out}} + {{m|la|spectō||look at}}, {{glossary|frequentative}} of {{m|la|speciō||see}}.

express.raw: From {{bor|en|fr|exprès}}, from {{der|en|la|expressus}}, past participle of {{m|la|exprimere}} (see [[#Etymology 2|Etymology 2]], below).

instrument.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|instrument}}, from {{der|en|fro|instrument}}, from {{der|en|la|īnstrūmentum||an implement, tool}}, From {{suffix|la|īnstruō|t1=build, construct; arrange|mentum||nocat=1}}.

destroy.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*strew-}} From {{inh|en|enm|destroyen}}, from {{der|en|fro|destruire}}, {{der|en|la-vul|*destrugō}}, from Classical {{der|en|la|dēstruō}}, from {{m|la|dē-|t=un-, de-}} + {{m|la|struō|t=to build}}.

chain: to mark out, point out, describe, design, contrive
design.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:designen<ety:der<fro:designer<ety:der<la:designō>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|designen}}, from {{der|en|fro|designer}}, from {{der|en|la|designō||to mark out, point out, describe, design, contrive}}, from {{m|la|de-}} (or {{m|la|dis-}}) + {{m|la|signō||to mark}}, from {{m|la|signum||mark}}. {{doublet|en|designate}}.

host.raw: {{etymid|en|from strangers-and-hospitality-referent origins}} {{etymon|en|id=guest receiver|:inh|enm:hoste<id:host>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|hoste}}, from {{der|en|fro|oste}} (French: {{m|fr|hôte}}), from {{der|en|la|hospitem}}, accusative of {{m|la|hospes||a host, also a sojourner, visitor, guest; hence, a foreigner, a stranger}}, from {{m|itc-pro|*hostipotis}}, an old compound of {{m|la|hostis}} and the root of {{m|la|potis}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰóstipotis||master of guests}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*gʰóstis||stranger, guest, enemy}} and {{m|ine-pro|*pótis||owner, master, host, husband}}. U

reply.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*pleḱ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|replyen}}, {{m|enm|replien}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|replier||to reply}}, from the {{der|en|la|replico|replicō, replicāre|t=to fold back}} (in Late or Medieval Latin "to reply, repeat"), from {{m|la|re}} + {{m|la|plicō||to fold}}; the noun derives from the verb by [[nominalisation]]. Doublet of {{m|en|replicate}} and {{m|en|replica}}.

appear.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*peh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|apperen}}, {{m|enm|aperen}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|aparoir}} ({{cog|fr|apparoir}}), from {{der|en|la|appāreō||to appear}}, from {{m|la|ad||to}} + {{m|la|pāreō||to come forth, to become visible}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*peh₂s-|*peh₂-s-|watch, see}}, s-present of {{m|ine-pro|*peh₂-||protect}}.

discover.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:discoveren<ety:bor<fro:descovrir>>}} From {{inh|en|enm|discoveren}}, from {{der|en|fro|descovrir}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|discoperīre}} < {{m|la|discooperiō|discooperiō, discooperīre}}, from {{der|en|la|dis-}} + {{m|la|cooperiō}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|onfindan}}.

possible.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁es-}} From {{inh|en|enm|possible}}, from {{der|en|fro|possible}}, from {{der|en|la|possibilis||possible}}, from {{m|la|possum|posse, possum|to be able}}; see [[power]]. Displaced {{ncog|enm|acumendlic|t=possible}}, from {{ncog|ang|ācumendlīċ|t=possible}}. Compare also {{ncog|ang|mihtelīċ|t=strong, capable, powerful, possible}}, which was cognate with {{ncog|goh|mahtlīh|t=possible}} and {{ncog|non|máttulígr|t=mighty, possible}}. Compare also {{ncog|nl|mogelijk||possible}} and {{ncog|de|möglich||possible}}.

international.raw: {{ety|en|:af|inter-|national|tree=1}} From {{af|en|inter-|national}}. Introduced in modern English by {{w|Jeremy Bentham}} in his ''[[s:An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation|An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation]]'', 1780.

collection.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*leǵ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|colleccioun}}, {{m|enm|collection}}, from {{der|en|fro|collection}}, from {{der|en|la|collēctiō|collēctiō, collēctiōnem}}, from {{m|la|collēctus}}, from {{m|la|colligō||collect together}}, composed of {{prefix|la|con|legō|gloss2=bring together, gather, collect|nocat=1}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*leǵ-||to gather, collect}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|collect|ion}}.

invent.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷem-}} From {{inh|en|enm|inventen}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|inventer}}, from {{der|en|la|inventus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|inveniō||come upon, meet with, find, discover}}, from {{m|la|in||in, on}} + {{m|la|veniō||come}}; see [[venture]]. Compare [[advent]], [[covent]], [[event]], [[prevent]], etc.

invention.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|invencion}}, {{m|enm|invencioun}}, from {{der|en|la|inventiō}} either directly or via {{der|en|frm|invencion}}, from {{der|en|la|inveniō|invenīre|to [[discover]], [[find]], [[invent]]}}, from {{m|la|in-||[[in-]]: [[in]], [[into]]}} + {{m|la|veniō|venīre|to [[come]]}}. {{doublet|en|inventio}}. {{surf|en|invent|-ion}}.

celebrate.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|celebraten}}, from {{af|enm|celebrat|-en|t1=celebrated|pos1=also used as the past participle of {{m|enm||celebraten}}|alt1=celebrat(e)|id2=infinitival|nocat=1}}, {{bor+|enm|la|celebrātus|nocap=1|nocat=1}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|celebrō|t=frequent, go to in great numbers, celebrate, honor, praise}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|celeber|t=frequented, populous}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|fæġnian}} and ''{{l|ang|frēolsian}}''.

daily.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|dayly}}, from {{inh|en|ang|dæġlīċ}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*dagalīk}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*dagalīkaz|t=daily}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|day|ly|id2=adjectival}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|dayly}}, {{m|sco|daly|t=daily}}, {{cog|nds-de|dagelk}}, {{m|nds-de|dagelik|t=daily}}, {{cog|nl|dagelijks|t=daily}}, {{cog|de|täglich|t=daily}}, {{cog|da|daglig|t=daily}}, {{cog|sv|daglig|t=daily}}, {{cog|is|daglegur|t=daily}}.

trust.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|trust|trust, trost|t=trust, protection}}. Long considered a borrowing from {{cog|non|traust|t=confidence, help, protection}}, from {{cog|gem-pro|*traustą}}, but the root vocalism is incompatible, so ''trust'' has come to be considered a reflex of an unattested {{inh|en|ang|*trust}}, from a rare zero-grade Proto-Germanic variant of the same root also attested in {{cog|gmh|getrüste|t=host}}.<ref>{{cite-journal|title=Getting a word in: Contact, etymology and English vocabulary in the twelfth century|author=Richard Dance|year=2014|journal=Journal of the British Academy|volume=2|u

flight.raw: {{etymon|en|id=flying|:inh|enm:flight<id:flying>|tree=1}} [[Image:MiG-17F Top View.JPG|thumb|right|A [[wikipedia:Mikoyan MiG-17|Mikoyan MiG-17F]] [[jet]] in '''flight''']] [[File:Short flight of stairs.jpg|thumb|A '''flight''' of stairs.]] From {{inh|en|enm|flight}}, from {{inh|en|ang|flyht||flight}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*fluhti||flight}}, derived from {{m|gem-pro|*fleuganą||to fly}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*plewk-||to fly}}, enlargement of {{m|ine-pro|*plew-||flow}}. Analyzable as {{suffix|en|fly|t|id2=th}} (variant of {{m|en|-th}}).

sight.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:sighte|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|sighte}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sihþ|t=something seen; vision}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sihti|t=seeing, sight}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|see|t|id2=th}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|cim|gazicht|t=sight, vision; pupil}}, {{cog|nl|gezicht|t=face; sight, vision}}, {{m|nl|zicht|t=sight, vision}}, {{cog|de|Gesicht|t=face; sight, vision}}, {{m|de|Sicht|t=view; sight; visibility}}, {{cog|lb|Gesiicht|t=face}}, {{m|lb|Siicht|t=view; sight}}, {{cog|yi|געזיכט|t=face}}, {{cog|da|sigt|t=sight; visibility}}, {{cog|nb,nn|sikt|t=visibility}}, {{cog|sv|

speaker.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:spekere<alt:spekere, speker>|tree=+}} From {{inh|en|enm|speker}}, {{m|enm|spekere}}, an alteration (with change of suffix) of {{der|en|ang|speca}}, {{m|ang|spreca|t=speaker}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*sprekô|t=speaker}}, equivalent to {{affix|en|speak|-er|id2=agent noun}}. Compare {{cog|stq|Spreeker|t=speaker}}, {{cog|fy|sprekker|t=speaker}}, {{cog|nl|spreker|t=speaker}}, {{cog|nds-de|Spreker|t=speaker}}, {{cog|de|Sprecher|t=speaker}}.

speech.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:speche<ety:inh<ang:spǣċ<ety:from<ang:sprǣċ>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|speche}}, from {{inh|en|ang|spǣċ}}, {{m|ang|sprǣċ||speech, discourse, language}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sprāku||speech, language}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*spereg-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*spreg-||to make a sound}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|spraak||speech}}, {{cog|de|Sprache||language, speech}}. More at {{l|en|speak}}.

knowledge.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:knoweleche|tree=1|id=information}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵneh₃-|*leyg-|id2=jump}} From {{inh|en|enm|knoweleche}}, {{m|enm|knowleche|t=knowledge}}, from late {{inh|en|ang|cnāwelǣċ|t=acknowledgement}}, from {{m|ang|cnāwan|t=to know}} + {{m|ang||-lǣċ(e)}}, variant of {{m|ang|-lāc|t=-ation}} modified after the related verbal suffix {{m|ang|-lǣċan}}. Related to {{cog|enm|knowelechen|t=to find out, acknowledge}}, {{cog|ang|cnāwelǣċing|t=acknowledging, acknowledgement}}.

thought.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:thought|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*teng-|id=think}} From {{inh|en|enm|thought}}, {{m|enm|ithoȝt}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þōht}}, {{m|ang|ġeþōht}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*þą̄ht}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*þanhtaz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*gaþanhtą||thought}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*teng-||to think}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|thocht||thought}}, {{cog|stq|Toacht||thought}}, {{cog|fy|oandacht|dacht|attention, regard, thought}}, {{cog|nl|gedachte||thought}}, {{cog|de|Andacht|Andacht|reverence, devotion, prayer}}, {{cog|is|þóttur||thought}}. Related to [[thank]], [[think]].

traveller.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|traveler}}, {{m|enm|travelour}}, {{m|enm|travailere}}, {{m|enm|travailour|t=worker", also "traveller}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|travel|er|id2=agent noun}}. Compare {{cog|xno|travailur}}, {{m|fro|travailour}}, {{cog|fro|travailleor}}, {{m|fro|travelleeur}}, {{m|fro|travelier}}.

alive.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:alyve}} From {{inh|en|enm|alyve}}, {{m|enm|alive}}, {{m|enm|alife}}, {{m|enm|olive}}, {{m|enm|olife}}, {{m|enm|on live}}, {{m|enm|on life}}, from {{inh|en|ang|on līfe|t=alive|lit=in life" or "in (the) body}}, from {{m|ang|on|t=on, in}} + {{m|ang|līfe}}, dative singular of {{m|ang|līf|t=life}}. In this sense, replaced {{noncog|ang|cwic}} (whence {{noncog|en|quick}}). Equivalent to {{af|en|a-|life}}. Compare {{cog|nl|in leven|t=alive|lit=in life}}, {{cog|de|am Leben|t=alive|lit=at life" or "at living}}.

natural.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵenh₁-}} {{inh+|en|enm|natural}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|natural}}, {{m|fro|naturel}}, from {{der|en|la|nātūrālis}}, from {{m|la|nātus}}, the perfect participle of {{m|la|nāscor|t=be born|pos=verb}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|ġecynde}}. {{surf|+suf|en|nature|al|alt1=natur(e)}}.

exact.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eǵ-|id=drive}} From {{der|en|la|exāctus}} (the verb via {{inh|en|enm|exact}}), perfect passive participle of {{m|la|exigō||demand, claim as due; measure by a standard, weigh, test}}, from {{m|la|ex||out}} + {{m|la|agō||drive}}.

geography.raw: {{etymon|en|:uder|frm:géographie<ety:uder<la:geōgraphia>>|tree=1}} From {{uder|en|frm|géographie}}, from {{uder|en|la|geōgraphia}}, from {{uder|en|grc|γεωγραφία||a [[description]] of the [[earth]]}}, from {{m|grc|γῆ||[[earth]]}} + {{m|grc|γράφω||[[write]]}}. {{doublet|en|geographia}}.

transport.raw: {{ety|en|tree=1|:inh|enm:transporten<ety:bor<fro:transporter>>|:af<surf>|trans-<id:across, beyond>|port<id:carry>}} {{inh+|en|enm|transporten}}, a borrowing from {{der|en|fro|transporter|t=carry or convey across}}, from {{der|en|la|trānsportō|trānsportāre|to carry over, take across, carry, convey, remove, transport}}, from {{af|la|trāns-<id:beyond><t:across, over, to the farther side of>|portō<id:carry><t:to bear, carry, convey, take>|nocat=1}}. {{surf|en|trans-<id:across, beyond><t:beyond, across, through>|port<id:carry><t:to carry, bear, or convey; to bring>}}.

import.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|importen}}, from {{der|en|fro|emporter}}, {{m|fro|importer}}, from {{der|en|la|importō|t=bring in from abroad, import|pos=verb}}, from {{m|la|in||in, at, on; into}} + {{m|la|portō||to carry, bear; convey}}.

transform.raw: {{etymon|en|id=change appearance|:inh|enm:transformen|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|transformen}}, from {{der|en|fro|transformer}}, from {{der|en|la|transformo|transformo, transformare}}, from {{m|la|trans||across|pos=preposition}} + {{m|la|forma||form}}.

signal.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*sek-}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|id=follow}} From {{der|en|fro|segnal}}, {{m|fro|seignal}} or {{der|en|la-med|signāle}}; noun use of the neuter of {{der|en|la-lat|signālis}}, from {{der|en|la|signum}}; verb use from 1805, as a shortened from ''[[signalize]]'' (1650s). {{doublet|en|signum|sign}}.

motor.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:motour<ety:der<la:mōtor>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|motour|t=[[controller]], [[prime mover]]; [[God]]}}, from {{der|en|la|mōtor|t=[[mover]]; that which [[move]]s something}}, from {{m|la|mōtō||to set in motion}}.

chain: a field, a plain, a place of action
champion.raw: {{etymon|en|id=winner|:inh|enm:champioun<id:combatant>|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*kh₂em-}} From {{inh|en|enm|champioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|champion}}, from {{der|en|la-med|campio|t=combatant in a duel, champion}}, from {{der|en|frk|*kampijō|t=fighter}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*kampijō|t=combat soldier}}, a derivative of {{m|gmw-pro|*kampijan|t=to battle, to campaign}}, itself a derivative of {{m|gmw-pro|*kamp|t=battlefield, battle}}, ultimately a borrowing in West-Germanic from {{der|en|la|campus|t=a field, a plain, a place of action}}.

sunburn.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|*sunne burnen}}, {{m|enm|*sonne brennen}}, {{m|enm|*sunne brennen}} (suggested by derivatives {{m|enm|sonne brennynge}}, {{m|enm|sunne brennynge|t=sunburn|lit=sun-burning}} and {{m|enm|sunne brente|t=sunburnt}}, equivalent to {{compound|en|sun|burn}}. Compare {{cog|fy|sinnebrân|t=sunburn}}, {{cog|nl|zonnebrand|t=sunburn}}, {{cog|de|Sonnenbrand|t=sunburn}}, {{cog|sv|solbränna|t=sunburn}}, and {{cog|is|sólbruni|t=sunburn}}, as well as {{ncog|ang|sunbryne||sunburn}}.

climber.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|clymbere}}, {{m|enm|clymber|t=one who climbs, climber}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=clī̆mber|pos=n|id=MED8035}}</ref> from {{m|enm|climben|t=to climb; to ascend, fly upward, rise; to slope upwards; to approach God in prayer; to advance; to overcome, triumph; to aspire; to be presumptuous}}<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=clī̆mben|pos=v|id=MED8034}}</ref> + {{m|enm|-er}}, {{m|enm|-ere|pos={{glossary|suffix}} forming {{glossary|agent noun}}s}}.<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=-ē̆r(e|pos=''suf.''(1)|noformat=1|id=MED14294}}</ref> The English word is analysable as {{af|en|climb|pos1=verb|-er|pos

foreigner.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:foreyner|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|forner}}, {{m|enm|foreyner}}, {{m|enm|foroner}}, {{m|enm|forenere}}, augmentation of earlier {{m|enm|forein|t=foreigner}}, from the adjective. Equivalent to {{af|en|foreign|-er|id2=occupation}}. Use of the ''-er'' suffix may be due to analogy with {{m+|enm|straunger|t=stranger}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|elþēodiġ}}.

foreign.raw: {{ety|en|tree=1|:inh|enm:foreyn|:influence<unc>|reign}} From {{inh|en|enm|foreyn,forein}}, from {{der|en|fro|forain}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*forānus||outsider, [[outlander]]}}, from {{der|en|la|forās||outside, outdoors}} or {{m|la|forīs||outside, outdoors}}.

leader.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:ledere|tree=1|text=++}} {{surf|en|lead|-er}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|leader|t=leader}}, {{cog|fy|lieder|t=leader}}, {{cog|nl|leider|t=leader}}, {{cog|de|Leiter|t=leader, conductor, manager}}, {{cog|da|leder|t=leader, manager}}, {{cog|sv|ledare|t=leader, conductor, director}}, {{cog|is|leiðari|t=leader, conductor}}.

lead.raw: {{etymon|en|id=metal|:inh|enm:led}} From {{inh|en|enm|led}}, {{m|enm|leed}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lēad|t=lead}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*laud|t=lead}}, possibly borrowed from {{der|en|cel-pro|*ɸloudom}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*plewd-|t=to flow}}.

rocky.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|rokki}}, {{m|enm|rokky|t=rocky}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=rokkī|pos=adj|id=MED37796}}</ref> from {{m|enm|rok}}, {{m|enm|rokke|t=rock; a rock or stone; large rock by a coast or in the sea; rocky outcrop on a mountain, cliff; castle, citadel, stronghold}}{{nb...|roc, rock, rocke, roke|otherforms=1}}<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=rok(ke|pos=''n.''(1)|noformat=1|id=MED37789}}</ref> + {{m|enm|-i|pos={{glossary|suffix}} forming {{glossary|adjective}}s}}.<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=-ī̆|pos=suf|id=MED21577}}</ref> {{m|enm||Rok}}, {{m|enm||rokke}} are derived from:

woolen.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂welh₁-|id=wool}} From {{inh|en|enm|wollen}}, {{m|enm|wullen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wyllen}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wullīnaz|t=woollen}}, equivalent to {{af|en|wool|-en|id2=made of}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|wollin}}, {{m|sco|wolne}}, {{m|sco|wowne|t=woollen}}, {{cog|nl|wollen|t=woollen}}, {{cog|de|wollen|t=woollen}}, {{cog|da|uldne|t=woollen}}, {{cog|nb|ullen||fuzzy; woolen}}.

truly.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|truely}}, {{m|enm|treuly}}, {{m|enm|treuli}}, {{m|enm|trewely}}, {{m|enm|treoweliche}}, {{m|enm|treowliche}}, from {{inh|en|ang|trēowlīċe|t=faithfully; truly}}, equivalent to {{af|en|true|-ly|id2=adverbial}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|trouwelijk}}, {{cog|gml|truwlike}}, {{cog|de|treulich}}, {{cog|sv|trolig}}, {{cog|is|trygglega}}.

peaceful.raw: {{wikidata lexeme|L40770}} From {{inh|en|enm|peesful}}, {{m|enm|pesful}}, {{m|enm|paisful}}, {{m|enm|pesefull}}. {{surf|en|peace|-ful|pos=adjective}}. Displaced native Old English [[friþsum]].

peace.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:pees|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|pees}}, {{m|enm|pes}}, {{m|enm|pais}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|peis}} and {{der|en|fro|pais||peace}}, from {{der|en|la|pāx||peace}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*peh₂ḱ-||to fasten, stick, place}}, related to {{cog|la|pacīscor||agree, stipulate}}, {{cog|la|pangō||fasten, fix}}; see {{l|en|pact}}. {{doublet|en|pax}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|sibb}}, ''{{l|ang|frēols}}'', and broadly ousted {{m|ang|friþ}} (modern {{m|en|frith}}).

weakness.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|weyknesse}}, replacing earlier {{cog|enm|wocnesse}}, {{m|enm|wakenes}}, {{m|enm|wacnesse|t=weakness}}, from {{cog|ang|wācnes|t=weakness}}. Equivalent to {{af|en|weak|-ness}}.

competition.raw: Borrowed from {{bor|en|fr|compétition}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|competitio|competītiō, competītiōnem}}, from {{der|en|la|competō}}, from {{m|la|con-}} + {{m|la|petō}}. {{surf|en|compete|-ition}}.

invitation.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|invitacioun}}, {{m|enm|ynvytacioun}}, from {{der|en|la|invītātio}}, reinforced by {{cog|frm|invitation}}. {{surf|en|invite|-ation}}. Displaced native {{ncog|enm|lathinge}} from {{ncog|ang|laþung}} (see dialectal {{ncog|en|lathing}}).

education.raw: {{etymon|en|id=teaching|:der|la:ēducātiō<id:education>}}{{root|en|ine-pro|*dewk-}} {{bor+|en|frm|éducation}}, from {{der|en|la|ēducātiō||a breeding, bringing up, rearing}}, from {{m|la|ēducō||to educate, train}}, from {{m|la|ēdūcō||to lead forth, to take out; to raise up, to erect}}. See {{l|en|educate}}.

pollution.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|pollucioun}}, {{m|enm|pollucion|t=desecration, impurity}}, from {{der|en|xno|pollutiun}}, {{der|en|frm|pollution}}, {{m|frm|pollucion}}, and their source, post-classical {{der|en|la|pollūtiō||defilement, desecration; nocturnal emission}} (4th century), from the participial stem of {{m|la|polluō||to soil, defile, contaminate}}, from {{m|la|por-||before}} + {{m|la|-luō|t=to smear}}, related to {{m|la|lutum||mud}} and {{m|la|luēs||filth}}. Compare {{cog|grc|λῦμα|t=filth, dirt, disgrace}} and {{m|grc|λῦμαξ|t=rubbish, refuse}}, {{cog|sga|loth|t=mud, dirt}}, {{cog|lt|lutynas|t=pool

protection.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:-<ety:bor<fro:-<ety:der<la-lat:prōtēctiō>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|-}}, from {{der|en|fro|-}}, from stem of {{der|en|la-lat|prōtectiō|t=a covering over}}, from {{der|en|la|prōtēctus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|protego|prōtegere|to protect, cover in front}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|ġesċildnes}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|protect|ion}}.

movement.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:mevement<ety:bor<fro:movement>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|mevement}}, from {{der|en|fro|movement}} (modern {{cog|fr|mouvement}}), from {{m|fro|movoir}} + {{m|fro|-ment}}; cf. also {{der|en|la-med|movimentum}}, from {{der|en|la|movere||move}}. {{doublet|en|moment|momentum}}. In this sense, displaced native {{ncog|ang|styring}}, which led to {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|stirring}}.

disagree.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|disagre|t=to refuse to assent to}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=disagrẹ̄ |pos=v|id=MED11756}}</ref> from {{der|en|xno|disagreer}}, {{m|fro|disagrer}}, {{m|fro|desagreer|t=to refuse assent}}, from {{der|en|fro|desagreer}}, {{m|fro|desagrëer|t=to be disagreeable; to be unpleasant}} (modern {{cog|fr|désagréer|t=to displease}});<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=v|id=53455|date=September 2017|nodot=yes}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=v}}</ref> the English word is analysable as {{af|en|dis-|agree}}.

overnight.raw: Inherited from {{inh|en|enm|overnyght}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ofer niht|t=through the night, overnight}}, equivalent to {{af|en|over|night}}. Verbal use (late 19th c.) may have been influenced by {{cal|en|de|übernachten|notext=1}} (16th c.), though it could also have developed independently. Compare also {{cog|nl|overnachten|t=to overnight}}, {{cog|gml|ȫvernachten|t=to overnight}}, {{cog|fy|oernachtsje|t=to overnight}}, {{cog|stq|uurnoachtje|t=to overnight}}.

weight.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*weǵʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|weight}}, {{m|enm|weiȝte}}, {{m|enm|weght}}, {{m|enm|wight}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wiht}}, {{m|ang|ġewiht||weight}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wihtiz}} {{gloss|"weight"; compare {{m|gem-pro|*weganą||to move}}}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*weǵʰ-||to move; pull; draw; drive}}. Equivalent to {{suffix|en|weigh|t|id2=th|pos2=abstract nominal suffix}}.

height.raw: {{etymon|en|id=stature|:inh|enm:heighte<ety:inh<ang:hīehþu<id:height>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|heighte}}, {{m|enm|heiȝþe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hēahþu}}, {{m|ang|hēhþo}}, {{m|ang|hīehþu|t=height}}, {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hauhiþu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hauhiþō}} (compare {{m|gem-pro|*hauhaz}}). Equivalent to {{af|en|high|-t|id2=th|pos2=abstract nominal suffix}}. The regular pronunciation is now obsolete {{IPAchar|/heɪt/}} (as with other words in {{m|en||-eight}}); the modern form developed early on, at first as a variant, by analogy with the underlying adjective.

length.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|lengthe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lengþ}}, {{m|ang|lengþu}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*langiþu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*langiþō}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|long|th|id2=abstract nominal|pos2=abstract nominal suffix}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|lenth}}, {{m|sco|lainth||length}}, {{cog|stq|Loangte||length}}, {{cog|fy|lingte}}, {{m|fy|langte||length}}, {{cog|nl|lengte||length}}, {{cog|nds-de|Längde}}, {{m|nds-de|Längd}}, {{m|nds-de|Längte}}, {{m|nds-de|Längt||length}}, {{cog|da|længde||length}}, {{cog|sv|längd||length}}, {{cog|is|lengd||length}}.

strength.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*strengʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|strengthe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|strengþu||strength}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*strangiþu||[[strongness]]; strength}}, equivalent to {{af|en|strong|-th|id2=abstract nominal|pos2=abstract nominal suffix}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|strengte||strength}}, {{cog|nds-de|Strengde}}, {{m|nds-de|Strengte||[[harshness]]; [[rigidity]]; [[strictness]]; [[severity]]}}.

warmth.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|warmth}}, {{m|enm|warmeth}}, {{m|enm|wermþe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*wiermþu|t=warmth}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*warmiþu|t=warmness; warmth}}, corresponding to {{suffix|en|warm|th|id2=abstract nominal|pos2=abstract nominal suffix}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Waarmte|t=warmth}}, {{cog|fy|waarmte|t=warmth}}, {{cog|nl|warmte|t=warmth}}, {{cog|nds-de|Warmte}}, {{m|nds-de|Warmt|t=warmth}}.

truth.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:treuthe|tree=1|text=++}} Equivalent to {{affix|en|true|-th|id2=abstract nominal}}. {{doublet|en|troth}}. Cognate with {{cog|no|trygd||trustworthiness, security, insurance}}, {{cog|is|tryggð||loyalty, fidelity}}.

growth.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰreh₁-}} From {{suffix|en|grow|th|id2=abstract nominal|pos2=abstract nominal suffix}}. Compare {{cog|ofs|grēd}} {{gloss|"meadow, pasture"; > {{cog|frr|greyde|t=growth, pasture}}}}, {{cog|gmh|gruote}}, {{m|gmh|gruot|t=greens, fresh growth, shoot}}, {{cog|non|gróðr}} {{gloss|"growth, crop"; > {{cog|fo|grøði}}, {{cog|da|grøde|t=fruits}}, {{cog|sv|gröda|t=crop, harvest}}}}. More at {{l|en|grow}}.

width.raw: {{PIE word|en|dwóh₁}} From {{suf|en|wide|th|id2=abstract nominal|pos2=abstract nominal suffix}}, possibly by analogy with {{cog|non|vídd|t=width}}, though this is unlikely, as the word is not attested before the end of the 16th century and was historically unknown in Scots and the traditional dialect of Northern England, where one would expect Old Norse influence to be the strongest (these varieties traditionally employed {{m|en|wideness}} instead). Replaced {{cog|enm|wide}}, {{m|enm|wyde|t=width}}.

metro.raw: {{etymon|en|id=subway|:bor|fr:métro<id:metro>}} From {{bor|en|fr|métro}}, clipping of {{m|fr|métropolitain}} (from {{der|en|grc|μήτηρ||mother}} + {{m|grc|πόλις||city}}), as in the ''Chemin de fer métropolitain'', an early name for the Paris Métro. This name was a direct translation of "Metropolitan Railway", which was the original name of the earliest part of the [[London Underground]], constructed in 1863.

spider.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)penh₁-}} {{inh+|en|enm|spithre}}, {{m|enm|spider}}, from {{inh|en|ang|spīþra|t=spider}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*spinþrijō}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*spinnaną||to spin}}. Mostly displaced {{l|en|attercop|t=spider, unpleasant person}}, now a dialectal term.

eagle.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|egle}}, from {{der|en|xno|egle}}, from {{der|en|fro|aigle}}, from {{der|en|la|aquila}}. Displaced native {{cog|enm|earn|ern, earn, arn}}, from {{cog|ang|earn|t=eagle}}. More at {{m|en|erne}}.

Compare {{cog|fr|pierrot}} and {{cog|oc|parrat}}. A number of origins have been suggested for {{m|fr|perroquet}}, such as Spanish {{m|es|periquito}} and Italian {{m|it|parrocchetto}}. The relationship between these various words is disputed. Replaced earlier {{m|en|popinjay}}.

Compare {{cog|fy|hoarn}}, {{cog|nl|hoorn}}, {{cog|nds|Hoorn}}, {{m|nds|horn}}, {{cog|de|Horn}}, {{cog|da|-}} and {{cog|sv|horn}}, {{cog|got|𐌷𐌰𐌿𐍂𐌽}}.

cage.raw: From {{der|en|enm|cage}}, from {{der|en|fro|cage}}, from {{der|en|la|cavea}}. {{doublet|en|cadge|cavea}} and related to {{m|en|jail}}.

woolly hair; thin hair; soft nap or pile on cloth; quills hedgehog; leafage
hair on top of head; nap, pile
the circles of white hair between the brows of the Buddha or other deity
the circles of white hair between the brows of the Buddha or other deity

bamboo.raw: {{etymon|en|id=plant|:bor|nl:bamboe<id:bamboo>|tree=1}} {{bor+|en|nl|bamboe}}, from {{der|en|pt|bambu}}, from {{der|en|ms|bambu}}, from {{der|en|kn|ಬಂಬು}}, variant form of {{m|kn|ಬೇವು}}. Cognate with {{cog|ml|വേപ്പ്}}, {{cog|ta|வேம்பு}}, {{cog|te|వేప}}, from {{cog|dra-pro|*wēmpu||[[neem]]}}.

theatre.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:theater<alt:theater, theatre>|tree=+}} From {{inh|en|enm|theater}}, {{m|enm|theatre}}, from {{der|en|fro|theatre}}, from {{der|en|la|theatrum}}, from {{der|en|grc|θέατρον||a place for viewing}}, from {{m|grc|θεάομαι||to see, watch, observe}}. <!--===Pronunciation=== ** {{audio|en|en-mi-theater.ogg|Audio (MI)}} what does MI mean? Michigan? This audio sounds strange and we already have an American audio sample. * {{hyphenation|en|thea|tre||the|a|tre}}-->

market.raw: {{dercat|en|ett}} From {{inh|en|enm|market}}, from late {{inh|en|ang|market||market}} and {{der|en|xno|markiet}} ({{der|en|fro|marchié}}); all ultimately from {{der|en|la|mercātus||trade, market}}, from {{m|la|mercor||to trade, deal in, buy}}, itself derived from {{m|la|merx||wares, merchandise}}. {{doublet|en|mart}}. Cognate with {{cog|fy|merk||market}}, {{cog|nl|markt}}, {{cog|de|Markt}}, {{cog|da|-}} and {{cog|no|marked||market}}, {{cog|fo|-}} and {{cog|is|markaður||market}}, {{cog|sv|marknad||market}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|stapol}}.

restaurant.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|fr:restaurant|tree=1}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|fr|restaurant}}, present participle of the verb {{m|fr|restaurer}}, corresponding to {{der|en|la|restaurans|restaurans, restaurantis}}, present participle of {{m|la|restauro||to restore}}, from the name of the 'restorative' soup served in the first establishments.

company.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*peh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|companye||a team; companionship}}, from {{der|en|fro|compaignie||companionship}} (Modern French: {{m|fr|compagnie}}), possibly from {{der|en|la-lat||*compania}}, but this word is not attested. {{cog|fro|compaignie}} is equivalent to {{cog|fro|compaignon}} (Modern French: {{m|fr|compagnon}}) + {{m|fro|-ie}}. More at {{m|en|companion}}.

square.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|square}}, {{m|enm|sqware}}, {{m|enm|squyre}}; from {{der|en|fro|esquarre}}, {{m|fro|esquerre}}, (modern {{cog|fr|équerre}}), from {{der|en|la-vul|*exquadra}}, from {{der|en|la|-}} {{prefix|la|ex|quadro|nocat=1}}, from {{m|la|quadrus}} (compare {{m+|en|quad}} and {{m|en|quadra}}). {{dbt|en|squad|squadra}}.

corner.raw: {{ety|en|id=angle|:inh|enm:corner}} From {{inh|en|enm|corner}}, from {{der|en|xno|cornere}} (compare {{cog|fro|cornier}}, {{m|fro|corniere|t=corner}}), from {{der|en|fro|corne|t=corner, angle|lit=a horn, projecting point}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*corna|t=horn}}, from {{der|en|la|cornua}}, plural of {{m|la|cornū|t=projecting point, end, horn}}. The sense of "angle, corner" in Old French is not found in Latin or other Romance languages. It was possibly calqued from {{cog|frk|*hurnijā|t=corner, angle}}, which is similar to, and derived from {{m|frk|*hurn}}, the Frankish word for "horn".

gate.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:gate<id:entryway>|id=doorway}} From {{inh|en|enm|gate}} (the forms {{m|enm|ȝate}} and {{m|enm|ȝeat}} yielded the dialectal doublet {{m|en|yate}}), from the plural of {{inh|en|ang|ġeat}} (specifically {{m|ang|gatu}}), from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*gat}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*gatą||hole, opening}}.

entrance.raw: From {{uder|en|frm|entrance||entry}}. Replaced native {{cog|enm|ingang||entrance, admission}}, from {{cog|ang|ingang||ingress, entry, entrance}}.

chain: departure, going out; way by which one may go out, egress; (''figuratively'') conclusion, termination; (''figuratively'') death; income, revenue
exit.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:exit<ety:der<la:exitus>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|exit}}, from {{der|en|la|exitus|t=departure, going out; way by which one may go out, egress; (''figuratively'') conclusion, termination; (''figuratively'') death; income, revenue}}, from {{m|la|exeō|t=to depart, exit; to avoid, evade; (''figuratively'') to escape; of time: to expire, run out}} + {{m|la|-tus|pos=suffix forming action nouns from verbs}}.<ref name="OED">Compare {{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=40268483|date=December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{R:Lexico|pos=n}}</ref> ''Exeō'' is derived from {{m|la|ex-|pos=prefix meaning ‘out,

lift.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|liften}}, {{m|enm|lyften}}, from {{der|en|non|lypta||to lift, air|lit=to raise in the air}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*luftijaną||to raise in the air}}, related to {{m|gem-pro|*luftuz||roof, air}}, perhaps from {{der|en|ine-pro|*lewp-||to peel, break off, damage}} or from a root meaning roof (see {{m|gem-pro|*luftuz}}). Cognate with {{cog|da|-}} and {{cog|nb|løfte||to lift}}, {{cog|nn|-}} and {{cog|sv|lyfta||to lift}}, {{cog|de|lüften||to air, lift}}, {{cog|ang|lyft||air}}. See above. 1851 for the noun sense "a mechanical device for vertical transport".

toilet.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*tek-|id=weave}} {{etymon|en|id=bathroom|:bor|frm:toilette<id:?>}} From {{der|en|frm|toilette}}, diminutive of {{m|fr|toile||cloth}}, from their use to protect clothing while shaving or arranging hair. From its use as a private room, ''toilet'' came to refer euphemistically to [[lavatories]] and then to its fixtures, beginning in the United States in the late 19th century.

place.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*pleth₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|place}}, conflation of {{inh|en|ang|plæċe|t=place, an open space, street}} and {{der|en|fro|place|t=place, an open space}}, both from {{der|en|la|platēa|t=plaza, wide street}}, from {{der|en|grc|πλατεῖα}}, shortening of {{m|grc|[[πλατεῖα]] [[ὁδός]]|t=broad way}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*pleth₂-|t=to spread}}, extended form of {{m|ine-pro|*pleh₂-|t=flat}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|stōw}}, {{m|ang|stede}} (partially), and {{m|ang|-ern}}. Compare also {{noncog|en|pleck|t=plot of ground}}, {{noncog|fy|plak|t=place, spot, location}}, {{noncog|nl|pl

tower.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|tour}}, {{m|enm|tur}}, {{m|enm|tor}}, from {{inh|en|ang|tūr}}, {{m|ang|tor}}, {{m|ang|torr}} {{gloss|"tower; rock"; > English {{l|en|tor}}}} and {{der|en|fro|tour}}, {{m|fro|toer}}, {{m|fro|tor}}; both from {{der|en|la|turris||a tower}}, {{der|en|grc|τύρρις}} {{q|Hesychius}}, {{m|grc|τύρσις}}. Displaced native [[Middle English]] {{l|enm|stepel}} for the general sense of "tower".

palace.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|paleys}}, from {{der|en|fro|palais}}, which comes from {{der|en|la|palātium}}, from {{m|la|Palātium}}, in reference to the [[Palatine]] ({{w|Palatine Hill}}), one of the seven hills of Rome, where the aristocracy of the Roman [[republic|Republic]]—and later, Roman emperors—built large, splendid residences.<ref>{{w|Palatine#Derivative_terms}}</ref><ref>https://web.archive.org/web/20190501165625/https://www.oxford-royale.co.uk/articles/14-fascinating-word-origins-english-language.html</ref> The name is ultimately either from {{der|en|ett|-}}, the same source as {{m|la|Pales||{{

season.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*seh₁-|id=sow}} From {{inh|en|enm|sesoun|sesoun, seson|time of the year}}, from {{der|en|fro|seson|seson, saison|time of sowing, seeding}}, from {{der|en|la|satiō||act of sowing, planting}} from {{m|la|satum}}, past participle of {{m|la|serō||to sow, plant}} from {{der|en|ine-pro|*seh₁-||to sow, plant}}. Akin to {{cog|ang|sāwan||to sow}}, {{m|ang|sǣd||seed}}. {{doublet|en|saison}}. Displaced native {{cog|enm|sele||season}} (from {{cog|ang|sǣl||season, time, occasion}}), {{cog|enm|tide||season, time of year}} (from {{cog|ang|tīd||time, period, yeartide, season}}).

thunder.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:thonder|id=noun|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|thonder}}, {{m|enm|thunder}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þunor|t=thunder}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*þunr}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*þunraz}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)ten-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*(s)tenh₂-||to thunder}}.

wet.raw: {{etymon|en|:af|enm:wet}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*wed-}} From {{inh|en|enm|wet||wet, moistened}}, {{m|enm|wett}}, {{m|enm|wette}}, past participle of {{der|en|enm|weten||to wet}}, from {{der|en|ang|wǣtan||to wet, moisten, water}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*wātijan}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*wētijaną||to wet, make wet}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wed-||water, wet}} (also the source of {{m|en|water}}).

dry.raw: Adjective and noun from {{inh|en|enm|drye}}, {{m|enm|dryge}}, {{m|enm|druȝe|drüȝe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|drȳġe|t=dry; parched, withered}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*drūgī}}, {{m|gmw-pro|*draugī}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*drūgiz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*draugiz|t=dry, hard}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰerǵʰ-|t=to strengthen; become hard}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*dʰer-||to hold, support}}. The verb derives from {{inh|en|enm|drien}}, from {{inh|en|ang|drȳġan|t=to dry}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*drūgijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*drūgiz|t=hard, desiccated, dry}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰerǵʰ-|t=strong, hard, solid}}. {{

fine.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|fin}}, {{m|enm|fyn}}, from {{der|en|fro|fin|t=fine, minute, exact}}, of obscure origin, but probably derived from {{der|en|la|fīniō|fīnīre|t=to finish}} or {{m|la|fīnis|t=boundary, limit, end}}, with an abstract sense of ''fine'' or ''thin'' also arising in many Romance languages (compare {{cog|it, pt, es|fino}}). {{doublet|en|fino}}.

degree.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|degre}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|degré}} (French: {{m|fr|degré}}), itself from {{der|en|la|gradus}}, with the prefix {{m|fro|de-}}.

temperature.raw: {{bor+|en|la|temperātūra}}<ref>{{R:Dictionary.com}}</ref> (cf. also {{cog|fr|température}}), from the past participle stem of {{m|la|tempero||to temper}}.

shine.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:schynen|id=to emit light|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|schynen}}, {{m|enm|schinen}} (preterite {{m|enm|schon}}, past participle {{m|enm|schynen}}), from {{inh|en|ang|sċīnan}} {{gloss|“to shine, flash; be resplendent”; preterite {{m|ang|sċān}}, past participle {{m|ang|sċinen}}}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*skīnan|t=to shine}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*skīnaną|t=to shine}}.

blow.raw: {{etymon|en|id=air|:inh|enm:blowen<id:to blow>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|blowen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|blāwan||to blow, breathe, inflate, sound}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*blāan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*blēaną||to blow}} (compare {{cog|de|blähen}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰleh₁-||to swell, blow up}} (compare {{cog|la|flō||to blow}} and {{cog|xcl|բեղուն||fertile}}).

chain: to fall, fail, decay, die, attack
fall.raw: Verb from {{inh|en|enm|fallen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|feallan|t=to fall, fail, decay, die, attack}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*fallan|t=to fall}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*fallaną|t=to fall}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*h₃elh₁-|t=to collapse, fall; to destroy}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|faw|t=to fall}}, {{cog|yol|vale}}, {{m|yol|vall}}, {{m|yol|vole|t=to fall}}, {{cog|frr|faal}}, {{m|frr|fåle|t=to fall}}, {{cog|stq|faale|t=to fall}}, {{cog|fy|falle|t=to fall}}, {{cog|bar|foin|t=to fall}}, {{cog|cim|ballan}}, {{m|cim|vallan|t=to fall}}, {{cog|nl|vallen|t=to fall}}, {{cog|de,nds|fallen|t=to

magazine.raw: {{etymon|en|id=nonacademic periodical|:inh|enm:magasyne|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|magasyne}}, from {{der|en|frm|magasin||warehouse, store}}, from {{der|en|it|magazzino||storehouse}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ar|مَخَازِن|g=p}}, plural of {{m|ar|مَخْزَن||storeroom, storehouse}}, [[noun of place]] from {{m|ar|خَزَنَ||to store, to stock, to lay up}}. {{etydate|1580s|ref={{R:Etymonline|pos=n}}}}. {{root|en|ar|خ ز ن}}

paper.raw: {{dercat|en|qsb-grc|egy}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:paper|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|paper}}, from {{der|en|xno|papier|paper}}, from {{der|en|roa-oca|paper}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|papȳrus}} (and given the Catalan suffix {{m|ca|-er}}), from {{der|en|grc|πάπυρος}}.

chain: a class or division of the people, assembly of people, the whole body of citizens called to arms, the army, the fleet, later a class or division in general
class.raw: {{ety|en|:bor|frm:classe<ety:der<la:classis>>}} From {{bor|en|frm|classe}}, from {{der|en|la|classis||a class or division of the people, assembly of people, the whole body of citizens called to arms, the army, the fleet, later a class or division in general}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kelh₁-|t=to call, shout}}. {{doublet|en|clas|classis}}.

lesson.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*leǵ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|lessoun}}, from {{der|en|fro|leçon}}, from {{der|en|la|lēctiō|lēctiō, lēctiōnem|a [[reading]]}}, from {{m|la|legō||to read; to gather}}. {{doublet|en|lection}}.

chain: lying under or near, adjacent, also subject, exposed
subject.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(H)yeh₁-}} From {{der|en|enm|subget}}, from {{der|en|fro|suget}}, from {{der|en|la|subiectus||lying under or near, adjacent, also subject, exposed}}, as a noun, {{m|la|subiectus||a subject, an inferior}}, {{m|la|subiectum||the subject of a proposition}}, past participle of {{m|la|subiciō||throw, lay, place}}, from {{m|la|sub||under, at the foot of}} + {{m|la|iaciō||throw, hurl}}, as a calque of {{der|en|grc|ὑποκείμενον}}.

Chinese.raw: From {{af|en|China|-ese}} under influence of [[Portuguese]] {{m|pt|chinês}}, replacing older {{m|en|Chinish}}. {{doublet|en|chinois}}. In its [[orientalist]] sense of "generically exotic, backwards, or poorly organized", sometimes a deliberate marketing strategy to increase sales, as with the German {{m|en|Chinese checkers}}. In its sense related to the orientation of stage lighting's barn doors, a reference to a supposed resemblance to East Asian eyes.

English.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:Englisch|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|Englisch}}, {{m|enm|English}}, {{m|enm|Inglis}}, from {{inh|en|ang|Englisċ||of the Angles; English}}, from {{m|ang|Engle||the [[Angles]]}}, a Germanic tribe {{suffix|ang||isċ|nocat=1}}; equivalent to {{suf|en|Engle|-ish}}. {{dbt|en|Anglish}}. Compare {{cog|fy|Ingelsk}}, {{cog|sco|Inglis}} (older {{m|sco|ynglis}}), {{cog|nl|Engels}}, {{cog|da|engelsk}}, {{cog|fro|Englesche}} (whence {{cog|fr|anglais}}), {{cog|de|englisch|||pos=|tr=|id=|g=}}, {{cog|es|inglés}}, all ultimately derived from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂enǵʰ-||narrow}} (compare {{cog|sa|

history.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*weyd-}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:historie|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|historie}}, from {{der|en|fro|estoire}}, {{m|fro|estorie||chronicle, history, story}} ({{cog|fr|histoire}}), from {{der|en|la|historia}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἱστορίᾱ||learning through research}}, from {{m|grc|ἱστορέω||to research, inquire (and) record}}, from {{m|grc|ἵστωρ||the knowing, wise one}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*weyd-||see, know}}. {{doublet|en|story|storey}}.

chain: the lid of an earthen vessel, an earthen vessel, an earthen pot
test.raw: [[Image:Sea urchin tests.jpg|thumb|right|Two sea urchin tests]] {{root|en|ine-pro|*ters-}} From {{inh|en|enm|test}}, {{m|enm|teste}}, from {{der|en|fro|test}}, {{m|fro|teste|t=an earthen vessel, especially a pot in which metals were tried}}, from {{der|en|la|testum|t=the lid of an earthen vessel, an earthen vessel, an earthen pot}}, from {{m|la|*terstus}}, past participle of the root {{m|la|*tersa||dry land}}. See [[terra]], [[thirst]]. The ''examination'' sense came via metaphor of the metallurgical sense: the way a metallurgist ''puts to the test'' their gold, a teacher may ''put to the test

answer.raw: {{wikidata lexeme|L42}} {{etymon|en|id=response|:inh|enm:answere<id:noun>|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂en-}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂ent-|*swer-|id2=swear}} From {{inh|en|enm|answere}}, {{m|enm|andsware}}, from {{inh|en|ang|andswaru||answer}}, from {{af|ang|and-|t1=against|swaru|t2=affirmation|nocat=1}}, (from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂ent-||front, forehead}} and {{der|en|ang|swerian||to swear}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*swer-}}), suggesting an original meaning of "a sworn statement rebutting a charge". The cognates suggest the existence of {{der|en|gem-pro|*andaswarō||a reply to a question}}. Cognate w

word.raw: [[File:About- General sign.ogv|thumb| The word ''about'' signed in [[American Sign Language]].]] {{root|en|ine-pro|*werh₁-|*dʰeh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|word}}, from {{inh|en|ang|word}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*word}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wurdą|t=word}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*werdʰom|t=word}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*werh₁-|t=to say, speak}}. {{doublet|en|verb|verve|vort}}; further related to {{m|en|vrata}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|wird|t=word}}, {{cog|frr|uurd}}, {{m|frr|Uurt}}, {{m|frr|wurd}}, {{m|frr|wårde}}, {{m|frr|wür|t=word}}, {{cog|stq|Woud}}, {{m|stq|Wud|t=word}}, {{cog|fy

sentence.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*sent-|id=perceive}} {{bor+|en|frm|sentence}}, from {{der|en|la|sententia||way of thinking, opinion, sentiment}}, from {{m|la|sentiēns}}, present participle of {{m|la|sentiō|t=to feel, think}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sent-||to feel}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|cwide}}.

story.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*weyd-}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:storie|id=event|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|storie}}, {{m|enm|storye}}, from {{der|en|xno|estorie}} by {{glossary|aphesis}}, from {{der|en|la|historia}}, from {{der|en|grc|ῐ̔στορῐ́ᾱ||learning through research}}. {{doublet|en|history|storey}}.

grade.raw: Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|grade||a grade, degree}}, from {{der|en|la|gradus||a step, pace, degree}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*graðus}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰradʰ-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*gʰredʰ-||to walk, go}}. {{doublet|en|gradus}}.

group.raw: {{etymon|en|id=set|:bor|fr:groupe<id:set>|:bor|it:gruppo<id:group>|tree=1}} From {{bor|en|fr|groupe|t=cluster, group}}, from {{der|en|it|gruppo}}, {{m|it|groppo|t=a knot, heap, group, bag (of money)}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|hād||tribe, group}}.

rule.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|reule}}, {{m|enm|rewle}}, {{m|enm|rule}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|riule}}, {{m|fro|reule}}, from {{der|en|la|regula||straight stick, bar, ruler, pattern}}, from {{m|la|regō||to keep straight, direct, govern, rule}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₃réǵeti||to straighten; right}}, from the root {{m|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-}}; see {{m|en|regent}}. {{doublet|en|rail|regal#Noun|regula|rigol}}.

chain: to take in error, to miscarry
mistake.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|mistaken}}, from {{der|en|non|mistaka|t=to take in error, to miscarry}}; equivalent to {{prefix|en|mis|take}}. Cognate with {{cog|is|mistaka|t=to mistake}}, {{cog|sv|missta|t=to mistake}} (before apocope {{m|sv|misstaga}}).

chain: sample, pattern, specimen, copy for imitation, etc.
example.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁em-}} From {{inh|en|enm|example}}, {{m|enm|exaumple}}, from {{der|en|fro|example}}, {{m|fro|essaumple}}, from {{der|en|la|exemplum|lit=what is taken out|t=sample, pattern, specimen, copy for imitation, etc.}}; see {{m|en|exempt}}. {{doublet|en|exemplum|sample}}. Displaced native {{ncog|enm|forebisne}}, from {{ncog|ang|forebȳsn}}; and {{ncog|enm|bisne}}, from {{ncog|ang|bȳsn}} (modern {{ncog|en|bizen}}).

idea.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|la:idea|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*weyd-}} {{bor+|en|la|idea||a (Platonic) idea; archetype}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἰδέα||notion, pattern}}, from {{m|grc|εἴδω||to see}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*weyd-||to know; see}}. Cognate with {{cog|fr|idée}}. {{doublet|en|idée}}. Related to {{doublet|notext=1|en|idol|idolum|eidolon}}.

glue.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:glew|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|glew}}, {{m|enm|glue}}, from {{der|en|fro|glu||glue, [[birdlime]]}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|glūs}} (stem {{m|la||glūt-}}), from {{der|en|la|glūten}}. Related to {{m|en|clay}}.

scissors.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|sisours}} (attested since 1350–1400), from {{der|en|fro|[[cisoir]]s}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|cīsōria}}, plural of {{m|la|cīsōrium||cutting tool}}; from {{der|en|la|-}} word root {{m|la||-cīsus}} (compare {{m|en|excise}}) or {{m|la|caesus}}, past participle of {{m|la|caedō||to cut}}. Partially displaced native {{ncog|ang|sċēara||scissors, shears}}, whence {{m|en|shears}}. {{doublet|en|chisel}}.

spell.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)pel-}} From {{inh|en|enm|spell}}, {{m|enm|spel}}, from {{inh|en|ang|spell|t=news, story}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*spellą|t=speech, account, tale}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)pel-|t=to tell}} or from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰel-|t=to speak, to sound}} with the [[s-mobile]] prefix. Cognate with dialectal {{cog|de|Spill}}, {{cog|is|spjall|t=discussion, talk}}, {{m|is|spjalla|t=to discuss, to talk}}, {{m|is|guðspjall|t=gospel}} and {{cog|sq|fjalë|t=word}}.

ask.raw: {{etymon|en|id=request|:inh|enm:asken|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|asken}}, {{m|enm|axen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|āscian}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*aiskōn}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂eys-|t=to wish; request}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|aaskje|t=to ask, demand, require}}, {{cog|fy|easkje|t=to ask, demand, require}}, {{cog|nl|eisen|t=to demand, require}}, {{cog|de|heischen|t=to ask, request, implore}}, {{cog|ru|иска́ть}}, {{cog|sa|इच्छति|tr=iccháti}} (whence {{cog|hi|ईछना}}.

understand.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|understanden}}, from {{inh|en|ang|understandan||t=to understand}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*understandan|t=to stand between, understand}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*understandaną|t=to stand between, understand}}, equivalent to {{cog|ang|under-|t=between, inter-}} + {{m|ang|standan|t=to stand}} (Modern English {{af|en|under-|stand}}). Cognate with {{cog|ofs|understonda|t=to understand, experience, learn}}, {{cog|goh|understantan|t=to understand}}, Middle {{cog|da|understande|t=to understand}}. Compare also {{cog|stq|understunda}}, {{m|stq|unnerstounde|t=to dare, survey, measure}},

practise.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|practizen|}}, a variant of {{m|enm|practisen}}, from {{der|en|frm|pratiser}}, {{m|frm|practiser|}}, from {{der|en|la-med|-}} {{m|la|practizo|}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|-}} {{m|la|practico||to do, perform, execute, propose, practise, exercise, be conversant with, contrive, conspire, etc.}}, from {{m|la|prāctica||practical affairs", "business}}, from {{der|en|grc|πρᾱκτική|}}, from {{m|grc|πρᾱκτικός||practical}}, from {{m|grc|πρᾱ́σσω|πρᾱ́σσειν|to do}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*per-|*per(h₂)-|to go over, cross}}.

fail.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:failen<ety:bor<fro:falir>>|tree=1}} {{inh+|en|enm|failen}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|falir}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*fallire}}, alteration of {{der|en|la|fallō|fallere|t=to deceive, disappoint}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro||*bʰāl-|t=to lie, deceive}}{{attn|ine-pro}} or {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)gʷʰh₂el-|t=to stumble}}.

discuss.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|discussen}}, from {{der|en|frm|-}} and {{der|en|xno|discusser}} ({{cog|fr|discuter}}), from {{der|en|la|discussus}}, past participle of {{m|la|discutiō||to strike or shake apart, break up, scatter; examine, discuss}}, from {{m|la|dis-||apart}} + {{m|la|quatiō||to shake}}.

chain: to flatten, spread out, make plain or clear, explain
explain.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|explanen}}, from {{der|en|fro|explaner}}, from {{der|en|la|explanō||to flatten, spread out, make plain or clear, explain}}, from {{m|la|ex-||out}} + {{m|la|planō||to flatten, make level}}, from {{m|la|planus||level, plain}}; see [[plain]] and [[plane]]. Compare [[esplanade]], [[splanade]]. Displaced {{ncog|ang|reċċan}}.

parent.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:parent<ety:bor<xno:parent><frm:parent>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|parent}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|parent}}, {{der|en|frm|parent}}, from {{der|en|la|parentem}}, accusative of {{m|la|parēns|id=parent|t=parent}}, present participle of {{m|la|pariō|t=to breed, bring forth}}.

cousin.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:cosyn}} The {{glossary|noun}} is derived from {{inh|en|enm|cosin}}, {{m|enm|cosine}}, {{m|enm|cosyn|t=blood relative, kinsman or kinswoman; any relative; nephew or niece; first cousin; grandson or granddaughter; descendant; godchild or godparent, or a relative of a godchild or godparent; (''figurative'') closely related or similar thing}}{{nb...|coosin, cosen, coseyn, cosigne, cosing, cossen, cossin, cossigne, cossine, cossyn, cossyne, cosyne, cosynne, cousin, cousine, cousyn, cozyn, cusin, cusine, cussyn, cusyn, kosen, kosin, kosyn|otherforms=1}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=cǒ

son.raw: {{etymon|en|id=male offspring|:inh|enm:sone<id:son>}} From {{inh|en|enm|sonn}}, {{m|enm|sone}}, {{m|enm|sun}}, {{m|enm|sune}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sunu||son}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sunu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*sunuz|t=son}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*suHnús|t=son}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sewH-|t=to bear; give birth}}.

baby.raw: {{etymon|en|id=young|:inh|enm:baby|:afeq|babe|-y<id:diminutive>|tree=1}} {{multiple images |direction = vertical |image1 = Baby.jpg |caption1 = A human baby |image2 = Baby ginger monkey.jpg |caption2 = A baby [[monkey#Noun|monkey]] |image3 = Smaller Babyelephant45 from wiki commons.jpg |caption3 = A baby [[elephant]] (sometimes called a [[calf]]) }}

kid.raw: [[Image:Goat kid444.jpg|thumb|right|A goat kid.]] From {{inh|en|enm|kide}}, from {{der|en|non|kið||young goat}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*kidją}}, {{m|gem-pro|*kittīną||goatling, kid}}, perhaps from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰaydn-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*ǵʰaydn-||goat}} or {{der|en|ine-pro|*gidʰ-||kid, goatling, little goat}}. Compare {{cog|sv|-}} and {{cog|da|kid}}, {{cog|de|Kitz}} and {{m|de|Kitze}}, {{cog|sq|kedh}} and {{m|sq|kec}}. The sense of {{m|en|child}} has been in use since the 1590s as [[slang]], and since the 1840s in informal use.<ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary}}</ref><ref>{{R:Grose Vulgar

girl.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:girle}} From {{inh|en|enm|gerle}}, {{m|enm|girle}}, {{m|enm|gyrle|t=young person (boy or girl)}}, perhaps from {{inh|en|ang|*gyrele}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|girl(e|n|MED18637|passage=?OE *gyrela, from earlier *gurw-}}</ref> from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*gurilā}}, from a zero-grade diminutive of {{af|gmw-pro|*gaurā|t1=young child|*-ilā|nocat=1}}. Ultimately of {{unk|en|nocap=1}} origin.<ref>{{R:EWddS|hw=Gör|page=272}}</ref><ref>{{R:nn:NEO|Gorre|176}}</ref> {{doublet|en|[[gal]]''/''[[gyal]]|gyaru}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|yol|gurl|t=child, girl}}, {{cog|de|Gör}}, {{m|de|Gör

people.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:peple}} From {{inh|en|enm|puple}}, {{m|enm|peple}}, {{m|enm|peeple}}, from {{derived|en|xno|people}}, from {{derived|en|fro|pueple}}, {{m|fro|peuple}}, {{m|fro|pople}}, from {{derived|en|la|populus|t=a people, nation}}, from {{der|en|itc-ola|populus}}, from earlier {{m|itc-ola|poplus}}, from even earlier {{m|itc-ola|poplos}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*poplos|t=army}} of unknown origin. {{doublet|en|pueblo}}. Gradually ousted native {{cog|en|lede}} and, partially, {{m|en|folk}}.

person.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:persoun|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|persoun}}, {{m|enm|personne}} et al., from {{der|en|xno|parsone}}, {{m|fro|persoun}} et al. ({{cog|fro|persone}}, {{cog|fr|personne}}), and its source {{der|en|la|persōna|t=mask used by actor; role, part, character}}, perhaps a loanword from {{der|en|ett|𐌘𐌄𐌓𐌔𐌖|t=mask}}. In this sense, displaced native {{m|en|man}}, which came to mean primarily "adult male" in Middle English; see {{ncog|ang|mann}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|hād||person, individual}}. {{doublet|en|parson|persona}}.

dad.raw: From [[w:Early Modern English|Early Modern English]] {{m|en|dadd}}, {{m|en|dadde}} {{gl|{{circa2|1500}}}}, undoubtedly older, from unrecorded {{inh|en|enm|*dadde}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} ultimate origin. Compare {{cog|fy|deite|t=dad, daddy}}, {{cog|swg|Dede|t=Godfather}}.

home.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:hom|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|hom}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hām}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*haim}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*haimaz|t=home, village}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*ḱóymos|t=village, home}}, from the root {{m|ine-pro|*tḱey-|}}. {{dbt|en|heyem}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|hame|t=home}}, {{cog|yol|haime}}, {{m|yol|hime}}, {{m|yol|hyme|t=home}}, {{cog|stq|Heem|t=home}}, {{cog|gsw|haim}}, {{m|gsw|hei}}, {{m|gsw|heim}}, {{m|gsw|hemmu|t=home}}, {{cog|bar|hama}}, {{m|bar|hame|t=home}}, {{cog|cim|hòam}}, {{m|cim|huam|t=home}}, {{cog|nl|heem}}, {{m|nl|heim|t=home}},

cogs: country, fields, lands; estate, farm; village
room.raw: {{etymon|en|id=space|:inh|enm:roum<id:space>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|roum|t=room, space}}, from {{inh|en|ang|rūm|t=room, space}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*rūm|t=room}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*rūmą|t=room}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*(H)rewH-|t=to root; to rip, tear}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*Hrew-|t=to tear out, open}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|frr|rüm|t=room, space}}, {{cog|stq,nds|Ruum|t=room, space}}, {{cog|nl|ruim|t=open space; cargo hold}}, {{cog|de,lb|Raum|t=room, space}}, {{cog|wym|raojm|t=room}}, {{cog|da,sv|rum|t=room, space}}, {{cog|fo,is|rúm|t=space, room}}, {{cog|nb,nn|rom|t=ro

daddy.raw: {{ety|en|:af|dad|-y<id:diminutive>|tree=1}} The {{lg|noun}} is probably derived from {{m|en|dad}} (although this word is attested later) + {{affix|en|-y|id1=diminutive|pos1={{lg|diminutive}} {{lg|suffix}}}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=1080365512|date=June 2026|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=n}}</ref>

yard.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:yerd<id:yard>|id=enclosure|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|yerd}}, {{m|enm|yard}}, {{m|enm|ȝerd}}, {{m|enm|ȝeard}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ġeard|t=yard, garden, fence, enclosure}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*gard}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*gardaz|t=enclosure, yard}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*gʰórdʰos}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰerdʰ-|t=to enclose}}.

mirror.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)mey-}} From {{inh|en|enm|mirour}}, from {{der|en|fro|mireor|t=mirror|lit=looker, watcher}}, from {{m|fro|mirer|t=look at}}, from {{der|en|la|mīror||wonder at}}, from {{m|la|mīrus||wonderful}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*smey-|t=to laugh, to be glad}}. Displaced native {{ncog|enm|schewere}}, {{m|enm|schawere}}, from {{ncog|ang|sċēawere|t=mirror|lit=watcher}}, which was also the word for "spy".

mum.raw: Alternative form of {{m|en|mam}}, or an abbreviation of {{m|en|mummy}}. Compare {{m|en|mom}}, {{m|en|mama}}.

chain: shiny; gleaming; radiant; happy; glossy; smooth; flat
glad.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵʰelh₂-}} From {{der|en|enm|glad}}, {{m|enm|gled}}, from {{der|en|ang|glæd||shining; bright; cheerful; glad}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*gladaz||shiny; gleaming; radiant; happy; glossy; smooth; flat}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰladʰ-}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*ǵʰelh₂-||to shine}}.

Lawton Roberts|chapter=Lecture I|title=Illustrated Lectures on Ambulance Work|edition=3rd|location=London|publisher=H. K. Lewis,{{nb...|136 Gower Street, W.C.}}|year=1888|section=figure 3|page=20|pageurl=https://archive.org/stream/illustratedlectu00robe/illustratedlectu00robe#page/20/mode/1up|oclc=14795323}}.}} |image2 = Bac

lonely.raw: From {{af|en|lone|-ly|id2=adjectival}}, or from an apheretic shortening of {{m|en|alonely}}. See {{l|en|lone}}.

chain: feeling or expressing grief, sorry, grieved, sorrowful, sad, mournful, bitter
sorry.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|sory}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sāriġ|t=feeling or expressing grief, sorry, grieved, sorrowful, sad, mournful, bitter}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sairag}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*sairagaz|t=sad}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*seh₂yro|t=hard, rough, painful}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|sairie||sad, grieved}}, {{cog|stq|seerich|t=sore, inflamed}}, {{cog|fy|searich||sad, sorry}}, {{cog|nds|serig||sick, scabby}}, {{cog|de|-}} dialectal {{m|de|sehrig||sore, sad, painful}}, Swedish {{m|sv|sårig}}. {{surf|+suf|en|sore|y|alt1=sor(e)}}. Unrelated to {{m|en|sorrow}} despite the similarity in form and m

cogs: to look, perceive, see; to note, observe; to comprehend, understand
wise.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*weyd-}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:wys<alt:wys, wyse>|tree=+}} From {{inh|en|enm|wys}}, {{m|enm|wyse}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wīs|t=wise}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wīsaz|t=knowledgeable, wise}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*wéydos|t=seeing; knowledge}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*weyd-|t=to see}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|fy|wiis|t=wise}}, {{cog|nl|wijs|t=wise}}, {{cog|de|weis}}, {{m|de|weise|t=wise}}, {{cog|nds|wies|t=wise; clever}}, {{cog|da,nb,nn,sv|vis|t=wise}}, {{cog|is|vís|t=wise; certain}}, {{cog|got|*𐍅𐌴𐌹𐍃|t=wise}}; also {{cog|ga|fios|t=knowledge; information}}, {{cog|gv|fys|t=knowled

brave.raw: From {{bor|en|frm|brave}}, borrowed from {{der|en|it|bravo}}, itself of uncertain origin (see there). {{doublet|en|bravo}}.

shy.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|shy||shy}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sċēoh||shy}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*skeuh||shy, fearful}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*skeuhaz||shy, fearful}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|skjou||shy}}, {{cog|nl|schuw||shy}}, {{cog|de|scheu||shy}}, {{cog|da|sky||shy}}.

lazy.raw: Attested since 1540, origin uncertain. Probably from {{bor|en|nds|-}} and {{der|en|gml|lasich|t=slack, feeble, lazy}},<ref>{{R:Dictionary.com}}</ref><ref>{{R:Merriam-Webster Online}}</ref> from {{m|gml|las}}, from {{der|en|osx|lask}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*lasiwaz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*laskaz|t=feeble, weak}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*las-|t=weak}}.

cogs: gallant, brave, magnificent, stately, handsome, fine
proud.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|proud}}, {{m|enm|prout}}, {{m|enm|prut}}, from {{inh|en|ang|prūd}}, {{m|ang|prūt|t=proud, arrogant, haughty}} (compare {{cog|ang|prȳtung|t=pride}}; {{m|ang|prȳde}}, {{m|ang|prȳte|t=pride}}, see also {{ncog|ang|deal}}), probably from {{der|en|fro|prod}}, {{m|fro|prut|t=brave, gallant}} (modern {{cog|fr|preux}}), from {{der|en|la-lat|prode|prōde|useful}}, derived from {{cog|la|prosum|prōdesse|t=to be of value}}; however, the Old English [[umlaut]] derivatives {{m|and|prȳte}}, {{m|ang|prȳtian}}, etc. suggest the word may be older and possibly native. Compare {{cog|non|prýði|t=or

number.raw: {{etymon|en|id=quantity|:inh|enm:nombre<id:number>|tree=1}} {{inh+|en|enm|number}}, {{m|enm|nombre}}, {{m|enm|numbre}}, {{m|enm|noumbre}}, from {{der|en|xno|noumbre|sc=Latn}}, {{der|en|fro|nombre|sc=Latn}}, from {{der|en|la|numerus||number}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*nem-||to distribute, to give, to take}}. Compare {{cog|stq|Nummer}}, {{m|stq|Nuumer}}, {{cog|fy|nûmer}}, {{cog|nl|nummer||number}}, {{cog|de|Nummer||number}}, {{cog|da|nummer||number}}, {{cog|sv|nummer||number}}, {{cog|is|númer||number}}. {{displaced|enm|ȝetæl}} and {{m|enm|rime}}; more at {{m|en|tell}}, {{m|en|tale}} and

zero.raw: {{number box|en|0}} {{wp}} {{root|en|ar|ص ف ر}} Collectively borrowed from {{bor|en|es-ear|zero}}, {{bor|en|frm|zero}}, and (their etymon) {{bor|en|roa-oit|zero}}, from {{der|en|la-med|zēphirum}}, from {{der|en|ar|صِفْر||nothing; [[cipher]]}}, itself calqued from {{der|en|sa|शून्य|tr=śūnyá|t=void; nothingness}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''n.'' and ''adj.''|noformat=1|id=4029618546}}</ref> {{doublet|en|cipher|chiffre}}. Cognate with {{cog|es|cero}} and {{cog|fr|zéro}}.

hundred.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:hundred|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|hundred}}, from {{inherited|en|ang|hundred}}, from {{inherited|en|gem-pro|*hundaradą}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*hundą}} (from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱm̥tóm}}) + {{m|gem-pro|*radą||count}}, a neuter variant of {{m|gem-pro|*radō||row, line, series}}.<ref name="Kroonen">{{R:gem:EDPG|head=*radō|page=401}}</ref> Compare {{cog|fy|hûndert}}, {{cog|nl|honderd}}, {{cog|nds|hunnert}}, {{m|nds|hunnerd}}, {{cog|de|Hundert}}, {{m|de|hundert}}, {{cog|da|hundred}}.

pair.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|paire}}, from {{der|en|fro|paire}}, from {{der|en|la|paria|t=equals}}, neuter plural of {{m|la|par|t=pair}}. Related to {{m|la|pār|t=equal|pos=adj}}. Compare {{cog|stq|Poor|t=pair}}, {{cog|fy|pear|t=pair}}, {{cog|nl|paar|t=pair}}, {{cog|de|Paar|t=pair}}, {{cog|it|paio|t=pair}}

piece.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|pece}}, {{m|enm|peece}}, {{m|enm|peice}}, from {{der|en|fro|piece}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|pettia|pecia}}, {{m|la|pettia|petia|t=broken piece, fragment; parcel of land}}, of {{unc|en|title=uncertain}} origin. Possibly ultimately from {{der|en|cel-gau|*pettyā}}, from {{der|en|cel-pro|*kʷezdis|t=piece, portion, quota}}. Compare {{cog|cy|peth|t=thing, stuff, junk}}, {{cog|br|pez|t=thing}}, {{cog|ga|cuid|t=part, portion}}. Compare {{cog|fr|pièce}}, {{cog|pt|peça}}, {{cog|es|pieza}}, {{cog|it|pezza}}, {{cog|it|pezzo}}. Displaced native {{ncog|enm|sticche}}, {{m|enm|stucche|t=piece,

Related to {{m|en|heave}}.

laugh.raw: {{wp}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:laughen<alt:laughen, laghen>|tree=+}} From {{inh|en|enm|laughen}}, {{m|enm|laghen}}, from (Anglian) {{inh|en|ang|hlæhhan}}, {{m|ang|hlehhan}}, (West Saxon) {{m|ang|hliehhan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hlahhjan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hlahjaną}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Germanic: {{cog|sco|lauch|t=to laugh}}, {{cog|yol|leeigh}}, {{m|yol|leigh|t=to laugh}}, {{cog|frr|laache}}, {{m|frr|lachi}}, {{m|frr|laake}}, {{m|frr|loache}}, {{m|frr|lååke|t=to laugh}}, {{cog|stq|laachje|t=to laugh}}, {{cog|fy|laitsje|t=to laugh}}, {{cog|gsw|lache|t=to laugh}}, {{cog|cim|lachan|t=to laugh}},

smile.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)mey-}} From {{inh|en|enm|smilen|t=to smile}}, from {{der|en|gml|*smîlen|t=to smile}}, from {{der|en|gmh|smielen}}, from {{der|en|goh|smielēn}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*smilēn|*smīlēn}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*smilāną|*smīlāną|t=to smile}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*smey-|t=to laugh, be glad, wonder}}.

cry.raw: The verb is from {{inh|en|enm|crien}} (13th century), from {{der|en|fro|crier}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*crītāre}}, generally thought to derive from {{m+|la-cla|quirito|quirītāre}} ({{m+|gmw-pro|*krītan}} has also been suggested as a source). The noun corresponds to {{inh|en|enm|cry}}, {{m|enm|crie}}, from {{der|en|fro|cri}}, a deverbal of {{m|fro|crier}}.

shout.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|shouten}}. Further origin {{unc|en|nocap=1}}. Possibly related to {{cog|enm|shooten||to shoot (out)}} or from or akin to {{uder|en|non|skúta||to chide, scold}}, {{cog|non|skúti}}, {{m|non|skúta||a taunt}}. See also the second, rare sense of the verb {{m|en|scout||to reject with contempt}}.

chain: to take, lay hold of, grasp, strike
take.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*teh₂g-|id=touch}} From {{inh|en|enm|taken|t=to take, lay hold of, grasp, strike}}, from {{inh|en|ang|tacan|t=to grasp, touch}}, probably of {{der|en|gmq}} origin, from {{der|en|non|taka|t=to touch, take}}. Alternatively, inherited from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*takan||to take; grasp, touch}}. Both from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*tēkaną|t=to touch}}, from pre-Germanic {{m|ine-pro||*deh₁g-|t=to touch}}, possibly a phonetically altered form of {{der|en|ine-pro|*teh₂g-|*te-th₂g-|id=touch|t=to touch, take}} (see there for details).<ref>{{R:gem:EDPG|head=*takan- ~ *tēkan-|page=507}}</ref><ref>{{R:

worry.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|worien|t=to choke, strangle}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wyrġan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wurgijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wurgijaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*werǵʰ-|t=bind, squeeze}}.

wish.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:wischen|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|wisshen}}, {{m|enm|wischen}}, {{m|enm|wuschen|wüschen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wȳsċan||to wish}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wunskijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wunskijaną||to wish}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wenh₁-||to wish, love}}.

love.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*lewbʰ-|id=love}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:love<id:affection>|id=affection|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|love}}, {{m|enm|luve}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lufu}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*lubu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*lubō}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*lewbʰ-|t=love, care, desire}}.

cogs: to like; put up with; align with
like.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*leyg-|id=like}} Verb from {{inh|en|enm|liken}}, from {{inh|en|ang|līcian||to like, to please}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*līkēn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*līkāną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*leyg-||image; likeness; similarity}}.

want.raw: {{ety|en|id=desire|:inh|enm:wanten<t:to lack, to need>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|wanten||to lack, to need}}, from {{der|en|non|vanta||to lack}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*wanatōną||to be wanting, lack}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*wanô||lack, deficiency}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₁weh₂-||empty}}. Cognate with {{cog|gmh|wan||not full, empty}}, {{cog|dum|wan||empty, poor}}, {{cog|ang|wana||want, lack, absence, deficiency}}, {{cog|la|vanus||empty}}. See {{l|en|wan}}, {{l|en|wan-}}.

need.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:nede<id:need>|id=noun|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|nede}}, a merger of two terms: * {{inh|en|ang|nīed}} (West Saxon), {{m|ang|nēd}} (Mercian), {{m|ang|nēad|t=necessity, compulsion, want}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*naudi}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*naudiz}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*neh₂w-|t=death}}. * {{inh|en|ang|nēod|t=desire, longing}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*niudi|t=desire, eagerness}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*new-||to incline, tend, move, push, nod, wave}}.

plan.raw: {{ety|en|:bor|fr:plan<id:map>}} {{bor+|en|fr|plan|t=flat surface, ground plot, map}}, from {{der|en|la|plānus}}. Some sources also argue for influence or alteration of {{der|en|fr|plant}}, from {{m|fr|plantar}}, from {{der|en|la|plantāre|t=set, fix in place}}. {{doublet|en|llano|piano|plane|plain}}.

decide.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*kh₂eyd-}} From {{inh|en|enm|deciden}}, from {{der|en|fro|decider}}, from {{der|en|la|dēcīdere}}, infinitive of {{m|la|dēcīdō|t=cut off, decide}}, from {{m|la|dē|t=down from}} + {{m|la|caedō|t=cut}}.

change.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:chaungen|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|changen}}, {{m|enm|chaungen}}, from {{der|en|fro|changier}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|cambiāre}}, from {{der|en|la|cambio|cambīre|to exchange, barter}}, derived from the noun {{m|la|cambium||change}} (whence was loaned the English {{lg|doublet}} {{dbt|en|cambium|notext=1}}), from {{der|en|cel-gau|cambion}}, earlier {{m|cel-gau||*kambyom|change}}, related to {{der|en|cel-pro|*kambos||twisted, crooked}}, possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro||*(s)ḱh₂(e)mbos}}, {{m|ine-pro||*(s)kh₂(e)mbos|crooked}}. More at {{l|en|skimp}}, {{l|en|scam}}; see also {{m+|in
