join.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*yewg-}} From {{inh|en|enm|joinen}}, {{m|enm|joynen}}, {{m|enm|joignen}}, from {{der|en|fro|joindre}}, {{m|fro|juindre}}, {{m|fro|jungre}}, from {{der|en|la|iungō|t=join, yoke|pos=verb}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*yewg-|gloss=to join, unite}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|iucian}}, {{m|ang|iugian}}, {{m|ang|ġeocian}}, {{m|ang|ġyċċan|t=to join; yoke}}. More at {{m|en|yoke}}.

Possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bud-|t=to shoot, sprout}}, which would make it cognate with {{cog|sa|बुन्द||tr=bundá|

clothes.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|clothes}}, {{m|enm|cloþes|pos=plural of {{m|enm|cloth}}, {{m|enm|cloþ|t=cloth, garment}}}}, from {{inh|en|ang|clāþas|t=clothes|pos=plural of {{m|ang|clāþ|t=cloth}}}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|cloth|es<id:plural>}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|clathes}}, {{m|sco|claes|t=clothes}}, {{cog|nl|klederen}}, {{m|nl|kleren|t=clothes}}, {{cog|de|Kleider|t=clothes}}, {{cog|da|klæder|t=clothes}}, {{cog|sv|kläder|t=clothes}}, {{cog|nb|klær|t=clothes}}, {{cog|nn|klede|t=clothes}}, {{cog|fo|klæði}}, {{m|fo|klæðir|t=clothes}}.

jeans.raw: {{etymon|en|:der|la:Genua}} From ''Gene(s)'' (also spelled ''Jean(s)''), an obsolete English name for the Italian city of [[Genoa]]. Compare {{m+|fr|Gênes}}. In the context of clothing, the term originally denoted a kind of coarse cotton (known more fully as ''Gene(s) [[fustian]]'') that was associated with Genoa. It began to be used for trousers made of such cloth in the 19th century. At this point, the final -''s'' was reanalysed as a plural ending.

shoe.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:scho<id:shoe>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|scho}}, {{m|enm|sho}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sċōh||shoe}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*skōh}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*skōhaz||shoe}}, of unclear etymology; possibly a derivation from {{m|gem-pro|*skehaną||to move quickly}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*skek-||to move quickly, jump}}. Eclipsed non-native {{noncog|enm|sabatine}}, {{m|enm|sabatoun|t=shoe}} from {{noncog|la-med|sabatēnum}}, {{m|la|sabatum|t=shoe, slipper}} (compare {{noncog|pro|sabatō}}, {{noncog|es|zapato|t=shoe}}, {{noncog|fr|sabot|t=wooden shoe, clog}}, {{noncog|it|ciabatta}}). The

Of obscure origin, but probably related to {{der|en|fro|bot||club-foot}}, {{m|fro|bot||fat, short, blunt}}, from Old {{der|en|frk|*butt}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*buttaz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*butaz||cut off, short, numb, blunt}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰewt-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*bʰewd-||to strike, push, shock}}; if so, a {{doublet|en|butt|nocap=1}}. Compare {{cog|non|butt||stump}}, {{cog|nds|butt||blunt, plump}}, {{cog|ang|bytt||small piece of land}}, {{m|ang|buttuc||end}}.

Equivalent to {{suf|en|poke|-et|id2=diminutive}}. {{doublet|en|pochette}}. Cognate with {{cog|du

ring.raw: {{etymon|en|id=circle|:inh|enm:ryng<id:circle>}} From {{inh|en|enm|ryng}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hring||ring, circle}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hring}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hringaz||ring}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)krengʰ-}}, extended nasalized form of {{m|ine-pro|*(s)ker-||to turn, bend}}. {{doublet|en|rank|rink}}, as well as indirectly {{dbt|en|range|notext=1}}.

size.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*sed-}} Attested since the 14th century, originally meant a “law or regulation that determines the amount to be paid”, from {{inh|en|enm|syse}}, {{m|enm|sise||regulation, control, limit}}, from {{der|en|fro|cise}}, {{m|fro|sise}}, aphetism of {{m|fro|assise||assize}}, from the verb {{m|fro|asseoir||to sit down}}, from {{der|en|la|assideo|assidēre}}, composed of {{affix|la|ad-|gloss1=to, towards, at|sedeō|gloss2=sit; settle down|nocat=1}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sed-}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|miċelnes|lit=bigness}}.

wear.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:weren<id:to wear>|tree=1}} {{inh+|en|enm|weren<id:to wear>}}, from {{inh|en|ang|werian||to clothe, cover over; put on, wear, use; stock (land)}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*waʀjan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wazjaną||to clothe}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wes-||to dress, put on (clothes)}}. Compare {{m|en|weary}}.

smart.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)merd-}} From {{inh|en|enm|smerten}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*smeortan||to smart}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*smertan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*smertaną||to hurt, ache}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)merd-||to bite, sting}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|smert}}, {{cog|nl|smarten}}, {{cog|de|schmerzen}}, {{cog|da|smerte}}, {{cog|sv|smärta}}.

The English word is analysable as {{suffix|en|Chri

Dragon Boat Festival.raw: {{calque|en|zh|龍船節}} or {{m|zh|龍舟節}}, an alternative name for {{m|zh|端午節}} from the races traditionally held on that day in southern China, now popularly connected with the legend of townspeople racing to throw [[zongzi]] into the [[Miluo]] River to preserve the body of the [[Chu]] poet and statesman [[:w:Qu Yuan|Qu Yuan]].

lantern.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|lanterne}} (13th century), via {{der|en|fro|lanterne}} from {{der|en|la|lanterna||lantern}}, itself a corruption of {{der|en|grc|λαμπτήρ||torch}} (see {{m|en|lamp}}, {{m|grc|λάμπω}}) by influence of {{der|en|la|lucerna||lamp}}. The spelling ''[[lanthorn]]'' was current during the 16th to 19th centuries and originates with a folk etymology associating the word with the use of [[horn]] as translucent cover. For the verb, compare {{cog|fr|lanterner}} to hang at the lamppost. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|lēohtfæt|lit=light-container}}.

calendar.raw: {{etymon|en|id=time system|:inh|enm:kalender<id:calendar>|tree=+}} From {{inh|en|enm|kalender}}, from {{der|en|fro|calendier}}, from {{der|en|la|calendarium||account book}}, from {{m|la|kalendae||the first day of the month}}, from {{m|la|kalō||to announce solemnly, to call out (the sighting of the new moon)}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kelh₁-}}. {{doublet|en|calendarium}}.

cogs: to become, will be; to be
future.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰuH-}} From {{inh|en|enm|future}}, {{m|enm|futur}}, from {{der|en|fro|futur}}, from {{der|en|la|futūrus}}, irregular future active participle of {{m|la|sum||to be}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰuH-||to become, be}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|bēo||to become, will be; to be}}. More at {{l|en|be}}. {{doublet|en|futur}}. Displaced native {{cog|ang|tōweard}}, which took on a different meaning as {{m|en|toward}}, and {{noncog|enm|afterhede|t=future|lit=afterhood}} in the given sense.

date.raw: {{etymid|en|fruit}} {{dercat|en|qsb-grc}} From {{inh|en|enm|date}}, from {{der|en|fro|date|id=fruit}}, {{m|fro|datil}}, {{m|fro|datille}}, from {{der|en|la|dactylus}} (likely via {{der|en|oc-pro-old|datil}}), from {{der|en|grc|δάκτυλος|t=finger}} (from the resemblance of the date to a human finger), probably a folk-etymological alteration of a word from a {{der|en|sem}} source such as {{der|en|ar|دَقَل|t=variety of date palm}} or {{der|en|he|דֶּקֶל|tr=deqel|t=date palm}}. {{dbt|en|dactyl|dactylus}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|fingeræppel}}, literally "''[[finger]]-[[apple]]''".

shoulder.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|schuldre}}, {{m|enm|sholder}}, {{m|enm|shulder}}, {{m|enm|schulder}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sċuldra}}, {{m|ang|sċuldor||shoulder}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*skuldru||shoulder}}, of uncertain origin. Perhaps related to {{der|en|gem-pro|*skelduz||shield}}, see {{l|en|shield}}. Cognate with {{cog|ofs|skuldere||shoulder}} ({{cog|fy|skouder||shoulder}}), {{cog|gml|scholder||shoulder}}, {{cog|nds|Schuller}}, {{m|nds|Schulder||shoulder}}, {{cog|nl|schouder||shoulder}}, {{cog|de|Schulter||shoulder}}.

finger.raw: {{PIE word|en|pénkʷe}} From {{inh|en|enm|fynger}}, {{m|enm|finger}}, from {{der|en|ang|finger||finger}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*fingr}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*fingraz||finger}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*penkʷrós}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*pénkʷe||five}}.

knee.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:kne|tree=1}} {{inh+|en|enm|kne}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cnēow}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kneu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*knewą}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro||*ǵnéw-o-m}}, a {{lg|thematic}} derivative of {{m|ine-pro|*ǵónu}}.

toe.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*deyḱ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|to}}, from {{inh|en|ang|tā}}, (Mercian) {{m|ang|tāhe}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*taihā}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*taihwǭ}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*tīhwaną||to show, announce}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*deyḱ-|t=to show}}.

back.raw: {{etymon|en|id=rear|:inh|enm:bak<id:hind>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|bak}}, from {{inh|en|ang|bæc}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*bak}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*baką}}, possibly from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*bʰeg-|t=to bend}}. The adverb represents an [[aphetic]] form of {{m|en|aback}}.

hair.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:her|tree=+}} From {{inh|en|enm|her}}, {{m|enm|heer}}, {{m|enm|hær}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hǣr}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hār}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hērą|t=hair}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kes-|t=to scrape, comb}}.

heart.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱerd-}}{{PIE word|en|ḱḗr}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:herte<id:heart>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|harte}}, {{m|enm|heorrte}}, {{m|enm|hert}}, {{m|enm|herte}}, {{m|enm|hierte}}, {{m|enm|hirte}}, {{m|enm|horte}}, {{m|enm|huerte}}, {{m|enm|hurte}}, from {{inh|en|ang|heorte|t=heart}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hertā}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hertô|t=heart}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*ḱḗr|t=heart}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*ḱerd-|t=heart}}. {{dbt|en|cardia}}; see also {{m|en|core}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|hert|t=heart}}, {{cog|yol|hart}}, {{m|yol|hearth|t=heart}}, {{cog|frr|hart}},

blood.raw: {{etymon|en|id=vital liquid|:inh|enm:blood<id:vital liquid>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|blood}}, from {{inh|en|ang|blōd}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*blōd}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*blōþą}}, possibly from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*bʰel-||}} ("to swell") + -ó- (thematic vowel) + -to (nominalizer), i.e. "that which bursts out".

chain: bone, tusk; the bone of a limb
cogs: break through, break into pieces, shatter
straight, right, favourable, advantageous, convenient, friendly, fair, keen
straight, direct, easy to deal with
bone.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:bon}} From {{inh|en|enm|bon}}, from {{inh|en|ang|bān|t=bone, tusk; the bone of a limb}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*bainą|t=bone}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*bainaz|t=straight}}, possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰeyh₂-|t=to hit, strike, beat}}.

skin.raw: {{etymon|en|id=layer|:inh|enm:skyn<id:skin>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|skyn}}, {{m|enm|skinn}}, from {{inh|en|ang|scinn}}, from {{der|en|non|skinn|t=animal hide}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*skinþą}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sken-|t=to split off}}, nasal variant of {{m|ine-pro|*skeh₁i-d-||to cut}}. Partially displaced native Old English {{m|ang|hȳd|t=skin, hide}}, from which derives {{l|en|hide}}.

voice.raw: {{etymon|en|id=sound|:inh|enm:voys}} {{dercat|en|itc-pro|ine-pro}} From {{inh|en|enm|voice}}, {{m|enm|voys}}, {{m|enm|vois}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|[[voiz]], [[voys]], [[voice]]}}, {{der|en|fro|[[vois]], [[voiz]]}} (Modern {{cog|fr|voix}}), from {{der|en|la|vōcem}}, accusative form of {{m|la|vōx|t=voice}}.

sick.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:sik|id=ill|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|sik}}, {{m|enm|sike}}, {{m|enm|seek}}, {{m|enm|seke}}, {{m|enm|seok}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sēoc|t=sick, ill}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*seuk}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*seukaz}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sewg-|t=to be troubled or grieved}}.

fever.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰegʷʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|fever}}, {{m|enm|fevere}}, from {{inh|en|ang|fefer}}, {{m|ang|fefor||fever}} and {{der|en|fro|fievre||fever}}, from {{der|en|la|febris||a fever}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰegʷʰ-||to burn}}. Displaced native {{cog|ang|hriþ||fever}}. Compare also {{cog|stq|Fiewer}}, {{cog|de|Fieber}}, {{cog|da|feber}}, {{cog|sv|feber}}. {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰegʷʰ-}}

cogs: to bluster; to riot; to cough (?)
cough.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|coughen}}, {{m|enm|coghen|t=to cough; to vomit}}{{nb...|coghe, couhen, couwhen, couwe, couwen, couȝen, couȝhen, couȝtthe, couȝwen, coȝen, cowen, cowff, cowghen, cowhen, cowȝen, koghe, kouȝen, kowen|otherforms=1}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*cohhian}} (compare {{cog|ang|cohhetan|t=to bluster; to riot; to cough (?)}}), from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*kuh-|t=to cough}}, ultimately of {{glossary|onomatopoeic}} origin.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''v.''{{sup|1}}|noformat=1|id=1058916649|date=July 2023|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=v}}</ref>

chain: the healing art, medicine, a physician's shop, a remedy, medicine
medicine.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*med-}} From {{inh|en|enm|medicin}}, from {{der|en|frm|medicine}}, from {{der|en|fro|medecine}}, from {{der|en|la|medicīna||the healing art, medicine, a physician's shop, a remedy, medicine}}, feminine of {{m|la|medicīnus||of or belonging to physic or surgery, or to a physician or surgeon}}, from {{m|la|medicus||a physician, surgeon}}. The extended sense of "Indigenous magic" is a {{calque|en|oj|mashkiki||medicine|nocap=1}} or {{m|oj|mide}} (or cognates in {{w|Algonquian languages|related languages}}) when used in compounds such as [[Grand Medicine Society]], [[medicine lodge

chain: bloodmoney, weregild, fine, price paid, penalty
pain.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*kʷey-|id=pay}} From {{inh|en|enm|peyne}}, {{m|enm|payne}}, from {{der|en|fro|-}} and {{der|en|xno|peine|peine, paine}}, from {{der|en|la|poena||punishment, pain}}, from {{der|en|grc|ποινή||bloodmoney, weregild, fine, price paid, penalty}}, from {{der|en|grk-pro|*kʷoinā́}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kʷoynéh₂|t=payment}} (whence also {{cog|sla-pro|*cěnà|t=price}}).

cogs: to push, bump, attack, storm, invade
hurt.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|hurten}}, {{m|enm|hirten}}, {{m|enm|hertan|t=to injure, scathe, knock together}}, from {{der|en|fro-nor|hurter}} {{gloss|"to ram into, strike, collide with"; > Modern {{cog|fr|heurter}}}}, perhaps from {{der|en|frk|*hūrt|t=a battering ram}}, cognate with {{cog|cy|hwrdd|t=ram}} and {{cog|kw|hordh|t=ram}}. Compare {{cog|gem-pro|*hrūtaną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*hreutaną|t=to fall, beat}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*krew-|t=to fall, beat, smash, strike, break}}; however, the earliest instances of the verb in Middle English are as old as those found in Old French, which leads to the possibili

rest.raw: {{etymon|en|id=relief|:inh|enm:reste|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|rest}}, {{m|enm|reste}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ræst}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*rastu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*rastō}}, of uncertain origin; possibly derived from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₁reh₁-|t=to rest}} or {{m|ine-pro|*Hre(h₁)s-|t=to flow, rush}}. Cognate with {{cog|fy|rêst|t=rest}}, {{cog|nl|rust|t=rest}}, {{cog|de|Rast|t=rest}}, {{cog|sv|rast|t=rest}}, {{cog|no|rest|t=rest}}, {{cog|is|röst|t=rest}}, {{cog|sga|árus|t=dwelling}}, {{cog|de|Ruhe|t=calm}}, {{cog|sq|resht|t=to stop, pause}}, {{cog|cy|araf|t=quiet, calm, gentle}}, {{cog|lt|ro

wake.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*weǵ-}} A merger of two related verbs of similar form and meaning: * {{inh|en|enm|waken}}, {{inh|en|ang|wacan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wakan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wakaną}}. * {{inh|en|enm|wakien}}, {{inh|en|ang|wacian}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wakēn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wakāną}}.

wash.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:waschen|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|wasshen,waschen||to wash}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wascan||to wash}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*waskan||to wash}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*waskaną,*watskaną||to wash, get wet}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wed-||wet, water}}.

brush.raw: [[File:Brush (PSF).jpg|thumb|Two kinds of '''brushes'''.|upright=1.15]] {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:brusshe<ety:bor<fro:broisse<ety:inh<la-vul:*brustia<ety:bor<frk:*bursti>>>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|brusshe}}, from {{der|en|fro|broisse}} (Modern {{cog|fr|brosse}}), from {{der|en|la-vul|*brustia}}, from {{der|en|frk|*bursti}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*burstiz|t=bristle}}, or also {{der|en|la-vul|*bruscia}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*bruskaz|t=tuft, thicket, underbrush}}, which could be from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰrusgo-}}.<ref>{{R:gem:EDPG|bruska|80}}</ref>

comb.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|comb}}, from {{inh|en|ang|camb||comb}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kamb}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kambaz||comb}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*ǵómbʰos||tooth}}, a {{doublet|nocap=1|en|cam}}. The verb is derived from the noun and displaced the older verb {{m|en|kemb}}.

deaf.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:def}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰewbʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|def}}, {{m|enm|deef}}, from {{inh|en|ang|dēaf}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*daub||deaf}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*daubaz||deaf or stunned}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*dʰewbʰ-||to whisk, smoke, darken, obscure}}. Cognate with {{cog|grc|τυφλός||blind}}. See also {{m|en|dumb}}. {{doublet|en|daff|dof|dowf}}.

fit.raw: {{ety|en|id=suitable|:inh|enm:fit<t:an adversary of equal power><unc>|tree=1}} Possibly from {{inh|en|enm|fit||an adversary of equal power}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} further origin. The original sense appears to have been "to marshal or deploy troops", which shifted to "to suit (troops to a certain location" > "suitable", and may be further related to {{cog|is|fitja|t=to web, knit, cast on}}.<ref>https://www.etymonline.com/word/fit#etymonline_v_5980</ref>

tongue.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|tongue}}, a late spelling of {{m|enm|tonge|tong(e)|id=tongue}}, {{m|enm|tunge|tung(e)}}, from {{inh|en|ang|tunge}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*tungā||tongue}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*tungǭ||tongue}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s||tongue}}. {{doublet|en|langue|lingua}}. {{col-top|3|cog}} * Germanic: {{cog|fy|tonge}}, {{cog|nl|tong}}, {{cog|lb|Zong}}, {{cog|de|Zunge}}, {{cog|da,nb,nn|tunge}}, {{cog|fo,is,sv|tunga}}, {{cog|got|𐍄𐌿𐌲𐌲𐍉}}. * Italic: {{cog|ast,ca|llengua}}, {{cog|an|luenga}}, {{cog|fr|langue}}, {{cog|gl,it,la|lingua}}, {{cog|roa-leo|llingua}}, {{cog|mwl|lhéngua}}, {

neck.raw: {{ety|en|id=bodypart|:inh|enm:nekke|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|nekke}}, {{m|enm|nakke}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hnecca}}, {{m|ang|*hnæcca|t=neck, nape}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hnakkō}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hnakkô|t=nape, neck}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*knog-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*kneg-|t=back of the head, nape, neck}}.

match.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:macche|id=pairing}} From {{inh|en|enm|macche}}, {{m|enm|mecche}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mæċċa}}, {{m|ang|ġemæċċa|t=companion, mate, wife, one suited to another}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*makkjō}}, {{m|gmw-pro|*gamakkjō|t=partner, equal}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*makô}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*mag-|t=to knead, work}}. Compare {{cog|da|mage|t=mate}}, {{cog|is|maki|t=spouse}}.

hobby.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|hoby|t=small horse, pony}}, a variant or alteration of {{m|enm|hobyn|t=a small ambling horse}}, of {{unc|en|title=uncertain and disputed origin}}. According to one theory the term is derived from ''Hobin'', a pet name of {{m|en|Robert}} or {{m|en|Robin}}, at the time frequently used as a [[proper name]] for a workhorse (compare {{m|en|dobbin}}).

guitar.raw: {{etymon|en|id=instrument|:bor|es:guitarra<id:instrument>|tree=1}} From {{bor|en|es|guitarra}}, from {{der|en|ar|قِيثَارَة}}, from {{der|en|grc|κῐθᾰ́ρᾱ}}. {{doublet|en|cithara|cither|zither}}, but not related to {{m|en|sitar}}.

flute.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|fleute}}, {{m|enm|floute}}, {{m|enm|flote}}, from {{der|en|fro|flaute}}, {{m|fro|fleüte}}, from {{der|en|oc-pro-old|flaut|flaüt}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin. Perhaps ultimately from three possibilities: * Blend of Provencal {{m|oc|flaujol|t=flageolet}} + {{m|oc|laüt|t=[[lute]]}} * From Latin {{m|la|flātus|t=blowing}}, from {{m|la|flāre|t=to blow}} * Imitative. {{doublet|en|flauta|fluyt}}.

film.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:filme|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|filme}}, from {{inh|en|ang|filmen|t=film, membrane, thin skin, foreskin}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*filmīn-}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*filmīn-|t=thin skin, membrane}} (compare {{cog|gem-pro|*felma-|t=skin, hide}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro||*pél-mo-|t=membrane}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*pel-|t=to cover, skin}}. Cognate with {{cog|ofs|filmene|t=thin skin, human skin}}, {{cog|dum|velm}}, {{m|dum|vilm|t=fleece, film, membrane}}, {{cog|goh|felm|t=peel, skin, wrap}}, {{cog|ang|*felma}} (in {{m|ang|ǣġerfelma|t=egg membrane}}). Related also to {{cog|nl|vel|t=she

chess.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*tek- (receive)}} {{ety|en|id=Q718|:inh|enm:ches|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|ches}}, {{m|enm|chesse}}, from {{der|en|fro|eschés}}, plural of {{m|fro|eschec}}, from {{der|en|la-med|scaccus}}, from {{der|en|ar|شَاه||king [in chess]}}, from {{der|en|fa-cls|شاه|tr=šāh||[[shah]], king}}, from {{der|en|pal|𐭬𐭫𐭪𐭠|ts=šāh}}, from {{der|en|peo|𐏋|ts=xšāyaθiya}}.

rope.raw: {{etymid|en|cord}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁reyp-}} From {{inh|en|enm|rop|id=rope}}, {{m|enm|rope}}, from {{inh|en|ang|rāp|t=rope, cord, cable}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*raip}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*raipaz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*raipą|t=rope, cord, band, ringlet}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₁roypnós|t=strap, band, rope}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*h₁reyp-|t=to peel off, tear; border, edge, strip}}.

cogs: to crush, pound, pound in mortar, stamp
stamp.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:stampen|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|stampen||to pound, crush}}, from assumed {{inh|en|ang|*stampian}}, variant of {{cog|ang|stempan||to crush, pound, pound in mortar, stamp}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*stampōn}}, {{m|gmw-pro|*stampijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*stampōną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*stampijaną||to trample, beat}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*stemb-||to trample down}}.

chain: head, face; appearance; reception, hospitality; meal, dinner, food
cheer.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:chere}} From {{inh|en|enm|chere}}, from {{der|en|xno|chere}}, from {{der|en|fro|chiere||head, face; appearance; reception, hospitality; meal, dinner, food}} (obsolete Modern {{cog|fr|chère|id=visage}}—not related to {{m|fr|cher||dear}}), from {{der|en|la-lat|cara||head|id=head}}. The verb is derived from the noun.

tennis.raw: {{ety|en|tree=1|:inh|enm:tennys//teneys//tenis<ety:der<fro:tenir<alt:tenir, ~nez>>>}} From {{inh|en|enm|tennys,teneys,tenis}}, from {{der|en|fro|tenez|pos={{lg|second person|second-person}} {{lg|plural number|plural}} {{lg|imperative mood|imperative}} of {{m|fro|tenir|t=to hold}}}}.

grey.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰreh₁-}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:grey|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|grey}}, from {{inh|en|ang|grēġ}} (Anglian). The spelling {{m|en|grey}} reflects the Anglian vowel development, whereas the variant {{m|en|gray}} stems from the West Saxon form {{m|ang|grǣġ}} (through Middle English {{m|enm|gray}}). Further derived from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*grēwaz}} (compare {{cog|nl|grauw}}, {{cog|de|grau}}, {{cog|non|grár}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ǵʰreh₁-||to green, to grow}} (compare {{cog|la|rāvus||grey}}, {{cog|cu|зьрѭ||to see, to glance}}, {{cog|ru|зреть||to watch, to look at}} (archaic), {{co

gray.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰreh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|gray}}, from {{inh|en|ang|grǣġ}} (West Saxon). The spelling {{m|en|gray}} reflects the West Saxon vowel development, whereas the variant {{m|en|grey}} stems from the Anglian form {{m|ang|grēġ}} (through Middle English {{m|enm|grey}}). Further derived from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*grāu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*grēwaz|t=grey}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ǵʰreh₁-|t=to green, to grow}}.

chain: line, cable, rope, hawser, series, row, rule, direction
line.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|id=path|enm:line<id:rope>|:influence|frm:ligne|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|line}}, {{m|enm|lyne}}, from {{inh|en|ang|līne||line, cable, rope, hawser, series, row, rule, direction}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*līnā}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*līnǭ||line, rope, flaxen cord, thread}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*līną||flax, linen}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*līno-||flax}}. Influenced in {{m+|enm|-|w=1}} by {{m|frm|ligne||line}}, from {{m|la|linea}}. More at {{m|en|linen}}.

point.raw: {{ety|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:poynt}} From {{inh|en|enm|poynt}}, from {{der|en|fro|point|g=m||dot; minute amount}}, from {{der|en|la|pūnctum|t=a hole punched in; a point, puncture}}, substantive use of {{m|la|pūnctus|g=m}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|pungō|t=to prick, punch}}; alternatively, from {{der|en|fro|pointe|g=f||sharp tip}}, from {{der|en|la|pūnctus|pūncta|g=f|pos=past participle}}, all from {{der|en|itc-pro|*pungō|t=to sting, prick}}.

round.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|round}}, {{m|enm|rounde}}, from {{der|en|fro-nor|rount|roünt}}, {{m|fro|rund}}, {{der|en|fro|ront}}, {{m|fro|runt}}, {{m|fro|reont}} ( > {{cog|fr|rond}}), from both {{der|en|la-lat|retundus}} and the original {{der|en|la|rotundus}}. The noun developed partly from the adjective and partly from the corresponding French noun {{m|fr|rond}}. {{dbt|en|rotund}}.

pink.raw: [[File:Color icon pink.svg|thumb|Various shades of '''pink''']] [[File:Gartennelke 1.jpg|thumb|'''Pinks''': carnation cultivars]] [[File:Sundays on Columbia Rd (Unsplash).jpg|thumb|Two doors in different shades of '''pink''' (left: [[peach]], right: [[bubblegum]])]] Origin {{unc|en|nocap=1}}; perhaps from {{cog|nl|pinken|t=to blink}} or the English verb {{m|en|pink#Etymology 6|pink}} from the same source.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pink|v.2|144212|June 2006}}</ref> Perhaps from the notion of the petals being {{m|en|pink#Etymology 4|pinked}}. An earlier word for similar flesh-like colors, mostly displa

mutton.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|motoun}}, {{m|enm|moton}}, from {{der|en|fro|mouton||sheep}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|moltō}}, from {{der|en|cel-gau|*multon-}}, from {{der|en|cel-pro|*moltos||ram, wether}}. {{doublet|en|mouton}}.

butter.raw: {{PIE word|en|gʷṓws}} {{etymon|en|id=dairy|:inh|enm:buter|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*tewh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|buter}}, {{m|enm|butter}}, from {{inh|en|ang|butere}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*buterā}}, from {{der|en|la|būtȳrum}}, from {{der|en|grc|βούτῡρον||cow cheese}}, compound of {{m|grc|βοῦς||ox, cow}} and {{m|grc|τῡρός||cheese}}.

sugar.raw: {{etymon|en|id=sugar sugar|:inh|enm:sugre|tree=1|text=++}} Akin to {{cog|grc|κρόκη||pebble}}, whence the words {{m|en|crocodile}} and {{m|en|krokodil}} are derived. {{doublet|en|jaggery|sucro-}}.

chocolate.raw: {{etymon|en|id=cocoa bean candy|:bor|es:chocolate<id:cocoa bean candy>|tree=2}} {{bor+|en|es|chocolate}}, from {{der|en|nci|chocolātl}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin. See that entry for more information.

pie.raw: {{dercat|en|itc-pro|ine-pro}} From {{inh|en|enm|pye}}, {{m|enm|pie}}, {{m|enm|pey|t=baked dish, filled pastry}}, possibly attested earlier ({{circa2|1199|short=yes}}) in the surname {{m|enm|Piehus|gloss=pie-house?}}. Further origin {{unc|en|title=uncertain}}.

jam.raw: First attested in the early 18th c. as a verb meaning “to press, be pressed, be wedged in”. Compare dialectal {{m|en|jammock|t=to press, squeeze, crush into a soft mass, chew food"; also "a soft, pulpy substance}}. Perhaps from {{inh|en|enm|chammen}}, {{m|enm|champen}} {{gl|"to bite upon something, gnash the teeth"; whence modern {{m|en|champ}}, {{m|en|chomp}}}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin; probably originally {{onomatopoeic|en|title=onomatopoeic}}.

honey.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|hony|hony, honi}}, from {{inh|en|ang|huniġ}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hunag}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hunagą}} (compare {{cog|stq|Hunich}}, {{cog|fy|hunich}}, {{cog|nds-de|Honnig}}, {{cog|de|Honig}}), from earlier {{m|gem-pro|*hunangą}} (compare {{cog|frr|honning}}, {{m|frr|hönning}}, {{cog|fy|huning}}, {{cog|nl|honing}}, {{cog|da,nb,nn|honning}}, {{cog|sv|honung}}, {{cog|fo|hunangur}}, {{cog|is|hunang}}), from {{inh|en|ine-pro||*kn̥h₂onk-o-s}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*kn̥h₂ónks}}.

snack.raw: {{ety|en|:bor|dum:snacken<ety:uder<gmw-pro:*snakkōn<ety:inh<gem-pro:*snakkōną>>>>}} From {{bor|en|dum|snacken|t=to snack}}, possibly from {{der|en|gem-pro|*snakkōną||to smack one's lips, open one's mouth to eat; to snatch (with one's mouth?), snack on}}, whence also {{dbt|en|''[[snack#Etymology_2|etymology 2]]''|notext=1}}; ultimately {{onomatopoeic|en|nocap=1|nocat=1}}. Cognate with {{cog|de|schnäken|t=to snack}}. More at {{l+|gem-pro|*snak-}}.

chain: measure, time, occasion, set time, time for eating, meal

onion.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|onyoun}}, {{m|enm|oynoun}}, from {{der|en|fro|oignon}}, from {{der|en|la|ūniōnem}}, accusative of {{m|la|unio#Etymology 3|ūniō|t=onion}}, which had also been borrowed into Old English as {{m|ang|yne}}, {{m|ang|ynnelēac|t=onion}} (> {{cog|enm|hynne-leac}}, {{m|enm|henne-leac}}). Displaced the inherited term {{m|en|ramsons}}. * {{sense|soy}} Stems from a {{w|4chan}} [[wordfilter|word filter]] which changes the word {{m|en|soy}} to ''onions''. cucumber.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|cucumer}}, {{m|enm|cucumber}}, from {{der|en|fro|cocombre}}, ultimately from {{der|en|la|cucumis|cucumis, cucumerem}} (possibly through an {{der|en|pro|-}} intermediate). Probably of Pre-Italic {{der|en|qfa-sub}} origin. {{etydate|late 14c.}} Displaced native {{ncog|en|earthapple}} (see which for more), which has since acquired other senses.

mushroom.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:muscheron|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|muscheron}}, {{m|enm|musseron|}}, from {{der|en|xno|musherum}}, {{m|fro|moscheron}}, from {{der|en|fro|moisseron}}, of {{unk|en|title=obscure}} origin: probably derived from {{der|en|fro|mosse}}, {{m|fro|moise}} {{gl|"moss"; whence also {{m+|fr|mousse}}}}, as the use first applied to a type of fungus which grows in moss, from {{der|en|frk|*mosu|t=moss}} or {{der|en|odt|*mosa|t=moss}}, akin to {{cog|goh|mosa|t=moor, swamp}}, {{cog|goh|mos|t=moss, bog}}, {{cog|goh|mios|t=moss, mire}}, {{cog|ang|mēos|t=moss}}, {{cog|ang|mōs|t=bog, marsh}},

drink.raw: {{etymon|en|id=verb|:inh|enm:drynken}} {{inh+|en|enm|drynken}}, {{m|enm|drinken}}, from {{inh|en|ang|drincan|t=to drink, swallow up, engulf}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*drinkan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*drinkaną|t=to drink}}, of uncertain origin; possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰrenǵ-|t=to draw into one's mouth, sip, gulp}}, nasalised variant of {{m|ine-pro|*dʰreǵ-|t=to draw, glide}}.

cola.raw: {{etymon|en|id=kola|:der|nic:-}} From a {{der|en|nic}} language, compare {{cog|tem|kola}}, {{cog|mnk|kola}}. The beverage "[[Coca-Cola]]" was what made the term widely known, and popularized the spelling with ''c'' instead of ''k''.

yogurt.raw: {{etymon|en|id=food|:bor|ota:یوغورت<id:yogurt><tr:yoğurt>|tree=1}} {{bor+|en|ota|یوغورت|tr={{l|tr|yoğurt}}}}.<ref>{{R:Merriam-Webster Online}}</ref><ref>{{R:Dictionary.com}} (including ''The American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language'', fourth edition, 2004)</ref><ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref> Ultimately from {{der|en|trk-pro|*yogrut}}.

glass.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:glas}} From {{inh|en|enm|glas}}, from {{inh|en|ang|glæs}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*glas}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*glasą}}, possibly related to {{cog|gem-pro|*glōaną||to shine}} (compare {{m|en|glow}}), and ultimately from the {{der|en|ine-pro|-}} root {{m|ine-pro|*ǵʰleh₁-||to shine, shimmer, glow}}.

dish.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|dissh}}, {{m|enm|disch}}, from {{inh|en|ang|disċ|t=plate; bowl; dish}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*disk|t=table; dish}} (whence also {{m+|sla-pro|*dъska}}, whence {{cog|bg|дъска́}}, {{cog|pl|deska}}, {{cog|ru|доска́}}), {{cog|ru|чан}}) from {{der|en|la|discus}}. {{doublet|en|dais|desk|disc|discus|disk|diskos}}.

order.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂er-}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:ordre<ety:der<fro:ordne<ety:inh<la:ōrdō<alt:ōrdinem>>>>>|tree=++}} From {{inh|en|enm|ordre}}, from {{der|en|fro|ordre}}, {{m|fro|ordne}}, {{m|fro|ordene||order, rank}}, from {{der|en|la|ōrdinem}}, accusative of {{m|la|ōrdō||row, rank, regular arrangement|lit=row of threads in a loom}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*ordō||to arrange}}, probably ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro||*h₂or-d-}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*h₂er-}}.
