ail.raw: {{inh+|en|enm|eilen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|eġlan}}, {{m|ang|eġlian||to trouble, afflict}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*aglijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*aglijaną|t=to trouble, vex}}, cognate with {{cog|got|𐌰𐌲𐌻𐌾𐌰𐌽||to distress}}.

anchor.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:anker|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|anker}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ancor}}, {{m|ang|ancra}}, from {{der|en|la|ancora}}, from (or cognate with) {{der|en|grc|ἄγκυρα}}. The modern form is a sixteenth-century modification after the {{cog|la-med|-}} spelling {{m|la|anchora}}. {{doublet|en|ancora|anker|angora|Ankara}}.

ancient.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|auncien}}, from {{der|en|fro|ancien}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*anteānus}}, composed of {{der|en|la|ante||before}} + {{m|la|-ānus|pos=adjective-forming suffix}}. The non-etymological {{glossary|excrescent}} /t/ is by analogy with the common ending {{m|en|-ent}}.

chain: grief, pain, trouble, affliction, vexation, sorrow, wrath
anger.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂enǵʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|anger|t=grief, pain, trouble, affliction, vexation, sorrow, wrath}}, from {{der|en|non|angr}}, {{m|non|ǫngr|t=affliction, sorrow}} (compare {{cog|non|ang}}, {{m|non|ǫng|t=troubled}}), from {{der|en|gem-pro|*angazaz|t=grief, sorrow}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂enǵʰ-|t=narrow, tied together}}.

attach.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:attachen<ety:bor<fro:atachier>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|attachen}}, from {{der|en|fro|atachier}}, variant of {{m|fro|estachier||bind}}, derived from {{m|fro|estache||stick}}, from {{der|en|frk|*stakkā}}, {{m|frk|*stakō|t=stick}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*stakô|t=pole, bar, stick, stake}}. {{doublet|en|attack}}. More at {{m|en|stake}}, {{m|en|stack}}.

attack.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|fr:attaque|tree=1}} {{bor+|en|fr|attaque}}, derived from the verb {{m|fr|attaquer}}, from {{der|en|it|attaccare|t=to join, attach}} (used in {{m|it||attaccare battaglia|t=to join battle}}), from {{der|en|frk|*stakkijan|t=to stick, stick to, attach}}. {{doublet|en|attach}}. Displaced native {{ncog|enm|onresen}}, from {{ncog|ang|onrǣsan|t=to attack}}; and {{ncog|enm|resinge|t=an assault, attack}} (compare {{m+|ang|onrǣs|t=an attack}}).

badge.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰewgʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|badge}}, {{m|enm|bagge}}, {{m|enm|bage}}, {{m|enm|bagy}}, from {{der|en|xno|bage}} or {{der|en|la-med|bagea}}, {{m|la|bagia|t=sign, emblem}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin. Possibly derived from {{der|en|la-med|baga|t=ring}}, from {{der|en|osx|bāg}}, {{m|osx|bōg|t=ring, ornament}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*baugaz|t=ring, bracelet, armband}}; or possibly the Anglo-Norman word is derived from an earlier, unattested English word (compare {{cog|ang|bēag|t=ring, bracelet, collar, crown}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|bagie}}, {{m|sco|badgie}}, {{m|sco|bawgy|t=b

bathe.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰeh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|bathen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|baþian||to bathe, wash}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*baþōn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*baþōną||to bathe}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰeh₁-||to warm}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|boadje||to bathe}}, {{cog|nl|baden||to bathe}}, {{cog|nds-de|baden||to bathe}}, {{cog|de|baden||to bathe}}, {{cog|da|bade||to bathe}}, {{cog|sv|bada||to bathe}}, {{cog|is|baða||to bathe}}. More at {{m|en|bath}}. Compare also {{m|en|bask}}.

bead.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷʰedʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|bede||a prayer}}, also “a bead for counting prayers” in {{m|enm|[[a]] [[peire]] [[of]] [[bede]]s|lit=a pair of beads}}, from {{der|en|ang|bedu}}, {{m|ang|bed}}, {{m|ang|ġebed||a request, entreaty, prayer}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*bedu}}, {{m|gmw-pro|*bed}}, {{m|gmw-pro|*gabed}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*bedō}}, {{m|gem-pro|*bedą}}.

beak.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|bec}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|bec}}, {{der|en|fro|bec}}, from {{der|en|la|beccus}}, from {{der|en|cel-gau|*bekkos}}, from {{der|en|cel-pro|*bekkos||beak, snout}}, possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bak-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*baḱ-||pointed stick, peg}}. Cognate with {{cog|br|beg||beak}}. Compare {{cog|stq|Bäk||mouth; muzzle; beak}}; Dutch {{m|nl|bek||beak; bill; neb}}.

beat.raw: {{ety|en|id=stroke|:inh|enm:beten|tree=+}} {{inh+|en|enm|beten}}, from {{der|en|ang|bēatan|t=to beat, pound, strike, lash, dash, thrust, hurt, injure}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*bautan}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*bautaną|t=to push, strike}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|nl|boten}}, {{m|nl|botten}}, {{m|nl|butten|t=to push, strike}}, {{cog|de|boßen|t=to thrash}}, {{cog|got|*𐌱𐌰𐌿𐍄𐌰𐌽|t=to beat, strike}} (whence, probably, {{cog|gl,pt|botar|t=to expel; to throw}}); also {{cog|la|fūstis|t=club, cudgel, knobbed stick, staff}}, {{m|la|*fūtō|t=to strike}}, {{cog|sq|bahe}}, {{m|sq|hobe|t=sling}}, {{

chain: to come (to), approach, arrive, enter, meet with, fall in with; happen, befall; befit
cogs: to come, arrive, reach a destination
become.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷem-}} A compound of the sources of {{af|en|be-|come}}. From {{inh|en|enm|becomen}}, {{m|enm|bicumen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|becuman|t=to come (to), approach, arrive, enter, meet with, fall in with; happen, befall; befit}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*bikwemaną||to come around, come about, come across, come by}}, equivalent to {{prefix|en|be|t1=about, around|come}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|becum||to come, arrive, reach a destination}}, {{cog|frr|bekommen}}, {{m|frr|bykommen||to come by, obtain, receive}}, {{cog|fy|bikomme||to come by, obtain, receive}}, {{cog|nl|bekomen||to come by,

beige.raw: {{ubor|en|fr|(dialectal) [[beige]]}}, from {{der|en|fro|bege||color of undyed wool or cotton}}, from an Alpine language (compare Franco-Provençal {{m|frp|bézho}}, Romansch {{m|rm|besch||dull grey}}), from {{der|en|la-vul|*bysseus||cottony grey}} (compare {{cog|fr|bis}}, {{cog|ca|bis}}, {{cog|it|bigio|bigio}}), from {{der|en|la-lat|byssus|t=cotton}}, from {{der|en|grc|βύσσος|t=cotton homespun}}, from {{der|en|sem}} (compare {{der|en|he|-}}/{{der|en|arc|-}} {{m|he|בוץ||tr=būṣ}}). {{doublet|en|bice}}.

cogs: to hold dear, valuable, or satisfactory, approve of, believe
believe.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:bileven|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|beleven}}, {{m|enm|bileven}}, from {{inh|en|ang|belīefan|t=to believe}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*bilaubijan|t=to believe}}, equivalent to {{af|en|be-|leave|t2=to give leave or permission to, permit, allow, grant}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|beleve|t=to believe}}, {{cog|ofs|bilēva|t=to permit}}, {{cog|dum|beloven|t=to believe, entrust}}, {{cog|gml|belö̂ven|t=to believe}}, {{cog|gmh|belouben|t=to believe}}.

bet.raw: From 16th-century criminal slang, perhaps from {{inh|en|enm|bet|t=something better, advantage, luck}}, from {{inh|en|ang|bet}}, {{m|enm|bett|t=better|pos=adverb}}; or, alternatively from {{m|en|abet}}, from {{inh|en|enm|abet}}, {{m|enm|abette}}, from {{der|en|fro|abet|t=incitement to evil}}, from {{der|en|fro|abeter|t=to entice}}, from {{m|fro|a-||to}} + {{m|fro|beter|t=hound on, urge, to bait}}; ultimately from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*baitijan|t=to bait, entice}}, related to {{cog|ang|bǣtan|t=to bait}}. More at {{l|en|abet}}.

branch.raw: [[File:Acacia constricta branch.jpg|thumb|Tree branches]] {{dercat|en|cel}} From {{inh|en|enm|branche}}, {{m|enm|braunche}}, {{m|enm|bronche}}, from {{der|en|fro|branche}}, {{m|fro|branke}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|branca|t=footprint”, later also “paw, claw}} (whence {{cog|gmh|pranke}}, {{cog|de|Pranke|t=paw}}), of {{unk|en|title=unknown}} origin.

break.raw: {{etymon|en|id=separate|:inh|enm:breken|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|breken}}, from {{inh|en|ang|brecan||to break}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*brekan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*brekaną||to break}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*bʰreg-||to break}}. {{doublet|en|bray}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognates of Germanic origin include {{cog|sco|brek||to break}}, {{cog|fy|brekke||to break}}, {{cog|nl|breken||to break}}, {{cog|nds|breken||to break}}, {{cog|de|brechen||to break}}, {{cog|fr|broyer||to crush, grind}}, {{cog|got|𐌱𐍂𐌹𐌺𐌰𐌽|t=to break, destroy}}, {{cog|no|brek||desire, yearning}}.

breathe.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:brethen<ety:der<breeth>>}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰreh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|brethen|t=to breathe, blow, exhale, odour}}, derived from {{der|en|enm|breth|t=breath}}. Eclipsed {{noncog|enm|ethien}} and {{m|enm|orðiæn}}, from {{noncog|ang|ēþian}} and {{m|ang|orþian|t=to breathe}}; as well as {{noncog|enm|anden}}, {{m|enm|onden}}, from {{noncog|non|anda|t=to breathe}}. More at {{l|en|breath}}.

chain: broad, flat, open, extended, spacious, wide, ample, copious
broad.raw: {{etymon|en|id=wide|:inh|enm:brod<id:wide>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|brood}}, {{m|enm|brode}}, from {{inh|en|ang|brād|t=broad, flat, open, extended, spacious, wide, ample, copious}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*braid}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*braidaz|t=broad, wide}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|yol|brode|t=broad}}, {{cog|frr|bread}}, {{m|frr|breeđ}}, {{m|frr|briad}}, {{m|frr|briid}}, {{m|frr|briidj|t=wide}}, {{cog|stq,fy|breed|t=broad, wide}}, {{cog|bar|brad}}, {{m|bar|broad|t=broad, wide}}, {{cog|gmw-cfr,lb|breet|t=broad, wide}}, {{cog|nl|breed|t=broad, wide

bubble.raw: Partly {{onom|en|title=imitative}}, also influenced by {{m|en|burble}}. Compare {{cog|dum|bobbe||bubble}} > {{cog|nl|bubbel||bubble}}, {{cog|nds|bubbel||bubble}}, {{cog|da|boble||bubble}}, {{cog|sv|bubbla||bubble}}. The word was first used in its economic sense in association with the collapse of the {{w|South Sea Company}} in 1720, based on the metaphor of an inflated soap bubble bursting.

bull.raw: {{multiple images | image1 = Taureau charolais au pré.jpg | caption1 = A Charolais bull ({{sno|en|Q693690}}) | image2 = Toro de lidia monument, Tordesillas, Valladolid, Spain - 20050630.jpg | caption2 = A statue of a Spanish fighting bull }}

bush.raw: [[Image:Buxus sempervirens 2.jpg|thumb|right|A bush (woody plant)]] From {{inh|en|enm|bush}}, probably continuing {{inh|en|ang|*busċ}}, {{m|ang|*bysċ}} (possibly reflected in place names), from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*busk}}.

butcher.raw: {{word|en|ine|bʰúǵs}} From {{inh|en|enm|bocher}}, {{m|enm|boucher}}, from {{der|en|fro|bouchier|t=goat slaughterer}}, from {{der|en|fro|bouc|t=goat}}, from {{der|en|la-med|buccus|t=he-goat}}, from {{der|en|frk|*bukk}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*bukkaz|t=male goat, male deer}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰuǵ-|t=buck, ram}}. See also {{cog|en|buck}}.

buzz.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|*bussen}} (suggested by {{m+|enm|bussyng|t=buzzing}}), of [[onomatopoeic]] origin. Cognate with {{cog|sco|bizz|t=to buzz}}. Compare {{cog|enm|bunning|t=buzzing}}, {{cog|enm|hossing|t=buzzing}}, {{noncog|enm|bissen|t=to hush}}.

calm.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|calm}}, {{m|enm|calme}}, from {{der|en|frm|calme}}, probably from {{der|en|roa-oit|calma}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin. {{m|it|calma|Calma}} may derive from {{der|en|la-lat|cauma||heat of the midday sun}}, from {{der|en|grc|καῦμα||heat, especially of the sun}}, from {{m|grc|καίω||to burn}}, or possibly from {{der|en|la|caleō}}. Compare also {{ncog|lng|*chalm}}, {{m|lng|*chalma|t=frozenness}}, ultimately from {{noncog|gem-pro|*kalmaz|t=frozenness, cold}}.

ceiling.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|celing||paneling; (bed) cover or hanging}}, from {{m|enm|celen||to cover or panel walls}} (from {{der|en|fro|celer||to conceal}}) + {{m|enm|-ing|pos=gerund-forming suffix}}. {{surf|en|ceil|-ing}}.

chef.raw: {{ety|en|:ubor|fr:chef|tree=1}} {{ubor|en|fr|chef}} (from the positions of {{m|fr|chef [[d']][[office]]}} and {{m|en|chef de cuisine}}),<ref>{{R:OED Online}}</ref> from {{der|en|fro|chief||head, leader}} (English {{doublet|en|chief|notext=1}}), from {{der|en|la-vul|capus||head}} (from which also {{m|en|captain}}, {{m|en|chieftain}}), from {{der|en|la|caput||head}} (possibly related to English {{m|en|cap||head covering}}).

chew.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵyewh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|chewen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ċēowan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*keuwan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kewwaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ǵyewh₁-}}. Cognate with {{cog|fy|kôgje}}, {{cog|nds|käwwen}}, {{cog|nl|kauwen}}, {{cog|de|kauen}}; also {{cog|la|gingīva||gums}}, {{cog|txb|śuwaṃ||to eat}}, {{cog|pl|żuć||to chew}}, {{cog|fa|جویدن|tr=javidan}}, {{cog|ps|ژُوَل|tr=žovạl|t=to bite, gnaw}}.

chain: group of dancers and singers; dance
group of dancers and singers, choir, chorus; dance accompanied by song; round dance
chorus.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵʰer-|id=enclose}} {{dercat|en|grk-pro|ine-pro}} The {{glossary|noun}} is borrowed from {{bor|en|la-med|chorus|t=church choir}}, {{bor|en|la|chorus|t=group of dancers and singers; dance}}, from {{der|en|grc|χορός|t=group of dancers and singers, choir, chorus; dance accompanied by song; round dance}};<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=32365|date=December 2020|nodot=1}}. {{R:Lexico|pos=n}}</ref> The {{glossary|verb}} is derived from the noun.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=v|id=32366|date=March 2019|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=v}}</ref> {{doublet|en|choir|chore|hora}}.

chain: priest, clergyman, cleric”, also generally “learned man, clerk
clerk.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*kelh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|clerc}}, from {{inh|en|ang|clerc}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|clēricus||priest, clergyman, cleric”, also generally “learned man, clerk}}, from {{der|en|grc|κληρικός|t=of the clergy|pos=adj. in church jargon}}, from {{m|grc|κλῆρος|t=lot, inheritance”, originally “shard used in casting lots}}. {{doublet|en|cleric}}.

cloth.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|cloth}}, {{m|enm|clath}}, from {{inh|en|ang|clāþ|t=cloth, clothes, covering, sail}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*klaiþ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*klaiþą|t=garment}}, perhaps from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gleyt-|t=to cling to, cleave, stick}} (compare {{cog|sq|ngjit|t=to stick, attach, glue}}), a form of {{m|ine-pro|*gleh₁y-|t=to smear; to stick}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|clath|t=cloth}}, {{cog|frr|klaid|t=dress, garment}}, {{cog|stq|Klood|t=dress, apparel}}, {{cog|fy|klaad}}, {{m|fy|kleed|t=cloth, article of clothing}}, {{cog|nl|kleed|t=robe, dress}}, {{cog|nds|kleed|t=dress, garment}}, {{

clothe.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|clothen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*clāþian|t=to clothe}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*klaiþōną|t=to clothe}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gley-|t=to adhere to, stick}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|kleden}}, {{cog|de|kleiden}}, {{cog|sv|kläda}}, after [[apocope]] {{m|sv|klä}}. See also {{m|en|cloth}}, {{m|en|clad}}.

clover.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|clovere}}, {{m|enm|claver}}, from {{inh|en|ang|clāfre}}, earlier {{m|ang|clǣfre}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*klaibrā}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Kleeuwer}},<!--West Frisian "klaver" is from Dutch, thus not relevant here--> {{cog|nds|[[Klaver]], [[Klever]]}}, {{cog|nl|klaver}}, all “clover”. More distantly also related with {{cog|de|Klee}}.

chain: to ball up, clump together; lump, swelling
clue.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*glew-}} Variant of {{m|en|clew|t=a ball of thread or yarn}}, from {{inh|en|enm|clew}}, {{m|enm|clewe}}, {{m|enm|clowe}}, {{m|enm|clue}}, {{m|enm|clwe}}, {{m|enm|clyw}}, {{m|enm|clywe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|clēowen}}, {{m|ang|clīewen}}, {{m|ang|clīowen}}, {{m|ang|clīwen}}, {{m|ang|clȳwe}}, {{m|ang|clȳwen|t=ball, sphere; skein}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kliuwīn|t=ball, clump}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kliuwīną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*klewô|t=bale, ball, clump, mass}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*glew-|t=to ball up, clump together; lump, swelling}}. Sense evolution with reference to the one whi

coin.raw: [[Image:Silver tetradrachm MET DP139641.jpg|thumb|right|An Ancient Greek coin, circa 315–308 BC, made of silver]] [[File:England, Anne, 1702-1714 - Guinea - 1969.204 - Cleveland Museum of Art.tif|thumb|An English coin, 1703, made of gold]] {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:coyn<id:coin>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|coyn}}, from {{der|en|fro|coigne||wedge, cornerstone, die for stamping}}, from {{der|en|la|cuneus||wedge}}. {{doublet|en|coign|cuneus}}. See also {{m|en|quoin||cornerstone}}. Displaced {{ncog|enm|mynt}}, from {{ncog|ang|mynet}} (whence modern {{cog|en|mint}}), which was derived from {{ncog|la|monē

chain: to coincide, to be equal to, to be capable of
compete.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*peth₂-}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|competer}}, from {{der|en|la|competō|competere|t=to coincide, to be equal to, to be capable of}}, from {{m|la|com-||with}} + {{m|la|petō||to seek; to aim for, strive for}}. Compare {{cog|la|competītor||competitor}}.

complete.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*pleh₁-}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:compleet<t:full,complete>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|compleet|t=full, complete}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|complet}} or {{der|en|la|completus}}, past participle of {{m|la|compleō|t=to fill up, to complete}} (whence also {{m|en|complement}}, {{m|en|compliment}}), from {{m|la|com-}} + {{m|la|pleō|t=to fill, to fulfill}} (whence also {{m|en|deplete}}, {{m|en|replete}}, {{m|en|plenty}}), ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*pleh₁-|t=to fill}} ({{cog|en|full}}).

conceit.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:conceyte|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|conceyte}}, formed from {{m|enm|conceyven}} by analogy with pairs such as (Modern English) {{m|en|deceive}}~{{m|en|deceit}}, {{m|en|receive}}~{{m|en|receipt}} etc. {{doublet|en|concept|concetto}}. Akin to {{cog|pt|conceito}}.

conceive.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id=seize}} From {{inh|en|enm|conceyven}}, from {{der|en|fro|concevoir}}, {{m|fro|conceveir}}, from {{der|en|la|concipio|concipiō, concipere|to devise, to conceive}}.

confuse.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵʰewd-}} {{back-formation|en|confused}}, from {{der|en|enm|confused||frustrated, ruined}}, from {{der|en|xno|confus}}, from {{der|en|la|cōnfūsus}}, past participle of {{m|la|cōnfundō}}.

chain: to knock, strike; to search for, procure
conquer.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|conqueren}}, from {{der|en|fro|conquerre}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|conquaero|conquaerere|to knock, strike; to search for, procure}}, from {{der|en|la|con-}} + {{m|la|quaero|quaerere|to seek, acquire}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|oferwinnan}}.

contest.raw: {{PIE word|en|tréyes}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*steh₂-}} From {{der|en|fr|contester}}, from {{der|en|fro|-}}, from {{der|en|la|contestor|t=to call to witness}}.

cot.raw: {{ety|en|:bor|hi:खाट|id=bed}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|hi|खाट}}, from {{der|en|pra-sau|𑀔𑀝𑁆𑀝𑀸}}, from {{der|en|sa|खट्वा||bedstead}}. Ultimately of {{der|en|dra}} origin.

creature.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱer-|id=grow}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:creature<id:a created thing>}} {{inh+|en|enm|creature|id=a created thing|t=a created thing}}, borrowed via {{der|en|fro|creature}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|creātūra|id=creature}}, from {{m|la|creō}}.{{ref|name=COED-etym|{{cite-book|title=The Concise Oxford English Dictionary|edition=eleventh}}}} {{surf|en|create|-ure}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|ġesċeaft}}. {{doublet|en|craythur|critter}}.

crystal.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|crystal}}, {{m|enm|cristal}}, {{m|enm|criȝstall}}, representing a merger of {{inh|en|ang|cristalla}} (from Latin {{m|la|crystallus}}) and {{der|en|xno|cristall}}, {{der|en|fro|cristal}} (from Latin {{m|la|crystallum}}). The Latin is derived from {{der|en|grc|κρύσταλλος||clear ice}}, from {{m|grc|κρύος||frost}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*krews-||hard, hard outer surface, crust}}.

cuff.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|cuffe}}, {{m|enm|coffe|t=glove, mitten}}, of obscure origin. Perhaps from {{inh|en|ang|cuffie|t=hood, cap}}, from {{der|en|la-med|cofia}}, {{m|la|cofea}}, {{m|la|cuffa}}, {{m|la|cuphia|t=helmet, headdress, hood, cap}}, from {{der|en|frk||*kuf(f)ja|t=headdress}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*kuppju}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*kupjō|t=cap}}. Cognate with {{cog|gmh|kupfe|t=cap}}.

cushion.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|quysshyn}}, from later {{der|en|fro|coissin}} (modern {{m|fr|coussin}}), from {{der|en|la-vul|*coxīnus||seat pad}}, derived from {{der|en|la|coxa||hip, thigh}} (with the suffix possibly after {{m+|la|pulvīnus||pillow}}), ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*koḱs-|t=joint, limb}}.

cycle.raw: {{etymon|en|id=cicle|:inh|enm:cicle|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*kʷel-}} From {{inh|en|enm|cicle|t=fixed length period of years}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|cyclus}}, from {{der|en|grc|κύκλος||circle}}, from {{der|en|grk-pro||*kúklos}}, {{m|grk-pro||*kʷókʷlos}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kʷékʷlos||circle, wheel}}.

debt.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰeh₁bʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|dette}}, {{m|enm|dett}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|dete}} ({{cog|fr|dette}}), from {{der|en|la-med|dēbita}}, from {{der|en|la|dēbitum||what is owed, a debt, a duty}}, neuter of {{m|la|dēbitus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|dēbeō||to owe}}, contraction of {{m|la|*dehibeō||I have from}}, from {{m|la|de||from}} + {{m|la|habeō||to have}}. {{doublet|en|debit}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|eofot}}.

deceit.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id=seize}} From {{inh|en|enm|deceyte}}, from {{der|en|fro|deceite}}, {{m|fro|deçoite}}, from {{m|fro|decevoir||to [[deceive]]}}, from {{der|en|la|decipio|dēcipere|to cheat, mislead}}.

deceive.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id=seize}} From {{inh|en|enm|deceyven}}, from {{der|en|xno|deceivre}}, from {{der|en|la|dēcipiō||to deceive; beguile; entrap}}, from {{m|la|dē-||from}} + {{m|la|capiō||to seize}}; see [[captive]]. Compare [[conceive]], [[perceive]], [[receive]]. Displaced native {{cog|ang|beswīcan}}.

deny.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁eǵ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|denyen}}, from {{der|en|fro|denoier||to deny, to repudiate}} ({{cog|fr|dénier}}), from {{der|en|la|denegare||to deny, to refuse}}, from {{m|la|de-||away}} and {{m|la|negare||to refuse}}, the latter ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*né||no, not}}. {{doublet|en|denegate}}.

depot.raw: From {{bor|en|fr|dépôt}}, from {{der|en|fro|depost}}, from {{der|en|la-med|dēpositum}}, from {{der|en|la|-}}, participle of {{m|la|depono|dēpōnō, dēpōnere}}. {{doublet|en|deposit}}.

derby.raw: From {{w|Epsom Derby}} horse race, {{named-after|en|Edward Smith-Stanley, 12th Earl of Derby|wplink==|nocap=1}}. Ultimately from [[Derby]].

detach.raw: From {{der|en|fro|destachier}}, from the same root as {{m|en|attach}}; compare {{cog|fr|détacher}} and Portuguese and Spanish {{m|pt|destacar}}.

die.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|deyen}}, probably from {{der|en|non|deyja}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*dawjaną||to die}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|sweltan}}, whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|swelt}}, and {{noncog|ang|steorfan}}, whence modern {{m|en|starve}}. {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰew-|id=die}}

diet.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|diet}}, {{m|enm|dyet}}, {{m|enm|diete}}, from {{der|en|fro|diete}}, from {{der|en|la-med|dieta||regimen, regulation; assembly}}, from {{der|en|la|diaeta}}, from {{der|en|grc|δίαιτα}}.

different.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:different|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|different}}, from {{der|en|fro|different}}, from {{uder|en|la|differēns}}, present active participle of {{m|la|differō||to differ}}. See also {{m|en|differ}}. Mostly {{lg|displaced|supplanted}} native {{noncog|ang|ungelic}} in common usage, which lives on as {{m|en|unalike}} in {{w|Modern English}}.

digest.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eǵ-|id=drive}} From {{inh|en|enm|digesten|}}, from {{der|en|la|dīgestus|}}, past participle of {{m|la|dīgerō||carry apart}}, from {{m|la|dī-}} (for {{m|la|dis-||apart}}) + {{m|la|gerō||to carry}}, influenced by {{cog|frm|digestion|}}. Partly displaced native {{ncog|ang|meltan}} (intransitive) and {{m|ang|mieltan}} (transitive), both “to melt, to digest,” whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|melt}}.

divide.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:dividen<ety:der<la:dīvidō>>|tree=1}} {{PIE word|en|dwóh₁}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|dividen}}, from {{der|en|la|dīvidō|dīvidere|t=to divide}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|tōdǣlan}} related to {{noncog|en|deal|id=division}} which formerly meant a “portion” or “part” of something.

dodge.raw: Likely from dialectal {{m|en|dodge}}, {{m|en|dod}}, {{m|en|dodd|t=to jog, trudge along, totter", also "to jerk, jig}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin. Perhaps from unrecorded {{inh|en|enm|*dodden}}, ultimately from {{der|en|gem-pro|*dud-|t=to move}}, related to {{cog|ang|dydrian}}, {{m|ang|dyderian|t=to delude, deceive}}, {{cog|enm|dideren|t=to tremble, quake, shiver}}, {{cog|en|dodder}}, {{cog|no|dudra|t=to tremble}}.

doe.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁(y)-}} From {{inh|en|enm|do|id=doe|t=(female) fallow deer}}, from {{inh|en|ang|dā}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*daihā|t=female deer, mother deer}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁(y)-|t=to suck (milk), to suckle}}.

dough.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:dogh|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|dow}}, {{m|enm|dogh}}, {{m|enm|dagh}}, from {{inh|en|ang|dāg}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*daigaz||dough}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*dʰeyǵʰ-||to knead, form, mold}}.

drought.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|droughte}}, {{m|enm|droghte}}, {{m|enm|drouȝte}}, from {{inh|en|ang|drūgaþ}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|droogte}}, {{cog|nds|Dröögde}}. {{surf|+suf|en|dry|t|id2=th|pos2=abstract nominal suffix}}.

due.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰeh₁bʰ-}} From {{der|en|enm|dewe}}, {{m|enm|dew}}, {{m|enm|due}}, from {{der|en|fro|deu|deü|due}}, past participle of {{m|fro|devoir||to owe}}, from {{der|en|la|dēbeō|dēbēre|t=to owe}}, from {{prefix|la|dē|habeō|gloss1=from|t2=to have|nocat=1}}.

ebb.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|ebbe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ebba||ebb, tide}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*abbjā}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*abjô}}, {{m|gem-pro|*abjǭ}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*ab||off, away}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*apó}}.

chain: to entangle, fabricate, to make use of
employ.raw: {{wikidata lexeme|L5510}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*pleḱ-}} From late {{inh|en|enm|emploien}}, {{m|enm|imploien}}, {{m|enm|emplien||to apply to a specific purpose}}, from {{der|en|xno|emploier}}, {{der|en|fro|emploiier||to entangle, fabricate, to make use of}},<ref name="MED">{{R:MED|id=MED13481|entry=emploien|pos=v}}</ref><ref name="MWO">{{R:MWO}}</ref> ultimately from {{der|en|la|implicō|implicāre|to infold, entangle, involve, engage}}, from {{m|la|in-||in}} + {{m|la|plicō|plicāre|to fold}}. {{doublet|en|imply|implicate}}.

employee.raw: From {{suf|en|employ|-ee}}.<ref name="MWO">{{R:MWO}}</ref><ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref> {{etydate|early 19th century}}, possibly modeled after {{der|en|fr|employé}}.<ref name="MWO"/><ref>{{R:OED Online|id=7018874683|noformat=1|pos=''n''.<sup>1</sup>}}</ref>

emu.raw: [[File:Pštros - panoramio.jpg|thumb|Emu ({{taxfmt|Dromaius novaehollandiae|species}}; ''sense 2'')]] {{ety|en|id=bird|:bor<unc>|pt:ema|tree=1}} {{unc|en|Probably}} from {{bor|en|pt|ema|t={{q|originally}} [[rhea]] [[bird]]}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|part of speech=n|id=61455|date=1891|nodot=yes}}; {{R:New English Dictionary|entry=Emeu, emu|volume=III|page=120|column=3}}</ref>

ending.raw: {{etymon|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:endynge}} From {{inh|en|enm|endynge}}, {{m|enm|endyng}}, {{m|enm|endinge}}, from {{inh|en|ang|endung}}, {{m|ang|ġeendung|t=ending}}, equivalent to {{af|en|end|-ing|id2=gerund noun}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|ending|t=ending}}, {{cog|de|Endung|t=ending}}.

engage.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*wedʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|engagen}}, from {{der|en|fro|engagier|t=to pledge, engage}}, from {{der|en|fro|en-|t=in, under}} + {{m|fro|gage|t=pledge}}, from {{der|en|frk|*wadi|t=pledge}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*wadją|t=pledge, guarantee}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wedʰ-|t=to pledge, redeem a pledge; guarantee, bail}}, equivalent to {{af|en|en-|gage}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|weddian|t=to engage, covenant, undertake}}, {{cog|de|wetten|t=to bet, wager}}, {{cog|is|veðja|t=to wager}}. More at {{l|en|wed}}.

chain: one who designs, constructs, or operates military works for attack or defence, etc.; machine designer
cogs: one constructing or using an engine

entertain.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ten-}} From {{inh|en|enm|entertenen}}, from {{der|en|frm|entretenir}}, from {{der|en|fro|entretenir}}, from {{m|fro|entre||among}} + {{m|fro|tenir||to hold}}, from {{der|en|la|inter}} + {{m|la|teneō||hold, keep}}. For the noun, compare {{cog|fr|entretien}}.

estimate.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|estimat}}, {{bor+|enm|la|aestimātus||valuing, estimate|pos=only used in the ablative singular: ''"aestimātū..."'' (in valuing...)|nocap=1|nocat=1}}, from {{af|la|aestimō|-tus|id2=action noun|t2=action noun-forming suffix|nocat=1}}.

fate.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰeh₂-|id=speak}} From {{inh|en|enm|fate}}, from {{der|en|la|fāta||prediction}}, plural of {{m|la|fātum}}, from {{m|la|fātus||spoken}}, from {{m|la|for||to speak}}. In this sense, displaced native {{ncog|ang|wyrd}}, whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|weird}}.

chain: to get and bring back, fetch; to come for, get and take away; to steal; to carry away to kill; to search for; to obtain, procure
cogs: to apprehend, catch; to grasp; to understand
to catch, grasp; to capture, seize
fetch.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ped-}} The {{glossary|verb}} is derived from {{inh|en|enm|fecchen|t=to get and bring back, fetch; to come for, get and take away; to steal; to carry away to kill; to search for; to obtain, procure}} {{nb...|facch, facche, facchen, fach, fache, fæchen, fatche, feccean, fecche, fecchen, fecchenn, fecchyn, fech, fechchen, feche, fechen, fechin, fechyn, fetche, fetchen, fetchyn, focche, focchen, fochche, foche, fotche, vacche, vacchen, vecche, vecchen, vechchen,|otherforms=1}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=fecchen|pos=v|id=MED15419}}</ref> from {{inh|en|ang|feċċan}}, {{m|ang|fæċċan}

floss.raw: {{wp|dental +}} [[Image:Spinning candy floss.jpg|thumb|right|A woman spinning candy floss.]]

fold.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*pel-|id=fold}} The verb is from {{inh|en|enm|folden}}, from {{inh|en|ang|fealdan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*falþan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*falþaną||to fold}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*pel-||to fold}}.

folk.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:folk|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*pleh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|folk}}, from {{inh|en|ang|folc}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*folk}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*fulką}}, possibly from {{inh|en|ine-pro||*pl̥h₁-gós}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*pleh₁-||to fill}}.

forfeit.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|forfait}} from ca. 1300, from {{der|en|fro|forfait||crime}}, originally the past participle of {{m|fro|forfaire||to transgress}}, and {{der|en|la-med|foris factum}}. During the 15th century, the sense shifted from the crime to the penalty for the crime. {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-}}

frolic.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*prew-|*leyg-|id2=like}} From {{der|en|nl|vrolijk||cheerful}}, from {{der|en|dum|vrolijc}}, from {{der|en|odt|frōlīk}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*frawalīkaz}}. Compare {{cog|de|fröhlich||blitheful, gaily, happy, merry}}.

fudge.raw: Probably a variant of {{m|en|fadge||to fit}}, the confectionery sense having evolved from the meaning of “merging together” or “turning out as expected”.

chain: a supply, or the act of furnishing
furniture.raw: From {{uder|en|frm|fourniture||a supply, or the act of furnishing}}, from {{m|frm|fournir||to [[furnish]]}}.

fuzz.raw: {{unc|en}}. Some dictionaries suggest a {{bor|en|gem}} source; compare {{cog|nds|fussig|gloss=loose; spongy}}, {{cog|nl|voos|gloss=unsound; rotten}}. Others, such as ''Webster's New College Dictionary'', suggest a {{back-form|en|fuzzy|nocap=9}}. The ''Oxford English Dictionary'' suggests, “Perhaps {{onomatopoeic|en|title={{glossary|imitative}}}} of the action of blowing away light particles.”

garage.raw: {{ety|en|:bor|fr:garage|tree=1}} {{bor+|en|fr|garage|t=keeping under cover, protection, shelter}}, derivative of {{der|en|fr|garer|t=to keep under cover, dock, shunt, guard, keep}}, from {{der|en|frm|garer}}, {{m|frm|garrer}}, {{m|frm|guerrer}}; partly from {{der|en|fro|garir}}, {{m|fro|warir}} (from Old {{der|en|frk|*warjan}}); and partly from {{der|en|fro|varer|t=to fight, defend oneself, protect}}, from {{der|en|non|varask||to defend oneself}}, reflexive of {{m|non|vara|t=to ware, watch out, defend}}; both ultimately from {{der|en|gem-pro|*warjaną||to defend, ward off}}, {{m|gem-pro|*warōną

garlic.raw: {{inh+|en|enm|garlek}}, {{m|enm|garlik}}, from {{inh|en|ang|gārlēac|t=garlic|lit=spear-leek}}, from {{m|ang|gār}} {{gl|"spear"; in reference to its sharp, tapering leaves}} + {{m|ang|lēac|t=leek}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|garlic|t=garlic}}, {{cog|fo|geirleykur|t=garlic}}, {{cog|is|geirlaukur|t=garlic}}.

gas.raw: {{etymon|en|id=matter|:bor|nl:gas<id:matter>|tree=1}} {{bor+|en|nl|gas}}, {{coin|en|occ=chemist|Jan Baptist van Helmont|nocap=1|nocat=1}} in ''Ortus Medicinae''. Derived from {{der|en|grc|χάος|t=chasm, void, empty space}}; perhaps also inspired by {{m|nl|geest|t=breath, vapour, spirit}}. {{doublet|en|chaos}}. {{etydate|1648}}.

gear.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:gere<id:gear><ety:bor<non:gervi>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|gere}}, a borrowing from {{der|en|non|gervi}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*garwijaną|t=to prepare}}. See also adjective {{m|en|yare}}, {{m|en|yar}} from the same root via Old English.

gecko.raw: [[File:Asian House Gecko female.jpg|thumb|A [[common house gecko]] ({{taxfmt|Hemidactylus frenatus|species}})]] The modern form was probably borrowed into English and other European languages from {{der|en|nl|gekko}} (1718). Contemporary English forms were {{m|en|chacco}} (1711) and {{m|en|jackoa}} (1724). The further origin is not quite clear. Some sources mention a supposed {{der|en|ms|gekok}}, {{m|ms|gekoq}}, or {{m|ms|gekop}}, which would be imitative of the gecko’s [[chirp]]ing sound. Another theory derives it from {{der|en|ace|gèh-gòh||busy}}.

gem.raw: {{inh+|en|enm|gemme}}, {{m|enm|gimme}}, {{m|enm|yimme}}, {{m|enm|ȝimme}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ġimm}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*gimmu|t=gem}} and {{der|en|fro|gemme|t=gem}}, both from {{der|en|la|gemma|t=a swelling bud; jewel, gem}}. {{dbt|en|gemma|Gemma}}.

geyser.raw: {{ety|en|:bor|is:w:Geysir<ety:from<is:geysa>>|tree=1}} From {{bor|en|is|Geysir||Gusher}}, the {{der|en|is|-}} name of a particular [[hot spring]] in [[Iceland]] (see [[w:Geysir|Wikipedia]]), from the verb {{m|is|geysa||to [[gush]]}}, from {{der|en|non|geysa||to [[gush]]}}, which is mentioned in English as early as the 1760s in ''The Annual Register'', as “Geyser, a wonderful spring in the valley of Haukadal”.<ref>{{cite-web |titleurl=http://www.evs-translations.com/blog-com/geyser/ |title=source EVS Translations |accessdate=6 February 2014 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140125013945

ghost.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵʰéysd-}} The {{lg|noun}} is derived from {{inh|en|enm|gost}}, from {{inh|en|ang|gāst}}, {{m|ang|gǣst|t=breath, spirit, soul, ghost}} (compare modern {{cog|en|Holy Ghost}}), from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*gaist}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*gaistaz}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*ǵʰéysdos}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*ǵʰéysd-|t=anger, agitation}}.<ref name="OED">Compare {{R:OED Online|pos=n.'' and ''adj|id=6509148342|date=September 2025|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=n}}</ref>

giant.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:geaunt}} From {{inh|en|enm|geaunt}}, {{m|enm|geant}}, from {{der|en|fro|geant}}, {{m|fro|gaiant}} (Modern {{cog|fr|géant}}) from {{der|en|la-vul|*gagās}}, {{m|la||gagant-}}, from {{der|en|la|gigās}}, {{m|la|gigant-}}, from {{der|en|grc|γίγας||giant}}. Cognate to {{m|en|giga-||1,000,000,000}}. Largely Displaced native {{ncog|ang|ent||giant}}, {{ncog|ang|eoten||giant or [[jötunn]]}}, and {{ncog|ang|þyrs||giant or ogre}}. Compare {{m+|en|ent|t=giant tree-man}}, {{m|en|ettin|t=giant or troll}} and {{m|en|thurse|t=giant}}.

girdle.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰerdʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|girdel}}, {{m|enm|gerdel}}, {{m|enm|gurdel}}, from {{inh|en|ang|gyrdel}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*gurdil}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*gurdilaz|t=girdle, belt}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|gird|le}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|stq|Gäddel|t=belt}}, {{cog|fy|gurdle}}, {{m|fy|gurle}}, {{m|fy|gurl|t=belt}}, {{cog|nl|gordel|t=belt}}, {{cog|de|Gürtel|t=belt}}, {{cog|yi|גאַרטל|t=belt}} (whence {{doublet|en|gartel|notext=1}}, a doublet of girdle), {{cog|sv|gördel|t=girdle}}, {{cog|is|gyrðill|t=girdle}}. {{col-bottom}}

gnaw.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|gnawen}}, {{m|enm|gnaȝen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|gnagan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*gnagan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*gnaganą|t=to gnaw}}, probably from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰnēgʰ-|t=to gnaw, scratch}}.

gnome.raw: {{wp|Gnome}} {{ety|en|:bor|fr:gnome}} From {{bor|en|fr|gnome||gnome}}, from {{der|en|la-new|gnomus}}, used by {{w|Paracelsus}} as a synonym for {{m|la|pygmaeus||pygmy}}.

gone.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|gon}}, {{m|enm|igon}}, {{m|enm|gan}}, {{m|enm|ȝegan}}, from {{inh|en|ang|gān}}, {{m|ang|ġegān}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*gānaz||gone}}, past participle of {{m|gem-pro|*gāną||to go}}. Cognate with West Germanic {{cog|sco|gane||gone}}, {{cog|fy|gien||gone}}, {{cog|nds|gahn||gone}}, and {{cog|nl|gegaan||gone}}.

greenhouse.raw: From {{af|en|green|house}} {{gloss|"house for growing [[greens]]"}}, in reference to the produce grown within.

grew.raw: From {{inherited|en|enm|grew}}, from {{inherited|en|ang|grēow}} (''first and third person past tense of'' {{m|ang|grōwan}}), from West Germanic ''*greu'', from Northwest Germanic ''*grerō'', from {{inherited|en|gem-pro|*gegrō}} (''first and third person past tense of'' {{m|gem-pro|*grōaną}}), [[Appendix:Glossary#reduplication|reduplication]] of ''*grōaną''.

grind.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|grynden}}, from {{inh|en|ang|grindan|t=to grind}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*grindan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*grindaną|t=to crush, grind}}.

guard.raw: [[File:Guard (2529280868).jpg|right|thumb|A guard (person protecting or watching over something)]] {{etymon|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:garde|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|garde}}, from early {{der|en|frm|-}} or late {{der|en|fro|guarde|t=a guardian, warden, keeper}} (whence modern {{cog|fr|garde}}), from the verb {{m|fro|guarder}}. {{doublet|en|garda}}, which is from {{cog|ga|-}}.

guava.raw: {{etymon|en|id=fruit|:bor|es:guayaba<id:fruit>|tree=1}} Recorded since 1555, from {{bor|en|es|guayaba}}, from {{der|en|tnq|*wayaba}}.<ref>{{R:LPCA|113}}</ref> {{doublet|en|guayaba}}, which is now rare or obsolete.

guess.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰed-}} From {{inh|en|enm|gessen|pos=verb}} and {{inh|en|enm|gesse|pos=noun}}, probably of {{der|en|gmq|-}} origin, from {{der|en|gmq-oda|getse}}, {{m|gmq-oda|gitse}}, {{m|gmq-oda|getsa|t=to guess}}, from {{der|en|non|*getsa}}, {{m|non|*gitsa}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*gitisōną|t=to guess}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*getaną|t=to get}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰed-|t=to take, seize}}.

guilt.raw: {{etymon|en|id=responsibility for wrongdoing|:inh|enm:gilt<ety:inh<ang:gylt<t:guilt, sin, offense, crime, fault>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|gilt}}, {{m|enm|gult}}, from {{inh|en|ang|gylt|t=guilt, sin, offense, crime, fault}}, of obscure origin. Possibly related with {{m+|ang|ġieldan|t=to pay, requite, punish}} (whence {{m|en|yield}}), from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*guldijā}} (whence {{cog|gmh|gülte|t=debt, fee, financial duty}}, {{cog|gml|gülde}}, {{cog|de|Gülte}}), from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*geldan||to pay for}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*geldaną||to pay}}. However, neither the Old English stem form nor i

gulf.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|gulf}}, {{m|enm|goulf}}, {{m|enm|golf}}, from {{der|en|fro|golf}}, from {{der|en|it|golfo}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|colfos}}, from {{der|en|grc|κόλπος||bosom, gulf}}, of obscure origin, but possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kʷelp-||to curve, arch}}.

guru.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷreh₂-}} {{bor+|en|hi|गुरु}} / {{bor|en|pa|ਗੁਰੂ}}, from {{der|en|sa|गुरु||venerable, respectable}}, originally "heavy" and in this sense cognate to English {{m|en|grieve}} and, more distantly, {{m|en|brute}}. {{doublet|en|grave}}. A traditional, though flawed etymology based on the [[w:Advayataraka Upanishad|Advayataraka Upanishad]] (line 16)<ref>{{cite-web|url=http://www.yousigma.com/religionandphilosophy/advayataraka.html|title=Advaya Taraka Upanishad(English Translation)|accessdate=December 15, 2011|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120206140012/http://www.yousigm

hammock.raw: Borrowed from {{bor|en|es|hamaca}}, from {{der|en|tnq|*hamaka}} (compare {{cog|arw|hamaka}}, {{cog|guc|jama'a}}), from {{der|en|awd-pro|*maka}}. Columbus, in the narrative of his first voyage, says: “A great many Indians in canoes came to the ship to-day for the purpose of bartering their cotton, and '''hamacas''', or nets, in which they sleep.”

chain: boldly; hardily; without ease; in a way that causes pain; not easily; only by degrees
hardly.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|hardely}}, {{m|enm|hardliche}}, from {{inh|en|ang|heardlīċe|t=boldly; hardily; without ease; in a way that causes pain; not easily; only by degrees}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|hard|-ly|id2=adverbial}}. Compare {{cog|nl|hardelijk}}, {{cog|de|härtlich}}.

hatchet.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)kep-}} From {{inh|en|enm|hachet}}, a borrowing from {{der|en|fro|hachete}}, diminutive of {{m|fro|hache||axe}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*happia}}, from {{der|en|frk|*happjā}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*hapjǭ}}, {{m|gem-pro|*habjǭ|t=knife}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kop-|t=to strike, to beat}}. Cognate with {{cog|goh|happa}}, {{m|goh|heppa}}, {{m|goh|habba|t=reaper, sickle}}, {{cog|de|Hippe|t=billhook}}, {{cog|nl|heep}}, {{m|nl|hiep|t=billhook}}, and {{cog|grc|κοπίς}}. Mostly displaced native {{ncog|ang|handæx}}, whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|hand axe}}.

hawk.raw: {{wp}} [[File:Northern Goshawk ad M2.jpg|thumb|A Eurasian goshawk ({{taxfmt|Astur gentilis|species}})]]

heat.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*keHy-}} {{etymid|en|hotness}} From {{inh|en|enm|hete}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hǣtu}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*haitī}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*haitį̄|t=heat}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*keHy-|t=heat; hot}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|hete||heat}}, {{cog|stq|Hatte||heat}}, {{cog|goh|heizī||heat}}. Related also to {{cog|nl|hitte||heat}}, {{cog|de|Hitze||heat}}, {{cog|sv|hetta||heat}}, {{cog|fo,is|hiti||heat}}. Related to [[hot]].

hiccup.raw: From earlier {{m|en|hickop}}, alteration of earlier {{m|en|hicket}}, {{m|en|hyckock}}, from {{m|en|hic}} ({{onomatopoeic|en|title=onomatopoeic}}) + {{m|en|-ock|pos=diminutive suffix}}.

cogs: hanging; that upon which a thing is hung
any attachment by which something is hung or fastened
to cause to hang, hang up
hinge.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|henge||hinge}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*henġ}} or {{m|ang|*henġe|t=hinge}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*hangiju}} or {{m|gmw-pro|*hangī}}; compare {{cog|ang|*henġe|*henġe-}} in {{m|ang|henġeclif||overhanging cliff}}, {{cog|ang|henġen||hanging; that upon which a thing is hung}}. Akin to {{cog|sco|heenge||hinge}}, {{cog|stq|Hänge||hinge}}, {{cog|nds|henge||hook, hinge, handle}}, {{cog|nl|heng||moving leaf of a hinge}}, {{cog|nl|geheng||hinge}}, {{cog|dum|henghe|henghe, hanghe|hook, hinge, handle}}, {{cog|sco|hingel||any attachment by which something is hung or fastened}}, {{cog|nl|hengel

hint.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|hinten}}, {{m|enm|hynten}}, variant of {{m|enm|henten|t=to lay hold of, catch}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hentan|t=to seize, grasp}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hantijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hantijaną}}. {{doublet|en|hent}}. Related also to {{m|en|hunt}}.

chain: to hit, strike, make contact with
cogs: to hit, throw, pull out, release
hit.raw: {{ety|en|id=strike|:inh|enm:hitten|tree=+}} {{inh+|en|enm|hitten||to hit, strike, make contact with}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hittan||to meet with, come upon, fall in with}}, from {{der|en|non|hitta||to strike, meet}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*hittijaną|t=to come upon, find}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kh₂eyd-|t=to fall; fall upon; hit; cut; hew}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|fy|hitte|t=to meet}}, {{cog|nl|hitten|t=to hit, encounter}}, {{cog|da|hitte|t=to find}}, {{cog|fo|-}}, {{cog|is|-}}, {{cog|sv|hitta|t=to meet}}, {{cog|nn|hitta}}, {{m|nn|hitte|t=to meet; to find}}, {{cog|la|caedō|t=to kill

hoe.raw: {{etymid|en|from hewing-referent origins}} From {{inh|en|enm|howe}}, from {{der|en|xno|hoe|houe}}, from {{der|en|frk|*hauwā}}, derivative of {{der|en|frk|*hauwan|t=to hew}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*hawwaną}}. More at {{l|en|hew}}.

hole.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:hole<id:hol>|tree=1}} {{inh+|en|enm|hole}}, {{m|enm|hol}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hol||orifice, hollow place, cavity}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hol||hole}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hulą||hollow space, cavity}}, noun derivative of {{der|en|gem-pro|*hulaz||hollow}}, which is of uncertain ultimate origin. Related to {{m|en|hollow}}.

cogs: to clothe or adorn with honour
honest.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|honest}}, {{m|enm|honeste|id=good|t=honourable, appropriate, excellent}}, from {{der|en|fro|honeste}}, from {{der|en|la|honestus}}, from {{m|la|honor}}. For the verb, see {{cog|la|honestāre|t=to clothe or adorn with honour}}, and compare {{cog|fr|honester}}. Displaced native {{inh|en|ang|sōþfæst|lit=truth-firm}}.

hymn.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|ymne}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ymen}} (reinforced by {{der|en|fro|ymne}}), from {{der|en|la|hymnus}}, borrowed from {{der|en|grc|ὕμνος}}.

income.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|income}}, perhaps continuing (in altered form) {{inh|en|ang|incyme|t=an in-coming, entrance}}, equivalent to {{pre|en|in-|come}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Íenkúumen|t=income}}, {{cog|fy|ynkommen|t=income}}, {{cog|nl|inkomen}}, {{m|nl|inkomst|t=income, earnings, gainings}}, {{cog|nds-de|Inkumst|t=income}}, {{cog|de|Einkommen}}, {{m|de|Einkunft|t=income, earnings, competence}}, {{cog|da|indkomst|t=income}}, {{cog|sv|inkomst|t=income}}, {{cog|is|innkváma|t=income}}.

inn.raw: From {{der|en|enm|in}}, {{m|enm|inn}}, from {{der|en|ang|inn||a dwelling, house, chamber, lodging}}; akin to {{cog|is|inni||a dwelling place, home, abode}}, {{cog|fo|inni||home}}.

cogs: immediately, on the spot, at once
instant.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*steh₂-}} {{etymon|en|id=moment|:inh|enm:instant<t:infinitely short period of time><ety:der<fro:instant<t:assiduous, at hand><ety:der<la:īnstāns<t:present, pressing, urgent>>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|instant||infinitely short period of time}}, from {{der|en|fro|instant||assiduous, at hand|pos=adj}}, from {{der|en|la|instans|īnstāns, īnstantis|present, pressing, urgent|lit=standing near}}, present active participle of {{m|la|īnstō||to stand upon, be nearby}}, from {{prefix|la|in|stō|t1=after|t2=to stand|nocat=1}}. Compare {{cog|ang|instede||immediately, on the spot, at on

itch.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|icche}}, {{m|enm|ȝicche}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ġiċċe|t=itch}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*jukjǭ|t=itch}}, of unknown origin. Cognate with {{cog|sco|yeuk|t=itch, itchiness}}, {{cog|nl|jeuk|t=itch}}, {{cog|de|jucken|}}.

jazz.raw: {{unk|en}}. First attested around 1912 in a discussion of baseball; attested in reference to music around 1915. Numerous references suggest that the term may be connected to {{m|en|jasm}} and {{m|en|jism}}.<ref>{{cite-book|title=The Concise New Partridge Dictionary of Slang and Unconventional English|year=2014|isbn=1317625110}} says that most authorities derive it from {{m|en|jasm}}, a variant of {{m|en|jism}}. ''Partridge'' also says it was first recorded in reference to music in a 1917 Chicago ''Tribune'' advertisement for "Bert Kelly's Jaz {{sic}} Band", having previously been used in baseb

judge.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂yew-|*deyḱ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|juge}}, {{m|enm|jugge}}, from {{der|en|fro|juge}}, from {{der|en|la|iūdex|iūdex}}. Displaced native {{ncog|enm|deme}} (from {{noncog|ang|dēma|t=judge}}) and {{m|enm|demere}} (from {{ncog|ang|dēmere|t=judge}}), see also {{m|en|deemer}}, {{m|en|deemster}}.

karate.raw: {{bor+|en|ja|-}} {{ja-r|空%手|から%て}}, from {{ja-r|唐%手|から%て}}, an {{obor|ja|ryu|-|nocat=1|nocap=1}} {{ryu-r|唐手|とーでぃー|t=Chinese hand}}.

karma.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*kʷer-}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|sa|कर्म|tr=kárma}}, nom.sg. of {{m|sa|कर्मन्|tr=kárman|t=act, action, performance}}; first attested in English in 1785 in a translation of the ''{{w|Bhagavad Gita}}'' by {{w|Charles Wilkins}}.

kayak.raw: {{etymon|en|id=boat|:bor|iu:ᖃᔭᖅ}} {{bor+|en|iu|ᖃᔭᖅ||hunter's boat|sc=Cans}} (Inuvialuktun{{attn|ikt|should the preceding 'iu' be changed to 'ikt'?}}), from {{der|en|esx-esk-pro|*qayaʁ}}. Compare {{cog|kl|qajaq}} and {{cog|esu|qayaq}}.

kettle.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:ketel}} From {{inh|en|enm|ketel}}, also {{m|enm|chetel}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ċietel||kettle, cauldron}} and in [[Middle English]] possibly influenced by {{der|en|non|ketill}} and both from {{der|en|gem-pro|*katilaz||kettle, bucket, vessel}}, of uncertain origin and formation. Usually regarded as a borrowing of {{der|en|la-lat|catīllus||small bowl}}, diminutive of {{der|en|la|catinus||deep bowl, vessel for cooking up or serving food}}, however, the word may be Germanic confused with the Latin: compare {{cog|ang|cete||cooking pot}}, {{cog|goh|chezzi||a kettle, dish, bowl}}, {{co

kiss.raw: {{etymon|en|id=verb|:inh|enm:kissen}} From {{inh|en|enm|kissen}}, {{m|enm|kussen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cyssan|t=to kiss}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kussijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kussijaną|t=to kiss}}.

lamb.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|lamb}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lamb}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*lamb}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*lambaz}}, probably from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*h₁l̥h₁onbʰos}}, enlargement of {{m|ine-pro|*h₁elh₁én}}, ultimately from {{m|ine-pro|*h₁el-}}.

large.raw: From {{der|en|enm|large}}, from {{der|en|fro|large}}, from {{der|en|la|larga}}, feminine of {{m|la|largus||abundant, plentiful, copious, large, much}}, of uncertain ultimate origin; see there for more. Along with {{m|en|big}}, it mostly displaced {{cog|enm|stour|stoor}} and {{m|enm|muchel}} (the latter surviving in {{m|en|much}} under a different meaning).

laundry.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:lavendrie}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*lewh₃-}} From {{inh|en|enm|lavendrie}}, from {{der|en|fro|lavanderie}}, from {{der|en|la|lavandaria}}. See {{m|en|launder}}. [[File:Laundry in Paris.jpg|thumb|upright=1.1|A '''laundry''' (sense 2, room where laundering is done).]] [[File:Italian hanging laundry.jpg|thumb|upright=1.1|'''Laundry''' (sense 3, clothes in the process of being laundered) hanging on a [[clothesline]] to dry.]]

law.raw: {{etymon|en|id=rule|:inh|enm:lawe|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|lawe}}, {{m|enm|laȝe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lagu|t=law}}, borrowed from {{der|en|non|lǫg|t=law|lit=things laid down or firmly established}}, originally the plural of {{m|non|lag||layer, stratum, a laying in order, measure, stroke}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*lagą|t=that which is laid down}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*legʰ-|t=to lie}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|law|t=law}}, {{cog|is|lög|t=things laid down, law}}, {{cog|fo|lóg|t=law}}, {{cog|no|lov|t=law}}, {{cog|sv|lag|t=law}}, {{cog|da|lov|t=law}}, {{cog|fi|laki|t=law}}. Compare typologically d

lawn.raw: {{ety|en|id=ground|:from|en:laune<ety:from<en:laund>>|tree=1}} Early Modern English {{m|en|laune||turf, grassy area}}, alteration of {{m|en|laund||glade}}, from {{inh|en|enm|launde}}, from {{der|en|fro|lande||heath, moor}}, of {{der|en|gem|-}} or {{der|en|cel-gau|-}} origin, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*landą||land}} or {{der|en|cel-pro|*landā}}, both from {{der|en|ine-pro|*lendʰ-||land, heath}}.

league.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*leyǵ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|liege}}, {{m|enm|ligg}}, {{m|enm|lige|t=a pact between governments, an agreement, alliance}}, from {{der|en|frm|ligue}}, from {{der|en|it|lega}}, from the verb {{m|it|legare}}, from {{der|en|la|ligō|t=to tie}}.

leisure.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|leyser}}, from {{der|en|xno|leisir}}, variant of {{der|en|fro|loisir||to enjoy oneself}} (Modern {{cog|fr|loisir}} survives as a noun), substantive use of a verb, from {{der|en|la|licēre||be permitted}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|ǣmetta}}.

lie.raw: [[File:Bichon Frisé lying down.jpg|thumb|A dog '''lying''' in the grass.]] {{root|en|ine-pro|*legʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|lien}}, {{m|enm|liggen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|liċġan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*liggjan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*ligjaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*legʰ-}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|yol|lee}}, {{m|yol|lidge|t=to lie}}, {{cog|frr|lade}}, {{m|frr|lai}}, {{m|frr|laie}}, {{m|frr|lei}}, {{m|frr|lii}}, {{m|frr|läde}}, {{m|frr|läie|t=to lie; to lay}}, {{cog|stq|lääse|t=to lie; to lay}}, {{cog|fy|lizze|t=to lie}}, {{cog|gsw|ligge|t=to lie}}, {{cog|gmw-cfr|lijje|t=to lie}}, {

list.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:lī̆st<ety:inh<ang:līste>:der<fro:liste>:der<la-med:lista>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|list|lī̆st}}, {{m|enm|liste|lī̆ste|band, stripe; hem, selvage; border, edge, rim; list, specification; barriers enclosing area for jousting, etc.}}, from {{inh|en|ang|līste||hem, edge, strip}}, or {{der|en|fro|liste}}, {{m|fro|listre||border; band; strip of paper; list}}, or {{der|en|la-med|lista}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=lī̆st(e|pos=n.(2)|id=MED25749|accessdate=16 June 2018}}</ref> all from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*līstā}}, possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*leys-||to trace, track}}.

log.raw: {{etymon|en|id=Q193472|:inh|enm:logge<id:log>}} {{wp}} [[File:Log pile in Old Park Bottom Wood - geograph.org.uk - 1932189.jpg|thumb|A '''log''' pile ({{senseno|en|Q193472}})]]

machine.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|frm:machine|tree=1}} {{bor+|en|frm|machine}}, from {{der|en|la|māchina||a machine, engine, contrivance, device, stratagem, trick}}, from {{der|en|grc-dor|μᾱχᾰνᾱ́}}, cognate with {{cog|grc-att|μηχᾰνή||a machine, engine, contrivance, device}}, from which comes {{m|en|mechanical}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|searu}}.

chain: the handling or training of a horse, horsemanship, riding, maneuvers, proceedings
manage.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:*manage<ety:bor<fro:manege<ety:der<roa-oit:maneggiare<unc>>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|en-ear|manage|nocat=1}}, {{m|en|menage}}, from {{inh|en|enm|*manage}}, {{m|enm|*menage}}, from {{der|en|fro|manege||the handling or training of a horse, horsemanship, riding, maneuvers, proceedings}}, probably from {{der|en|roa-oit|maneggiare||to handle, manage, touch, treat}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*manizāre|t=handle}}, from {{der|en|la|manus|t=hand}} + {{m|la|-izō|-izāre|pos=verb-forming suffix}}. {{doublet|en|manège}}.

marry.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|marien}}, from {{der|en|xno|marïer}}, from {{der|en|la|marito|marītāre|t=to wed}}, from {{m|la|marītus|t=husband, suitor}}, from {{m|la|mās|t=man, male}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin. Possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*méryos||young man}}, same source as {{cog|sa|मर्य|tr=márya|t=suitor, young man}}. Compare its feminine derivatives: {{cog|cy|morwyn||girl}}, {{m|cy|merch||daughter}}, {{cog|gme-cgo|marzus||wedding}}, {{cog|grc|μεῖραξ||boy; girl}}, {{cog|lt|martì||bride}}, {{cog|ae|𐬨𐬀𐬌𐬭𐬌𐬌𐬀|t=yeoman}}.<ref>J.P. Mallory and D.Q. Adams, ''Encyclopedia of Indo-European Culture'', s.v.

mess.raw: Perhaps a corruption of {{der|en|enm|mesh|t=mash}}, compare {{m|en|muss}}, or derived from Etymology 2 "mixed foods, as for animals". Compare also {{cog|ang|mes|t=dung, excrement}}.

message.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*mey- (change)}} From {{inh|en|enm|message}}, from {{der|en|fro|message}}, from {{der|en|la-eme|missāticum}}, derived from {{der|en|la|mitto|mittere|t=send}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*meyth₂-|t=to exchange}}. Partially {{displaced|ang|ærende|nocap=1}} (whence {{m|en|errand}}).

mild.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:milde<id:mild><ety:der<ang:milde>>}} From {{inh|en|enm|milde}}, from {{inh|en|ang|milde||mild}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*mildijaz||mild}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*melh₂-||to beat, pound, grind|id=grind}}.

mimic.raw: {{ety|en|:uder|la:mīmicus|text=+|tree=1|nodot=1}}, from {{uder|en|grc|μῑμικός||belonging to mimes}}, from {{m|grc|μῖμος||imitator, actor}}; see [[mime]].

cogs: to mean, intend, purpose, determine, resolve
mind.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*men-|id=think}} From {{inh|en|enm|minde}}, {{m|enm|munde}}, {{m|enm|imynde}}, {{m|enm|imunde}}, {{m|enm|ȝemynde}}, {{m|enm|ȝemunde}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mynd}}, {{m|ang|ġemynd|t=mind, memory}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*mundi}}, {{m|gmw-pro|*gamundi}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*mundiz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*gamundiz|t=memory, remembrance}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*méntis|t=thought}} (compare also {{m|en|mantis}}, via Greek), from the root {{m|ine-pro|*men-|t=to think}}.

chain: place for making coins, coined money
mint.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*men- (think)}} From {{inh|en|enm|mynt}}, {{m|enm|munet|münet|money, coin}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mynet||coin}}, from late {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*munit}}, from {{der|en|la|monēta||place for making coins, coined money}}, from the temple of {{w|Juno Moneta}} (named for {{m|la|Monēta}} mother of the Muses), where coins were made. {{doublet|en|money|manat}}. The verb is from the noun; {{cog|ang|mynetian||to mint}} is a parallel formation.

moose.raw: Earlier ''mus'', ''moos'', from an {{der|en|alg-eas}} language name for the animal, such as {{der|en|wam|moos|moos, mws}}, {{cog|xnt|moos}} or {{cog|aaq|mos}} (cognate to {{cog|abe|moz}}), from {{der|en|alg-pro|*mo·swa||it strips}}, referring to how a moose strips tree bark when feeding: compare {{cog|wam|moos-u||he strips, cuts smooth}}.<ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref><ref>{{R:Dictionary.com}}</ref>

moth.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:mothe<ety:inh<ang:moþþe>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|moth,moththe,motthe,moght,mohþe,mouȝte}}, from {{inh|en|ang|moþþe,mohþe,mohþa}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*moþþā}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*maþô}} ~ {{m|gem-pro||*muttaz|insect, worm, maggot}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*mutn-,*mut-|t=worm}}.

mulch.raw: Probably from {{inh|en|enm|melsche}}, {{m|enm|molsh||soft}}, from {{inh|en|ang|melsċ}}, {{m|ang|milisċ||mellow; mild; sweet|lit=honeyed}}, probably from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*mili||honey}}. Compare {{cog|is|milska||a honeyed beverage}}.

chain: word, humour, companion, speech, account, rumour, fable
myth.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|grc:μῦθος}} From {{bor|en|grc|μῦθος||word, humour, companion, speech, account, rumour, fable}}. Attested in English since 1830. {{doublet|en|mythos}}.

neither.raw: {{word|en|ine|né}}{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂ey-|id1=life|*kʷ-}} Alteration (after {{m|en|either}}) of {{m|en|nauther}}, from {{inh|en|enm|neiþer}}, from {{inh|en|ang|nāwþer}}, contraction of {{m|ang|nāhwæþer}}, corresponding to {{m|en|no}} + {{m|en|whether}}. Compare {{noncog|la|neuter|t=neither}}. {{surf|+com|en|not|either}}.

notch.raw: Recorded since 1577, probably a {{rebracketing|en|[[an]] [[otch]]|nocap=1}}, from {{der|en|frm|oche||notch}}, itself from the {{der|en|fro|-}} verb {{m|fro|ochier||to notch}}, of uncertain origin, but possibly related to {{cog|fr|hocher}} and {{cog|en|nick||small cut, notch}}.

obey.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|obeyen}}, from {{der|en|xno|obeir}}, {{m|fro|obeier}} et al., {{der|en|fro|obeir}}, from {{der|en|la|oboediō}} (also {{m|la|obēdiō|t=to listen to, harken, usually in extended sense, obey, be subject to, serve}}), from {{m|la|ob-||before, near}} + {{m|la|audiō|t=to hear}}. Compare {{m|en|audient}}. In Latin, ''ob'' + ''audire'' would have been expected to become Classical Latin *''obūdiō'' (compare ''in'' + ''claudō'' becoming ''inclūdō''), but it has been theorized that the usual law court associations of the word for obeying encouraged a false [[archaism]] from ''ū'' to ''oe

occasion.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱh₂d-}} From {{inh|en|enm|occasioun}}, from {{der|en|frm|occasion}}, from {{der|en|fro|occasiun}}, from {{der|en|la|occāsiō|occāsiōnem}}, noun of action from perfect passive participle {{m|la|occāsus}}, from verb {{m|la|occidō}}, from prefix {{m|la|ob-||down", "away}} + verb {{m|la|cadō||fall}}.

cogs: triangle, point of land, odd number
odd.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|odde}}, {{m|enm|od|t=odd (not even); leftover after division into pairs}}, from {{der|en|non|oddi|t=odd, third or additional number; triangle}}, from {{m|non|oddr|t=point of a weapon}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*uzdaz|t=point}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wes-|t=to stick, prick, pierce, sting}} + {{m|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-|t=to set, place}}.

oil.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:oyle|id=noun|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|oyle}}, {{m|enm|oile|t=olive oil}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|oile}}, from {{der|en|la|oleum|t=oil, olive oil}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἔλαιον|t=olive oil}}, from {{m|grc|ἐλαία|t=olive}}. Compare {{cog|sla-pro|*lojь}}. More at {{m|en|olive}}. {{doublet|en|oleum}}. Supplanted {{cog|enm|ele|t=oil}}, from {{cog|ang|ele|t=oil}}, also from Latin. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|smireness||ointment, oil}}.

ought.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eyḱ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|oughte}}, {{m|enm|aughte}}, {{m|enm|aȝte}}, {{m|enm|ahte}}, from {{inh|en|ang|āhte}}, first and third person singular past tense of {{der|en|ang|āgan|t=to own, possess}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|owe|t}}.

oyster.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:oystre|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|oystre}}, from {{der|en|ang|ostre}}, reinforced or superseded by {{der|en|xno|oistre}}, which is from {{der|en|fro|oistre}}, {{m|fro|uistre}} (compare modern French {{m|fr|huître}}); both lines (Old English and Old French) from {{der|en|la|ostrea}}, from {{der|en|grc|ὄστρεον}}. {{dbt|en|ostro|t1=a purple dye}}.

chain: palm-tree, palm-branch, palm of the hand
palm.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*pleh₂-}} [[Image:1859-Martinique.web.jpg|thumb|upright=0.68|A '''palm''' tree ({{taxfmt|Cocos nucifera|species}})]] From {{inh|en|enm|palme}}, from {{inh|en|ang|palm}}, {{m|ang|palma|t=palm-tree, palm-branch}}, from {{der|en|la|palma|t=palm-tree, palm-branch, palm of the hand}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*pl̥h₂meh₂}}, {{m|ine-pro|*pl̥h₂emeh₂|t=palm of the hand}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*pleh₂-|t=flat}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|fana|t=a piece of cloth, patch, banner, flag, vane}}. {{doublet|en|vane}}.

panic.raw: The {{glossary|adjective}} is borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|panique}}, a word itself borrowed from {{der|en|grc|πανικός|t=pertaining to Pan}};<ref name="OED">{{R:OED Online|pos=''adj.'' and ''n.''{{sup|2}}|noformat=1|id=136852|date=June 2021|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|alt=panic{{sup|1}}|pos=n}}</ref> [[Pan]], the Greek god of fields and woods, was believed to be the source of mysterious sounds that caused contagious, groundless fear in herds and crowds, or in people in lonely spots.

patient.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*peh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|pacient}}, from {{der|en|frm|patient}}, from {{der|en|fro|pacient}}, from {{der|en|la|patiens}}, present participle of {{m|la|patior|t=to suffer, endure}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*peh₁-|t=to hate, hurt}}.

pattern.raw: From earlier {{m|en|patten}}, {{m|en|paterne}}, from {{inh|en|enm|patron||patron; example}}, from {{der|en|fro|patron}}, from {{der|en|la-med|patrōnus||patron}}. {{doublet|en|padrone|patron|Patronus|patroon}}.

peak.raw: From earlier {{m|en|peake}}, {{m|en|peek}}, {{m|en|peke}}, from {{inh|en|enm|pek}} (in place names), itself an alteration of {{m|enm|pike}}, {{m|enm|pyke}}, {{m|enm|pyk||a sharp point, pike}}, from {{inh|en|ang|pīc}}, {{m|ang|piic||a pike, needle, pin, peak, pinnacle}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*pīk}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*pīkaz||peak}}.

pension.raw: {{etymid|en|annuity}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)pend-}} From {{inh|en|enm|pencioun}}, {{m|enm|pensioun}}, from {{der|en|xno|pencione}}, {{der|en|fro|pencion}}, and their source, {{der|en|la|pēnsiō|t=payment, weight, rent, compensation}}, from the participle stem of {{m|la|pendō||to weigh}}. {{doublet|en|pensione}}.

perceive.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*keh₂p-}} From {{inh|en|enm|perceyven}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|percevoir}}, {{m|fro|perceveir}}, from {{der|en|la|percipiō}}, past participle {{m|la|perceptus||take hold of, obtain, receive, observe}}, from {{m|la|per||by, through}} + {{m|la|capiō||to take}}; see {{m|en|capable}}. Compare {{m|en|conceive}}, {{m|en|deceive}}, {{m|en|receive}}.

Possibly related to {{m|en|fat}}.

The adjective is probably back-formed from {{m|en|pitch-black}}, reinterpreting "pi

pleasant.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|plesaunte}}, from {{der|en|fro|plaisant}}. {{surf|en|please|-ant}}. Related to {{cog|nl|plezant||full of fun or pleasure}}. Partly displaced {{ncog|ang|wynsum}}, which became {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|winsome}}.

Cognate with {{cog|sco|pleuch|pleuch, plou}}, {{cog|frr|plog}}, {{cog|fy|ploech}}, {{cog|nds|Ploog}}, {{cog|nl|ploeg}}, {{cog|ru|плуг}}, {{cog|de|Pflug}}, {{cog|da|plov}}, {{cog|nb,nn,sv|plog}}, {{cog|is|plógur}}. power.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁es-}} {{etymon|en|id=force|:inh|enm:power<id:force>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|power}}, {{m|enm|poer}}, from {{der|en|fro|poeir}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|posso|potēre}}, from {{der|en|la|possum|posse}}, whence {{m+|en|potent}}. The forms suggest a hypothetical {{der|en|ang|-}} form *''prægn'', where *''æg'' would have evolved into Middle English *''ay'', but it is unclear if the word is of Germanic origin, from another European language, or loaned from a {{der|en|qfa-sub|-}}. In the Isle of Wight, a word ''prankle'' ("prawn") is recorded<ref>{{R:EDD|prankle}}</ref> and thought to be related.<ref name="OUP">[https://blog

print.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:*printen<ety:apheretic<enm:emprinten<ety:der<la:imprimo>>>>|id=write}} From {{inh|en|enm|*printen}}, {{m|enm|prenten}}, {{m|enm|preenten}}, an [[apheretic]] form of {{m|enm|emprinten}}, {{m|enm|enprinten||to impress; imprint}} (see {{l|en|imprint}}). Compare also Late {{cog|fro|printer}}, {{m|fro|preindre||to press}}, from {{cog|la|premere||to press}}.

protein.raw: From {{con|en|proto-|ein}}. Suggested by {{w|Jöns Jacob Berzelius}} in a letter to {{w|Gerardus Johannes Mulder}}, from {{bor|en|fr|protéine}} and {{der|en|de|Protein}}, both coined based on {{der|en|grc|πρωτεῖος||primary}}, from {{m|grc|πρῶτος||first}}.<ref>{{R:New English Dictionary}}</ref>

Displaced native {{cog|enm|sothen||to prove}}, from {{cog|ang|sōþian||to prove}}. {{doublet|en|probe}}. More at {{l|en|for}}, {{l|en|be}}, {{l

pun.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|ponnen}}, {{m|enm|ponen}}, {{m|enm|punen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|punian}}, {{m|ang|pūnian||to [[pound#Verb|pound]], [[beat#Verb|beat]], [[bray]], [[bruise#Verb|bruise]], [[crush#Verb|crush]], [[grind#Verb|grind]]}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*punōną||to break to pieces, [[pulverize]]}}. See {{m|en|pound}}. As a kind of word play, from the notion of “beating” the words into place.

push.raw: {{etymon|en|id=verb|:inh|enm:pushen<ety:bor<frm:pousser<ety:inh<fro:poulser<ety:inh<la:pulsō>>>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|pushen}}, {{m|enm|poshen}}, {{m|enm|posson}}, borrowed from {{der|en|frm|pousser}} (Modern French {{m|fr|pousser}}) from {{uder|en|fro|poulser|}}, from {{der|en|la|pulsare|t=to beat, strike}}, frequentative of {{m|la|pellere}} (past participle {{m|la|pulsus}}). {{doublet|en|pulsate|pulse#Verb|pos2=verb}}. Partly displaced native {{ncog|ang|sċūfan}}, whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|shove}}.

putt.raw: Borrowed from {{bor|en|sco|putt|t=to put}}.<ref>{{R:New English Dictionary}}</ref> Compare {{cog|dum|putten||to dig a pit}}. The {{cog|ang|putian||to push; thrust; put; place}} derivation is commonly assumed, although no longer valid. In Dutch, the word is instanced in a description of golf in an early seventeenth-century edition of Pieter van Afferden's ''Tyrocinium linguae latinae''.<ref>Heiner Gillmeister, “[https://web.archive.org/web/20210920074735/http://www.nga-earlygolf.nl/golfarchief/files/original/d7094f6c187c36f7d07f94ec065bc78d.pdf Über den Ursprung des Golfspiels]”, March 7, 2016.

quay.raw: The current spelling replaced the spelling ''key'' in the 1690s to emulate the spelling but (at least originally) not the pronunciation of the equivalent modern {{cog|fr|quai}}. From {{inh|en|enm|kay}}, {{m|enm|key}}, {{m|enm|kaye}}, {{m|enm|keye}}, from {{der|en|fro|kay}}, {{m|fro|cail}}, from {{der|en|cel-gau|*kagyum}}, {{m|cel-gau|cagiíun||enclosure}}, from {{der|en|cel-pro|*kagyom||pen, enclosure}} (compare {{cog|cy|cae||field}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kagʰyóm||enclosure}}. {{doublet|en|hedge|hey|id2=dance|t2=choreographic figure}}.

queue.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|queue}}, {{m|enm|quew}}, {{m|enm|qwew}}, {{m|enm|couwe}}, from {{der|en|xno|queue}}, {{m|fro|keu}} and {{der|en|fro|cöe}}, {{m|fro|cue}}, {{m|fro|coe|gloss=tail}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|cōda}}, from {{der|en|la|cauda}}. See also {{cog|frm|queu}}, {{m|en|cueue}}. {{doublet|en|coda|cola}}.

royal.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|royal}}, from {{der|en|fro|roial}} (Modern French {{m|fr|royal}}), from {{der|en|la|rēgālis}}, from {{m|la|rēx||king}}. {{doublet|en|regal|t1=befitting a king|real|t2=unit of currency|ariary|riyal}}. Cognate with {{cog|es|real}}, {{cog|it|reale}}, {{cog|ca|reial}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|cynelīċ}}.

rude.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|rude}}, from {{der|en|fro|rude}}, {{m|fro|ruide}}, from {{der|en|la|rudis|t=rough, raw, rude, wild, untilled}}.

chain: to take possession of; invest (person, court)
cogs: to quarrel, claim by law, accuse
seize.raw: Earlier {{m|en|seise}}, from {{inh|en|enm|seisen}}, {{m|enm|sesen}}, {{m|enm|saisen}}, from {{der|en|fro|seisir||to take possession of; invest (person, court)}}, from {{der|en|la-eme|sacio|sacīre|to lay claim to, appropriate}} (8th century) in the phrase {{m|la||ad propriam sacire}}, from Old Low {{der|en|frk|*sakjan||to sue, bring legal action}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*sakjaną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*sakōną}} (compare {{cog|ang|sacian||to strive, brawl}}), from {{der|en|gem-pro|*sakaną}} (compare {{cog|osx|sakan||to accuse}}, {{cog|goh|sahhan||to bicker, quarrel, rebuke}}, {{cog|ang|sacan||to quarrel

seldom.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:seldom|tree=1}} From late {{inh|en|enm|seldom}}, alteration of earlier {{m|enm|selden}} by analogy with adverbial datives such as {{m|en|whilom}}, from {{inh|en|ang|seldan||seldom}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*seldanā}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*seldanē}}.

self.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:self|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|salve}}, {{m|enm|self}}, {{m|enm|silf}}, from {{inh|en|ang|self}}, {{m|ang|seolf}}, {{m|ang|sylf}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*selbaz}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*selbʰ-|t=one's own}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognates with {{cog|stq|sälven}}, {{m|stq|säärm}}, {{m|stq|sääuwen|t=oneself}}, {{cog|fy|sels|t=oneself}}, {{cog|bar|söbe|t=identical, same}}, {{m|bar|söber|t=self}}, {{cog|nl|zelf|t=myself, oneself}}, {{cog|de|selber|t=self}}, {{m|de|selbst|t=by oneself}}, {{cog|lb|selwer|t=self}}, {{cog|yi|זעלב|t=same}}, {{cog|da|selv|t=self}}, {{cog|ovd|siuov|t=self

Both Latin and Germanic from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sent-|t=t

sheath.raw: {{multiple images |direction = vertical |image1 = Arms and Armor.jpg |caption1 = A [[princely]] [[Mughal Empire|Mughal]] [[sabre]] with a [[jewelled]] sheath ({{senseno|en|scabbard}}) or [[scabbard]]. |image2 = Leitungsende Abisoliert en.svg |caption2 = A diagram showing [[electrical]] [[wire#Noun|wires]] with sheaths ({{senseno|en|electrical cable}}) of different [[colour#Noun|colours]]. |image3 = CNN's Campbell Brown.jpg |caption3 = {{w|CNN}} [[journalist]] [[w:Campbell Brown (journalist)|Campbell Brown]] in a sheath dress ({{senseno|en|dress}}). }}

shelf.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:schelfe|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|schelfe}}, probably from {{inh|en|ang|sċielfe|sċylfe}}, {{m|ang|sċielfe|sċilfe|t=shelf, ledge, deck of a ship}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*skilfijā}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*skelfō|t=shelf, ledge, cliff}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)kelH-|t=to cut}}, distantly related to {{m|en|sculpt}}, {{m|en|carve}} and {{m|en|shell}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|schelf|t=hay loft, haystack}}, {{cog|nds-de|Schelf|t=haystack}}, {{cog|non|skjalf|t=bench}}.

shepherd.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|schepherde}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sċēaphierde}}, a compound of {{m|ang|sċēap|t=sheep}} and {{m|ang|hierde|t=herdsman}}, equivalent to modern {{af|en|sheep|herd|t2=herder}}.

chain: to decline to do, avoid, fear
shun.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)kewH-}} From {{inh|en|enm|schonen|t=to decline to do, avoid, fear}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sċunian|t=to shun, fear, avoid}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin, though probably ultimately connected to the {{der|en|ine-pro|-}} root {{m|ine-pro|*(s)kewH-|t=to cover, conceal}} via {{inh|en|gem-pro|*skunōną}}; see that entry for more discussion.

chain: to cause rapid movement, shoot a bolt, shut, bolt
cogs: to shut out, dam, protect, guard
shut.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:schitten}} From {{inh|en|enm|schitten}}, {{m|enm|schetten}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sċyttan||to cause rapid movement, shoot a bolt, shut, bolt}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*skuttjan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*skutjaną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*skuttijaną||to bar, bolt}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*skuttą}}, {{m|gem-pro|*skuttjō||bar, bolt, shed}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)kewd-||to drive, fall upon, rush}}. The Modern English word was originally a dialect form; the Old English word would have normally merged with {{m|en|shit}}.

side.raw: {{etymon|en|id=edge|:inh|enm:side|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|side}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sīde|t=side, flank}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*sīdǭ|t=side, flank, edge, shore}}, derived from {{m|gem-pro|*sīdaz}}, probably from {{der|en|ine-pro|*seh₁-|t=long, lasting}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Siede|t=side}}, {{cog|fy|side|t=side}}, {{cog|nl|zijde}}, {{m|nl|zij|t=side}}, {{cog|nds-de|Sied|t=side}}, {{cog|de|Seite|t=side}}, {{cog|da,nb,nn|side|t=side}}, {{cog|sv|sida|t=side}}.

simple.raw: {{ety|en|tree=1|:inh|enm:symple}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*sem-|*meh₁-|*pel-|id3=fold}} {{inh+|en|enm|symple}}, from {{der|en|fro|simple}}, from {{der|en|la|simplex|t=simple|lit=onefold}} (as opposed to {{m|la|duplex|lit=twofold|t=double}}), from {{m|la|semel|t=once, one time}} + {{m|la|plicō|t=to fold}}. See [[same]] and [[fold]]. Compare [[single]], [[singular]], [[simultaneous]], etc. Partially displaced native English {{m|en|onefold}}.

sin.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁es-}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:synne|id=noun|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|synne}}, {{m|enm|sinne}}, from {{inh|en|ang|synn||sin}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sunnju}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*sunjō||truth, excuse}} and {{m|gem-pro|*sundī}}, {{m|gem-pro|*sundijō||sin}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro||<nowiki>*</nowiki>h₁s-ónt-ih₂}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*h₁sónts}} {{gloss|"being, true", implying a verdict of "truly guilty" against an accusation or charge}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*h₁es-||to be}}; compare {{cog|ang|soþ|sōþ}} {{gloss|"true"; see {{l|en|sooth}}}}. {{doublet|en|suttee}}.

sink.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*sengʷ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|synken}}, from {{der|en|ang|sincan}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*sinkwan}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*sinkwaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sengʷ-||to fall, sink}}.

ski.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*skey-}} From {{der|en|no|-}} {{m|nb|ski}}, from {{der|en|non|skíð|t=stick of wood, snowshoe}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*skīdą|t=stick}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*skey-|t=to cut, split}} (see also {{m|en|shed}}). Cognate with {{cog|ang|sċīd|t=stick of wood}} (modern {{dbt|en|shide|notext=1}}), {{cog|goh|skit}} (Modern {{cog|de|Scheit|t=log}}).

slide.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:sliden|tree=1|text=++}} Cognate with {{cog|goh|slītan||to slide}} (whence {{cog|de|schlittern}}), {{cog|gml|slīden||to slide}}, {{cog|dum|slīden||to slide}} (whence {{cog|nl|slijderen}}, frequentative of now obsolete {{m|nl|slijden}}), {{cog|sa-ved|स्रेधति|tr=srédhati||to err, blunder}}.

soccer.raw: Originally [[British English]]; as an abbreviation for {{m|en|association football}}, via abbreviation {{suffix|en|assoc.|er|id2=Oxford|pos2=suffix}}; earlier {{m|en|socker}} (1885), also {{m|en|socca}} (1889), with {{m|en|soccer}} attested 1888.

chain: to verify, prove the validity of
to verify, prove, confirm, bear witness to

Cognate with {{cog|da|sande|t=to verify}}, {{cog|sv|sanna|t=to verify}}, {{cog|is|sanna|t=to verify}}. See also {{m|en|sooth}}. Displaced {{ncog|ang|frēfran|}}, {{m|ang|ġefrēfran||to comfort, console, soothe}}, and partially displaced {{ncog|ang|stillan|}}, {{m|ang|ġestillan||to calm, be

sort.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ser- (bind)}} From {{inh|en|enm|sort}}, {{m|enm|soort}}, {{m|enm|sorte}} (cognate {{cog|nl|soort}}, {{cog|de|Sorte}}, {{cog|da|sort}}, {{cog|sv|sort}}), borrowed from {{der|en|fro|sorte||class, kind}}, from {{der|en|la|sortem}}, accusative form of {{m|la|sors||lot, fate, share, rank, category}}.

soul.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:soule|id=spirit|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|soule}}, {{m|enm|sowle}}, {{m|enm|saule}}, {{m|enm|sawle}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sāwol|t=soul, life, spirit, being}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*saiwalu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*saiwalō|t=soul}}, of an uncertain ultimate origin (see there for further information). {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|saul}}, {{m|sco|sowel|t=soul}}, {{cog|stq|Seele|t=soul}}, {{cog|fy|siel|t=soul}}, {{cog|gsw|Seel|t=soul}}, {{cog|gmw-cfr|Siel|t=soul}}, {{cog|nl|ziel|t=soul}}, {{cog|de|Seele|t=soul}}, {{cog|nds-de|Seel|t=soul}}, {{cog|lb|Séil|t=soul, spir

spook.raw: Borrowed from {{bor|en|nl|spook|t=ghost}}, from {{der|en|dum|spooc|t=spook, ghost}}, from {{der|en|odt|*spōk}}, ultimately from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*spōk}}.

staff.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*stebʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|staf}}, from {{inh|en|ang|stæf|t=letter of the alphabet}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*stab}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*stabaz}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|staf}}, {{cog|de|Stab}}, {{cog|da|stav}}, {{cog|sv|stav}}.
