steak.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:steike<ety:bor<non:steik>>}} From {{inh|en|enm|steike}}, from {{der|en|non|steik||roast; meat roasted on a stick}}. The verb is either from the noun or from {{m|non|steikja||to roast}}.

cogs: to be astonished, be stunned, be blocked
stupid.raw: {{etymon|en|:der|frm:stupide<ety:der<la:stupidus>>|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)tewp-}} From {{der|en|frm|stupide}}, from {{der|en|la|stupidus||struck senseless, amazed}}, from {{m|la|stupeō||be amazed or confounded, be struck senseless}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)tup-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*(s)tewp-||to push, stick}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)tew-||to push, hit}}. Cognate with {{cog|goh|stubarōn||to be astonished, be stunned, be blocked}}. Related also to {{cog|ang|stoppian||to block, stop}}. More at [[stop]].

such.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|such}}, {{m|enm|swuch}}, {{m|enm|swich}}, {{m|enm|swilch}}, {{m|enm|swulch}}, from {{inh|en|ang|swelċ}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*swalīk}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*swalīkaz|t=so formed, so like}}, equivalent to so + like. Cognate with {{cog|sco|swilk}}, {{m|sco|sic}}, {{m|sco|sik|t=such}}, {{cog|stq|suk|t=such}}, {{cog|fy|suk}}, {{m|fy|sok|t=such}}, {{cog|nds|sülk}}, {{m|nds|sulk}}, {{m|nds|suk|t=such}}, {{cog|nl|zulk|t=such}}, {{cog|de|solch|t=such}}, {{cog|da|slig|t=like that, such}}, {{cog|sv|slik|t=such}}, {{cog|is|slíkur|t=such}}. More at {{m|en|so}}, {{m|en|like}}.

suit.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:sute<id:clothes>|tree=1|text=++|doublet=suite}} Cognate with {{cog|it|seguire}} and {{cog|es|seguir}}. Related to {{m|en|sue}} and {{m|en|segue}}.

sum.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|summe}}, from {{der|en|fro|summe}}, from {{der|en|la|summa||highest point; sum}}, from {{m|la|summus||highest}}.

sword.raw: {{inh+|en|enm-wmi|sword}} ({{m|enm|swerd}} in most dialects), from {{inh|en|ang|sweord||sword}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*swerd||sword}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*swerdą||sword}}, possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*seh₂w-||sharp}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|frr|Swērt}}, {{m|frr|Swiirt}}, {{m|frr|swörd||sword}}, {{cog|stq|Swid}}, {{m|stq|Swäid||sword}}, {{cog|fy|swurd||sword}}, {{cog|nl|zwaard||sword}}, {{cog|de|Schwert||sword}}, {{cog|lb|Schwäert||sword}}, {{cog|wym|świert||sword}}, {{cog|yi|שווערד||sword}}, {{cog|da|sværd||sword}}, {{cog|fo|svørð||sword}}, {{cog|is|sverð||sword}}, {{cog|n

chain: hollow device for controlling the flow of liquid from a hole, cock, faucet, spigot; hole through which the liquid flows; the liquid which thus flows
tap.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*deh₂p-}} The {{glossary|noun}} is derived from {{inh|en|enm|tappe|t=hollow device for controlling the flow of liquid from a hole, cock, faucet, spigot; hole through which the liquid flows; the liquid which thus flows}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=tap(pe|pos=''n.''(1)|noformat=1|id=MED44515}}</ref> from {{inh|en|ang|tæppa}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*tappō}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*tappô|t=a plug, tap; peg; tapering stick}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*deh₂p-|t=to lose; to sacrifice}}.<ref>Compare {{R:OED Online|pos=''n.''{{sup|1}}|noformat=1|id=7871448854|date=September 2023|nodot=1}}

tape.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:tape|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|tape,tappe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|tæppa,tæppe||ribbon, tape}}; further origin unclear.

thorough.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*terh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|thoruȝ}}, {{m|enm|þoruȝ}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þuruh}}, a byform of {{inh|en|ang|þurh}}, whence comes {{cog|en|through}}. The adjective derives from the preposition and adverb. The word developed a syllabic form in cases where the word was fully stressed: when it was used as an adverb, adjective, or noun, and less commonly when used as a preposition.

though.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:thogh|tree=1}} From {{ncog|enm|though}}, {{m|enm|thogh}}, from {{der|en|non|*þóh}} (later {{m|non|þó}}). Superseded (in most dialects) {{inh|en|enm|thegh}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þēah||though, although, even if, that, however, nevertheless, yet, still; whether}}. Both the Old Norse and Old English are from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*þauh||though}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*to-}}, suffixed with {{der|en|gem-pro|*-hw}} < {{der|en|ine-pro|*-kʷe||and}}.

through.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*terh₂-}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:thurgh|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|thurgh}}, {{m|enm|thrugh}}, {{m|enm|thruch}}, {{m|enm|thruh}}, [[metathetic]] variants of {{m|enm|thurgh}}, {{m|enm|thurh}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þurh}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*þurhw||through}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*tr̥h₂kʷe}}, suffixed zero-grade from {{m|ine-pro|*terh₂-||to pass through}} + {{m|ine-pro|*-kʷe||and}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|frr|döör||through}}, {{cog|stq|truch||through}}, {{cog|fy|troch||through}}, {{cog|nl|door||through}}, {{cog|de|durch||through}}, {{cog|lb|duerch||through}}, {{cog|v

thumb.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*tewh₂-}} Derived from {{inh|en|enm|thombe}}, {{m|enm|thoume}}, {{m|enm|thoumbe||thumb}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þūma||thumb}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*þūmō||thumb}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*þūmô||thumb}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*tūm-||to grow}}.

chain: thus, in this way, as follows, in this manner, to this extent
thus.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|thus}}, {{m|enm|þus}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þus|t=thus, in this way, as follows, in this manner, to this extent}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*þus|t=so, thus}}, perhaps originally from a variant of the instrumental form of {{l|en|this}}, related to {{cog|ang|þȳs|t=by this, with this}}, {{cog|osx|thius|t=by this, with this}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|thus|t=thus}}, {{cog|frr|aldoz|thus}}, {{cog|stq|dus}}, {{m|stq|düs|t=thus}}, {{cog|fy|dus|t=thus}}, {{cog|nl|dus|t=thus, so}}, {{cog|gmh|dus|t=thus, as follows}}.

thyme.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰewh₂-}} From {{der|en|enm|tyme}}, from {{der|en|fro|thym}}, from {{der|en|la|thymum}}, from {{der|en|grc|θύμον|}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|boþen}}.

touch.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*dewk-}} From {{inh|en|enm|touchen}}, {{m|enm|tochen}}, from {{der|en|fro|tochier|t=to touch}} (whence Modern {{cog|fr|toucher}}; compare French doublet {{m|fr|toquer||to offend, bother, harass}}), from {{der|en|la-vul|*tuccō|t=to knock, strike, offend}}, from {{der|en|frk|*tukkōn|t=to knock, strike, touch}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*tukkōną|t=to tug, grab, grasp}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dewk-|t=to draw, pull, lead}}. Largely displaced native {{ncog|enm|rinen}}, from {{ncog|ang|hrīnan}} (whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|rine}}). Doublet of {{m|en|tuck}}.

chain: tough, tenacious, holding fast together; pliant; sticky, glutinous, clammy
tough.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*denḱ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|tough}}, {{m|enm|towgh}}, {{m|enm|tou}}, {{m|enm|toȝ}}, from {{inh|en|ang|tōh|t=tough, tenacious, holding fast together; pliant; sticky, glutinous, clammy}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*tą̄h(ī)}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*tanhuz|t=fitting; clinging; tenacious; tough}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*tinganą|t=to press upon, throng}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*denḱ-|t=to bite}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|stq|toai|t=tough}}, {{cog|bar|zaach}}, {{m|bar|zach|t=tough}}, {{cog|nl|taai|t=tough}}, {{cog|de|zäh}}, {{m|de|zähe|t=tough}}, {{cog|li|tiee|t=tough}}, {{cog|lb

tray.raw: {{etymon|en|id=object|:inh|enm:trey<id:tray>}} From {{inh|en|enm|trey|id=tray}}, from {{inh|en|ang|trēġ}}, {{m|ang|trīġ|t=wooden board, tray}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*trauwi}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*trawją|t=wooden vessel}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*drewo-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*dóru|t=tree; wood}}. Cognate with {{cog|non|treyja|t=carrier}}, {{cog|gmq-osw|trø|t=wooden grain measure}}, {{cog|nds|Treechel|t=dough trough}}, {{cog|grc|δροίτη|t=tub, vat}}, {{cog|sa|द्रोण|t=trough}}. Related to {{m|en|trough}} and {{m|en|tree}}.

trek.raw: {{ety|en|:bor|af:trek<id:to move>|tree=1}} From {{bor|en|af|trek}}, from {{der|en|nl|trekken}}, from {{der|en|dum|trekken|pos=weak verb}} and {{m|dum|treken|trēken|pos=strong verb|t=to trek, place, bring, move}}, from {{der|en|odt|*trekkan}}, {{m|odt|*trekan}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*trekan}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*trekaną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*trakjaną|t=to drag, haul, scrape, pull}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dreg-|t=to drag, scrape}}.

trough.raw: {{PIE word|en|dóru}} From {{inh|en|enm|trogh}}, from {{inh|en|ang|troh}}, {{m|ang|trog|t=a trough, tub, basin, vessel for containing liquids or other materials}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*trog}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*trugą}}, {{m|gem-pro|*trugaz}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*drukós}}, enlargement of {{m|ine-pro|*dóru||tree}}.

tub.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|tubbe}}, {{m|enm|tobbe}}, from {{der|en|dum|tubbe}} or {{der|en|gml|tubbe}}, {{m|gml|tobbe}}, further etymology unknown. Considered to be unrelated to {{m|en|tube}}.<ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref>

tube.raw: {{etymon|en|:der|frm:tube}} From {{der|en|frm|tube}}, from {{der|en|la|tubus|t=tube, pipe}}, related to {{m|la|tuba||long trumpet; war-trumpet}}, of obscure ultimate origin, but possibly connected to {{m|la|tībia||shinbone, reed-pipe}}; see there. {{doublet|en|tubus}}.

tune.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ten-}} From {{inh|en|enm|tune}}, an unexplained variant of {{m|en|tone}},<ref>http://www.dictionary.com/browse/tune?s=t</ref> from {{der|en|fro|ton}}, from {{der|en|la|tonus}}, from {{der|en|grc|τόνος|t=a tone}}. {{doublet|en|tone|ton|tonus}}.

unit.raw: Formerly {{m|en|unite}}, a later form of {{m|en|unity}}; see {{m|en|unity}}.

unlock.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|unloken}}, {{m|enm|unlouken}}, {{m|enm|onlouken}}, from {{inh|en|ang|onlūcan|t=to unlock}}, equivalent to {{pre|en|un|lock|id1=reversive}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|ontluiken|t=to unlock}}.

uphold.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|upholden}}, equivalent to {{prefix|en|up|hold}}. Compare {{cog|nl|ophouden||to stop, cease, hold up}}, {{cog|de|aufhalten||to stop, halt, detain}}. Compare also {{cog|gml|upholt}}, {{cog|non|upphald||uphold, support}}.

veil.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*weg-}} From {{inh|en|enm|veil}}, {{m|enm|veyl}}, from {{der|en|xno|-}} and {{der|en|fro-nor|veil||sail, veil, shroud}} ([[Francien]] Old French {{m|fro|voil}}, French {{m|fr|voile}}), {{der|en|la|vēlum||cloth, covering}}. Displaced {{noncog|enm|scleire}}, {{m|enm|scleyre}}, {{m|enm|sleyre}}, {{m|enm|slyre|t=veil}} (compare {{noncog|de|Schleier}}). {{doublet|en|velum|voile}}.

vein.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:veine|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|veine}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|veine}}, from {{der|en|la|vēna||a blood-vessel; vein; artery}} of uncertain origin. See {{m|la|vēna}} for more. {{doublet|en|vena}}. Displaced native {{m|enm|edre}}, from {{m|ang|ǣdre}} (whence {{m|en|edder}}).

vine.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:vyne|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*weh₁y-}} From {{inh|en|enm|vyne}}, from {{der|en|xno|vigne}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|vīnia}}, from {{der|en|la|vīnea|t=vines in a vineyard}}, from {{m|la|vīneus|t=related to wine}}, from {{m|la|vīnum|t=wine}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*wīnom}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wóyh₁nom|t=vine, wine}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*weh₁y-|t=to twist, wrap}}. {{doublet|en|wine}}.

vision.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*weyd-}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:visioun|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|visioun}}, from {{der|en|xno|visioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|vision}}, from {{der|en|la|vīsiō|t=vision, seeing}}, noun of action from the perfect passive participle {{m|la|visus|t=that which is seen}}, from the verb {{m|la|videō|t=to see}} + action noun suffix {{m|la|-iō}}.

vow.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁wegʷʰ-}} {{inh+|en|enm|vowe}}, {{m|enm|voue}}, that from {{der|en|fro|vut}}, in turn from {{der|en|la|vōtum||a promise, dedication, vow}}, from {{m|la|voveo|vovēre|to promise, vow}}. Not related to {{m|en|avow}}. {{doublet|en|vote}}.

voyage.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:viage}} From {{inh|en|enm|viage}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|viage}} and {{der|en|fro|voiage}}, from {{der|en|la|viaticum}}. The modern spelling is under the influence of Modern {{der|en|fr|voyage}}. {{doublet|en|viaticum}}.

waltz.raw: From {{bor|en|de|Walzer}}, from {{m|de|walzen||to dance}}, from {{der|en|goh|walzan||to turn}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*walt-||to turn}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*welH-||to turn}}. {{doublet|en|valse}}. More at {{m|gem-pro|*waltaną}}.

cogs: struggle, resistance, defense, effort, exertion, activity
war.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:werre<id:war>|tree=1}} {{inh+|en|enm|werre}}, from Late {{inh|en|ang|werre//wyrre||armed conflict}}, from {{der|en|xno|-}} and {{der|en|fro-nor|guerre//werre}} (compare modern {{cog|fr|guerre}}), from {{der|en|la-med|werra}}, from {{der|en|frk|*werʀu|t=confusion; quarrel}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wers-|t=to mix up, confuse, beat, thresh}}. Gradually displaced native {{ncog|ang|beadu}}, {{m|ang|hild}}, {{m|ang|ġewinn}}, {{m|ang|orleġe}}, {{m|ang|wīġ}}, and many others as the general term for "war" during the Middle English period.

chain: keeper, watchman, guard, guardian, protector; lord, king; possessor
ward.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*wer-|id=heed}} From {{inh|en|enm|warde}}, from {{inh|en|ang|weard||keeper, watchman, guard, guardian, protector; lord, king; possessor}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*warduz||guard, keeper}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wer-||to heed, defend}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|waard}}, {{cog|de|Wart}}.

weird.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*wert-}} From {{der|en|enm|werde}}, {{m|enm|wierde}}, {{m|enm|wirde}}, {{m|enm|wyrede}}, {{m|enm|wurde}}, from {{der|en|ang|wyrd||fate}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*wurdi}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*wurdiz}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wert-||to turn, wind}}. Cognate with {{cog|is|urður||fate}}. Related to {{cog|ang|weorþan||to become}}; more at {{l|en|worth#Etymology_2|pos=verb}}.

wheat.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|whete}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hwǣte}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hwaitī}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hwaitijaz}} (compare {{cog|fy|weet}}, {{cog|nl|weit}}, {{cog|nds|Weten}}, {{cog|de|Weizen}}, {{cog|da|hvede}}, {{cog|sv|vete}}, {{cog|nb|hvete}}, {{cog|nn|kveite}}, {{cog|fo,is|hveiti}}), from {{m|gem-pro|*hwītaz||white}}. More at {{m|en|white}}.

wilderness.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*wel-|*gʷʰel-|*dʰwes-}} From {{inh|en|enm|wildernes}}, {{m|enm|wildernesse|t=desolate or uninhabited place, desolation}}{{nb...|wildernese, wildernise, wildernosse, wildirnes, wilirnesse, wildirenes, wildurnes, wildurnesse, wildrenes, wildrenesse, wyldernesse, wyldernys|otherforms=1}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=wī̆ldernes(se|pos=n|id=MED52762}}</ref> and then either:

willow.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|wilwe}}, {{m|enm|welew}}, variant of {{m|enm|wilghe}}, from {{der|en|ang|weliġ}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*wilig}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*wiligaz}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*welik-}} (compare (Arcadian) {{cog|grc|ἑλίκη}}, {{cog|hit|𒌑𒂖𒆪||tr=welku|grass}}), from {{m|ine-pro|*wel-||twist, turn}}. Cognate to {{cog|fy|wylch}} and more distantly (via {{cog|gmw-pro|*wilgijā}}) to {{cog|nl|wilg}} and {{cog|de|Wilge}}.

cogs: to set apart; to separate out

worm.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:worm|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|werm,wirm,worm,worme,wrim,wurm,wyrm,wyrme}}, from {{inh|en|ang|weorm}}, {{m|ang|wurm}}, {{m|ang|wyrm}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wurmi}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wurmiz|t=worm; snake}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*wr̥mis|t=worm; larva}}, possibly from {{m|ine-pro|*wer-|t=to turn}}. {{doublet|en|vermin|wyrm}}, the latter of which is a fairly recent borrowing directly from the Old English.

worth.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*wert-}} From {{inh|en|enm|worth}}, from {{inh|en|ang|weorþ}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*werþ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*werþaz|t=worthy, valuable}}; from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wert-}}.

wreath.raw: {{multiple images |direction = vertical |image1 = Wreath.jpg |caption1 = A wreath. |image2 = POL COA Wałęsa.png |caption2 = A wreath, or torse, in argent (silver) and gules (red) lies atop the helmet, under the eagle. }}

wrist.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*wreyt-}} From {{inh|en|enm|wrist}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wrist}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wristu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wristuz}} (compare {{cog|ofs|wrist}}, {{cog|nds|Wrist}}, {{cog|de|Rist|t=back of hand, instep, withers}}, {{cog|sv|vrist}}), from {{der|en|gem-pro|*wrīþaną|t=to twist, turn}}. More at {{m|en|writhe}}.

yolk.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵʰelh₃-}} From {{inh|en|enm|yolke}}, {{m|enm|yelke}}, {{m|enm|ȝolke}}, {{m|enm|ȝelke}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ġeolca}}, {{m|ang|ġeoloca}}, {{m|ang|ġioleca|t=the yellow part, yolk}}, derived from {{der|en|ang|ġeolu|t=yellow}} + {{m|ang|-ca|pos=diminutive suffix}}.

chain: the state of being young; youth
youth.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:youthe|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|youthe}}, {{m|enm|youghte}}, {{m|enm|ȝouþe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ġeoguþ|t=the state of being young; youth}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*juwunþa}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*jugunþō}}, {{m|gem-pro|*jugunþiz|t=youth}}, corresponding to {{af|en|young|-th|id2=abstract nominal|pos2=abstract nominal suffix}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Juugd}}, {{cog|fy|jeugd}}, {{cog|nl|jeugd}}, {{cog|nds-de|Jöögd}}, {{cog|de|Jugend}}.

autobus.raw: {{etymon|en|:af|auto-<id:automobile>|bus<id:omnibus>|tree=1}} {{multiple images |direction = vertical |image1 = Bus TCM ligne 1 - Mulhouse 1966.jpg |caption1 = An autobus ''(sense 1)'' in [[Mulhouse]], [[Haut-Rhin]], [[France]], in 1966. |image2 = Tour de france 2005 10th stage mpk 09.jpg |caption2 = The autobus ''(sense 2)'' at [[stage#Noun|Stage]] 10 of the {{w|2005 Tour de France}}. }}

chain: glad, happy, joyful; causing joy, joyous; gentle, mild; gracious, merciful; bright, shining; beautiful, fair
blithe.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰel-|id=shiny}} From {{inh|en|enm|blithe|t=glad, happy, joyful; causing joy, joyous; gentle, mild; gracious, merciful; bright, shining; beautiful, fair}}{{nb...|blide, bligh, bliht, blith, bliðe, bliþ, bliþe, bliȝe, blyde, blyth, blythe, blyþe|otherforms=1}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=blīthe|pos=adj|id=MED5249}}</ref> from {{inh|en|ang|blīþe|t=happy, gentle}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*blīþī}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*blīþiz|t=friendly; gentle, mild; pleasing}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰlī-|t=fine; light; pleasant}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰel-|t=shiny; white}}.<ref>Compare {{R

bough.raw: {{PIE word|en|bʰeh₂ǵʰús}} [[File:Lago Dobson 08.jpg|thumb|A bough ''(sense 1)'' of a [[pencil pine]] ({{taxlink|Athrotaxis cupressoides|species}}) in {{w|Mount Field National Park}}, [[Tasmania]], [[Australia]].]]

camouflage.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id1=head|*mewH-|*melh₂-|id3=grind|*pel-|id4=skin}} {{ety|en|:ubor|fr:camouflage|tree=1}} {{ubor|en|fr|camouflage}}, from {{m|fr|camoufler|t=to veil, disguise}}, alteration (due to {{m|fr|camouflet|t=smoke blown in one's face}}) of {{der|en|it|camuffare|t=to muffle the head}}, from {{m|it|ca-}} (from {{der|en|it|capo|t=head}}) + {{m|it|muffare|t=to muffle}}, from {{der|en|la-med|muffula|muffula, muffla|t=muff}}. This Medieval Latin, from which there is also {{cog|en|muffle}}, is either derived from a {{der|en|frk|*molfell|t=soft garment made of hide}} from {{m|gmw-pro|*m

cello.raw: {{clipping|en|violoncello}}, the original name, from {{der|en|it|violoncello||little [[violone]]}}, from {{m|it|violone||an early form of the [[double bass]]}} + {{m|it|-cello||[[-elle]]|pos=forming [[diminutive]]s}}, {{m|it|violone||big [[viola]]}} itself being derived from {{m|it|viola}} + {{m|it|-one||[[-oon]]|pos=forming [[augmentative]]s}}.

chain: sparkling wine from the Champagne region
champagne.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*kh₂em-}} [[File:Verre Champagne.jpg|thumb|A glass of champagne]] [[File:Blason Le Sars.svg|right|thumb|Azure, a church argent on a champagne or (arms of Le Sars).]]

chav.raw: Origin {{unc|en|nocap=1}}; probably of {{der|en|rme|-}} origin. Compare {{cog|rom|chavi|t=male child}} or {{m|rom|ćhavo}}, {{m|rom|shavo|t=female child}}, {{m|rom|chal|t=boy}}, {{m|rom|chavvy|t=mate, friend}}, compare {{cog|sv|tjej}}; possibly cognate with {{cog|pt|chavalo}}, {{cog|es|chaval}}, {{cog|de|Chabo}}, {{cog|ru|чувак}}, {{cog|hu|csávó}}. See also {{m|en|charva}}.

codeine.raw: From {{der|en|fr|codéine}}, from {{af|en|κώδεια|-ine|lang1=grc|t1=capsule of the poppy, poppy head}}.

combustion.raw: From {{uder|en|fro|combustion}}, from {{der|en|la|combustio}}, from {{m|la|comburere||to burn}}, itself from the intensifying prefix [[com-]] + the root [[burere]] (a faulty sep. of [[amburere]] "to burn around", itself from [[ambi-]] + [[urere]] "to burn, singe"); equivalent to {{suffix|en|combust|ion|nocat=1}}.

flak.raw: Borrowed from {{bor|en|de|FlaK}}, short for {{m|de|Fliegerabwehrkanone|'''''Fl'''ieger'''a'''bwehr'''k'''anone''|anti airplane cannon}}.

gasoline.raw: {{etymon|en|:af|gas<id:matter>|-ol<id:oil>|-ine<id:chemistry>|tree=1}} From {{suffix|en|gas|ol}} (suffix used in the names of oils) {{suffix|en||ine}} (suffix used in the names of derivatives). So called because it was originally used in the manufacture and enrichment of domestic gases, such as [[air gas]].<ref>{{cite book|last=O'Connor|first=Henry|year=1909|title=Petrol Air-Gas: A Practical Handbook on the Installation and Working of Air-Gas Lighting Systems for Country Houses|location=London|publisher=Crosby Lockwood & Son|page=14|url=https://archive.org/details/petrolairgasprac00oconrich/pa

ginkgo.raw: From {{der|en|ja|銀杏|tr=ginkyō}}, from {{der|en|zh|-}} {{zh-l|銀杏||silver apricot}}. ''Gink'''g'''o'' is the name that is printed in ''Amoenitatum exoticarum politico-physico-medicarum Fasciculi V [...]'' (1712) authored by {{w|Engelbert Kaempfer}}, the first Westerner to see the species. In his way of transcription ''gink'''y'''o'' would have been ''Gink'''j'''o'' or ''Gink'''i'''o'' but was printed as ''Gink'''g'''o''.<ref>Wolfgang Michel, [//catalog.lib.kyushu-u.ac.jp/opac_download_md/2898/Ginkgo_biloba2_revised_2011.pdf ''On Engelbert Kaempfer’s “Ginkgo”'', 2011]</ref> This was read by {{w|C

hearth.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|herth}}, {{m|enm|herthe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|heorþ}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*herþ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*herþaz}}, possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kerh₃-||heat; fire}}. Cognate with {{cog|fy|hurd}}, {{cog|nl|haard}}, {{cog|de|Herd}}, {{cog|sv|härd}}. {{etydate|{{w|Old English}} period}}.

heretic.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|heretyk}}, {{m|enm|heretike}}, from {{der|en|fro|eretique}}, from {{der|en|la-med|-}} or {{der|en|la-ecc|haereticus}}, from {{der|en|grc|αἱρετικός|t=able to choose, factious}}, itself from {{der|en|grc|αἱρέω|t=to choose}}.

hutch.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|hucche||storage chest}}, variation of {{m|enm|whucce}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hwiċe}}, {{m|ang|hwiċċe||box, chest}}. Spelling influenced by {{cog|fro|huche||chest}}, from {{cog|la-med|hūtica}}, from a different {{cog|gem}} root, from {{cog|frk|*hutta}}, from {{cog|gem-pro|*hudjō}}, {{m|gem-pro|*hudjǭ||box, hut, hutch}}. Akin to {{cog|ang|hȳdan||to conceal; hide}}. More at {{m|en|hide}}, {{m|en|hut}}.

chain: fluidity, liquidness, a fluid, a liquid
liquor.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|licour}}, from {{der|en|xno|licour}}, from {{der|en|la|liquor||fluidity, liquidness, a fluid, a liquid}}, from {{m|la|liqueo|liquere|to be fluid or liquid}}; see {{l|en|liquid}}. {{doublet|en|liqueur}}.

lithe.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|lithe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|līþe||gentle, mild}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*linþ(ī)}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*linþaz}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*lentos}}.

loathe.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|lothe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lāþian}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*laiþēn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*laiþāną}}. Cognate with {{cog|non|leiða|leiðask}} ( > {{cog|da|lede|ledes}}, {{cog|is|leiðast}}, all reflexive), {{cog|de|Leid}}.

lunatic.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*lewk-}} From {{inh|en|enm|lunatik}}, from {{der|en|fro|lunatique}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|lunaticus|t=moonstruck}}, derived from {{der|en|la|luna|t=moon}}, the connection stemming from the belief that changes of the moon caused intermittent insanity.

omnibus.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|fr:omnibus|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃ep-}} [[File:First vehicle to cross Holborn Viaduct.png|thumb|A horse-drawn '''omnibus''' ''(sense 1)'' in [[London]], UK, in 1902]] [[File:Shillibeer's first omnibus.png|thumb|Shillibeer's first '''omnibus''' of 1829]]

ore.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|or}}, {{m|enm|oor}}, blend of {{inh|en|ang|ōra|t=ore, unwrought metal}}, of uncertain origin, and {{m|ang|ār|t=brass, copper, bronze}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*aiʀ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*aiz}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*h₂éyos}}.

outrage.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|outrage}}, from {{der|en|fro|outrage}}, {{m|fro|oultrage||excess}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*ultrāticum}} ("a going beyond"), derived from {{der|en|la|ultrā||beyond}}. Later reanalysed as {{af|en|out-|rage}}, whence the contemporary pronunciation, though neither of these are etymologically related.

pal.raw: {{PIE word|en|bʰréh₂tēr}} {{dercat|en|inc-pro|iir-pro|ine-pro}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|rme|pal|t=brother, friend}}, from {{der|en|rom|phral|t=brother}}, from {{der|en|sa|भ्रातृ|t=brother}}. {{doublet|en|bhai|brother|bru|frater|friar|vai}}.

chain: one of the first, chief, excellent, noble
primate.raw: {{etydate|1876}}. From {{bor|en|fr|primate}}, from the {{glossary|substantivization}} of {{der|en|la|prīmās|prīmās, prīmātis|one of the first, chief, excellent, noble}}, same as [[#Etymology 2|Etymology 2]]. So named due to the belief that primates are the highest order of mammals or animals.

psalm.raw: From {{der|en|enm|salm}} or {{m|enm|psalme}}, from {{der|en|ang|psealm}}, later reinforced from {{der|en|fro|psalme}} (modern French {{m|fr|psaume}}), both from {{der|en|la|psalmus}}, from {{der|en|grc|ψαλμός||the sound emanating from twitching or twanging perhaps with the hands or fingers, mostly of musical strings}} (from {{m|grc|ψάλλω||to make a sound by striking, touching, plucking, rubbing, twanging, or vibrating}}), but later in New Testament times the meaning of {{m|grc|ψαλμός}} evolved from its Classical meaning of "a tune played to the harp" to a more general tune that could be played

ptarmigan.raw: From {{bor|en|gd|tarmachan}}, of unknown origin. The ''pt-'' comes from a mistaken belief in a Greek origin, as if related to {{m|en|ptero-||wing}}.

quiche.raw: {{bor+|en|fr|quiche}}, from [[Lorraine]] {{der|en|gmw-rfr|Küeche||cake}}, from {{der|en|gmh|kuoche}} ({{cog|de|Kuchen}}, {{cog|en|kuchen}}), from {{der|en|goh|kuocho}}, {{m|goh|kuohho}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*kōkô}} ({{cog|en|cookie}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gog-|t=ball-shaped object}}, whence also {{cog|en|cake}} (via {{cog|gem-pro|*kakǭ|t=cake}}). Compare {{cog|fa|کوکو|tr=kuku|t=quiche}}. More at {{l|en|cake}}.

sine.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|la:sinus<id:curve>|tree=1|id=trigonometry}} {{bor+|en|la|sinus||curve, bend; bosom}}, a translation of {{der|en|ar|جَيْب||bosom}}, a misidentification of the notation {{m|ar||جيب|tr=j-y-b}}, written without [[harakat|vowel diacritics]], standing for {{der|en|ar|جِيبَ||sine}}, in turn from {{der|en|sa|ज्या||sine, chord, bowstring}} through the similar {{der|en|sa|जीव||sine, chord, life, existence}}. {{doublet|en|sinus}}.

slough.raw: {{etymid|en|from skin-referent origins}} From {{inh|en|enm|slogh}}, {{m|enm|slugh}}, {{m|enm|slouh}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*sluk-}}, perhaps related to {{m|gem-pro|*sleupaną|t=to slip, sneak}} (compare {{cog|got|𐍃𐌻𐌹𐌿𐍀𐌰𐌽}}).

spiv.raw: {{unk|en}}. Perhaps from {{m|en|spiff}}, {{m|en|spiffy}}. ''Spiv'' was the nickname of Henry Bagster, a Londoner arrested a number of times in 1904-6 for activities as described below, and may have been the [[archetype]]. Also possibly from {{der|en|rom|spiv|t=sparrow}}, as active and opportunistic.

chain: to project out; stand out stiffly; to exert oneself, struggle
strut.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)ter-}} The {{glossary|verb}} is derived from {{inh|en|enm|strouten}}, {{m|enm|struten|t=to bulge, swell; to protrude, stick out; to bluster, threaten; to object forcefully; to create a disturbance; to fight; to display one's clothes in a proud or vain manner}}{{nb...|strote, stroute, strouʒten, strowte, strut, strute|otherforms=1}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=strǒuten|pos=v|id=MED43407}}</ref> from {{inh|en|ang|strūtian|t=to project out; stand out stiffly; to exert oneself, struggle}},<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''v.''{{sup|1}}|noformat=1|id=191974|date=1919}}</ref><ref name="L

sulfate.raw: From {{der|en|fr|sulfate}}, from {{der|en|la-new|sulphatum}}, taken from the expression {{m|la|acidum sulphatum||sulfuric acid}}, from {{m|la|sulphatus}}, from {{der|en|la|sulphur||sulfur}}. The term was first used in 1787 by the French chemist [[:w:Louis-Bernard Guyton de Morveau|L. B. G. De Morveau]]. Equivalent to {{af|en|sulfur|-ate|alt1=sulf(ur)|id2=chemical|t2=salt or ester}}.<ref>{{R:svenska.se|saob}}</ref>

teethe.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|tethen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|tēþan|t=to teethe}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*tanþijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*tanþijaną|t=to teethe}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*tanþs|t=tooth}}. Cognate with {{cog|de|zähnen|t=to provide with teeth}}.

cogs: material, stuff; gear, implement, instrument; application; cause, occasion, reason
timber.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*dem-}} From {{der|en|enm|tymber}}, from {{der|en|ang|timber}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*timr}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*timrą|t=building; timber}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dem-|t=to build; to arrange}} (see {{cog|ine-pro|*dṓm|t=home, house}}). {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|nl|timmer|t=building, construction; chamber, room}}, {{cog|de|Zimmer|t=room, timber}}, {{cog|lb|Zëmmer|t=room}}, {{cog|yi|צימער|t=room}}, {{cog|da,nb|tømmer|t=timber}}, {{cog|fo,is|timbur|t=timber, wood}}, {{cog|nn|timber}}, {{m|nn|tymbur}}, {{m|nn|tømmer|t=timber}}, {{cog|sv|timmer|t=timber}}, {{cog|go

accept.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:accepten}} First attested about 1380. From {{inh|en|enm|accepten}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|accepter}}, or directly from {{der|en|la|accepto|acceptō, acceptāre|receive}}, [[frequentative]] of {{m|la|accipiō}}, formed from {{m|la|ad-}} + {{m|la|capiō||to take}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|onfōn}}.

access.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|accesse}}, {{m|enm|acces}}, borrowed from {{der|en|frm|acces||attack, onslaught}} or from its source {{der|en|la|accessus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|accēdō||approach; accede}}, from {{m|la|ad||to, toward, at}} + {{m|la|cēdō||move, yield}}. {{doublet|en|accessus}}. First attested in the early 14th century. The sense "entrance" was first attested about 1380.

accessible.raw: {{etymon|en|:der|fr:-<ety:inh<la-lat:accessibilis>>|tree=1}} First attested in 1400, from {{der|en|fr|-}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|accessibilis|}}, from {{m|la|accessus|}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|accēdō||approach}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|access|ible}}.

ache.raw: {{inh+|en|enm|aken|pos=verb}}, and {{m|enm|ache|pos=noun}}, from {{inh|en|ang|acan|pos=verb}} (from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*akan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*akaną|id=ache|t=to ache}}) and {{m|ang|æċe|pos=noun}} (from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*aki}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*akiz}}), traditionally explained as from a {{inh|en|ine-pro|*h₂égos|nocat=1}}.

chain: to act upon, influence, affect, attack with disease
affect.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:affecten<ety:der<la:affectāre>>|id=influence|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|affecten}}, from {{der|en|la|affectāre}}, from {{der|en|la|affectus}}, the participle stem of {{der|en|la|afficere|t=to act upon, influence, affect, attack with disease}}, from {{m|la|ad-}} + {{m|la|facere||to make, do}}. {{surf|en|af-|la:affectus|alt2=-fect}}.

against.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:ayenes|tree=1}} Formed from {{inh|en|enm|ayenes}}, {{m|enm|agenes}}, {{m|enm|againes||in opposition to}}, a southern variant of {{m|enm|agen}}, or directly from {{m|en|again}}, either way with [[adverbial genitive]] singular ending {{m|en|-es}}; the parasitic {{m|en|-t|id=excrescent}} was added circa 1350, probably by confusion with the superlative ending {{m|en|-est}}. {{surf|en|again|-st|pos2=excrescent ending}}.

aggravate.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷreh₂-}} The {{glossary|adjective}} is {{etydate|1471|nocap=1}} in {{w|Middle English}}, the {{glossary|verb}} in 1530; from {{lbor|en|la|aggravātus|notext=1}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|aggravō||to add to the weight of, make worse, oppress, annoy}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}} and {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|ad-||to}} + {{m|la|gravō||to make heavy}}, from {{m|la|gravis||heavy}} + {{m|la|-ō|id=denominative|pos=verb-forming suffix}}. See {{m|en|grave}} and

allow.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:allowen<ety:bor<xno:alouer<ety:from<fro:aloer<id:allaudare>><fro:aloer<id:allocare>>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|allowen}}, {{m|enm|alowen}}, a borrowing from {{der|en|xno|allouer}}, {{m|fro|alouer}}, from {{der|en|la-med|allaudō|allaudāre}}, merged with {{m|fro|alouer}}, from {{der|en|la-med|allocō||to assign}}. {{doublet|en|allaud}} (via {{m|la|allaudāre}}) or {{m|en|allocate}} (via {{m|la|allocāre}}).

alphabet.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:alphabete<ety:bor<la-cla:alphabētum>>|tree=1}} <div>From {{inh|en|enm|alphabete}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la-cla|alphabētum}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἀλφάβητος}}, from {{m|grc|ἄλφα}} and {{m|grc|βῆτα}}, the names of the first two letters of the [[Greek alphabet]], {{m|grc|Α}} and {{m|grc|Β}}, lowercase forms {{m|grc|α|tr=-}} and {{m|grc|β|tr=-}}. The Greek names derived from {{m|en|aleph}}, the name of the {{der|en|phn|-}} letter {{m|phn|𐤀||ox}} and {{m|en|beth}}, the name of the letter {{m|phn|𐤁||house}}, so called because they were pictograms of those objects, having develope

animate.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂enh₁-}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:animate<alt:animat(e)>|text=+|tree=1|nodot=1}}, from {{der|en|la|animātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|animō||to fill with breath, quicken, encourage, animate}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|anima||soul, spirit, breath}}; see {{m|en|anima}}. The {{glossary|verb}} derives from the {{glossary|adjective}}, see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}.

annex.raw: Borrowed from {{bor|en|fr|annexe}}, from {{der|en|la|annexus}}. More at Etymology 2. See also {{af|en|an-#Etymology_4}}.

announce.raw: {{etymon|en|:der|fro:anoncier|tree=1}} From {{der|en|fro|anoncier}}, from {{der|en|la|annuntio|annūntiāre}}, from {{m|la|ad}} + {{m|la|nūntiō|t=report, relate}}, from {{m|la|nūntius|t=messenger, bearer of news}}. See {{m|en|nuncio}}. {{doublet|en|annunciate|}}. See also {{af|en|an-#Etymology_4}}.

approach.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:aprochen<ety:bor<fro:aprochier>>|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*-kʷe}} From {{inh|en|enm|aprochen}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry= ap(p)rōchen|pos=v|id=MED1992}}</ref> borrowed from {{der|en|fro|aprochier}} (modern {{cog|fr|approcher}}), from {{der|en|la-lat|appropio|appropiāre}}, a verb based on {{der|en|la|prope|t=near}},<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=v|id=9838|date=March 2021|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=v}}</ref> ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*pro-}} (a variant of {{m|ine-pro|*per-|id=before|t=before, in front; first}}) + {{m|ine-pro|*-kʷe|t={{glossary|suffix}} forming [[distributive]]

argument.raw: {{wikidata lexeme|L4501}} {{etymon|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:argument<ety:bor<xno:arguement<ety:der<la:argūmentum>>>>|:afeq|argue|-ment|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂erǵ-}} {{dercat|en|itc-pro|ine-pro}} From {{inh|en|enm|argument}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=argūment|pos=n|id=MED2217}}</ref> from {{der|en|xno|-}} and {{der|en|fro|arguement}}, from {{der|en|la|argumentum}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=10663|date=March 2021|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=n}}</ref> The English word is analysable as {{suffix|en|argue|ment}}. {{doublet|en|argumentum}}.

arrange.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:arengen<ety:bor<fro:arangier>>|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)ker- (turn)}} Inherited from {{inh|en|enm|arengen}}, {{m|enm|arrangen|t=to draw up a battle line}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|arengier}}, {{m|fro|arangier|t=to put in a line, put in a row}}, derived from {{m|fro|reng}}, {{m|fro|rang}}, {{m|fro|ranc|t=line, row, rank}}, from {{der|en|frk|*hring|t=ring}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*hringaz}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)krengʰ-}}, a form of {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)ker-||to turn, bend}}.

chain: to go up, climb up to
ascend.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|ascenden}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|ascendre}}, from {{der|en|la|ascendō||to go up, climb up to}}, from {{m|la|ad||to}} + {{m|la|scandō||to climb}}; see {{m|en|scan}}. Unrelated to {{m|en|accede}} other than common {{m|la||ad}} prefix.

aspect.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|aspect}}, from {{der|en|la|aspectus||look, sight; appearance}}, from {{m|la|aspiciō||see; catch sight of; inspect}}, from {{m|la|ad-||to, towards, at}} + {{m|la|speciō||look, look at, behold; observe}}.

assist.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:assisten<ety:bor<fro:assister<ety:inh<la:assistō>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|assisten}}, from {{der|en|fro|assister|t=to assist, to attend}}, from {{der|en|la|assistō|t=stand at, bestand|pos=verb}}.

attend.raw: {{PIE word|en|h₂éd}}{{root|en|ine-pro|*tend-|id=stretch}} From {{inh|en|enm|attenden}}, {{m|enm|atenden|t=to devote oneself (to a task, etc.); to pay attention to (something), to look after; to consider (something); to expect or look forward to (something); to intend to do (something); to help or serve (someone), attend upon; to take care of (something)}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=attenden|pos=v|id=MED2913}}</ref> from {{der|en|fro|atendre|t=to await, wait for; to expect; to intend}}, from {{der|en|la|attendō|attendere}}, {{m|la|adtendō|adtendere|t=to pay attention to, attend; to direct or tur

attract.raw: From {{uder|en|la|attractus}}, past participle of {{m|la|attrahere||to draw to, attract}}, from {{m|la|ad||to}} + {{m|la|traho|trahere|to draw}}.

author.raw: {{etymon|en|id=creator|:inh|enm:auctour<id:author>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|auctour}}, from {{der|en|xno|autour}}, from {{der|en|fro|autor}}, from {{der|en|la|auctor}}, from {{m|la|augeō||to increase, originate}}. The {{m|en||h}}, also found in {{cog|frm|autheur}}, is [[unetymological]] as there is no {{m|la||h}} in the original Latin spelling. The OED attributes the ''h'' to [[Appendix:Glossary#contamination|contamination]] by {{m|en|authentic}}. {{doublet|en|auteur}}. {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂ewg-}}

cogs: that which can be bitten, food, bait
bait.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰeyd-}} {{etymon|en|id=lure|:inh|enm:bayte<id:bait>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|bayte}}, {{m|enm|bait}}, {{m|enm|beite}}, from {{der|en|non|beita|t=food, bait}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*baitō|t=that which is bitten, bait}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰeyd-|t=to cleave, split, separate}}. Cognate with {{cog|de|Beize|t=mordant, corrosive fluid; marinade}}, {{cog|ang|bāt|t=that which can be bitten, food, bait}}. Related to {{l|en|bite}}.

beer.raw: {{etymon|en|id=drink|:inh|enm:ber<id:beer><ety:inh<ang:bēor>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|ber}}, {{m|enm|bere}}, from {{inh|en|ang|bēor|t=beer}} ({{w|Oxford English Dictionary|Oxford OED}} notes: "rare, except in [[poetry]]"), from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*beuʀ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*beuzą|t=beer}} (putatively from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*bʰewsóm}}), meaning “brewer's yeast”.

below.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:bilooghe|:afeq|be-|low<id:at the bottom>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|bilooghe}}, equivalent to {{af|en|be-|low}}. Compare also earlier {{cog|enm|alogh}}, {{m|enm|alow}}, {{m|enm|aloȝ}}, {{m|enm|alowe|t=below}}, {{m|enm|benethen|t=beneath}}, {{cog|nl|omlaag|t=downwards}}.

biology.raw: {{etymon|en|id=life science|:lbor|la-new:biologia<id:biology>|tree=1}} {{bor+|en|la-new|biologia}} (1766), itself from {{der|en|grc|-}} {{suffix|grc|βίος|gloss1=bio-, life|λογία|gloss2=-logy, branch of study, to speak|nocat=1}}. {{surf|+af|en|bio-|-logy}}.

bishop.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|bischop}}, {{m|enm|bishop}}, {{m|enm|bisshop}}, {{m|enm|biscop}}, from {{der|en|ang|bisċop||bishop}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*biskop}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|biscopus|(e)biscopus}}, from classical {{cog|la|episcopus||[[overseer]], [[supervisor]]}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἐπίσκοπος||[[overseer]]}}, from {{m|grc|ἐπί||[[over]]}} + {{m|grc|σκοπός||[[watcher]]}}, used in Greek and Latin both generally and as a title of civil officers. Cognate with all European terms for the position in various Christian churches; compare also {{m+|enm|bisp|t=bishop}}.

bit.raw: {{ety|en|id=metal piece|:inh|enm:bitte|tree=+}} From {{inh|en|enm|bitte}}, {{m|enm|bite}}, from {{inh|en|ang|bita|t=bit; fragment; morsel}} and {{m|ang|bite|t=a bite; cut}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*bitô}} and {{m|gem-pro|*bitiz}}; both from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰeyd-|t=to split}}. More at {{l|en|bite}}.

blanket.raw: {{inh+|en|enm|blanket}}, {{m|enm|blonket}}, {{m|enm|blaunket}}, from {{der|en|fro-nor|-}} {{m|fro|blanket}}, {{m|fro|blancet|t=white horse", also "white woollen cloth or flannel; a type of jacket|lit=that which is white}} (whence Modern {{cog|fr|blanchet}}), diminutive of {{m|fro|blanc|t=white}}, of {{der|en|gem|-}} origin (compare {{cog|ang|blanca|t=white horse}}; see more at {{m|en|blank}}). Furthermore, the sense "white woollen cloth" is likely a {{calque|en|ang|hwītel|t=blanket; cloak, mantle|nocap=1|nocat=1}}, from {{m+|ang|hwīt|t=white}} + {{m|ang|-el|pos=diminutive suffix}}. Compare als

bride.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|bride}}, from {{inh|en|ang|brȳd|t=bride}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*brūdi}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*brūdiz|t=bride}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|yol|breede|t=bride}}, {{cog|stq|Bräid|t=bride}}, {{cog|gsw|Bruut|t=bride}}, {{cog|gmw-cfr|Brock}}, {{m|gmw-cfr|Brutt}}, {{m|gmw-cfr|Bruut|t=bride}}, {{cog|nl|bruid|t=bride}}, {{cog|de,lb|Braut|t=bride}}, {{cog|da,nb,nn,sv|brud|t=bride}}, {{cog|fo,is|brúður|t=bride}}, {{cog|nn|brud}}, {{m|nn|brur|t=bride}}, {{cog|got|𐌱𐍂𐌿𐌸𐍃|t=bride}}, {{cog|fr|bru|t=daughter-in-law}}, {{cog|fur|brût|t=daughter-in-law}} (from {{cog|goh|brut|t=br

bridegroom.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|brydgrome}}, {{m|enm|bridegome}}, from {{inh|en|ang|brȳdguma}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*brūdigumô}}; equivalent to Old English {{m|ang|brȳd||bride}} + {{m|ang|guma||man}}. Altered by folk etymology to end with {{m|en|groom}}, with it re-analyzed as or influenced by {{m|enm|grom}}, {{m|enm|grome||attendant}}, as ''guma'' was obsolete. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Brüüdicham}}, {{cog|nl|bruidegom}}, {{cog|af|bruidegom}}, {{cog|nds-de|Brödigam}}, {{m|nds-de|Brüdigam}}, {{m|nds-de|Brögam}}, {{m|nds-de|Brügam}}, {{cog|pdt|Briegaum}}, {{cog|de|Bräutigam}}, {{cog|nb|brudgom}}, {{cog|nn|bru

brilliant.raw: {{ety|en|id=shining|:bor|fr:brillant<id:shining>|tree=1}} {{bor+|en|fr|brillant}} (late 17th century), present participle of the verb {{m|fr|briller}}, from {{der|en|it|brillare}}, possibly from {{der|en|la|berillus}}, {{m|la|beryllus||a beryl, gem, eyeglass}}, from {{der|en|grc|βήρυλλος||beryl}}. {{surf|en|fr:briller|alt1=brill(er)|-i-|-ant}}.

brochure.raw: 1748, from {{bor|en|fr|brochure||stitched work}}, from {{m|fr|brocher||to stitch}}, from {{der|en|fro|brochier||to pierce}}, from {{m|fro|broche||awl}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|brocca}}, from {{der|en|la|broccus||pointy-toothed}}. {{doublet|en|broach}}.<ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary}}</ref>

brunch.raw: {{blend|en|breakfast|lunch}}. Attested from 1895 in British English and from 1930 in the United States.

captain.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:capitain|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|capitain}}, {{m|enm|capteyn}}, from {{der|en|fro|capitaine}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|capitāneus}}, from {{der|en|la|caput||head}} (English {{m|en|cap}}). Ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kap-}}. {{doublet|en|chieftain}}, also from Old French.

carve.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:kerven|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*gerbʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|kerven}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ceorfan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kerban}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kerbaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gerbʰ-||to scratch}}. Cognate with {{cog|fy|kerve}}, {{cog|nl|kerven}}, {{cog|nds|karven}}, {{cog|de|kerben|t=to notch}}; also {{cog|prg|gīrbin||number}}, {{cog|cu|жрѣбии||lot, tallymark}}, {{cog|grc|γράφειν||to scratch, etch}}.

cause.raw: * From {{inh|en|enm|cause}} (also with the sense of “a thing”), borrowed from {{der|en|fro|cause||a cause, a thing}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|causa||reason, sake, cause}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*kaussā}}, which is of unknown origin. {{doublet|en|chose|t1={{q|law}} a thing; personal property}}. See [[accuse]], [[excuse]], [[recuse]], [[ruse]]. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|intinga}}. * From {{inh|en|enm|causen}}, {{der|en|fro|causer}} and {{der|en|la-med|causāre}}.

changeable.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|chaungeable}}, from {{der|en|fro-nor|chaungeable}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|cambiāre|t=to change}}, equivalent to {{af|en|change|-able}}.

character.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:caracter<ety:bor<fro:caractere<ety:der<la:charactēr>>>>|tree=1}} From {{der|en|enm|caracter}}, from {{der|en|fro|caractere}}, from {{der|en|la|character}}, from {{der|en|grc|χαρακτήρ||type, nature, character}}, from {{m|grc|χαράσσω||to engrave}}. Displaced native {{noncog|en|thew}} from {{noncog|ang|þēaw}} ''(in the plural)'' and {{noncog|ang|hād||person, character}}. {{doublet|en|charakter}}.

charge.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:chargen<ety:der<fro:chargier>>|tree=+}} From {{inh|en|enm|chargen}}, from {{der|en|fro|chargier}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|carricō|t=to load}}, from {{der|en|la|carrus|t=a car, wagon}}; see [[car]]. {{doublet|en|cargo}}.

chase.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id=seize}} From {{inh|en|enm|chacen}}, from {{der|en|xno|chacer}}, {{der|en|fro|chacier}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*captiāre}}, from {{der|en|la|captō|captāre}}, frequentative of {{m|la|capiō|capere}}. Compare {{cog|fr|chasser||to hunt”, “to chase}}, {{cog|es|cazar||to hunt}}, {{cog|pt|caçar||to hunt}} , see {{cog|no|skysse||to hunt}}. {{doublet|en|catch}} and related to {{m|en|capture}}. Displaced native {{cog|ang|ōht}}, {{m|ang|ēhtnes}}, and {{m|ang|wāþ}}. Broadly overtook {{cog|ang|huntaþ}}.

chemist.raw: {{ety|en|:bor|fr:chimiste|tree=1}} First attested 1562, borrowed from {{bor|en|fr|chimiste}}, from {{der|en|la-med|chimista}}, from earlier {{m|la|alchimista|lit=[[alchemist]]}}, from {{der|en|ar|كيمياء|الْكِيمِيَاء}}, with article {{m|ar|اَلْ}} + {{der|en|grc|χυμεία||art of alloying metals}}, from {{m|grc|χύμα||fluid}}, from {{m|grc|χυμός||juice}}, from {{m|grc|χέω||to pour}}. The pronunciation with initial {{nowrap|/{{IPAlink|k}}/}} is based on the Graeco-Latin etymology rather than on the French word, where the pronunciation with {{nowrap|/{{IPAlink|ʃ}}/}} is based on native French orthogra

chemistry.raw: {{ety|en|:af|chemist|-ry|tree=1}} First coined 1605, from {{suf|en|chemist|ry}}. From {{m|en|chemist}}, {{m|en|chymist}}, from {{derived|en|la|alchimista}}, from {{derived|en|ar|كيمياء|اَلْكِيمِيَاء}}, from article {{m|ar|اَل}} + {{derived|en|grc|χυμεία||art of alloying metals}}, from {{m|grc|χύμα||fluid}}, from {{m|grc|χυμός||juice}}, from {{m|grc|χέω||to pour}}.

chick.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|chicke}}, {{m|enm|chike}}, variation of {{m|enm|chiken|t=chicken", also "chick}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ċicen}}, {{m|ang|ċycen|t=chicken}}. Sense of "young woman" dates to at least 1860 (compare {{m|en|chit|t=young, pert woman}}). More at {{l|en|chicken}}.

chieftain.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:cheveteyn|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|cheveteyn}}, {{m|enm|cheftayne}}, from {{der|en|fro|chevetaine}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|capitāneus}} (English {{m|en|captain}}), from {{der|en|la|caput||head}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kauput-}} (English {{m|en|head}}), itself from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kap-}}. {{doublet|en|captain}}; related to {{m|en|chief}}.

chain: chip; small piece of wood, shaving
cogs: to chop off the tip; snip
chip.raw: {{etymon|en|id=piece|:inh|enm:chippe|tree=1}} Noun from {{inh|en|enm|chip}}, {{m|enm|chippe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ċipp|t=chip; small piece of wood, shaving}}, from {{der|en|ang|*ċippian||to cut; hew}} – attested in {{cog|ang|forċippian|t=to cut off}} –, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kippōn|t=to cut; carve; hack; chop}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kippōną|t=to chip, chop}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ǵeyb-|t=to split; divide; germinate; sprout}}. Related to {{cog|nl|kip}}, {{m|nl|keep|t=notch; nick; score}}, {{cog|nl|kippen|t=to hatch}}, {{cog|nds-de|kippen|t=to cut; clip; trim; shorten}}, {{cog|de|k

collaborate.raw: {{back-formation|en|collaborator}}, from {{der|en|fr|collaborateur}}, or else modeled on {{uder|en|fr|collaborer}} or directly from {{uder|en|la-lat|collabōrātus}}, past participle of {{m|la|collabōrō|collabōrāre}}.<ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary|pos=v}}</ref> Displaced native {{ncog|ang|efnwyrċan}}.

combine.raw: {{PIE word|en|dwóh₁}} From {{inh|en|enm|combynyn}}, from {{der|en|frm|combiner}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|combīnō|combīnāre|t=unite, yoke together}}, from {{der|en|la|con-|t=together}} + {{m|la|[[binus|bīnī]]|t=two by two}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=v|id=1824744922}}</ref>

commercial.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|fr:commercial|tree=1}} From {{bor|en|fr|commercial||of, or pertaining to commerce}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|commercialis}}, from {{der|en|la|commercium}}. {{surf|en|commerce|-ial}}.

compress.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|compressen}}, from {{der|en|fro|compresser}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|compressare||to press hard/together}}, from {{der|en|la|compressus}}, the past participle of {{m|la|comprimō||to compress}}, itself from {{m|la|com-||together}} + {{m|la|premō||press}}.

conspicuous.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} From {{der|en|la|conspicuus||visible, striking}}, from {{m|la|[[conspicio|cōnspicere]]||to notice}}, from {{m|la|con-||with, together}} + {{m|la|[[specio|specere]]||to look at}}.

cooperate.raw: Originated 1595–1605 from {{der|en|la-lat|cooperātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la-lat|cooperor||to work with}}, see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}} for more. Equivalent to {{af|en|co-|operate}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|efnwyrċan}}.

correct.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|fr|correct}}, from {{der|en|la|correctus||improved, amended, correct}}, past participle of {{m|la|corrigere}}, {{m|la|conrigere||to make straight, make right, make better, improve, correct}}, from {{m|la|con-||together}} + combining form of {{m|la|rego|regō, regere|I rule, make straight}}.

correspond.raw: From {{der|en|frm|correspondre|}}, from {{der|en|la|com-||with}} + {{m|la|respondeo||to match, to answer to}}, equivalent to {{pre|en|co-|respond}}.

courage.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱerd-}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:corage|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|corage}}, from {{der|en|fro|corage}} ({{cog|fr|courage}}), from {{der|en|la-vul|*corāticum}}, from {{der|en|la|cor|t=heart}}. Distantly related to {{m|en|cardiac|t=of the heart}}, which is from Greek, but from the same Proto-Indo-European root. Displaced {{inh|en|enm|elne}}, {{m|enm|ellen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ellen||courage, valor}}.

course.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱers-}} {{etymon|en|id=sequence|:inh|enm:cours|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|cours}}, from {{der|en|fro|cours}}, from {{der|en|la|cursus||course of a race}}, from {{m|la|currō||run}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱers-||to run}}. {{doublet|en|cursus|cour}}.

crayfish.raw: Alteration (by [[folk etymology|folk etymological]] influence of {{m|en|fish}}) of {{der|en|enm|crevis}} (whence modern dialectal {{m|en|crevis}}), from {{der|en|fro|crevice}} {{gloss|"crayfish"; > Modern French: {{m|fr|écrevisse}}}}, from {{der|en|frk|*krabitjō|*krebitja|t=crayfish}}, diminutive of {{der|en|frk|*krabit|*krebit|t=crab}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*krabitaz||crab, cancer}}, possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gerbʰ-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*grebʰ-||to scratch, crawl}}, or from a {{der|en|qfa-sub}} word folk-etymologically influenced by this root.

credible.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱerd-|*dʰeh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|credible}}, borrowed from {{der|en|frm|credible}}, from {{der|en|la|crēdibilis||worthy of belief}}, from {{m|la|crēdō||believe}}; see [[credit]].

crowd.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:crouden|tree=+}} From {{inh|en|enm|crouden}}, from {{inh|en|ang|crūdan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*krūdan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*krūdaną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*kreudaną}}, ultimately from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*grewt-|t=to push; press}}. Cognate with {{cog|nds-de|kroden|t=to push, shove}}, {{cog|nl|kruien|t=to push, shove}}.

crown.raw:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)ker- (turn)}} {{inh+|en|enm|coroune}}, from {{der|en|xno|corone}}, from {{der|en|la|corōna||crown, wreath}}, from {{der|en|grc|κορώνη}}. {{doublet|en|corona|korona|koruna|krona|króna|krone}}. {{displaced|ang|corenbēag|t=crown}} and {{ncog|enm|kinehelm}}, {{m|enm|kynehelm}}, from {{ncog|ang|cynehelm|t=crown|lit=kinhelm” or “king's helm}}.
The paper sizes ({{senseno|en|paper size}}) are so called because the papers were originally watermarked with a crown.

crucial.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)ker- (turn)}} 1706, from {{bor|en|fr|crucial}}, a medical term for ligaments of the knee (which cross each other), from Latin {{m|la|crux|crux, crucis|cross}} (English {{m|en|crux}}), from the {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)ker-||to turn, to bend}}.

culture.raw: {{etymon|en|:der|frm:culture<ety:der<la:cultūra>>|tree=1}} From {{der|en|frm|culture|t=cultivation; culture}}, from {{der|en|la|cultūra|t=cultivation; culture}}, from {{m|la|cultus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|colō|t=till, cultivate, to grow, worship}} (related to {{m|la|colōnus}} and {{m|la|colōnia}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kʷel-|t=to move; to turn (around)}}.

define.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|definen}}, from {{der|en|fro|definer}}, variant of {{m|fro|definir}}, from {{der|en|la|dēfīniō|t=limit, settle, define}}, from {{m|la|dē}} + {{m|la|fīniō|t=set a limit, bound, end}}.

chain: to look down upon, despise, scorn
despise.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|despisen}}, from {{der|en|fro|despis-}}, stem of {{m|fro|despire}}, from {{der|en|la|dēspiciō|dēspicere|t=to look down upon, despise, scorn}}, from {{m|la|dē||down}} + {{m|la|speciō||to look at}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|forsēon}}.

chain: carry apart, put off, defer; differ
differ.raw: {{etymon|en|id=verb|:inh|enm:differren<id:differ>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|differren}}, from {{der|en|fro|differer}}, from {{der|en|la|differō||carry apart, put off, defer; differ}}, from {{m|la|dis-||apart}} + {{m|la|ferō||carry, bear}}. Compare {{cog|grc|διαφέρω}}. {{doublet|en|defer#Etymology 1|dilate#Etymology 2}}, see also [[infer]], [[confer]] and [[collate]], [[refer]] and [[relate]], as well as [[prefer]] and [[prelate]] among others.

differentiate.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|la-new:differentiātus<ety:from<differentiō<ety:from<la:differentia>>>>|tree=1}} From {{bor|en|la-new|differentiātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la-new|differentiō}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}} and {{af|en|-ate|id1=substantive|pos1=noun-forming suffix}}), from {{der|en|la|differentia||difference}}; see {{m|en|difference}}.

donate.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*deh₃-}} Circa 1845, back-formation from {{m|en|donation}} on the basis of {{l|en|-ate|id=verb|pos=verb-forming suffix}}, chiefly found in {{w|American English}}. Ultimately from {{der|en|la|dono|dōnāre|to give}}.

dwelling.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|dwellynge}}, {{m|enm|dwellyng||delay, continuance, abode}}, equivalent to {{af|en|dwell|-ing}}. More at [[dwell]].

dye.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰewh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|deye|id=dye}}, from {{inh|en|ang|dēah}}, {{m|ang|dēag||color, hue, dye}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*daugu||color, shade}}, from {{m|gmw-pro|*daugan||to conceal, be dark}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰewh₂-||to smoke, raise dust, camouflage}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|goh|tougan||dark, secretive}}, {{m|goh|tougal||dark, hidden, covert}}, {{cog|ang|dēagol}}, {{m|ang|dīegle||dark, hidden, secret}}, {{cog|ang|dohs}}, {{m|ang|dox||dusky, dark}}. See {{l|en|dusk}}. {{col-bottom}}

echo.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:eccho|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|eccho}}, {{m|enm|ecco}}, {{m|enm|echo}}, {{m|enm|ekko}}, from {{der|en|la-med|ēccō}}, from {{der|en|la|ēchō}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἠχώ}}, from {{m|grc|ἠχή||sound}}. Possibly from the same {{der|en|ine-pro|-}} root as {{m|en|sough}}.

cogs: relating to orderly arrangement of written material

economy.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*weyḱ-|*nem-|id2=distribute}} From {{inh|en|enm|yconomye}}, {{m|enm|yconomy}}, borrowed via {{der|en|fro|yconomie}} or [[w:Medieval Latin|Medieval Latin]]<ref>{{R:MED Online|īconomī(e|n|MED21656}}</ref> from {{der|en|la|oeconomia}}, from {{der|en|grc|οἰκονομία||management of a household, administration}}, from {{m|grc|οἶκος||house}} + {{m|grc|νέμω||distribute, allocate}}. {{surf|en|eco-|-nomy}}. The first recorded sense of the word '''economy''', found in a work possibly composed in 1440, is “the management of economic affairs”, in this case, of a monastery.

editor.raw: {{etymon|en|:der|la-med:ēditor|tree=1}} From {{der|en|la-med|ēditor}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|ēditor}},<ref>http://dictionary.reference.com/browse/editor</ref> from {{m|la|ēditus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|ēdō|t=give out, put forth, publish}}.

effect.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:effect<ety:bor<fro:effect>>|id=noun|tree=1}} Of the noun: from {{inh|en|enm|effect}}, from {{der|en|fro|effect}} (modern {{cog|fr|effet}}), from {{der|en|la|effectus||an effect, tendency, purpose}}, from {{m|la|efficiō||accomplish, complete, effect}}; see ''effect'' as a verb. Displaced {{inh|en|ang|fremming}}, {{m|ang|fremednes}} from {{m|ang|fremman}}.

efficient.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-}} 1398, “making,” from {{der|en|fro|-}}, from {{der|en|la|efficientem}}, nominative {{m|la|efficiēns}}, participle of {{m|la|efficere|t=work out, accomplish}} (see {{m|en|effect}}). Meaning “productive, skilled” is from 1787. ''[[efficiency|Efficiency]] apartment'' is first recorded [[wikipedia:1930|1930]], [[American English]]. <ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref>

eliminate.raw: {{bor+|en|la|ēlīminātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|ēlīminō||to turn out of doors, banish}}, from {{af|la|ex-|līmen|-ō|alt1=ē-|pos2=''līmin-'' in compounds|t2=a threshold|id3=denominative|pos3=first conjugation verb-forming suffix|nocat=1}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}), akin to {{noncog|la|līmes||a boundary}}; see also {{noncog|en|limit}} and {{m|en|limen}}.

empty.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|emty}}, {{m|enm|amty}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ǣmtiġ}}, {{m|ang|ǣmettiġ|t=vacant, empty, free, idle, unmarried|lit=without must or obligation, leisurely}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|-}} {{m|gem-pro|*uz-|t=out}} + {{der|en|gem-pro|*mōtijô}}, {{m|gem-pro|*mōtô|t=must, obligation, need}}, {{m|gem-pro|*mōtiþô|t=ability, accommodation}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*med-|t=measure; to acquire, possess, be in command}}. Related to {{m+|ang|ġeǣmtigian|t=to empty}}, {{m|ang|ǣmetta|t=leisure}}, {{m|ang|mōtan|t=can, to be allowed}}. More at [[mote]], [[meet]].

end.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:ende}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂ent-}} From {{inh|en|enm|ende}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ende}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*andī}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*andijaz|t=end}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*h₂entíos|t=forehead; front}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*h₂ent-|t=face; forehead; front}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*h₂en-|t=on, onto}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|yol|een}}, {{m|yol|eene|t=end}}, {{cog|stq|Eend}}, {{m|stq|Eende|t=end}}, {{cog|fy|ein|t=end}}, {{cog|gsw|End}}, {{m|gsw|Endi|t=end}}, {{cog|gmw-cfr|Eng}}, {{m|gmw-cfr|Enk|t=end}}, {{cog|cim|énte|t=end}}, {{cog|nl|eind}}, {{m|nl|einde}}, {{m

ensue.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|id=follow}} From {{uder|en|fro|-}} ''{{lang|fro|ensu-}}'',<ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref> stem of some conjugated forms of {{m|fro|ensuivre||follow close upon, come afterward}} (French {{m|fr|ensuivre}}); see {{m|en|sequel}}.

especial.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|especial}}, via {{der|en|fro|especial}}, from {{der|en|la|specialis}}, from {{m|la|species||appearance, form, beauty}}, from {{m|la|specere||to look}}. {{doublet|en|special}}. Related to {{m|en|species}}.

espionage.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} Recorded since 1793, from {{bor|en|fr|espionnage}}, from {{m|fr|espionner|t=to spy}}, from {{der|en|frm|espionner|t=to spy}}, from {{m|frm|espion|t=spy}}, from {{der|en|fro|espion|t=spy}}, from {{der|en|frk|*spehō|t=spy}}, from {{der|en|frk|*spehōn|t=to spy}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*spehōną|t=to spy, peek, peer}}. In modern times, the French pronunciation of the ''s'', which had fallen silent since the 13th century, was restored due to the influence of {{cog|it|spione|t=spy}}, and was therefore also adopted by the English. More at {{m|en|spy}}.

evoke.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*wekʷ-}} From {{der|en|fr|évoquer}}, from {{der|en|la|ēvocō|t=to call out, summon}}, from {{m|la|ex||out}} and {{m|la|vocō||call}}. Akin to {{m|en|voice}}.

chain: I am, I exist, appear, arise
exist.raw: From {{der|en|fr|exister}}, from {{der|en|la|exsisto|existō, exsistō|I am, I exist, appear, arise}}, from {{m|la|ex||out}} + {{m|la|sisto|sistere|to set, place}} (related to {{m|la|stō|stare|to stand, to be stood}}), ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*stísteh₂ti}}, from the root {{m|ine-pro|*steh₂-||stand}}; see {{m|en|stand}}. Compare {{m|en|assist}}, {{m|en|consist}}, {{m|en|desist}}, {{m|en|insist}}, {{m|en|persist}}, {{m|en|resist}}. Cognate with {{cog|es|existir}}, {{cog|fr|exister}}, {{cog|it|esistere}}, {{cog|de|existieren}}.

explosion.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|fr:explosion|tree=1}} From {{bor|en|fr|explosion}}, from {{der|en|la|explōsio}}, from {{m|la|explōdo||to drive out by clapping}}, from {{m|la|ex-}} and {{m|la|plōdo||to clap or strike}}. For more information see {{m|en|explode}}.

fancy.raw: {{ety|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:fansy<ety:from<fantasie>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|fansy}}, {{m|enm|fantsy}}, a contraction of {{m|enm|fantasy}}, {{m|enm|fantasye}}, {{m|enm|fantasie}}, from {{der|en|fro|fantasie}}, from {{der|en|la-med|fantasia}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|phantasia||an idea, notion, fancy, phantasm}}, from {{der|en|grc|φαντασία}}, from {{m|grc|φαντάζω||to render visible}},<ref>{{R:grc:LSJ|φαντασία}}</ref> from {{m|grc|φαντός||visible}}, from {{m|grc|φαίνω||to make visible}}; from the same root as {{m|grc|φάος||light}}; ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro||*bʰh₂-n̥-yéti}}, from the root

chain: to go through, carry forth, try
fear.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:fere<id:fear>|id=fright|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|feer}}, {{m|enm|fere|id=fear}}, {{m|enm|fer||fear}}, from {{inh|en|ang|fǣr|id=fear}}, {{m|ang|ġefǣr||calamity, sudden danger, peril, sudden attack, terrible sight|id=danger}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*fērō}}, {{m|gem-pro|*fērą||danger}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*per-||to go through, carry forth, try}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|gevaar||danger, risk, peril}}, {{cog|de|Gefahr||danger, hazard, risk}}, {{cog|da|fare||danger, hazard, risk}}, {{cog|fo,is|fár||accident, anger, calamity}}, {{cog|nb,nn|fare||danger}}, {{cog|sv|fara||danger, r

fence.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷʰen-}} From {{inh|en|enm|fence}}, {{m|enm|fens}}, short for {{m|enm|defence}}, {{m|enm|defens|t=the act of defending}}, from {{der|en|fro|defens}}, {{m|fro|defense}} (see [[defence]]).

flammable.raw: {{back-form|en|inflammable}}, which is used to avoid confusion with {{m|en|non-flammable}}, as the prefix ''[[in-#Etymology 2|in-]]'' is often used to mean "un-; non-", although it was originally meant in a sense closely related to {{m|en|en-}}.

flexible.raw: From {{der|en|frm|flexible}}, from {{der|en|la|flexibilis}}, from {{m|la|flectō||to bend, curve}}. Morphologically {{suffix|en|flex|ible}}.

chain: of the same family or clan
gentle.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵenh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|gentil||courteous, noble}}, from {{der|en|fro|gentil||high-born, noble}}, from {{der|en|la|gentilis||of the same family or clan}}, from {{m|la|gens||[Roman] clan}}. {{doublet|en|gentile|genteel|jaunty}}.

gill.raw: {{etymid|en|piscine organ}} From {{inh|en|enm|gille}}, {{m|enm|gylle|t=gill}}, of {{der|en|gmq|-}} origin, akin to {{cog|da|gælle}}, {{cog|sv|gäl}}, {{cog|no|gjelle}}, and further to {{cog|non|gjǫlnar|t=lips}}, which also may have had the meaning of "gills" (based on Old Danish {{m|non|fiskegæln|t=gills}}). The Old Norse word has been suggested as deriving from {{der|en|gem-pro|*gelunō|t=jaw}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰel-}}, which would make it root-cognate to {{cog|grc|χελύνη|t=lip, jaw}}, {{m|grc|χεῖλος|t=lip}}.

golf.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|gmw-msc:golf}} The word is first known in English from the 17th century as a {{glossary|borrowing}} from {{bor|en|gmw-msc|golf}}, {{m|gmw-msc|gouff}}. Although the etymology is uncertain, the most likely origin is that it comes from the {{der|en|dum|colve}}, {{m|dum|colf||club}}, ultimately from {{der|en|gem-pro|*kulbaz||club}}, related to {{cog|de|Kolben|t=piston, rod}}, {{cog|sv|kolv|t=piston, rod}}, {{cog|ang|clopp|t=rock; cliff}}, {{cog|en|kelp}}.

government.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:governement|tree=+}} From {{inh|en|enm|governement}}, from {{der|en|fro|governement}} (modern French {{m|fr|gouvernement}}), from {{m|fro|governer}} (see {{m|en|govern}}) + {{m|fro|-ment}}. Morphologically {{suffix|en|govern|ment}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|gerec}}, {{m|ang|leodweard}}, {{m|ang|ræden}}, {{m|ang|rǣding}} and {{m|ang|ealdordōm}}.

chain: (noun) a graduate of a university; (adjective) graduate, having graduated
graduate.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|graduat|alt=graduat(e)|t=(noun) a graduate of a university; (adjective) graduate, having graduated|pos=also used as the past participle of {{m|enm|graduaten||to graduate}}}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la-med|graduātus||graduated, graduate}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la-med|graduō||to graduate}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|gradus||step}} + {{m|la|-ō|id=denominative|pos=verb-forming suffix}}. The noun is originally derived within Latin from the adjective via [[substantivization]], see

guarantee.raw: {{ety|en|:der|fro:guarantie|tree=1}} From {{der|en|fro|guarantie}} (perhaps via a later {{der|en|es|garante}}), from the verb {{m|fro|guarantir||to protect, assure, vouch for}}, ultimately from {{der|en|frk|*warjan||to ward off}}. {{doublet|en|guaranty|warranty}}.

guardian.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:gardein|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|gardein}}, {{m|enm|garden}}, from {{der|en|fro|guardein}}, from the verb {{m|fro|guarder}}, of {{der|en|gem}} origin. Compare {{cog|fr|gardien}}. {{doublet|en|warden}}. {{surf|en|guard|-ian}}.

hall.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱel- (cover)}} {{inh+|en|enm|halle||hall}}, from {{inh|en|ang|heall||hall, dwelling, house, palace, temple, law-court}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hallu||hall}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hallō||hall}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱel-||to hide, conceal}}.

happen.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:happenen|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|happenen}}, {{m|enm|hapnen}}, augmented from {{der|en|enm|happen|t=to come to pass, happen}}, perhaps from {{inh|en|ang|hæppan|t=to move accidentally, slip}} and/or from {{der|en|non|*happa}}, {{m|non|*heppa}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*hampijaną|t=to fit in, be fitting}}. Equivalent to {{af|en|hap|t1=a chance, occurrence, byfall|-en|id2=inchoative|pos2=verbal suffix}}.

cogs: benign or devouring or destroying enemies
hate.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:hate|tree=1|id=hatred}} From {{inh|en|enm|haate}}, {{m|enm|hat}}, {{m|enm|hate|pos=noun}}, probably from {{der|en|ang|hatian|t=to hate|pos=verb}} and/or {{der|en|non|hatr|t=hate|pos=noun}}.<ref>{{R:MED Online|hāte|n|MED20089}}</ref><ref>{{R:OED Online|hate|n|4548401353}}</ref><ref>{{R:enm:Gersum|hate|n|10647}}</ref><ref>{{R:en:ODEE|hate|430|3}}</ref> Merged with {{cog|enm|het}}, {{m|enm|hete|t=hate}}, from {{der|en|ang|hete}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*hati}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*hataz|t=hate}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱeh₂d-|t=angriness, hatred}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate wi

chain: to heal, cure, save, greet, salute
heal.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|helen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hǣlan||to heal, cure, save, greet, salute}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hailijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hailijaną||to heal, make whole, save}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kéh₂ilos||healthy, whole}}. Derived from the adjective at hand in {{m|en|whole}}.

hoarse.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|hors}}, {{m|enm|hos}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hās}}, {{m|ang|*hārs}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*haisaz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*haisraz}}, akin to {{cog|non|háss}} (West Norse) and {{m|non|heiss}} (East Norse) (whence {{cog|is|hás}}, {{cog|nn|hås}}, {{cog|nb|hes}} and {{cog|sv|hes}}).

humour.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*wegʷ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|humour}}, from {{der|en|fro|humor}}, {{m|fro|humour}}, from {{der|en|la|hūmor}}, correctly {{m|la|ūmor|t=liquid}}, from {{m|la|hūmeō}}, correctly {{m|la|ūmeō|t=to be moist}}. The ''h'' in these words, which was silent in late Classical Latin, is [[w:folk etymology|folk etymological]], due to the erroneous association with the word {{m|la|humus|t=soil}}.

hump.raw: Probably borrowed from {{bor|en|nl|homp|t=hump, lump}} or {{bor|en|gml|hump|t=heap, hill, stump}}, from {{der|en|osx|*hump||hill, heap, thick piece}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*humpaz||hip, height}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kumb-||curved}}. Compare {{cog|gem-pro|*huppōną||to hop}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kewb-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*ḱewb-}} (unnasalised root), and {{cog|en|hub}} (a softened variant without nasal?).

illegal.raw: {{bor+|en|fr|illégal}}, from {{der|en|la-med|illegalis}}, from {{der|en|la|legalis}}, {{surf|en|il-|legal|nocap=1}}. In senses relating to immigration, via {{clip|en|illegal alien|nocap=1}} or {{m|en|illegal immigrant}}.

illiterate.raw: {{etydate|r|1425|1475}}, in {{w|Middle English}}; from {{inh|en|enm|illiterat|illiterat(e)|uneducated, ignorant of Latin}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|illīterātus}}, {{m|la|illitterātus||unlearned, ignorant}}, itself from {{m|la|in-||un-}} + {{m|la|līterātus}}, {{m|la|litterātus||furnished with letters}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|lītera}}, {{m|la|littera||letter, character}}. The {{glossary|noun}} was derived from the {{glossary|adjective}} by {{glossary|substantivization}}, see {{af|en|-ate|id1=substantive|pos1=noun-forming suffix}}.

illusion.raw: From {{der|en|fro|illusion}}, from {{der|en|la|illūsiō||}}, from {{m|la|illudo|illūdere|}}, from {{m|la|in-||at, upon}} + {{m|la|lūdere||to play, mock, trick}}. Displaced native {{cog|en||[[dwimmer#Etymology|dwimmer]]}}.

immature.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*meh₂-|id=good}} From {{bor|en|frm|immature}}. Partially displaced {{m|en|unripe}}, from {{noncog|ang|unrīpe|t=unripe, immature}}. {{surf|en|im-<pos:expressing negation; [[not]]>|mature}}.

include.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)kleh₂w-}} From {{inh|en|enm|includen}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|inclūdō|inclūdere|t=to shut in, enclose, insert}}, from {{m|la|in-||in}} + {{m|la|claudo|claudere|to shut}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)kleh₂w-|*kleh₂w-|key, hook, nail}}. {{doublet|en|enclose}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|belūcan}} (“to include,” also “to shut in”).

incredible.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱerd-|*dʰeh₁-}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:incredible<ety:der<la:incrēdibilis>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|incredible}}, from {{der|en|la|incrēdibilis||that cannot be believed}}, from {{m|la|in-||not}} + {{m|la|crēdibilis||worthy of belief}}, from {{m|la|crēdō||believe}}, equivalent to {{af|en|in-|credible}}.

inflammable.raw: From {{der|en|frm|inflammable}}, from {{der|en|la-med|īnflammābilis}}, from {{der|en|la|inflammo|īnflammāre|t=to set on fire}}, from {{m|la|in|t=in, on}} + {{m|la|flamma|t=flame}}. {{surf|en|inflame|-able|lit=able to be inflamed}}.

chain: to shape, form, train, instruct, educate
inform.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|informen}}, {{m|enm|enformen}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|enformer}}, {{m|fro|informer||to train, instruct, inform}}, from {{der|en|la|īnfōrmō||to shape, form, train, instruct, educate}}, from {{m|la|in-||into}} + {{m|la|fōrma||form, shape}}, equivalent to {{prefix|en|in|form}}.

chain: endowed with good natural capacity, gifted with genius
ingenious.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵenh₁-}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|ingénieux}}, from {{der|en|fro|engenious}}, from {{der|en|la|ingeniōsus|t=endowed with good natural capacity, gifted with genius}}, from {{m|la|ingenium|t=innate or natural quality, natural capacity, genius}}, from {{af|la|in-|t1=in|gignere|t2=to produce|nocat=1}}, {{der|en|itc-ola|genere}}. See also {{m|en|engine}}.

inquire.raw: From {{bor|en|la|inquīrō||to seek for}}, composed of {{m|la|in-|t=in, at, on; into}} + {{m|la|quaerō|t=to seek, look for}}, of uncertain origin, but possibly from {{der|en|itc-pro|*kʷaizeō}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kʷeh₂-|t=to acquire}}. Displaced {{cog|enm|enqueren}} (from {{cog|fro|enquerre}}, of the same source) and native {{cog|enm|speir|t=ask, inquire}}.

inspect.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} From {{uder|en|la|inspectum}}, past participle of {{m|la|inspicio|inspicere|to look into}}, from {{m|la|in||in}} + {{m|la|specio|specere|to look at}}, equivalent to {{confix|en|in|spect}}.

interrogate.raw: {{lbor|en|la|interrogātus}}, the {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{der|en|la|interrogō||to inquire, interrogate}}, see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}.

irregular.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|irreguler}}, from {{der|en|fro|irreguler}}, from {{der|en|la-med|-}} or {{der|en|la-lat|irrēgulāris}}, from {{m|la|in-}} + {{m|la|regularis}}, equivalent to {{af|en|ir-|regular}}.

irrigate.raw: {{etydate|1615}}; {{bor+|en|la|irrigātus|nocap=1}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|irrigō}}, see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}. See also {{cog|enm|irrigat|irrigat(e)|t=watered, irrigated}}.

irritate.raw: {{bor+|en|la|irrītātus|id=excite}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|irrītō|t=excite, irritate, incite, stimulate|id=excite}}, see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}.

ketchup.raw: {{ety|en|:bor<unc>|ms:kecap<id:sauce>|tree=+}} {{unc|en}}, but probably ultimately from {{der|en|nan-hbl|膎汁|tr=kê-chiap|t=[[fish sauce]]|lit=[[pickled]] [[fish]] [[juice]]}}, via {{bor|en|ms|kecap//kicap|t= any dark clear sauce from soybeans, fish, etc.}}, though the precise path is unclear – there are related words in various Chinese languages. Various other theories exist – see [[w:Ketchup#Etymology|Ketchup: Etymology]] for extended discussion.

chain: to strike out with the foot
cogs: bent backwards, the belly jutting forward
kick.raw: [[File:Boykickingball-slowmotion-tokyo-20160423.webm|thumb|thumbtime=2|A boy kicking a ball (sense 3).]] From {{inh|en|enm|kyken|t=to strike out with the foot}}, from {{der|en|non|kikna|t=to sink at the knees}} and {{m|non|keikja|t=to bend backwards}} (compare {{cog|non|keikr|t=bent backwards, the belly jutting forward}}), from {{der|en|gem-pro|*kaikaz|t=bent backwards}}, of uncertain origin. Perhaps from {{der|en|gem-pro|*kī-}}, {{m|gem-pro|*kij-|t=to split, dodge, swerve sidewards}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ǵeyH-|t=to sprout, shoot}}. Compare also {{cog|nl|kijken|t=to look}}, {{cog|gml|kīken|

kill.raw: {{ety|en|id=to put to death}} From {{inh|en|enm|killen}}, {{m|enm|kyllen}}, {{m|enm|cullen|cüllen|t=to strike, beat, cut}}, of obscure origin. Cognate with {{cog|sco|kele}}, {{m|sco||keil|t=to kill}}. * Perhaps from unattested {{inh|en|ang|*cyllan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kwulljan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kwuljaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʷelH-|t=to throw, hit, hurt by throwing}}. * Or, possibly a variant of {{inh|en|ang|cwellan|t=to kill, murder, execute}} (see {{l|en|quell}}). * Or, from {{der|en|non|kolla|t=to hit on the head, harm}}, related to {{cog|no|kylla|t=to poll}}, {{cog|dum|kol

kingly.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|kyngly}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*cyninglīċ|t=kingly, royal}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|king|ly|id2=adjectival}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|koninklijk||kingly, royal}}, {{cog|de|königlich||kingly}}, {{cog|sv|kunglig||kingly}}. Compare also {{cog|ang|cynelīċ||kingly, royal, public}}.

knave.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|knave}}, {{m|enm|knafe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cnafa||child, boy, youth; servant}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*knabō}}. Cognate to Dutch [[knaap]] and German [[Knabe]].

kowtow.raw: From either {{bor|en|yue|叩頭}} or {{bor|en|cmn|叩頭}}. {{lit|knock head}}.

ladder.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱley-|id=incline}} {{inh+|en|enm|ladder}}, {{m|enm|laddre}}; from {{der|en|ang|hlǣder}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*hlaidriju}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*hlaidrijō}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱlóydʰrom}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*ḱley-||to lean}}.

laser.raw: {{etymon|en|LASER<id:light beam>|id=light beam|tree=1}} From [[LASER]], {{acronym|en|w:light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation|nocap=1}}. {{coin|en|Gordon Gould|nat=American|occ=physicist|in=1957|nobycat=1}}. Originally called an ''optical [[maser]]''.

chain: course, journey; way, street, waterway; leading, carrying; maintenance, support
load.raw: The sense of “burden” first arose in the 13th century as a secondary meaning of {{inh|en|enm|lode}}, {{m|enm|loade}}, which had the main significance of “way, course, journey”, from {{inh|en|ang|lād||course, journey; way, street, waterway; leading, carrying; maintenance, support}} (ultimately from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*laidō||leading, way}}, {{der|en|ine-pro|*leyt-||to go, go forth, die}}.

logic.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|logike}}, from {{der|en|fro|-}} and {{der|en|la|logicus}}, from {{der|en|grc|λογῐκός}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|flitcræftlīċ}}.

chain: a charge, order, command, commission, injunction
mandate.raw: [[File:League of Nations mandate Middle East and Africa.png|thumb|A map showing Middle Eastern and African mandates.]] {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)meh₂-||*deh₃-}} {{etydate|1521}}; {{bor+|en|la|mandātum|t=a charge, order, command, commission, injunction|nocap=1}}, [[substantivize]]d from the {{glossary|neuter}} forms of {{m|la|mandātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|mandō|t=to commit to one's charge, order, command, commission, literally to put into one's hands}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=substantive|pos1=noun-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|manus|t=hand}}

mat.raw: {{etymid|en|from bed-related origins}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:matte|id=carpet|tree=1}} [[File:Mat-0001.jpg|thumb|a door'''mat''' (1)]] [[File:P1020503-1.jpg|thumb|a beer '''mat''' or coaster (2)]] [[File:Yoga_mat.jpg|thumb|a yoga '''mat''']] {{inh+|en|enm|matte||mat}}, from {{inh|en|ang|meatte||mat}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|matta||mat made of rushes}}, from {{der|en|xpu|-}} or {{der|en|phn|-}} (compare {{cog|he|מיטה|מיטה \ מִטָּה|bed, couch|tr=mitá}}). Cognate with {{cog|de|Matte||mat}}, {{cog|da|måtte||mat}}, {{cog|fo|-}} and {{cog|is|motta||rug, mat}}, {{cog|no|matte||mat, rug}}, {{cog|sv|matta||ca

cogs: to mean, to plan, to intend
mean.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|menen||to intend; remember; lament; comfort}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mǣnan||to mean, complain}}, {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*mainijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*mainijaną||to mean, think; complain}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*meyn-||to think}}, or perhaps from {{der|en|ine-pro|*meyno-}}, extended form of {{der|en|ine-pro|*mey-}}.

mere.raw: {{ety|en|id=only|:inh|enm:mere<ety:bor<xno:meer<ety:inh<fro:mier>>>>}} From {{inh|en|enm|mere}}, {{m|enm|mer}}, from {{der|en|xno|meer}}, from {{der|en|fro|mier}}, from {{der|en|la|merus|t=pure, unmixed, undiluted}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*mer-|t=to sparkle, gleam}}.

metaphor.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰer-}} From {{der|en|frm|métaphore}}, from {{der|en|la|metaphora}}, from {{der|en|grc|μεταφορά}}, from {{m|grc|μεταφέρω||to transfer, apply}}, from {{m|grc|μετά||with, across, after}} + {{m|grc|φέρω||to bear, carry}}.

mighty.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*megʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|mighty}}, {{m|enm|mightie}}, {{m|enm|mighti}}, {{m|enm|myghty}}, {{m|enm|miȝty}}, {{m|enm|maȝty}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mihtiġ}}, {{m|ang|mehtiġ}}, {{m|ang|meahtiġ}}, {{m|ang|mæhtiġ|t=mighty}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*mahtīg|t=mighty}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*mahtīgaz|t=mighty}}, equivalent to {{af|en|might|-y}}.
