mix.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*meyḱ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|mixen}} (attested in past tense as {{m|enm|mixed}}, {{m|enm|myxyd}}), from {{inh|en|ang|[[*mixian]]}}, {{m|ang|[[miscian]]}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*miskijan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*miskijan|t=to mix}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro||*miḱ-sḱé-ti}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*meyǵ-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*meyḱ-|t=to mix}}.

chain: pertaining to memory or remembrance, memorial
mnemonic.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*men-|id=think}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|la-lat|mnemonicus}} or its {{glossary|etymon}} {{bor|en|grc|μνημονῐκός|t=pertaining to memory or remembrance, memorial}} + {{m+|en|-ic|w=1|pos={{glossary|suffix}} meaning ‘of or pertaining to’ forming adjectives}}. {{m|grc||Mνημονῐκός}} is derived from {{m|grc|μνήμων|t=mindful, remembering}} + {{m|grc|-ῐκός|pos=suffix meaning ‘of or pertaining to’ forming adjectives}}; while {{m|grc||μνήμων}} is from {{m|grc|μνάομαι|t=to be mindful, remember}} (from {{der|en|ine-pro|*men-|t=to mind; to think}}) + {{m|grc|-μων|pos=suffix forming adjectiv

moderate.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*med-}} From {{inh|en|enm|moderat|alt=moderat(e)||moderate, temperate}}, {{bor+|en|la|moderātus|nocap=1}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|active}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|moderor||to regulate, to restrain, to moderate}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la||moder-}}, {{m|la||modes-}}, a stem appearing also in {{m|la|modestus||moderate, discreet, modest}}, from {{m|la|modus||a measure}}; see [[mode]] and [[modest]]. {{doublet|en|moderato}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|ġemetlīċ||moderate}} and {{m|ang|metegian||to moderate}}.

motion.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*m(y)ewh₁-}} {{inh+|en|enm|mocioun}}, {{m|enm|mocion}}, from {{der|en|xno|motion}}, {{der|en|frm|motion}}, and their {{glossary|etymon}} {{der|en|la|mōtiō|t=movement, motion}}, related to {{m|la|moveo|movēre}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*m(y)ewh₁-||to move}}.

mount.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*men-|id=stand out}} From {{inh|en|enm|mount}}, {{m|enm|munt}}, from {{inh|en|ang|munt}}, from {{der|en|la|mōns|t=a hill, mountain}}, from a root seen also in {{m|la|ēmineō||to project, to protrude}} (English {{m|en|eminent}}). {{doublet|en|mons}}. Not related to {{m|en|mound}}.

needle.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:nedle|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)neh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|nedle}}, from {{inh|en|ang|nǣdl}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*nāþlu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*nēþlō}}, from pre-Germanic {{m|gem-pro|*neh₁-tleh₂}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)neh₁-|t=to spin, twist}}.

news.raw: {{etymon|en|id=new things|:inh|enm:newes<ety:af<newe<id:new>><-s<id:plural>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|newes}}, {{m|enm|newys|t=new things}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|new#Noun<pos:n>|s<pos:plural suffix>}}. Compare {{cog|stq|Näis|t=news}}, [[w:East Frisian Low Saxon|East Frisian]] {{m|nds|näjs|t=news}}, {{cog|fy|nijs|t=news}}, {{cog|nl|nieuws|t=news}}, {{cog|nds-de|Neeis|t=new things; news}}, though, unlike the English word, those {{lg|cognate}}s originated as {{lg|genitive}}s, not as {{lg|plural}}s. Sometimes erroneously claimed to be an [[acronym]] of "North, East, West, South" or "Noteworth

nonsense.raw: {{etymon|en|:af|non-<id:not>|sense|tree=1}} From {{af|en|non-<id:not>|t1=no, none, lack of|sense}}, from c. 1610. Compare the semantically similar {{cog|fy|ûnsin|t=nonsense}}, {{cog|nl|onzin|t=nonsense}}, {{cog|de|Unsinn|t=nonsense}}, {{cog|en|unsense|t=nonsense}}.

chain: run to meet, run against, befall, present itself
occur.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱers-}} Originally "meet (in argument)", borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|occurrer}}, from {{der|en|la|occurrō||run to meet, run against, befall, present itself}} from prefix {{m|la|ob-||against}} + verb {{m|la|currō||run, hurry, move}}.

offer.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰer-}} From {{inh|en|enm|offer}}, from {{inh|en|ang|offrian||offer or make a sacrifice}} rather than from {{der|en|fro|offre||offer}}, from {{m|fro|offrir||to offer}}, from {{der|en|la|offerō||to present, bring before}}. Compare {{cog|frr|offer||sacrifice, donation, fee}}, {{cog|nl|offer||offering, sacrifice}}, {{cog|de|Opfer||victim, sacrifice}}, {{cog|da|offer||victim, sacrifice}}, {{cog|is|offr||offering}}. See verb below.

oppose.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*tḱey-}} From {{inh|en|enm|opposen}}, from {{der|en|fro|opposer}}, from {{der|en|la|ob||before, against}} + {{der|en|la-med|pono||to put}}, taking the place of {{der|en|la|oppono|opponere|to oppose}}.

cogs: to change; to switch; to alternate
other.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:other|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|other}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ōþer||other, second}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*ą̄þar}}, {{m|gmw-pro|*anþar}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*anþeraz||other, second}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*h₂énteros||other}}.

parachute.raw: Borrowed from {{bor|en|fr|parachute}}, from {{m|fr|para-||protection against}} (as in {{m|fr|parasol}}) and {{m|fr|chute||fall}}. {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱh₂d-}}

chain: sign for start of a new section of discourse
paragraph.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|paragraf}}, from {{der|en|frm|paragraphe}} from {{der|en|la|paragraphus|t=sign for start of a new section of discourse}}, from {{der|en|grc|παράγραφος}}, from {{m|grc|παρά||beside}} and {{m|grc|γράφω||to write}}. {{doublet|en|paragraphos}}.

pat.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|pat|t=a blow, stroke}}, alteration (with loss of medial ''l'') of {{m|enm|*plat}} (> {{cog|sco|plat|t=a blow, buffet}}), from {{inh|en|ang|plætt|t=a sounding blow, a smack}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*platt|t=a smack, slap, blow}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*plat-|t=to strike, beat}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*blod-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*bled-|t=to strike, beat}}. Cognate with {{cog|dum|plat|t=a smack, blow, slap}}, {{cog|gml|plat|t=a smack, blow, beating}}, {{cog|gmh|plaz}}, {{m|gmh|blaz|t=a resounding blow, bang, crash}}. For loss of {{m|en||l}}, compare {{m|en|patch}} for {{m|en|platch}};

peel.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|pelen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|pilian}} and {{der|en|fro|peler}}, {{m|fro|pellier}}; both from {{der|en|la|pilo|pilō, pilāre|to remove hair from, depilate}}, from {{m|la|pilus|t=hair}}. {{doublet|en|pill}}.

perspective.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|perspective|perspective, perspectif}}, attested since 1381, from {{der|en|fro|-}} or {{der|en|frm|-}}, from the first word of the {{der|en|la-med|perspectiva|perspectiva ars|science of optics}}, the feminine of {{der|en|la|perspectivus||of sight, optical}}, from {{m|la|perspectus}}, the past participle of {{m|la|perspicere||to inspect, look through}}, itself from {{m|la|per-||through}} + {{m|la|specere||to look at}}; the noun sense was influenced or mediated by {{cog|it|prospettiva}}, from {{m|it|prospetto||prospect}}.

phenomenon.raw: {{etymon|en|:der|la-lat:phaenomenon|tree=1}} From {{der|en|la-lat|phaenomenon|t=appearance}}, from {{der|en|grc|φαινόμενον|t=thing appearing to view}}, neuter present middle participle of {{m|grc|φαίνω|t=I show}}.

photography.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|fr:photographie|tree=1}} From {{bor|en|fr|photographie}}. {{surf|en|photo-|-graphy}}, together meaning "drawing with light" or "representation by means of lines", "drawing". From {{m|grc|φῶς||of light}}, and {{m|grc|γράφω||write, draw}}.

chain: worth, price, money spent, wages, reward
price.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|price||price, prize, value, excellence}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|pris}}, {{m|fro|preis}}, from {{der|en|la|pretium||worth, price, money spent, wages, reward}}; compare [[praise]], [[precious]], [[appraise]], [[appreciate]], [[depreciate]], etc.

promise.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*mey- (change)}} From {{inh|en|enm|promis|promis, promisse}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|promesse}}, from {{der|en|la-med|prōmissa}}, {{der|en|la|prōmissum|t=a promise}}, feminine and neuter past participles of {{m|la|prōmittō|t=to send forth, to say beforehand, to promise}}, from {{m|la|pro||forth}} + {{m|la|mittere||to send}}; see {{m|en|mission}}. Compare {{m|en|admit}}, {{m|en|commit}}, {{m|en|permit}}, etc. Displaced native {{m|ang|ġehātan||to promise}} and {{m|ang|ġehāt||a promise}}.

propose.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id1=before|*tḱey-}}{{word|en|ine|*h₂epó}} From {{inh|en|enm|proposen}}, from {{der|en|xno|proposer|pos=v}}, {{m|fro|propos|pos=n}}, {{der|en|frm|proposer|pos=v}}, {{m|frm|propos|pos=n}}, from {{der|en|la|propono|prōpōnō, prōpōnere}}, with conjugation altered based on {{m|fro|poser}}. {{doublet|en|propound}}.

prospect.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|prospecte}}, from {{der|en|la|prōspectus|t=view, sight, prospect; panorama}}, from {{m|la|prōspiciō|t=to look forward}} + {{m|la|-tus|pos=suffix forming action nouns}}, from {{m|la|pro||before, forward}} + {{m|la|speciō}}, {{m|la|spiciō|t=to look, to see}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=3574110376}}</ref> {{surf|en|pro-|-spect}}. {{doublet|en|prospectus|prospekt}}. {{senseno|en|prospekt|cap=1}} is a {{semantic loan|en|ru|проспе́кт|nocap=1}}. The verb is from the noun.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''v.''{{sup|2}}|noformat=1|id=6664283087}}</ref>

psychology.raw: From {{bor|en|fr|psychologie}}, from {{der|en|la-ren|psychologia}}, from {{der|en|grc|ψυχή|t=soul}} + {{m|grc|-λογία||study of}}, equivalent to {{confix|en|psycho-|-logy}}. The Latin term is believed by some to have been coined in a lost treatise by Croatian humanist {{w|Marko Marulić}} (1450–1524), but this is disputed by other scholars. It is {{etydate|1570s|nocap=1}}, at which time it was apparently already current, and may be a Hellenization of the established expression {{m|la|[[dē]] [[animā]]||on the soul}} in titles.<ref>{{cite-book|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=4SS0fcbm3xMC

ready.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂er-}} From {{inh|en|enm|redy}}, {{m|enm|redi}}, {{m|enm|rædiȝ}}, {{m|enm|iredi}}, {{m|enm|ȝerædi|ȝerǣdi}}, alteration ({{suffix|en||y}}) of earlier {{m|enm|ired|irēd}}, {{m|enm|irede}}, {{m|enm|ȝerad|ȝerād|ready, prepared}}, from {{inh|en|ang|rǣde}}, {{m|ang|ġerǣde}} (also {{m|ang|ġerȳde}}) {{gloss|"prepared, prompt, ready, ready for riding (horse), mounted (on a horse), skilled, simple, easy"}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*garaidijaz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*raidijaz}}, from base {{m|gem-pro|*raidaz||ready}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂reh₁dʰ-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*h₂reh₁-||to count, put in or

reason.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂er-}} From {{inh|en|enm|resoun}}, {{m|enm|reson}}, from {{der|en|xno|raisun}} ({{der|en|fro|raison}}), from {{der|en|la|ratiō}}, from {{m|la|ratus}}, past participle of {{m|la|reor||reckon}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂reh₁-||to think}}, reanalysed root of {{m|ine-pro|*h₂er-||to put together}}. Displaced {{l+|ang|racu||logic, reason}} and native {{cog|enm|-rede|reden|pos=found in compounds}}, from {{cog|ang|rǣden|t=condition, stipulation, calculation, direction}}, from the same Proto-Indo-European source (compare {{cog|fy|reden|t=reason}}, {{cog|nl|reden|t=reason}

refer.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰer-}} From {{inh|en|enm|referren}}, from {{der|en|fro|referer}}, from {{der|en|la|referre}}. The noun (used in journalism) is from the verb. {{doublet|en|relate}}. See also [[infer]], [[collate]] and [[confer]], [[delate]] and [[defer]], as well as [[prelate]] and [[prefer]] among others.

reflect.raw: From {{uder|en|fro|reflect|reflecter|to bend back, turn back}}, from {{uder|en|la|reflectō||to reflect}}, from {{m|la|re-||again}} + {{m|la|flectō||to bend, to curve}}. Compare {{cog|en|reflex}}.

regal.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|regal}}, from {{der|en|fro|regal||regal, royal}}, from {{der|en|la|rēgālis||royal, kingly}}, from {{m|la|rex||king}}; also {{m|la|regere||to rule}}. {{doublet|en|royal|t1=belonging to a monarch|real|t2=unit of currency|ariary|riyal}}. Cognate with {{cog|es|real}}, {{cog|it|reale}}, {{cog|ca|reial}}.

reign.raw: {{ety|en|tree=1|:inh|enm:regnen}} {{inh+|en|enm|regnen}}, from {{der|en|fro|reignier}}, from the {{der|en|la|-}} verb {{m|la|rēgnō}}, and the noun {{m|la|rēgnum}}. {{doublet|en|regnum}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|rīċe||a reign}} and {{m|ang|ricsian||to reign}}.

remove.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:removen<ety:bor<xno:remover<ety:from<fro:removoir>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|removen}}, from {{der|en|xno|remover}}, {{m|fro|removeir}}, from {{der|en|fro|remouvoir}}, from {{der|en|la|removeo|removēre}}, from {{m|la|re-}} + {{m|la|moveo|movēre|to move}}, equivalent to {{affix|en|re-|move}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|āfierran}}.

residence.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*sed-}} {{inh+|en|enm|residence}}, from {{der|en|fro|residence}}, from {{der|en|la-med|residentia}}, from {{m|la|residēns}}, present participle of {{m|la|resideō}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|reside|-ence}}. {{dbt|en|residencia}}.

restive.raw: Modification of earlier {{m|en|restiff}}, from {{inh|en|enm|restyf}}, from {{der|en|fro|restif}}, from {{m|fro|rester||to stay, remain}}, from {{der|en|la|restō}}. * Shares an etymology with [[rest]] ("to remain," ''obsolete'') *''{{w|Merriam-Webster}}'' states that this word was originally used to describe horses that disobeyed commands. Presumably, then, the word came to mean ''fidgety'' or ''anxious'' more broadly.<ref>{{R:Merriam-Webster Online|restive}}</ref>

retrospect.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|la|retrōspectum}}, from {{m|la|retrōspicio||to look back at}}, equivalent to {{confix|en|retro|spect}}. Compare {{m|en|review}}.

chain: any measured flow or movement, symmetry, rhythm
rhythm.raw: {{etymon|en|:der|la:rhythmus|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*srew-}} First coined in 1557, from {{der|en|la|rhythmus}}, from {{der|en|grc|ῥυθμός||any measured flow or movement, [[symmetry]], rhythm}}, from {{m|grc|ῥέω||to flow, run, stream, gush}}.

cogs: to have fallen; to have flopped
rise.raw: From {{der|en|enm|risen}}, from {{der|en|ang|rīsan}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*rīsan}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*rīsaną|t=to rise}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₁rey-|t=to arise, rise}}. According to Kroonen (2013), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₃er-|t=to rise, spring}}. See also {{l|en|raise}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|nl|rijzen|t=to rise}}, {{cog|de|reisen|t=to fall|id=fall}}, {{cog|li|rieze|t=to rise}}, {{cog|fo,is|rísa|t=to rise}}, {{cog|nn|risa}}, {{m|nn|rise|t=to rise}}, {{cog|got|*𐍂𐌴𐌹𐍃𐌰𐌽|t=to rise}} (whence {{m|got|𐌿𐍂𐍂𐌴𐌹𐍃𐌰𐌽|t=to arise}}). Non-Germanic cognates include {{cog|kw|ardh|t=heig

cogs: mate, fellow, corresponding part; exactly like, the same
both, each, everyone, fellow, together, corresponding part; exactly like, in pairs, in line; same
same.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*sem-}} From {{inh|en|enm|same}}, from {{der|en|non|samr|t=same}} and/or {{inh|en|ang|same}}, {{m|ang|sama|t=same}} in the phrase {{m|ang||swā same (swā)|in like manner, in the same way (as)}}, both from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*samaz|t=same}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*somHós|t=same}}. {{dbt|en|some|-some}}.

scope.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} {{etymon|en|id=aim|:der|it:scopo<t:purpose>|tree=1}} From {{der|en|it|scopo||purpose}}, from {{der|en|la|scopus||target}},<ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref><ref>{{R:Merriam-Webster Online}}</ref> from {{der|en|grc|σκοπός}}, from {{m|grc|σκέπτομαι}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}}. Etymologically related to {{m|en|skeptic}} and {{m|en|spectrum}}.

scrub.raw: Late {{inh|en|enm|scrub}} in the sense of "stunted tree," a variant of {{m|enm|schrub||shrub, bush}}, from {{der|en|ang|scrybb}}. {{doublet|en|shrub}}.

set.raw: {{ety|en|id=put down|:inh|enm:setten|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|setten|}}, from {{inh|en|ang|settan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sattjan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*satjaną}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*sodéyeti}}, causative of {{m|ine-pro|*sed-||to sit}}.

shave.raw: {{inh+|en|enm|shaven}}, {{m|enm|schaven}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sċafan|t=to shave, scrape, shred, polish}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*skaban}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*skabaną|t=to scrape}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*skabʰ-|t=to cut, split, form, carve}}.

shorten.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|shortnen}}, {{m|enm|schortenen}}, equivalent to {{af|en|short|-en|pos2=verbal suffix|id2=inchoative}}. In some senses, a continuation (in altered form) of {{inh|en|enm|schorten|t=to make short, shorten}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sċortian|t=to become short}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*skurtōną|t=to shorten}}.

shower.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:schour|id=rain|tree=2}} From {{inh|en|enm|schour||shower}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sċūr||shower}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*skūru||shower}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*skūrō||storm, short shower}}, probably from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)ḱēwer-|t=north, north wind, cold wind, rain shower}}.

signature.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*sek-}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|id=follow}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|signature}}, or from {{bor|en|la-med|signātūra}}, future active periphrastic of verb {{m|la|signo|signāre}} from {{m|la|signum||sign}}, + {{m|la|-tūra}}, feminine of {{m|la|-tūrus}}, future active periphrastic suffix. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|handseten|lit=hand setting}}.

silly.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|seely}}, {{m|enm|seli|sēlī}},<ref>''Middle English Dictionary'', [http://quod.lib.umich.edu/cgi/m/mec/med-idx?type=byte&byte=172254099 "sēlī (adj.)"].</ref> from {{inh|en|ang|sǣliġ}}, {{m|ang|ġesǣliġ|t=lucky, fortunate}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sālīg}}, from {{m|gmw-pro|*sāli}}; equivalent to {{af|en|seel<t:happiness, bliss>|-y<id:adjectival>}}. {{doublet|en|Seelie}}.

since.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|syns}}, {{m|enm|synnes}}, contraction of earlier {{m|enm|sithens}}, {{m|enm|sithence}}, from {{m|enm|sithen||after, since}} ( + {{m|enm|-s}}, adverbial genitive suffix), from {{inh|en|ang|sīþþan}}, from the phrase {{m|ang||sīþ þǣm|after/since that (time)}}, from {{m|ang|sīþ||since, after}} + {{m|ang|þǣm}} dative singular of {{m|ang|þæt|}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|sinds||since}}, {{cog|de|seit||since}}, {{cog|da|siden||since}}, {{cog|is|síðan||since}} {{cog|sco|syne||since}}.

singe.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|sengen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|senġan}}, {{m|ang|sænċġan||to singe, burn slightly, scorch, afflict}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sangijan||to burn, torch}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*senk-||to burn}}. Cognate with {{cog|fy|singe}}, {{m|fy|sinzje|t=to singe}}, {{cog|stq|soange|t=to singe}}, {{cog|nl|zengen||to singe, scorch}}, {{cog|nds-de|sengen|t=to singe}}, {{cog|de|sengen||to singe, scorch}}, {{cog|is|sangur|t=singed, burnt, scorched}}.

skeptic.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|sceptique}} (but with a pronunciation closer to that of the Latin etymon), or possibly directly from {{bor|en|la-lat|scepticus}} (originally attested only in the plural {{m|la|Scepticī|t=the sect of Skeptics}}), from {{der|en|itc-pro|*spektos|t=see, observing}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*speḱ-|t=to see}}, compare to {{m|grc|σκοπέω|t=to view, examine}}.

smog.raw: {{blend|en|smoke|fog}}.<ref name="BackgroundOfBlending">{{cite-book|title=Globalistics and Globalization Studies: Global Transformations and Global Future|author=Olga Kornienko, Grinin L, Ilyin I, Herrmann P, Korotayev A|pages=220–225|url=https://hal-hprints.archives-ouvertes.fr/hprints-01794187/document|ISBN=978-5-7057-5026-9|year=2016|location=Volgograd|publisher=Uchitel Publishing House|chapter=Social and Economic Background of Blending|chapterurl=https://www.socionauki.ru/upload/socionauki.ru/book/files/globalistics_and_globalization_studies_5_en/220-225.pdf}}</ref>

sneeze.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*pnew-}} From {{inh|en|enm|snesen|t=to sneeze}}, alteration of earlier {{m|enm|fnesen|t=to sneeze}}, from {{inh|en|ang|fnēosan|t=to sneeze, snort}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*fneusan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*fneusaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*pnew-|t=to breathe, pant, snort, sneeze}}. Cognate with dialectal {{cog|nl|fniezen|t=to sneeze}}, {{cog|non|fnýsa|t=to snort}}.

society.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|id=follow}} {{etymon|en|:bor|frm:societé<id:society>|id=companionship|tree=1}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|societé}}, from {{der|en|fro|societé}}, from {{der|en|la|societas|societās, societātem|fellowship, association, alliance, union, community}}, from {{m|la|socius||associated, allied; partner, companion, ally}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sokʷ-yo-||companion}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-||to follow}}. {{etydate|1530s}}.<ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref>

species.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} From {{uder|en|la|speciēs||appearance; quality}}, from {{m|la|speciō||see}} + {{m|la|-iēs}} suffix signifying [[abstract]] noun. {{doublet|en|spice}}.

specious.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|speciose,specious}}, from {{der|en|xno|specious}}, {{der|en|frm|specieux}}, and their etymon {{der|en|la|speciōsus|t=good-looking}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''adj.'' and ''n.''|noformat=1|id=4532132448}}</ref>

spectacle.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|spectacle}}, from {{der|en|frm|spectacle}}, from {{der|en|la|spectāculum||a show, spectacle}}, from {{m|la|spectō||to see, behold}}, frequentative of {{m|la|speciō||to see}}. See {{m|en|species}}. {{doublet|en|spectaculum}}.

spectator.raw: Borrowed from {{bor|en|la|spectātor}}, from [[frequentative]] verb {{m|la|spectō||watch}}, from {{m|la|speciō||look at}}. Equivalent to {{suffix|en|spectate|or}}. {{doublet|en|speculator}}.

spectrum.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|la:spectrum|tree=1}} From {{bor|en|la|spectrum||appearance, image, apparition}}, from {{m|la|speciō||look at, view}}. {{doublet|en|specter}}. See also {{m|en|scope}}.

speculate.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} {{bor+|en|la|speculātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|active}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|speculor||to watch, observe, examine, spy}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|specula||a watchtower}}, ultimately from {{m|la|speciō||to look at}}.

spice.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:spice<id:plant substance>|id=plant substance|tree=1}} {{inh+|en|enm|spice}}, from {{der|en|fro|espice}} (modern {{m|fr|épice}}), from {{der|en|la-lat|speciēs||spice, good, ware}}, from {{der|en|la|speciēs||kind, sort}}. {{doublet|en|species}}.

spy.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|spien}}, aphetic variant of earlier {{m|enm|espien||to espy}}, from {{der|en|fro|espier||to spy}}, from {{der|en|frk|*spehōn||to spy}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*spehōną||to see, look}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-||to look}}. Akin to {{cog|de|spähen||to spy}}, {{cog|nl|spieden||to spy}}.

chain: to be in motion, move, agitate, stir, disturb, trouble
stir.raw: {{etymon|en|id=stiren|:inh|enm:stiren|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|stiren}}, {{m|enm|sturien}}, {{m|enm|steren}}, from {{inh|en|ang|styrian|t=to be in motion, move, agitate, stir, disturb, trouble}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*sturiz|t=turmoil, noise, confusion}}, related to {{cog|gmw-pro|*staurijan|t=to destroy, disturb}}. Cognate with {{cog|non|styrr|t=turmoil, noise, confusion}}, {{cog|de|stören||to disturb}}, {{cog|nl|storen||to disturb}}.

stripe.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|stripe}}, {{m|enm|strype}}, from {{der|en|dum|-}} or {{der|en|gml|strîpe}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*strīpā}}, {{m|gmw-pro|*strīpō}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*strīpô}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Striepe|t=stripe, strip}}, {{cog|fy|stripe|t=stripe}}, {{cog|nl|streep|t=stripe}}, {{cog|nds-de|Striepe}}, {{m|nds-de|Striep}}, {{m|nds-de|Streep|t=stripe}}, {{cog|de|Streifen|t=stripe, strip, band}}, {{cog|da|stribe|t=stripe}}.

stuff.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|stuf}}, {{m|enm|stuffe}}, from Anglo-{{der|en|la|stuffa}} and its etymon {{der|en|fro|estofe}}, {{m|fro|estoffe}}, {{m|fro|estuf}}, {{m|fro|estuffe}}, {{m|fro|stoffe}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=stuf(fe|pos=n|id=MED43448}}</ref> from {{m|fro|estoffer}}, {{m|fro|estofer|t=to provide what is necessary, equip, stuff}}, borrowed from {{der|en|goh|stoffōn}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*stoppōn|t=to clog up, block, fill}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''n.''{{sup|1}}|noformat=1|id=6841369943}}</ref><ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary|pos=n|v=22216}}</ref> More at {{m|en|stop}}.

chain: to go under, go from under, come under, approach, follow, take the place of, receive by succession, prosper, be successful
succeed.raw: From {{der|en|fro|succeder}}, from {{uder|en|la|succedo|succedere|to go under, go from under, come under, approach, follow, take the place of, receive by succession, prosper, be successful}}.

chain: to offer, hold up, bear, suffer
suffer.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰer-}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:suffren|tree=1<!--|text=++-->}} From {{inh|en|enm|suffren}}, from {{der|en|xno|sofrir|suffrir}}, from {{der|en|la|sufferō|sufferre|t=to offer, hold up, bear, suffer}}, from {{m|la|sub-|t=up, under}} + {{m|la|ferō|t=to carry}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰer-|t=to bear, carry}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|þrōwian}}.

suffix.raw: {{bor+|en|la|suffīxus||suffix}}, from {{af|la|sub-|t1=under|fīxus|pos2=perfect passive participle of {{m|la|[[figo|fīgere]]||to fasten, fix}}|nocat=1}}, equivalent to {{con|en|sub-|-fix}}.

suggest.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eǵ-|id=drive}} Coined based on {{uder|en|la|suggestus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|suggerō|t=bring up, bring under, lay beneath, furnish, supply, excite, advise, suggest|pos=verb}}, from {{m|la|sub|t=from below, under}} + {{m|la|gerō|t=bear, carry|pos=verb}}.

suggestion.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|suggestion}}, from {{der|en|xno|suggestioun}}, {{m|fro|sugestiun}}, from {{der|en|la|suggestiō}}, from {{m|la|suggerō|t=suggest|pos=verb}}, from {{der|en|la|sub-|t=from below, up}} + {{m|la|gerō|t=to bring}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|suggest|ion}}. Related to {{cog|en|[[up-]], [[cast]]}}.

summon.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*men- (think)}} From {{uder|en|xno|somoundre}}, from {{uder|en|fro|sumundre}}, from {{uder|en|la|summoneo|summonēre}}, itself from {{m|la|sub}} + {{m|la|moneo|monēre}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*monéyeti}}, causative from {{m|ine-pro|*men-||to think}}.

chain: to fill up, make full, complete, supply
supply.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:supplien|id=provide}} From {{inh|en|enm|supplien}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|soupleer}}, {{m|fro|souploier}}, from {{der|en|la|suppleo||to fill up, make full, complete, supply}}. The Middle English spelling was modified to conform to Latin etymology.

surrogate.raw: From {{der|en|la|surrogātus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|surrogō||to choose someone as a substitute}}; a variant of {{m|la|subrogō}}, from {{m|la|sub||under}} + {{m|la|rogō||ask}}.

suspect.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} From {{der|en|fro|suspect}}, from {{der|en|la|suspectus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|suspiciō|t=mistrust, suspect}}, from {{m|la|sub||under}}, + {{m|la|speciō||watch, look at}}.

sustain.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ten-}} From {{inh|en|enm|susteinen}}, {{m|enm|sustenen}}, from {{der|en|fro|sustenir}} ({{cog|fr|soutenir}}), from {{der|en|la|sustineō|sustineō, sustinēre|t=to uphold}}, from {{m|la|sub-|t=from below, up}} + {{m|la|teneō|t=hold|pos=verb}}.

chain: a sign by which one infers something; a mark, token, badge, ticket, tally, check, a signal, watchword, outward sign
symbol.raw: {{ety|en|:der|fr:symbole|tree=1}} [[File:Religious syms.png|thumb|upright|Symbols of various religions.]] From {{bor|en|fr|symbole}}, from {{der|en|la|symbolus}}, {{m|la|symbolum||a sign, mark, token, symbol, in Late Latin also a creed}}, from {{der|en|grc|σύμβολον||a sign by which one infers something; a mark, token, badge, ticket, tally, check, a signal, watchword, outward sign}}, from {{m|grc|συμβάλλω||to throw together, dash together, compare, correspond, tally, come to a conclusion}}, from {{m|grc|σύν||with, together}} + {{m|grc|βάλλω||to throw, put}}.

system.raw: {{multiple images |direction = vertical |image1 = Ceres solarsystem.jpg |caption1 = The [[solar system]] ''(sense 1.6)'' |image2 = Grand staff.svg |caption2 = [[musical notation|Musical notation]] indicating a system ''(sense 1.3)'', which consists of a [[treble staff]] ''(top)'' and a [[bass staff]] linked by a [[brace#Noun|brace]] ''(left)'' |image3 = Blausen 0316 DigestiveSystem.png |caption3 = The human [[digestive system]] ''(sense 1.4)'' }}

telescope.raw: From {{confix|en|tele-|-scope}}. From {{der|en|la|tēlescopium}}, from {{der|en|grc|τηλεσκόπος||far-seeing}}, from {{m|grc|τῆλε||afar}} + {{m|grc|σκοπέω||to look at}}.

tent.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ten-}} From {{inh|en|enm|tente||}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|tente|}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*tenta||tent}}, from the feminine of {{der|en|la|tentus||}}, ptp. of {{m|la|tendere||to stretch, extend}}, or contracted from {{m|la||*tendita}} as an alternate past participle. Displaced native {{cog|enm|tilt|tild, tilt|tent, tilt}}, from {{cog|ang|teld||tent}}. Compare {{cog|es|tienda||store, shop; tent}}.

tip.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:tip|id=end}} From {{inh|en|enm|tip}}, {{m|enm|typ}}, {{m|enm|tippe|t=tip}}, of {{unc|en|title=obscure and uncertain}} origin. Perhaps distantly related to {{m|en|top}}.

tonic.raw: {{etymon|en|id=tension|:uder|grc:τονῐκός|tree=1}} From {{uder|en|grc|τονικός}}, from {{m|grc|τόνος}}. 17th century writers believed health to be derived from firmly stretched muscles, thus ''tonic''; the extension of ''tonic medicine'' appeared in the late 18th century. {{surf|en|tone|-ic|alt1=ton(e)}}.

chain: disorderly group, a little crowd or people
trouble.raw: Verb is from {{inh|en|enm|troublen}}, {{m|enm|trouble}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|troubler}}, {{m|fro|trobler}}, {{m|fro|trubler}}, metathetic variants of {{m|fro|tourbler}}, {{m|fro|torbler}}, {{m|fro|turbler}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*turbulō}}, from {{der|en|la|turbula||disorderly group, a little crowd or people}}, diminutive of {{m|la|turba||stir; crowd}}. The noun is from {{inh|en|enm|trouble}}, {{m|enm|troble}}, from {{der|en|fro|troble}}, from the verb.

tummy.raw: Imitating a child's attempt to say {{m|en|stomach}}, via archaic colloquialism {{m|en|stummy}}. Compare {{m|en|twee}} and {{m|en|pasghetti}} for similar phonetic reductions.

tunnel.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:tonnel<ety:bor<fro:tonel>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|tonnel}}, from {{der|en|fro|tonel|tonel(e)}}, diminutive of {{m|fro|tone||cask}}, a word of uncertain origin and affiliation, although some linguists assume that it came from {{der|en|la-lat|tunna}}. Related to {{cog|ang|tunne||tun; cask; barrel}}. More at {{m|en|tun}}.

typhoon.raw: English texts mention {{m|en|typhon}}, {{m|en|tiphon}} as a Greek word for "whirlwind" since at least the 1550s,<ref name="Etymonline">{{R:Etymonline}}</ref><ref>Richard Eden, ''Decades of the New World'' (1555), translating ''De orbe novo decades'' by Peter Martyr, published in '''1895''' by Edward Arber in ''The First Three English Books on America'', page 81: "These tempestes of the ayer (which the Grecians caule ''Tiphones'', that is, whyrle wyndes) they caule, ''Furacanes''{{SIC}}: which they say, doo often tymes chaunce in this Ilande: {{...}}"</ref> referring to {{cog|grc|τυφῶν}},<ref n

unfriend.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|unfreend}}, {{m|enm|onfrend}}, equivalent to {{prefix|en|un|friend|pos1=noun/adjective prefix|id1=negative}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|unfrend||unfriend}}. Compare {{cog|ang|unfriþmann}}, {{m|ang|unwine}}.

chain: institution of higher learning, body of persons constituting a university
university.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|universite||institution of higher learning, body of persons constituting a university}} from {{der|en|xno|université}}, from {{der|en|fro|universitei|}}, from {{der|en|la-med|-}} stem of {{m|la|universitas}}, in juridical and {{der|en|la-lat|-}} "a number of persons associated into one body, a society, company, community, guild, corporation, etc"; in {{der|en|la|-}}, "the whole, aggregate," from {{m|la|universus||whole, entire}}. {{surf|en|universe|-ity}}.

until.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|vntil}}, {{m|enm|until}}, {{m|enm|untill}}, {{m|enm|ontil}}, {{m|enm|ontill}}, perhaps representing a northern variant of {{cog|enm|unto}} (see Modern English {{m|en|unto}}). {{surf|+pre|en|un|t1=against; toward; up to|id1=until|till|id2=inh-en-enm-til}}.

visible.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*weyd-}} From {{inh|en|enm|visible}}, from {{der|en|fro|visible}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|visibilis||that may be seen}}, from {{der|en|la|videre||to see}}, past participle {{m|la|visus}}; see [[vision]]. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|ġesewenlīċ}}.

warden.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:wardein|id=guard|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|wardein}}, from {{der|en|xno|wardein}}, from {{m|fro|warder|t=to guard}}, variant of {{der|en|fro|guarder|t=to guard}} (whence modern {{cog|fr|garder}}, also {{cog|en|guard}}), from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wardāną}}; related to {{cog|goh|wartēn|t=to watch}}. Compare {{m|en|guardian}}, {{cog|fr|gardien}}, from {{cog|fro|guardian}}, {{m|fro|guardein}}. Compare also {{m|en|ward}} and {{m|en|reward}}. {{doublet|en|guardian}}.

warranty.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:warantie<ety:der<xno:warrantie<ety:from<xno:guarantie>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|warantye}}, {{m|enm|warantie}}, from {{der|en|xno|warrantie}}, an {{uder|en|fro-nor|-}} variant of {{der|en|fro|guarantie}} (Modern {{cog|fr|garantie}}). {{doublet|en|guarantee|guaranty}}. More at {{m|en|warrant}}.

wedding.raw: {{ety|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:weddynge}} From {{inh|en|enm|wedding}}, {{m|enm|weddynge}}, from {{inh|en|ang|weddung|t=betrothal, espousal}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|wed|ing|id2=gerund noun}}. Cognate with {{cog|dum|weddinghe}}.

chain: to rush, to whizz, to squeal, to whine
whine.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱwey-}} From {{inh|en|enm|whynen}}, {{m|enm|hwinen}}, {{m|enm|whinen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hwīnan|t=to rush, to whizz, to squeal, to whine}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hwīnan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hwīnaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱwey-|t=to hiss, whistle, whisper}}. Cognate with {{cog|non|hvína}}, whence {{cog|is|hvína}}, {{cog|nn|kvina}}, {{cog|sv|vina}}, and {{cog|da|hvine}}. Despite the strong similarity in sound and meaning, not related with {{noncog|de|weinen}}, {{noncog|nl|wenen}}, from {{m+|gem-pro|*wainōną}} (for which see dialectal {{m+|en|ween#Etymology 3|ween|to

whole.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:hol<id:whole>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|whol}}, {{m|enm|hol|id=whole}}, {{m|enm|hole||healthy, unhurt, whole}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hāl||healthy, safe}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hail}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hailaz||whole, safe, sound}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*kéh₂ilos||healthy, whole}}.

wine.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:wyn<id:wine>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|wyn}}, {{m|enm|win}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wīn}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wīn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wīną}}, either directly or via {{der|en|la|vīnum}} (from {{der|en|itc-pro|*wīnom}}) from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wóyh₁nom||wine}}. {{doublet|en|vine|vino}}.

wipe.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*weyp-}} From {{inh|en|enm|wipen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wīpian||to wipe, rub, cleanse}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wīpōn||to wipe}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*weyp-||to twist, wind around}}. Cognate with {{cog|de|wippen||to bob}}, {{cog|sv|veva||to turn, wind, crank}}, {{cog|got|𐍅𐌴𐌹𐍀𐌰𐌽||to wreathe, crown}}, {{cog|ang|swīfan||to revolve, sweep, wend, intervene}}, {{cog|sa|वेपते|tr=vépate||to tremble}}. More at {{l|en|swivel}}, {{l|en|swift}}.

wrap.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|wrappen||to wrap, fold}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin. Perhaps related to {{cog|frr|wrappe|t=to press into; stop up}}, dialectal {{cog|da|vrappe|t=to stuff, cram}}, {{cog|gml|rincworpen|t=to envelop, wrap}}, {{cog|gml|wrempen|t=to wrinkle, scrunch the face}}, all perhaps tied to {{der|en|ine-pro|*werp-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*werb-|t=to turn, twist, bend}}.

version.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*wert-}} {{bor+|en|frm|version}}, from {{der|en|la-med|versiō}}, from {{der|en|la|vertō|t=to turn}}. Used in English since 16th century.

chosen.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|chosen}}, {{m|enm|ychosen}}, {{m|enm|ichosen}}, re-analysed variant of {{m|enm|coren}}, {{m|enm|icoren}}, {{m|enm|ȝecoren|t=chosen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|coren}}, {{m|ang|ġecoren|t=chosen}}, past participle of {{der|en|ang|ċēosan|t=to choose}}. Morphologically equivalent to {{suf|en|choose|-en|id2=past participle|pos2=past participle ending}}.

drunk.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|drunke}}, {{m|enm|drunken}}, {{m|enm|ydrunke}}, {{m|enm|ydrunken}}, from {{inh|en|ang|druncen}}, {{m|ang|ġedruncen||drunk}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*drunkanaz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*gadrunkanaz||drunk; drunken}}, past participle of {{der|en|gem-pro|*drinkaną||to drink}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|dronken}}, {{cog|fy|dronken}}, {{cog|nl|dronken}}, {{m|nl|gedronken}}, {{cog|nds-de|drunken}}, {{m|nds-de|bedrunken}}, {{cog|de|trunken}}, {{m|de|getrunken}}, {{m|de|betrunken}}, {{cog|sv|drucken}}, {{cog|is|drukkinn}}.

eaten.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|eten}}, from {{inh|en|ang|eten}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*etan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*etanaz}}; morphologically {{suffix|en|eat|en<id:past participle>}}.

lay.raw: {{ety|en|id=place|:inh|enm:leyen|tree=1}} {{inh+|en|enm|leyen}}, {{m|enm|leggen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|leċġan|t=to lay}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*laggjan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*lagjaną||to lay}}, causative form of {{inh|en|gem-pro|*ligjaną|t=to lie, recline}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*legʰ-|t=to lie, recline}}.

rung.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|rung}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hrung}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hrungu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hrungō}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|rong|t=pole, stanchion}}, {{cog|de|Runge|t=stake, pole, stanchion}}, {{cog|got|𐌷𐍂𐌿𐌲𐌲𐌰|t=a staff}}.

shown.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|schauen}}, {{m|enm|schewen|pos=past participle}}, alternative form of {{m|enm|schawid}}, {{m|enm|schewed}}, past participle of {{der|en|enm|schewen|t=to show}}. Morphologically equivalent to {{suf|en|show|n<id:past participle>}}.

taken.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|taken}}, {{m|enm|takenn}}, from {{inh|en|ang|tacen}}, {{m|ang|*ġetacen}}, from {{der|en|non|tekinn}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*tēkanaz}}, past participle of {{der|en|gem-pro|*tēkaną|t=to take; grasp; touch}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|takin}}, {{m|sco|tane}}, {{cog|da|tagen}}, {{cog|sv|tagen}}, {{cog|is|tekin}}.

worn.raw: By analogy to past participles like {{m|en|torn}} from {{m|en|tear}} and {{m|en|sworn}} from {{m|en|swear}}.

flown.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|flowen}}, {{m|enm|floȝen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|flogen}}, {{m|ang|ġeflogen}}, past participle of {{der|en|ang|flēogan|t=to fly}}.

chain: to fell, to cause to fall
fell.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|fellen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|fellan}}, {{m|ang|fiellan|t=to cause to fall, strike down, fell, cut down, throw down, defeat, destroy, kill, tumble, cause to stumble}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*fallijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*fallijaną|t=to fell, to cause to fall}}, causative of {{der|en|gem-pro|*fallaną|t=to fall}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₃elh₁-|*h₂peh₃lH-}}.

spoke.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*spey-}} From {{inh|en|enm|spoke}}, from {{inh|en|ang|spāca}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*spaikā}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*spaikō}}. Compare {{cog|sco|spaik||spoke}}, {{cog|nl|spaak}} and {{m+|en|spike}}.

threw.raw: From {{inherited|en|enm|threw}}, from {{inherited|en|ang|þrēow}} (''first and third person past tense of'' {{m|ang|þrāwan}}), from West Germanic ''*þreu'', from Northwest Germanic ''*þrerō'', from {{inherited|en|gem-pro|*þeþrō}} (''first and third person past tense of'' {{m|gem-pro|*þrēaną}}), [[Appendix:Glossary#reduplication|reduplication]] of ''*þrēaną''.

woke.raw: Shortened from {{m|en|woken}} or {{m|en|woken up}}, or derived from dialectal use of {{m|en||woke|pos=past participle of ''wake''}}. The sense of being aware of social injustice dates to at least the 1930s. The derogatory use has been most commonly used as of the 2020s.

meant.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|ment}}, {{m|enm|mente}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mǣnan|mǣnde, mǣndon}}, etc. Equivalent to {{suf|en|mean|-t}}.

stood.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|stod}}, from {{inh|en|ang|stōd}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*stōþ}}, {{m|gem-pro|*stōd-}}, past tense of {{m|gem-pro|*standaną|t=to stand}}.

ground.raw: {{etymon|en|id=earth|:inh|enm:ground<id:surface>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|ground}}, from {{inh|en|ang|grund}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*grundu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*grunduz}}. Cognate with {{cog|fy|grûn}}, {{cog|nl|grond}} and {{cog|de|Grund}}.

rose.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*Hwerdʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|rose}}, {{m|enm|roose}}, from {{inh|en|ang|rōse}}, but with its vowel influenced by {{der|en|fro|rose}}, both from {{der|en|la|rosa}}. {{box-top|cognates and more remote and uncertain etymology}} The Latin is of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin, but likely via {{der|en|osc|-}} from {{der|en|grc|ῥόδον|t=rose}} (Aeolic {{m|grc|ϝρόδον}}), from {{der|en|peo|sc=Latn|*vr̥dah||flower}} (compare {{cog|ae|𐬬𐬀𐬭𐬆𐬜𐬀|𐬬𐬀𐬭𐬆𐬜𐬀-}}, {{cog|sog||tr=ward}}, {{cog|xpr|wâr|sc=Latn}}, late {{cog|pal|tr=gwl|ts=gul|sc=Latn}}, {{cog|fa|گل|tr=gol|t=rose, flower}}, and Middle Iranian

meeting.raw: {{ety|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:meeting<alt:meeting, meting><ety:inh<ang:mēting<id:meeting>><ang:ġemēting>>}} From {{inh|en|enm|meeting}}, {{m|enm|meting}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mēting}}, {{m|ang|ġemēting|t=meeting, assembly, association, society}}, equivalent to {{af|en|meet|-ing|id2=gerund noun}}. Cognate with {{cog|fy|moeting|t=meeting, encounter}}, {{cog|nl|ontmoeting|t=meeting, encounter}}, {{cog|gml|mö̂tinge|t=meeting}}. Compare also {{cog|nds-de|Möte|t=meeting, encounter}}, {{cog|da|møde|t=meeting, encounter}}, {{cog|sv|möte|t=meeting, encounter}}, {{cog|is|mót|t=meeting}}. Related to {{m|en|moo

spirit.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:spirit|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|spirit}}, from {{der|en|fro|espirit||spirit}}, from {{der|en|la|spīritus||breath; spirit}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)peys-||to blow, breathe}}. Compare {{m|en|inspire}}, {{m|la|respire}}, {{m|la|transpire}}, all ultimately from Latin {{m|la|spīrō||to breathe, blow, respire}}. In this sense, displaced native {{noncog|enm|gast}} (from {{ncog|ang|gāst}}), whence modern {{noncog|en|ghost}}. {{doublet|en|spiritus|spirytus|sprite|spright|esprit}}.

refuse.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵʰewd-}} Borrowed into late {{inh|en|enm|-}} from {{der|en|frm|refusé}}, past participle of {{m|frm|refuser||to refuse}}. Displaced native Middle English {{m|enm|wernen||to refuse}} likely due to the similar sounding {{cog|enm|warnen}}

entry.raw: {{inh+|en|enm|entre}}, from {{der|en|fro|entree}} (feminine past participle of the verb {{m|fro|entrer}}, Modern {{cog|fr|entrée}}). From {{der|en|la|intrō}}. {{dbt|en|entrada|entrée}}.

interrupt.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:interrupten<ety:der<la:interruptus>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|interrupten}}, derived from {{der|en|la|interruptus}}, past participle of {{m|la|interrumpo|interrumpere|to break apart/off, interrupt}}, from {{m|la|inter||between}} + {{m|la|rumpo|rumpere|to break}}.

erupt.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*Hrewp-}} From {{bor|en|la|eruptus}}, past participle of {{m|la|ērumpō||to break out (of), to burst out (from)}}, from {{m|la|e||out}} + {{m|la|rumpō||to break}}.

bankrupt.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*Hrewp-}} {{partial calque|en|it|bancarotta|lit=a broken bench}}, from {{m|it|banca||[[bank]]|lit=[[bench]]}} + {{m|it|rotto|rotta|broken, rupted}}, which refers to an out-of-business bank, having its bench physically broken, signifying that the working moneylender was insolvent.

rupture.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|frm:rupture<ety:der<la:ruptūra>>|la:ruptūra|tree=1}} {{bor+|en|frm|rupture}}, or its source, {{bor|en|la|ruptūra||a breaking, rupture (of a limb or vein)}} and {{der|en|la-med|ruptūra||a road, a field, a form of feudal tenure, a tax, etc.}}, from the participle stem of {{m|la|rumpo|rumpere|to break, burst}}. {{doublet|en|roture}}.

pedal.raw: [[File:Bicycle pedal animation.gif|thumb|Animation of a Bicycle Pedal]] {{root|en|ine-pro|*ped-}} {{ety|en|id=lever|:bor|fr:pédale<id:lever>|tree=1}} {{bor+|en|fr|pédale}}, itself borrowed from {{der|en|it|pedale}}, from {{der|en|la|pedālis}}. {{surf|en|ped-|-al}}.

chronology.raw: {{etymon|en|:af|chrono-|-logy|tree=1}} From {{confix|en|chrono|t1=relating to time|logy|t2=study of, account of}}, after {{bor|en|la-new|chronologia}} from {{der|en|grc|χρόνος|t=time}} + {{m|grc|λόγος|t=reason, explanation}}. Literally "time reason" in [[Modern Greek]].

mortal.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*mer-|id=die}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:mortal//mortel<ety:uder<fro:mortal//mortel<ety:uder<la:mortālis>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|mortal}}, {{m|enm|mortel}}, from {{der|en|fro|mortal}}, {{m|fro|mortel}}, and their source {{der|en|la|mortālis}}, from {{m|la|mors||death}}. In this sense, displaced native {{m|en|deadly}}, from {{noncog|ang|dēadlīċ}}.

immortal.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*mer-|id=die}} From {{der|en|la|immortālis}}, from prefix {{m|la|im-||not}} (from {{m|la|in-}}) + {{m|la|mortālis||mortal}} (from {{m|la|mors||death}}, combining form {{m|la|mort-}} + adjectival suffix {{m|la|-alis}}), equivalent to {{af|en|im-|mortal}}. Displaced native {{m|en|undeadly}}, from {{noncog|ang|undēadlīċ}}.

survive.raw: {{ety|en|:der|la:supervivo<alt:supervīvere>}} From {{der|en|xno|survivre}}, {{der|en|fro|survivre}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|supervivo|supervīvere|t=to outlive}}, from {{der|en|la|super|t=over}} + {{m|la|vivere|t=to live}}, akin to {{m|la|vita|t=life}}. See {{m|en|vivid}}. Compare {{m|en|devive}}, {{m|en|revive}}. Displaced native {{ncog|en|thrive}}.

revive.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷeyh₃-}} The {{lg|verb}} is derived from Late {{inh|en|enm|reviven}}, {{m|enm|revyven|t=to recover from illness; to regain consciousness; to return to life after death; to happen again, recur; to be rejuvenated, renewed; (''figurative'') to bring back; (''alchemy'') of a metal: to be restored to its original form}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=revīven|pos=v|id=MED37386}}</ref> from {{der|en|xno|reviver}}, {{m|xno|revivre|t=to return to life after death; to rejuvenate, renew; to make (a law or legal document) valid again}}, {{der|en|frm|revivre}}, and {{der|en|fro|revivre|t=to

vital.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷeyh₃-}} From {{inh|en|enm|vital}}, from {{der|en|fro|vital}}, from {{der|en|la|vītālis||of life, life-giving}}, from {{m|la|vīta||life}}, from {{m|la|vīvō||to live}}. {{doublet|en|jiva|quick}}.

thermal.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷʰer-}} From {{der|en|fr|thermal}}, from {{der|en|la-new|*thermalis}}, from {{der|en|grc|θέρμη||heat}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʷʰer-||to heat, warm}}.

microscope.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}} {{etymon|en|id=optical instrument|:bor|it:microscopio<id:optical instrument>|tree=1}} From {{bor|en|la-new|microscopium}} and {{bor|en|it|microscopio}}, from {{der|en|grc|μικρός||small}} + {{m|grc|σκοπέω||to look at}}, equivalent to {{af|en|micro-|-scope}}.

hydrogen.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|fr:hydrogène|tree=1}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|fr|hydrogène|t=hydrogen}}, {{lg|coined}} by the French chemists {{w|Louis-Bernard Guyton de Morveau}} (1737–1816) and {{w|Antoine Lavoisier}} (1743–1794) from {{m|fr|hydro-|pos={{lg|prefix}} meaning ‘water’}} + {{m|fr|-gène|pos={{lg|suffix}} denoting a producer of something}},<ref>Compare {{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=1557804719|date=September 2024|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=n}}</ref> from the fact that water is produced as a compound when hydrogen is oxidized.

aquarium.raw: {{etymon|en|id=tank|:bor|la:aquārius<alt:aquārium>|tree=1}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|la|aquārium}}, neuter of {{m|la|aquārius||of or pertaining to water}}, from {{m|la|aqua}} {{suffix|en||arium}}. {{doublet|en|ewer}}; see also {{m|en|Aquarius}}. Also claimed to be {{coined|en|Philip Henry Gosse|nat=English|occ=naturalist|nocap=1}}, as a {{blend|en|nocap=1|aquatic|vivarium}}.<ref>{{cite-web|en|title=World's first aquarium|work=London Zoo|publisher=[[w:London Zoo|London Zoo]]|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240405204332/https://www.londonzoo.org/zoo-stories/history-of-london-zoo/worlds-fi

aquatic.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|frm:aquatique<ety:der<la:aquāticus>>|tree=1}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|aquatique||living in water}}, from {{der|en|la|aquaticus||relating to water}}, from {{m|la|aqua||water}}.

marine.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:marin}} Recorded since c.1420 as {{inh|en|enm|marin}}, borrowed from {{der|en|frm|marin}}, from {{der|en|fro|-}}, from {{der|en|la|marinus||of the sea}}, itself from {{m|la|mare||sea}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*móri||body of water, lake}} (cognate with {{cog|ang|mere||sea, lake, pool, pond}}, {{cog|nl|meer}}, {{cog|de|Meer}}, all from {{cog|gem-pro|*mari}}). The modern pronunciation is presumably due to the influence of modern {{cog|fr|marine}}, feminine singular of {{m|fr|marin}}.

solar.raw: {{ety|en|id=of the sun|:inh|enm:solar<ety:bor<la:sōlāris>>|tree=1}} From Late {{inh|en|enm|solar}}, from {{der|en|la|sōlāris}}, from {{m|la|sōl|t=sun}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sóh₂wl̥|t=sun}}.

cosmos.raw: [[File:Rho Ophiucus Widefield.jpg|thumb|A [[photograph#Noun|photograph]] of a [[portion#Noun|portion]] of the cosmos ''({{senseno|en|universe}})''.]]

chain: the art of dress and ornament
cosmetic.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱens-}} From {{der|en|fr|cosmétique}}, from {{der|en|grc|κοσμητική||the art of dress and ornament}}, {{m|grc|κοσμητικός}}, from {{m|grc|κοσμητής||orderer, director, decorator}}, from {{m|grc|κοσμέω||to order, to arrange, to rule, to adorn, to equip, to dress, to embellish}}, from {{m|grc|κόσμος|t=order}}. {{surf|en|cosmos|-etic}}.

democratic.raw: {{ety|en|:bor|frm:democratique<ety:lbor<la-lat:democraticus<ety:bor<grc:δημοκρᾰτῐκός>>>>|la-lat:democraticus|tree=1}} From {{der|en|frm|democratique|t=pertaining to democracy, democratic}} (modern {{cog|fr|démocratique}}), and its {{glossary|etymon}} {{der|en|la-lat|democraticus|t=pertaining to democracy, democratic; democrat}}, from {{der|en|grc|δημοκρᾰτῐκός|t=of or for democracy; favouring or suited for democracy}}, from {{m|grc|δημοκρᾰτῐ́ᾱ|t=democracy}} + {{m|grc|-ῐκός|pos={{glossary|suffix}} with the sense ‘of or pertaining’ to forming {{glossary|adjective}}s}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=adj.

sympathy.raw: {{bor+|en|frm|sympathie}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|sympathīa||feeling in common}}, from {{der|en|grc|σῠμπᾰ́θειᾰ||fellow feeling}}, from {{af|grc|σῠμπᾰθής|-ῐᾰ|t1=affected by like feelings; exerting mutual influence, interacting|t2=-y|pos2=nominal suffix|nocat=1}}. Equivalent to {{af|en|sym-|-pathy|t1=acting or considered together|t2=feeling}}.

apathy.raw: From {{der|en|fr|apathie}}, from {{der|en|la|apathīa}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἀπάθεια|t=impassibility”, “insensibility”, “freedom from emotion}}, from {{m|grc|ἀπαθής|t=not suffering or having suffered”, “without experience of}}, from {{m|grc|ἀ-|t=not}} + {{m|grc|πάθος|t=anything that befalls one”, “incident”, “emotion”, “passion}}. {{doublet|en|apatheia}}, which was borrowed directly from [[Ancient Greek]].

dynamic.raw: {{etymon|en|:der|fr:dynamique|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*dewh₂-}} From {{bor|en|fr|dynamique}}, from {{der|en|grc|δυναμικός||powerful}}, from {{m|grc|δύναμις||power}}, from {{m|grc|δύναμαι||I am able}}.

dynamite.raw: {{coin|en|Alfred Nobel|nobycat=1|in=1867}}. Ultimately from {{der|en|grc|δύναμις||power}} {{suffix|en||ite}}, most likely under the influence of {{m|en|dynamo}} or {{m|en|dynamic}}.

language.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:langage|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|langage}}, {{m|enm|language}}, from {{der|en|fro|language}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*linguāticum}}, from {{der|en|la|lingua||tongue, speech, language}}, from {{der|en|itc-ola|dingua||tongue}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s||tongue, speech, language}}. {{doublet|en|langaj}}. {{displaced|ang|ġeþēode}}. Mostly, but not fully, displaced native {{cog|en|tongue}}, in this specific sense, in common as well as academic usage.

verb.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*werh₁-|*dʰeh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|verbe}}, directly from {{der|en|la|verbum||word, verb}}, reinforced by {{der|en|fro|verbe}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*werdʰo-}}. {{doublet|en|verve|word}}.

verbal.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*werh₁-}} From {{der|en|fro|verbal}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|verbālis|t=belonging to a [[word]]}}. Equivalent to {{suffix|en|verb|al}}.

adverb.raw: {{ety|en|id=lexical category|:bor|fr:adverbe<id:adverb>|:afeq|ad-|verb}} {{bor+|en|fr|adverbe}}, from {{der|en|la|adverbium}}, from {{af|la|ad-<t:to>|verbum<alt:verb(um)><t:word, verb>|-ium|nocat=1}}, so called because it is used to supplement other words (not specifically verbs). {{surf|en|ad-|verb}}.

constellation.raw: {{PIE word|en|ḱóm}}{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eHs-}} {{multiple images |total_width = 338 |image1 = Orion1~.jpg |image2 = Orion (constellation) Art.png |footer = A [[photograph#Noun|photograph]] of the constellation [[Orion]] ''(left)'' with an [[illustration]] of how the constellation is supposed to represent the [[hunter]] [[w:Orion (mythology)|Orion]] in [[Greek#Adjective|Greek]] [[mythology]]. }}

liberal.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁lewdʰ-}} The adjective is from {{der|en|fro|liberal}}, from {{der|en|la|līberālis|t=befitting a freeman}}, from {{m|la|līber|t=free}}; it is attested since the 14th century. The noun is first attested in the 1800s.

deliver.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁lewdʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|deliveren}}, from {{der|en|xno|-}} and {{der|en|fro|delivrer}}, from {{der|en|la|dē}} + {{m|la|līberō||to set free}}.

confidence.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰeydʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|confidence}}, from {{der|en|la|cōnfīdentia}} (possibly via {{der|en|fro|confidence}}), from {{m|la|cōnfīdō||believe, confide in}} from {{m|la|con-||with}} + {{m|la|fīdō||trust}}.

chain: confident, i.e. self-confident, in a good or bad sense, bold, daring, audacious, impudent
confident.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰeydʰ-}} From {{der|en|frm|confident}}, from {{der|en|la|confidens||confident, i.e. self-confident, in a good or bad sense, bold, daring, audacious, impudent}}, present participle of {{m|la|confidere||to trust fully, confide}}. See {{m|en|confide}}.

faith.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰeydʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|feith|faith}} (also {{m|enm|fay}}), borrowed from {{der|en|fro|foi|fei, feid}}, from {{der|en|la|fidēs|fidem}}. {{dbt|en|foy}}. Displaced native {{cog|ang|ġelēafa}}, which was also a word for {{m|en|belief}}.

illuminate.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|illuminaten}}, borrowed from {{bor|en|la|illūminātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|illūminō||lighten, light up, show off}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}} for more), from {{af|la|in|lūminō|t2=light up|nocap=1|nocat=1}}, from {{m|la|lumen|lūmen|light}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|lȳman||to glow, shine}}. More at {{l|en|leam}}.

chain: of or pertaining to the middle
median.raw: Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|median}}, from {{der|en|la|mediānus||of or pertaining to the middle|pos=adjective}}, from {{m|la|medius||middle}} (see [[medium]]), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*médʰyos||middle}}. {{doublet|en|mean|mizzen}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|midde}}, {{m|ang|middel||middle}}. More at {{l|en|middle}}.

immediate.raw: From {{der|en|fro|immediat}} ({{cog|fr|immédiat}}), borrowed from {{der|en|la-lat|immediātus||without in-between, moderation}}, from {{der|en|la|in}} + {{m|la|mediātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|mediō||to halve, to be in the middle}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|medius||middle}}. {{surf|en|in-|alt1=im-|mediate}}.

chain: new, fresh, recent, recently made or done, strange, rare
novel.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*new- (new)}} From {{inh|en|enm|novel}}, from {{der|en|fro|novel||new, fresh, recent, recently made or done, strange, rare}} (modern {{m|fr|nouvel}}, {{m|fr|nouveau}}), from {{der|en|la|novellus||new, fresh, young, modern}}, diminutive of {{m|la|novus||new}}. {{doublet|en|nouveau}}.

innovation.raw: {{bor+|en|frm|innovation}}, from {{der|en|fro|innovacion}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|innovatio|innovatio, innovationem}}, from {{der|en|la|innovo|innovo, innovatus}}. Morphologically {{suffix|en|innovate|-ion}}.

annual.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:annuel|tree=1}} First attested around 1382 as {{inh|en|enm|annuel}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|annuālem}}, {{m|la|annuālis}}, related to {{der|en|la|annālis}}, adjective form of {{m|la|annus|t=year}}. Used to categorize plants since 1710.

anniversary.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:anniversary<ety:bor<xno:anniversarie>:bor<fro:anniversaire>:bor<frm:anniversaire>:bor<la-cla:anniversārius>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|anniversary,annyversarie,annyverary,annyversarye,anyversarye}}, from {{der|en|xno|aniversarie,anniversarie}} and {{der|en|xno,fro,frm|aniversaire,anniversaire}} (modern {{cog|fr|anniversaire}}) and their {{glossary|etymon}} {{der|en|la-cla|anniversārius|t=yearly|ng=in {{der|en|la-med|-}} also used as a noun, meaning {{m-g|anniversary}}, along with the {{glossary|neuter}} form {{m|la|anniversārium}}}}, from {{m|la|annus||year}} + {{m|la|ver

chain: to copy off, transcribe, sketch off, describe in painting or writing
describe.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)kreybʰ-}} From {{der|en|enm|descriven}}, from {{der|en|fro|descrivre}}, from {{der|en|la|dēscrībō||to copy off, transcribe, sketch off, describe in painting or writing}}, from {{m|la|dē||off}} + {{m|la|scrībō||write}}; see [[scribe]] and [[shrive]]. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|āmearcian}}.

description.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)kreybʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|descripcioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|description}} and its etymon, {{der|en|la|dēscrīptiō}}, noun of action of {{m|la|dēscrībō||to describe}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|describe|tion}}.

script.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:scrit|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)kreybʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|scrit}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|escrit}}, from {{der|en|la|scriptum}} (something written), from {{m|la|scrībō||write}}.

subscribe.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:subscriben<ety:bor<la:subscrībō<alt:subscrībere>>>}} From {{inh|en|enm|subscriben}}, {{m|enm|subskryben}}, from {{der|en|la|subscrībō|subscrībere|t=write beneath}}. {{surf|en|sub-|scribe}}. Compare its native {{noncog|en|-}} equivalent {{m|en|underwrite}}.

project.raw: {{ety|en|:bor|la:prōiectus}} From {{bor|en|la|prōiectus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|prōiciō||throw forth, extend; expel}}.

reject.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(H)yeh₁-}} From Late {{inh|en|enm|rejecten|}}, from {{der|en|la|reiectus}}, past participle of {{m|la|reicio|reicere|to throw back}}, from {{m|la|re-||back}} + {{m|la|iacio|iacere|to throw}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|āweorpan|lit=to throw out}}.

adjective.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|adjectif}}, {{m|enm|adjective}}, from {{der|en|fro|adjectif}}, from {{der|en|la|adiectivus}}, from {{m|la|adiciō}} + {{m|la|-īvus}}, from {{m|la|ad-||to, towards, at}} + {{m|la|iaciō||throw}}. The Latin word {{m|la|adiectivus}} in turn was a calque of {{noncog|grc|ἐπιθετικόν|t=added}}, a derivative of the compound verb {{m|grc|ἐπιτίθημι}}, from which also comes {{m|en|epithet}}.

inject.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*(H)yeh₁-}} From {{der|en|la|iniectus|iniectus, injectus}}, participle of {{m|la|iniciō|iniciō, injiciō|t=to throw in}}, from {{af|la|in-|iaciō<t:I throw>|nocat=1}}.

introduce.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*dewk-}} From {{inh|en|enm|introducen}}, from {{der|en|fro|introduire}}, from {{der|en|la|intrōdūcō}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₁énteros||inner, what is inside}} and {{m|ine-pro|*dewk-}}.

produce.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:produce<ety:der<la:prōdūcō>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|produce}}, from {{der|en|la|prōdūcō|t=to lead forth}}, from {{m|la|prō-||forth, forward}} + {{m|la|dūcō|t=to lead, bring}}.

reduce.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*dewk-}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:reducen<ety:der<fro:reduire>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|reducen}}, from {{der|en|fro|reduire}}, from {{der|en|la|redūcō||reduce}}; from {{m|la|re-||back}} + {{m|la|dūcō||lead}}. See {{m|en|duke}}, and compare with {{m|en|redoubt}}.

product.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:product<ety:der<la:prōductus>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|product}}, from {{der|en|la|prōductus}}, perfect participle of {{m|la|prōdūcō}}, first attested in English in the mathematics sense.

geometry.raw: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:gemetry<ety:bor<fro:geometrie<ety:der<la:geōmetria>>>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|gemetry}}, {{m|enm|geometrie}}, from {{der|en|fro|geometrie}} (modern {{cog|fr|géométrie}}),<ref>{{R:MED|id=MED18350|entry=ǧēmetrī(e|pos=n}}</ref> from {{der|en|la|geōmetria}}, from {{der|en|grc|γεωμετρία||geometry, land-survey}}, from {{m|grc|γεωμέτρης||geometer, land measurer}}, from {{m|grc|γῆ||earth, land, country}} + {{m|grc|-μετρία||measurement}}, from {{m|grc|μέτρον||a measure}}. {{surf|en|geometer|-y|id2=abstract noun}} or {{af|en|geo-|-metry}}. {{doublet|en|gematria}}. Displaced nati

lunar.raw: {{multiple images |direction = vertical |image1 = FullMoon2010.jpg |caption1 = The [[full moon]] seen from [[Earth]] on 22 October 2010 |image2 = A Man on the Moon, AS11-40-5903 (21039130393).jpg |caption2 = {{w|Buzz Aldrin}} photographed on the lunar surface ''(adjective sense 1)'' by {{w|Neil Armstrong}}, who is [[reflect]]ed in Aldrin’s [[visor]]. The two [[astronaut]]s, together with fellow [[crewmember]] [[w:Michael Collins (astronaut)|Michael Collins]], were part of the {{w|Apollo 11}} [[spaceflight]] that [[land#Verb|landed]] [[human being]]s on the [[Moon]] for the first time on 20 Jul

astronomy.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|astronomie}}, {{m|enm|astronemy}}, from {{der|en|fro|astronomie}}, equivalent to {{af|en|astro-|-nomy}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|tungolcræft}}.

navy.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|nave}}, {{m|enm|navye}}, from {{der|en|xno|-}}, {{der|en|fro|navie}}, from {{der|en|la|nāvigia}} < {{m|la|nāvigium}}, from {{der|en|la|nāvigō}}, {{m|la|nāvis||boat}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*néh₂us}}. Compare {{cog|grc|ναῦς||ship}}, {{cog|fa|ناو||boat, warship|tr=nâv}}, {{cog|sa|नाव||ship}}, {{cog|ang|nōwend||mariner, sailor}}. {{surf|en|la:nāvis|alt1=nav-|-y}}.

chain: cutting, cutting off, excision, amputation of diseased parts of the body, etc.
section.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*sek-}} From {{der|en|enm|seccioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|section}}, from {{der|en|la|sectiō||cutting, cutting off, excision, amputation of diseased parts of the body, etc.}}, from {{m|la|sectus}}, past participle of {{m|la|secāre||to cut}}. More at {{l|en|saw}}.

chain: a piece cut off, a strip, segment of the earth, a strip of tinsel
segment.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*sek-}} From {{der|en|la|segmentum||a piece cut off, a strip, segment of the earth, a strip of tinsel}}, from {{m|la|secāre||to cut}}.

negative.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁eǵ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|negative}}, {{m|enm|negatif}}, from {{der|en|fro|negatif}}, from {{der|en|la|negātīvus|t=that denies, negative}}, from {{m|la|negāre|t=to deny}}; see {{m|la|negate}}.

medical.raw: {{etymon|en|:bor|fr:médical|tree=1}} Borrowed from {{bor|en|fr|médical}}, from {{der|en|la-med|medicālis}}, from {{der|en|la|medicus}}. Replaced {{cog|ang|lǣċe||doctor (physician)}}, which is cognate with {{cog|is|læknir||doctor}}.

remedy.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*med-}} From {{inh|en|enm|remedie}}, from {{der|en|fro|*remedie}}, {{m|fro|remede}}, from {{der|en|la|remedium||a remedy, cure}}, from {{m|la|re-||again}} + {{m|la|mederi||to heal}}. {{doublet|en|remeid}}.

cogs: the poem ''{{w|Metamorphoses}}'' by the Roman poet {{w|Ovid}} or its contents
metamorphosis.raw: {{ety|en|:lbor|la:metamorphōsis|tree=1}} {{lbor|en|la|metamorphōsis}}, from {{der|en|grc|μεταμόρφωσις|t=transformation}}, from {{m|grc|μεταμορφόω|t=to transform, disguise}} + {{m|grc|-σῐς|pos={{glossary|suffix}} forming {{glossary|abstract noun}}s or {{glossary|noun}}s of action, process, or result}}; the former is from {{m|grc|μετᾰ-|pos={{glossary|prefix}} forming terms concerning change}} + {{m|grc|μορφόω|t=to shape, form}}.<ref name="OED">{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=7374725284}}</ref><ref name="Etymonline">{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary|pos=n}}</ref> The prefix is from the {{glossary|prepositi

chain: allegiance, fealty; faithfulness, trust; agreement made in good faith
fidelity.raw: {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰeydʰ-}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:fidelite|tree=1}} From Late {{inh|en|enm|fidelite|t=allegiance, fealty; faithfulness, trust; agreement made in good faith}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=fīdẹ̄litẹ̄|pos=n|id=MED15884}}</ref> from {{der|en|fro|fidélité|t=faithfulness, fidelity}} (modern {{cog|fr|fidélité}}), from {{der|en|la|fidēlitās|t=faithfulness, fidelity}}, from {{m|la|fidēlis|t=dependable, trustworthy; faithful, loyal}} + {{m|la|-tās|pos={{lg|suffix}} forming {{lg|feminine}} {{lg|abstract noun}}s denoting a state of being}}. {{m|la||Fidēlis}} is derived from {{m|la|fidēs|t=bel

geology.raw: From {{confix|en|geo|logy}}, partly after {{der|en|la-ren|geōlogia}}, from {{der|en|grc|γεω-||earth}} + {{der|en|la|-logia||the study of}}, from {{der|en|grc|-λογία}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=5248334874}}</ref>

forecast.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|forecasten}}, {{m|enm|forcasten}}, equivalent to {{prefix|en|fore-|cast}}. The noun is from {{inh|en|enm|forecast}}, {{m|enm|forcast}}.

foresee.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|foreseen}}, {{m|enm|forseen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|foresēon}}; equivalent to {{pre|en|fore-|see}}. Similar formations in {{noncog|nl|voorzien}}, {{noncog|de|vorsehen}}, {{noncog|la|prōvideō}}, (whence {{m|en|provide}} and {{m|en|purvey}}), {{noncog|grc|πρόοιδα}}, {{noncog|pl|przewidzieć}}, {{noncog|ru|провидеть}}.

foreword.raw: Morphologically {{prefix|en|fore|word}}. {{cal|en|de|Vorwort}}, itself a {{cal|en|la|praefatio|t=preface|nocap=1}}. Cognate with {{cog|nds-de|Vörwoord|t=foreword}}, {{cog|nl|voorwoord|t=foreword}}, {{cog|fy|foarwurd|t=foreword}}, {{cog|da|forord|t=preface; proviso}}, {{cog|sv|förord|t=foreword}}. Compare also {{inh|en|ang|forword}}, {{m|ang|foreword|t=proviso; condition}}.

forehead.raw: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:forhed|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|forhed}}, {{m|enm|forheed}}, from {{inh|en|ang|forehēafod}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*forēhaubid}}, corresponding to {{prefix|en|fore|head}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|foreheid||forehead}}, {{cog|nl|voorhoofd||forehead}}, {{cog|de|Vorhaupt||forehead}}, {{cog|da|forhoved||brow; forehead; face}}. Compare also {{cog|fy|foarholle||forehead}}, {{cog|nds-de|Vörkopp||forehead}}.

semicolon.raw: {{etymon|en|:af|semi-<t:half>|colon<id:punctuation>|text=+|tree=1|nodot=1}},<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=1166150387|date=June 2026|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=n}}</ref> from the fact that the mark is a [[colon]] (“{{l|mul|:}}”) with the lower half replaced by a [[comma]] (“{{l|mul|,}}”).

antonym.raw: From {{bor|en|fr|antonyme}} (1840s and 1850s), which was modeled on earlier {{m|fr|synonyme}} and influenced by the [[etymon#Noun|etymons]] of {{der|en|grc|ἀντωνυμία||pronoun}}; credit for popularization of the French loanword's [[naturalize#English:_linguistics|naturalization]] into English is given principally to Charles John Smith and his 1867 book ''Synonyms and Antonyms: Or, Kindred Words and Their Opposites. Collected and Contrasted.''<ref name="Smith-1867">{{cite-book |en |author=Charles John Smith |origyear=1867 |year=1868 |title=Synonyms and Antonyms: Or, Kindred Words and Their Oppos

cogs: to fail; go wrong; become wayward
misread.raw: From {{inh|en|enm|misreden}}, from {{inh|en|ang|misrǣdan|t=to advise wrongly; read wrongly}}, equivalent to {{af|en|mis-|read}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|misräide|t=to go wrong, fail}}, {{cog|nl|misraden|t=to guess wrongly}}, {{cog|de|missraten|t=to fail; go wrong; become wayward}}. For the noun, compare {{cog|ang|misrǣd||misguidance; misconduct}}.

preview.raw: From {{af|en|pre-|view}}; compare {{cog|fro|preveu|preveü}}, past participle of {{m|fro|preveoir||to foresee}}.

superman.raw: A {{calque|en|de|Übermensch|nocap=1}}; {{prefix|en|super-|man}}. The German word was introduced by the philosopher {{w|Friedrich Nietzsche}} (1844–1900) in his work ''Also sprach Zarathustra'' (''{{w|Thus Spoke Zarathustra}}'', 1883), and rendered in English as ''superman'' by Irish playwright {{w|George Bernard Shaw}} (1856–1950) in the play ''{{w|Man and Superman}}'' (1903) and by {{w|Thomas Common}} (1850–1919) in his 1909 translation of Nietzsche’s work.

photographer.raw: {{etymon|en|:af|photograph|-er<id:agent noun>|tree=1}} From {{af|en|photograph|-er|id2=agent noun}}, from {{uder|en|grc|φωτός|}}, genitive singular of {{m|grc|φῶς||light}} (fōs) and {{m|grc|γράφω||I [[write]]}}. {{surf|en|photograph|er}}.

parallel.raw: From {{bor|en|frm|parallèle}} and its etymon {{bor|en|la|parallēlus,parallēlos}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''n.'', ''adj.'', and ''adv.''|noformat=1|id=8954533823}}</ref> The verb is from the noun.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=v|id=5087416642}}</ref> See also [[para-]] and [[allo-]].
